chunks.text: p) Adequate toilet and hand washing facilities;

chunks.text: q) Wireless Internet and email communication services; separate internet services must be provided for operations (results services, ISSF TV, administration) and for the public;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: r) A Medal Ceremony area or a portable Medal Ceremony podium and backdrop that can be set up on the Finals Range;

chunks.text: 6.4.3 General Standards for 10m, 25m, 50m and 300m Rifle and Pistol Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.1 New 25m, 50m and 300m outdoor ranges should be constructed in such a way that the sun is behind the athlete as much as possible during the competition day. The range design must ensure that there are no shadows on the targets.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.2 Ranges must have a line of targets and a firing line. The firing line must be parallel to the line of targets.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.3 The design and construction of the range may provide the following features:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a). The range may, if necessary, be surrounded by safety walls;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Protection against the exit of accidental or unaimed shots from the range may be provided by transverse baffle systems between the firing line and the line of targets;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c). 10m ranges must be indoor ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) 25m and 50m ranges should, whenever possible, be outdoor ranges, but may, exceptionally, be indoor or closed ranges if required by legal or climatic conditions; or Finals Hall.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) 300m ranges should have at least 285m open to the sky;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) 50m ranges should have at least 35m open to the sky;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g)- 25m ranges should have at least 12.5m open to the sky; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) 25m and 50m Finals ranges may be indoor or outdoor ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.4 There must be sufficient space behind the firing points for the range officials and the Jury to perform their duties. There must also be a space provided for spectators. This area must be separated from the area for athletes and officials by a suitable barrier located at least 7.0m behind the firing line.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.5 Each range must be equipped with a large clock (a countdown clock is recommended) at each end of the range where the time can clearly be seen by athletes and officials. The Finals Range preparation area must also have a clock. Range clocks must be synchronized with results computers so that all timing devices show the same time. Rifle and Pistol Finals Ranges must have a count- down timer that shows the time remaining for each shot. Shotgun Ranges must have a count-down timer to use in controlling preparation times.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.6 Target frames or mechanisms must be marked with numbers (starting from the left) corresponding to their firing point number. The numbers must be large enough to easily be seen by persons with normal vision under normal conditions. The numbers should be of alternating and contrasting colours. On 25m targets, each group of five (5) targets must be lettered, starting with the A group on the left. 25m targets must also be individually numbered using numbers 11-20 for the targets in groups A and B, numbers 21-30 for groups C and D, etc.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4 Wind Flags for 50m Ranges and 300m Rifle Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.1 Rectangular wind flags, which indicate air movements on the range, should be made of a cotton or polyester material weighing approximately 150 g/m?. Wind flag height must correspond with the central area of the bullets’ flight paths without interfering with the bullet flight paths or athletes’ views of the targets. The colour of the wind flags must contrast with the background. Dual colour or striped wind flags are permitted and recommended. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 209

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.44.2 Wind Flag Dimensions and Locations

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.44.3 On 50m ranges, wind flags are to be placed at fixed distances from the firing line, on imaginary lines separating each firing point and its corresponding target from the adjacent points and targets. Flags must be placed on the athlete’s side of any safety baffle supports.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.44.4 If a 50m range is also used as a 10m enclosed range the 10m wind flags must be placed far enough down range so that they give an accurate indication of the wind.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.44.5 On 300m ranges, wind flags are to be placed at the above distances from the firing line on imaginary lines separating every fourth (4th) firing point and its corresponding target from the next point and target. Flags must be placed on the athlete's side of any safety baffle supports.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.6 Athletes must check the wind flags before the Preparation and Sighting Time starts to be sure they do not obscure their targets. Only Range Officers or Jury Members may reposition wind flags.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.7 Private wind indicators and the repositioning of wind flags by athletes are prohibited. 210 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.text: 6.4.5.1 Shooting distances must be measured from the firing line to the target face.

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.5.2 Shooting distances must be as exact as possible, subject to the following allowable variations.

chunks.text: 6.4.5.3 In combined 50m Rifle, Pistol and Moving Target ranges, the allowable variation can be increased to +2.50m for Moving Target. The opening must be accordingly adjusted.

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.54 The firing line must be clearly marked. The range distance must be measured from the target line to the edge of the firing line nearest to the athlete. The athlete’s foot or, in the prone position the athlete's elbow may not be placed on or in front of the firing line.

chunks.text: 6.4.6.3 Horizontal Variations for Firing Points on 50m and 10m Moving Target and 25m Pistol Ranges The centre of the firing points must be located as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.7 General Firing Point Standards for Rifle and Pistol Ranges The firing point must be stable, rigid and constructed so that it does not vibrate or move. From the firing line to approximately 1.20m rearward, the firing point must be level in all directions. The remainder of the firing point must either be level or may slope to the rear with a few centimetres drop.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.7.1 If shooting is done from tables, the tables must be approximately 2.20m long and 0.8m to 1.00m wide, rigid, stable and removable. Shooting tables may slope to the rear a maximum of 10cm.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.7.2 Firing Point Equipment. Firing points must be equipped with:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: a) Abench or stand, 0.70m — 1.00m high; rifle athletes may not place any item or material on the table to change its height;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) A mat for shooting in the prone and kneeling positions. Athletes must not alter shooting mats provided by the range. The front portion of the mat must be of a compressible material not more than 50mm thick, and approximately 50cm x 80cm in size and measuring not less than 10mm when compressed with the measuring device used to measure the thickness of Rifle clothing. The remainder of the mat must have a maximum thickness of 50mm and a 212 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: minimum thickness of 2mm. The minimum overall size must be 80cm x 200cm. An alternative of two mats is permitted, one thick and one thin, but together they must not exceed the dimensions indicated. The use of private mats is prohibited;

chunks.text: c) A chair or stool for the athlete on Qualification ranges; no chairs or stools for athletes may be placed on or near the firing points on Finals ranges;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: d) On new ranges, wind screens forward of the firing line are not recommended, but when necessary to ensure that wind conditions are as equal as possible throughout the range, wind screens may be used; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) When it is necessary to install dividing screens on the 300m firing line, they should be made of transparent material on a light frame. Screens should extend at least 50cm forward of the firing line, and be approximately 2.00m high.

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.8 Firing Point Standards for 300m Ranges The size of the firing point must not be less than 1.60m wide x 2.50m long. The width of the firing point may be reduced only if any dividing screens are constructed so that an athlete in the prone position can place his left leg in an adjacent firing point without disturbing that athlete.

chunks.text: 6.4.11.1 Roofs and screens of 25m ranges must provide the athlete with adequate shelter from wind, rain, sun and ejected cartridge cases.

chunks.text: 6.4.11.2 The firing point must be roofed or covered at a minimum height of 2.20m above the level of the firing point.

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.3 25m ranges must be divided into sections that are composed of two (2) groups of five (5) targets. Two (2) of five (5) targets are one bay.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.4 In 25m events, athletes must be squadded with one athlete in each group of five (5) targets for the Rapid-Fire Pistol event, and with four (4) (targets 1-2- 4-5), three (3) (targets 1-3-5) or exceptionally five (5) (all targets) athletes in a group of five (5) targets for the 25m Pistol, 25m Centre Fire Pistol and 25m Standard Pistol events.

chunks.text: 6.4.11.5 25m ranges may be either open or divided by protected walkways. In open ranges, target officers move from the firing line area to the targets. The screens must not obscure the officials’ and spectators’ views of the athletes.

chunks.text: 6.4.11.11 Function Firing Range. A specially designated and supervised function firing range, without targets, must be provided for athletes to test guns.

chunks.text: c) 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol Rapid-Fire Stage: Facing for three (3) seconds for each shot, alternating with an edge-on face away time of seven (7) seconds (0.1 second).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.13 Standards for 25m Electronic Scoring Target Systems When electronic scoring targets are used, the timing equipment must be set to add a total of 0.3 seconds to each established scoring time. This includes the established firing time +0.1 second (tolerance) plus an after-time of +0.2 second. The after-time ensures that shots that would have been valid skid- shots on paper turning targets, are scored according to the same standard on electronic targets. The green lights remain on for the required time +0.1 sec. and the electronic target must continue to record and score valid shots for an additional 0.2sec. after-time. Many 25m EST systems now have both the red and green light display positioned at the top of the target frame. 214 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.text: 6.4.14 Indoor Range Light Requirements (Lux) Type of Indoor General Lighting | Target Lighting Range Recommended Minimum Finals Ranges must have a minimum general lighting of 500 lux and minimum of 1000 lux on the firing line. For new ranges lighting of about 1500 lux on the firing line is recommended.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: 6.4.14.1 All indoor ranges must have artificial illumination providing the necessary amount of light without glare or distracting shadows on the targets or firing points. The background area behind the targets must be a non-reflecting, light even neutral colour.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.14.2 Measuring target illumination on targets with external lighting must be done with the measuring device held at the level of the target and pointed toward the firing point (A). Measuring target illumination on targets with internal lighting must be done by measuring reflected light from the target face.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.14.3 Light measurements can also be done in Lumen, especially LED lighting.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15 Standards for Moving Target Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.1 The range must be so arranged that the target moves horizontally in both directions across an open area with a constant speed. This area, where the target may be fired upon, is called the “opening”, wich the target is moving over.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.2 The protective walls on both sides of the opening must be of such a height that no part of the target is visible until it reaches the opening. The edges must be marked with a colour differing from that of the target. If a sled wider than the target is used, the effective target area shall be clearly marked in such a way that the moment at which the target becomes fully visible or completely obscured is unambiguous.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.3 Targets for 50m are placed on a trolley or target carrier. The trolley may move on rails, cable, or a similar system and must be moved by a driving unit which can be regulated accurately for speed. Targets for 10m are not changed for left and right.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.4 The shooting station must be arranged so that the athlete is visible to spectators. The shooting station must be protected from rain. The athlete should also be protected from sun and wind if this does not prevent spectators from seeing him.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.5 The shooting station must be at least 1.00m wide and aligned with a centre - line perpendicular to the target. The dry firing position must be located to the left of the shooting station. The shooting station must be screened on both sides with separating partitions so the athlete is not disturbed by dry firing or other extraneous influences. The separating partition between the firing point and the dry firing point must not be longer than to allow the dry firing athlete to watch the READY position of the competition athlete by observing the muzzle movement of his rifle.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.6 In front of the athlete there must be a bench or a table 0.70m — 1.00m high.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.7 Behind the athlete there must be a place for the Range Officer and at least one member of the Jury. The Register Keepers must be located either behind or at the side of the shooting station.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.8 Moving times for the targets are: Timing should preferably be done by using an electronic timer that is started and stopped by switches mounted on the rail. If this method cannot be used, timing may be done by using three (3) stop watches operated by three different persons. The middle (median) of the three (3) times must be counted. If the moving time is found to be less or more than that specified, range personnel or the Jury must regulate the time to within the specified moving time standards. If the timer is built into the starting control, the timing must be examined by the Jury and sealed.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.9 Timing must be electronically controlled and continually displayed for inspection by athletes and officials. Any deviation must be corrected immediately. 216 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.16.1 Special Standards for 50m Moving Target Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) There must be a vertical wall on both sides of the opening for the protection of operating personnel and scorers;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) There must be an embankment behind the opening. In front of the opening there must be a low wall to conceal and protect the target carrying mechanism; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The visible length of the target track must be: 10.00m (+0.05m/-0.00m) as seen from the firing point. This must be considered when measuring the opening since the distance between the visible corner of the wall and the target increases the distance over which the target is visible.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d)Wind flags are not permitted for 50m Moving Target. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 ©ISSF 217

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.16.2 Standards for 10m Moving Target Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If target changing and shot evaluation is done behind the target carrier, there must be sufficient protection for operating personnel and scorers. The target changing and evaluation must be supervised by a member of the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Behind the opening there must be a backstop to stop pellets and prevent ricochets. The target carrying mechanism must be protected by a front cover plate;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The visible length of the target track must be: 2.00m (+0.01m/-0.00m) as seen from the firing point. This must be considered when measuring the opening since the distance between the visible corner of the wall and the target increases the distance over which the target is visible;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Two shooting stations may be installed and used alternately, to save time. In this case, the two firing points must not deviate from the standards; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) When electronic scoring targets are used, the timing equipment must be set to give the nominal exposure times plus 0.1 second. This should ensure that the earlier appearance of the EST aiming mark is allowed for.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.17 General Standards for Shotgun Venues

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.17.1 Shotgun venues in the Northern Hemisphere should be laid out so shooting is toward a north to north-easterly direction. Venues in the Southern Hemisphere should be laid out so shooting is toward a south to south-easterly direction. These arrangements place the sun to the back of the athlete and on the target as much as possible.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.17.2 10m Ranges Where necessary and feasible, new Shotgun venues must be constructed with a reasonably level shot fall zone that is free of obstacles (a minimum of 90m from the front edge of the trap station), to permit mechanical salvage and the recovery of lead pellets. Net systems may also be installed to capture lead pellets.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.17.3 When Shotgun venues include more than one range, ranges must be identified, starting on the left, with letters (A, B, C, etc.) or numbers (1, 2, 3, etc.),.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.18 Standards for Trap Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.18.1 The Trap Pit The trap pit must be constructed so that the upper surface of the roof is on the same elevation as the surface of the shooting stations. Interior measurements of the trap pit should be approximately 20m from end to end, 2.00m from front to rear, and 2.00m to 2.10m from the floor to the underside of the roof. These dimensions will allow freedom of movement for working personnel and sufficient storage space for targets (see Figures).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.18.2 Distances Between Trap Pits The distance between the centre of machine fifteen (15) on Range A and the centre of machine one (1) on Range B must not be less than 35m. For pre- existing ranges with a distance less than 35m, as specified above, the Jury may reduce the throwing angles of the settings of machine 13 of Range A, and machine three (3) of Range B, if necessary, to prevent those targets from crossing over, into the target flight path of the adjoining range and disturbing those athletes. 218 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.18.3 The Traps (Target Throwing Machines) Each trap pit must have 15 traps attached to the front wall of the pit. The traps must be divided into five (5) groups of three (3). The centre of each group must be indicated only by a painted mark on the top of the roof which must be positioned so that it must indicate the point above the centre trap of each group at which a target must emerge when set to throw at zero (0) degrees. . The painted mark must be in the form of an isosceles triangle (the length, the sides of the triangle must be between 0.40m + 0.05m). The triangle must be positioned with its base in line with the edge of the roof of the trap pit. The distance between the traps within each group must be equal, from 1.00m to

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 1.10m. The distance between the centre traps of adjacent groups should be

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 3.00m to 3.30m. For existing ranges this may be 3.00m to 6.00m.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) In the case of use of machines with left-hand (clockwise) rotation of throwing arms the distance between the left side (viewed from behind) and the centre machine in each group may be reduced to less than the prescribed

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 1.00m to 1.10m (see also Rule 6.4.19.3).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The traps must be installed in the pit so that the pivot point of the throwing arm is 0.50m (+0.10m) below the top surface of the roof of the trap pit and set back 0.50m (+0.10m) from the front edge of the roof when the trap is set at the 2m elevation. This is defined as the Throwing Point. Traps may be fully automatic (self-loading and cocking), semi-automatic (hand loaded and self- cocking), or manual (hand loaded and cocked). Each trap must be provided with a means of sealing its elevation angle, and main spring tension after these have been inspected and approved by the Jury. All traps must be provided with a means of making target throwing settings on a precise setting. All traps which are hand loaded must have two stops fixed to them. The stops are necessary to prevent accidental or deliberate movement of the target forward or backward on the throwing arm, thus changing the preset directions of the target. Each trap must have the elevation and angle sectors marked in increments of 10 degrees.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The traps must be released by an electric-manual or electric-microphone system. The control system must be placed in such a position that the puller can clearly see and hear the call of the athlete. The release devices must guarantee equal distribution of targets to each athlete in a series of 25 targets. This distribution must be: ten (10) targets to the right, ten (10) targets to the left and five (5) targets to the centre. With the correct distribution, in a series of 25 targets, each group of traps must throw two (2) targets from the left trap, two (2) from the right trap and one (1) from the centre trap as the athletes progress from station 1 to 5. The 15 machines in each shooting range must be of the same make and model, no mixture of machines at the same range is permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The five (5) shooting stations must be arranged on a straight line at a distance of 15m + 0.05m to the rear of the front edge of the trap pit. Each station must be prominently marked with a square 1.00m x 1.00m which is centred on a line perpendicular to the line of shooting stations and extending through the painted mark which indicates the zero (0) degree exit point above the middle machine in each group of three. A sixth station must be marked about 2.00m to the rear and slightly to the left of Station 1 where athlete number 6 may take his position. In the Final Range, two additional waiting stations (7 & 8) to be positioned 1m behind station 6. All EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 219

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: eight (8) shooting stations may have a table or bench where the athletes can place their extra cartridges and other equipment. The stations must be firm and level in all directions. Each station must have at the front right and left hand corners a block of wood, piece of carpet or rubber about 15cm square or round upon which the athlete may rest his shotgun.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) For Trap Finals, medium intensity coloured lamps must be fitted to each microphone stand at a height of 40cm to 75cm to indicate when the microphone is live. The lamp system must be constructed to indicate a pause (microphone dead) of 5-25 seconds after each athlete has shot at a predetermined number of targets. At the end of the pause, the Referee must command “READY” and the athlete next to shoot must have a further 12 sec. preparation time to call for the target.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) 3.00m to 4.00m behind the line of shooting stations a path must be provided for mandatory use by the athletes moving from station 5 to stations 6, 7 or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8. Athletes must not pass between the path and the shooting stations. A wire, rope or other suitable barrier is to be erected 7.00m to 10.00m behind the return walkway. No spectators are to be allowed within this barrier. The Referee and Jury Members are responsible for enforcing this rule. The shooting stations, Referee stand and operator stand should have adequate protection from sun and rain, except that Finals ranges should, if possible, be open. 220 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.19 Standards for Skeet Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.19.1 A Skeet field consists of two houses (high house and low house) and eight (8) shooting stations. Stations 1 through 7 are arranged on a segment of a circle with a 19.20m radius and a base chord of 36.80m (with a tolerance of +0.25m) which is 5.50m from the centre point of the circle which is marked by a stake.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The centre of the circle which is marked by a stake also marks the base of the target crossing point.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Station 1 is located at the left end of the base chord and station 7 at the right end when standing anywhere on the segment of the circle and facing the centre stake. Stations 2 through 6 are located on the segment of the circle at points equidistant from each other (the distance between the centre of the front of the stations 1 and 2, 2 and 3, etc., is 8.13m +,+°+m on chord). Stations 8 and 4 are located at the centre of the base chord (see Figure).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Shooting stations 1 through 7 are 0.90m +0.05m x 0.90m +0.05m square, with two sides parallel to a radius of the circle drawn through the station marker (centre of the station). Shooting station 8 is rectangular, 0.9m +0.05m wide by 1.85m +0.05m long, with its long sides parallel to the base chord. The location of each shooting station must be accurately indicated. The markers for shooting stations 1 through 7 are on the centre of the side nearest the target crossing point. The marker for shooting station 8 is on the centre point of the base chord. All eight (8) shooting stations must be on the same level, within +0.05m difference in elevation.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.4.19.2 Target Distances, Angles and Elevations

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Each house must contain a clay target throwing machine in a fixed position. The throwing arm of the target throwing machine in the high house, when in a horizontal position, should be 2.80m +0.10m above the level of station 1 and the throwing arm in the low house should be 0.80m +0.10m above the level of station 7. The two target throwing machines must be of the same make and model.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Targets thrown from the high house must emerge at a point 0.90m + 0.05m behind the station marker 1 (measured along the extended base chord) and 3.05m +0.05m above the level of the station. Targets thrown from the low house must emerge at a point 0.9m + 0.05m behind station marker 7 (measured along the extended base chord) (moved 0.75m + 0.05m to the exterior of the base chord) and 1.05m + 0.05m above the level of station 7.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Targets properly released must pass through a circle 0.90m - 0.95m in diameter, located 4.60m +0.05m above the centre point.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) In calm weather conditions targets must carry a distance of 68.00m +1.00m as measured from the face of the house behind stations 1 and 7. If the correct distance cannot be verified by measurement, the Jury will decide the trajectory of the targets.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The shooting boundaries of stations 1 to 7 are 40.30m +0.10m from the face of each house. For station 8 the shooting boundary is determined by the crossing point between a straight line running from station 4 to station 8 and the target crossing point. Suitable markers must be placed on the target flight path, at points 40.30m +0.1m from both the high house and the low house, to indicate the shooting boundaries. Similar markers must be placed at 67.00m and 69.00m to indicate the distance a regular target must fly. The tops of these distance markers should indicate the ground level. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 223

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) A safety shield must be installed at the opening of each trap house so that the trap operator is not visible to an athlete on any station. This precaution is mandatory as a safety measure to protect the operator from possible injury from direct or ricocheting shot, and the athletes from broken targets emerging from the opening of the trap house. A wire, rope or other suitable barrier is to be erected 10.00m to 13.00m behind Station 4 and parallel to the base chord. No spectators are allowed within this barrier. The Referee and Jury Members are responsible for the enforcement of this Rule.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) The traps must be released by an electric-microphone system (see note below) with a timer device which must be installed so as to allow the operator to see and hear the athletes. For all ISSF Championships the use of a timer is mandatory. chunks.text: 6.6 CHAMPIONSHIP ADMINISTRATION

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1 Championship Programme and Schedule The administration of ISSF Championships shall be carried out in accordance with this Rule, except that the administration of Olympic and Continental Games Shooting Championships shall be carried out in accordance with the charter and regulations of the IOC or the appropriate Continental NOC organization.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.1 Official Championship Programme. The office of the ISSF Secretary General will provide a standardized Championship Programme and coordinate the preparation of an Official Championship Programme with each Organizing Committee to be finalized in November of the year before the Championship. The Official Championship Programme, including invitations, schedules, the official symbol or logo and entry forms will be posted on the ISSF website and the Organizing Committee must publish the Official Programme and send it to all ISSF Member Federations as soon as possible after it is finalized. It is recommended the ISSF Technical Delegate with the organising committee produce the general information and publish it online a minimum of 6 months before the start of the championship.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.2 Official Schedule. The office of the ISSF Secretary General, the Organizing Committee and the Technical Delegate appointed for the Championship must prepare a detailed Official Schedule for each Championship. Championship schedules should include an official arrival day, at least one day of Official Training, or Pre-Event Training (PET) the necessary competition days and an official departure day. World Championship schedules, including Official Training days and the opening and closing ceremonies, should not exceed 20 days. Ranges may be open for additional Unofficial Training before the Official Training Day (PET) at the option of the Organizing Committee and the ISSF. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 229

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.3 Official Schedules must provide dates and times for Opening Ceremony, unofficial Training, Pre-Event Training, Elimination Relays, Qualification Relays or Rounds for Shotgun, Technical Meeting, Equipment Control availability, Finals Reporting Times, Finals and Medal Ceremonies. When creating Programmes for ISSF Championships, a minimum period of one and a half hours must be allowed between end of Qualification and Final Reporting time. Schedule changes, as approved by the Technical Delegate, must be made as soon as possible after the Final Entry Deadline and distributed to all participating delegations.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.4 Entry Status and Limits. National Federations may enter a maximum of three (3) athletes per nation per event who are competing for awards (in-competition) in ISSF Championship events. In addition, in World Cups, the Organizing Committee may accept a maximum of two additional athlete entries per nation, per event, that may compete for Ranking Points Only (RPO), Olympic MQS status (MQS only) or participate out-of-competition (OOC), however, RPO, MQS or OOC status is only possible if there are more than three (3) starts in an event for that country.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.5 Maximum Entry. The Organizing Committee and Technical Delegate must establish the Maximum Entry (range capacity) for each event on the programme. Final entries that exceed the maximum entry for an event will be placed on a waiting list and will only be accepted if entry spaces become available before the Late Entry Deadline.

chunks.text: 6.6.2 Technical Meeting A Technical Meeting conducted by the Competition Director and Technical Delegate(s) must be scheduled on the day before the first competition day to inform team leaders about competition details and any schedule changes. A separate Technical Meeting may be arranged for shotgun events if more advantageous for arriving teams.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.6.3.1 Official Training. Official Training will be allocated within the programme if time permits.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.6.3.2 Pre-Event Training (PET). Pre-Event Training must be provided for every individual event on the programme, before Elimination or Qualification for that event starts. For Rifle, Pistol and Moving Target individual events, each athlete must be allowed to train on his allocated competition target for a minimum of 40 minutes per relay (30 minutes per relay for Rapid-Fire Pistol, 15 minutes per athlete for Moving Target) on a day before the event, where ever possible. This is in addition to the Official Training day(s) in the programme (for Shotgun, see Rule 9.6.2.1). If Mixed Team events follow comparable individual events, Pre-Event Training with open target allocations may be scheduled for these events when time is available in the schedule. If PET for Mixed Team events is provided for in the programme, this should be for a minimum of 30 minutes.

chunks.text: 6.6.3.3 Unofficial Training. In addition to Official Training and scheduled Pre-Event Training, athletes should be given additional Unofficial Training opportunities when the shooting ranges are available, this will usually also be on Arrival Day.

chunks.text: 6.7.7.1 All athletes must be provided with a Bib Number (Start Number) to wear on the back of the outer garment above the waistline during the entire competition. Bib Numbers must display the athlete’s allocated number for that Championship, family name, initial and nation (IOC abbreviation only). If a flag of the nation is used, it must be placed to the left of the IOC abbreviation. The height of the letters in names should be as big as possible, but no letters or numbers may be less than 20mm (for Shotgun, see 9.13.2, 9.13.3).

If the Bib Number is available and not worn, the athlete may not compete. New Finals Start Numbers will be issued at Reporting Time prior to Shotgun Finals and 25m RFP Finals. Finals Start numbers will not be worn for other Rifle & Pistol Finals.

chunks.text: 6.7.9.1 Post-competition checks must be conducted after Elimination and Qualification competitions according to procedures specified in the “ISSF Equipment Control Guidelines.” The Equipment Control Jury is responsible for supervising the conduct of all post-competition checks. Judges of the same gender as the athletes must be available for clothing and taping checks. Failure of the following specific post-competition checks must result in disqualification (DSQ):

chunks.text: 6.8 COMPETITION JURY DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS Juries are responsible for advising, assisting and supervising the competition officials appointed by the Organizing Committee.

chunks.text: b) RTS (Results, Timing and Scoring) Juries supervise scoring and results operations; and produce the Competition Results Book in cooperation with the Official Results Provider.

chunks.text: d) VAR System. Jury (In case VAR is used) is responsible for functioning and controlling the VAR system, he will be designated to operate the monitor as needed during finals. He will oversee the system's operation and ensure its proper use in accordance with established protocols.

chunks.text: 6.8.1 Range Officers, RTS Officers and Referees appointed by the Organizing Committee and the ISSF are responsible for the actual conduct of the competitions while Juries act in an advisory and supervisory capacity. It is recommended that all Target Officers or other personnel who must go forward of the firing lines to perform their duties wear a vest in a fluorescent colour or high visibility armbands.

chunks.text: 6.9.1 Chief Range Officer (CRO) Duties and Functions A Chief Range Officer (CRO) must be appointed for each range, (Only one CRO for all shotgun ranges). The CRO is in charge of all Range Officers (RO) and range personnel and is responsible for the correct conduct of the shooting event. The CRO is responsible for giving all range commands and for ensuring the cooperation of range personnel with the Jury. The CRO is responsible for the rapid correction of any equipment failures and for making available the necessary experts and supplies to operate the range. It is strongly recommended that an Assistant CRO be appointed to serve as a backup for the CRO, especially in maintaining range documentation and Range Incident Reports (Form IR) regarding events and irregularities that occur during the competition. 238 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.9.2 Range Officer (RO) Duties and Functions (not in Shotgun). A Range Officer (RO) must be appointed for each Range Section or for each ten (10) firing points. Range Officers must:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Be responsible to the CRO for the conduct of the competition in the target section entrusted to them;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Check the names and Bib Numbers of athletes to ensure that they correspond with the start list;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Ensure that the athletes’ guns, equipment and accessories have been examined and approved;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Check athletes’ shooting positions and equipment and advise the Jury of any possible violations;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Ensure that the commands of the CRO are followed;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) Take necessary actions regarding a malfunction, protest, disturbance, or any other matter arising during the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) Receive verbal protests and immediately report them to a Jury Member;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) Record all irregularities, disturbances, penalties, malfunctions, cross-fires, extra time allowed, repeated shots authorized, etc. on Range Incident Report Forms (IR) and on the target or printer strip as appropriate; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) Refrain from any conversations with athletes or from making other comments regarding scores.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.9.3 Chief RTS (Results, Timing and Scoring) Officer (CRTSO) Duties and Functions The CRTSO must be appointed for each Championship. He is in charge of all RTSO and Entry and Results Personnel. The CRTSO is responsible for the correct conduct of all scoring and results operations at the Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.9.4 RTS Officers (RTSO) Duties and Functions (not in shotgun). One RTSO should be appointed for each range that is used for Qualification competitions. The RTSOs are responsible for working with the RTS Jury, Competition Jury, ROs and Official Results Provider to facilitate the conduct of scoring and results operations on their ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10 EST COMPETITION OPERATIONS

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.1 EST Technical Officers

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) EST Technical Officers are responsible for operating and maintaining the Electronic Scoring Target equipment;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) EST Technical Officers may advise Range Officers and Jury Members, but they must not make any decisions regarding the application of ISSF Rules; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) EST Technical Officers are designated by the Official Results Provider or the Organizer and must be persons with special training in EST operations and electronic competition management systems (computer software).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.2 Target Officers

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Target Officers are appointed by the Organizing Committee to assist in the operation and maintenance of EST: EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 239

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Before each relay of each event, Target Officers must ensure that there are no shot holes on the white surface of the target and that all shot marks on the frame are clearly indicated;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) During competitions, Target Officers patch Backing Targets and Backing Cards and change the Control Sheets; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Backing Targets, Backing Cards and Control Sheets must not be patched or changed until after all scoring is completed.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.3 Jury Member Duties — Electronic Scoring Targets

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.3.1 Member(s) of the RTS Jury must be present on the ranges to supervise scoring and results operations and assist in the resolution of any questions or protests relating to scoring. Members of the Competition Jury must assist in cases where actions or decisions need to be taken and there are only two or fewer RTS Jury Members available.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.3.2 Before each relay of an event, a Jury Member must inspect the electronic scoring targets to confirm that:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) There are no shot holes on the white surface of the target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Any shot marks on the frame are clearly indicated;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The Control Sheets are renewed; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The Backing Cards and Backing Targets have no shots outside of the central area that is covered by the Control Sheet.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.4 Shooting on Electronic Scoring Targets

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Athletes must familiarize themselves during training with the control buttons that alter the target presentation on the monitor screen (ZOOM) and that change from a Sighting target (SIGHTING) to a Match target (MATCH);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) In 10m, 25m and 50m single position events, changing from Sighting to MATCH shots is under control of range personnel. If any athlete is in doubt, he must ask a Range Officer for assistance;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) In 3-Position events, after athletes complete the kneeling or prone positions, changing from MATCH to Sighting and back to MATCH is the responsibility of the athlete. Athletes may fire unlimited Sighting shots before starting MATCH firing shots in the prone and standing positions. No additional time is allowed for these Sighting shots. If an athlete inadvertently fails to switch from MATCH to Sighting after changing positions, any shots recorded as extra shots in the previous position must be nullified and the target must be reset to Sighting.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Itis not permitted to obscure the athlete’s monitor-screen or any part of the screen. The whole screen must be visible to the Jury and range personnel;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Athletes and range officials must not touch the printer control panels and/ or printout before the end of the relay or event, except when authorized by the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) Athletes should sign the printout (next to the score total) before leaving the range to identify their score.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) When an athlete fails to sign the printout a Jury Member or range official should initial this printer strip to allow it to be sent to the RTS Office.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.5 Target Scoring Complaints During Sighting Shots 240 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: If an athlete complains during sighting shots about the correct recording or evaluation of the shot(s), the Jury may offer to move him to another firing point.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete will be given appropriate extra time;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The Jury will, as soon as possible, examine the sighting shot(s) on the original firing point by applying the Procedure for EST Examination; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If this subsequent examination confirms that the target on the original firing point provided correct results, the athlete will be penalized with the DEDUCTION of two (2) points from the lowest value shot of his first competition series.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.6 Failure of the Paper or Rubber Band to Advance If the Jury confirms that the problem causing an athlete complaint is because the paper or rubber band is not advancing properly:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete will be moved to a reserve position;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) He will be permitted unlimited sighting shots to be taken within the time remaining for the event plus any additional time granted;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) He will repeat the number of MATCH shots determined by the Jury plus the number of shots necessary to complete the event;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) After the relay, the RTS Jury will decide which shots are to be counted from each target; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The athlete will be credited with the scores of all shots that were correctly displayed on the monitor of the first target, plus the scores of all MATCH shots fired on the second target that were necessary to complete the course of fire.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.7 Protest Concerning a Shot Value If a shot registers and displays, but the athlete protests the value indicated in accordance with Rule 6.16.5.2:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) After the relay, the detailed printer results (LOG-Print) must be generated by the Technical or Range Officers for all firing lanes on which complaints or protests have been made, and for the immediately adjacent lanes, before the target systems are reset for the next relay;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) After the completion of the relay, the Procedure for EST Examination will be applied;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Any non-indicated or incorrectly indicated shot must be scored by the RTS Jury; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If the RTS Jury determines that a protested shot was scored correctly, a two (2) point penalty will be applied (6.16.5.2.c).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8 PROCEDURE FOR EXAMINING ELECTRONIC SCORING TARGETS FOLLOWING A SCORE PROTEST OR COMPLAINT

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.1 If there is a score protest, complaint or no indication of a shot, etc., a Jury Member must collect the following items (the number of the firing point and the orientation of the card, sheet or target, the relay and series and the time of collection must be noted on each):

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The Control Sheet (25m / 50m). If the location of any shot hole is out of the area of the Control Sheet, the geometric relation between the shot holes on the EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 241

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: Control Sheet and the Backing Card must be made before the Control Sheet is removed;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The Backing Card (25m / 50m / 300m);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The Backing Target (25m);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The black paper strip (10m);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The black rubber band (50m);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) The Range Incident Report;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) The LOG print; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) The data record from the electronic scoring target computer (if necessary).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.2 A Jury Member must examine the face of the EST and the frame and record the location of any shots outside the black aiming mark.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.3 No CLEAR LOG must be made before the RTS Jury has given permission.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.4 The number of shot holes must be counted and their location taken into account.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.5 Jury Members must examine these items and then make independent assessments before a formal Jury decision is made.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.6 A Jury Member must supervise any manual intervention of the control computer results (e.g. the recording of penalties, corrected scores after malfunctions etc.).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9 EST FAILURE These Rules apply to 10m, 50m and 300m EST. For procedures concerning 25m EST failures, see Rule 8.10. For procedures concerning Moving Target EST failures, see Rule 10.11.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9.1 When ALL Targets on a Range Fail

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The time of failure and the expired shooting time must be recorded by the Chief Range Officer and the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) All completed competition shots of each athlete must be counted and recorded. In the event of a range power supply failure, this may involve waiting until the power supply is restored to enable the number of shots registered by the target, not necessarily on the firing point monitor, to be established; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) After the failure is rectified and the full range is in operation, an additional five (5) minutes will be added to the competition time remaining. The time for recommencing is to be announced over the loudspeaker system at least five (5) minutes beforehand. Athletes must be allowed to resume their position in the five (5) minutes before the competition restarts. Unlimited sighting shots must be allowed during the remaining shooting time, but only before competition shots are resumed.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9.2 When a SINGLE Target Fails

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If the EST cannot be repaired within five (5) minutes, the athlete must be moved to a reserve position;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) When he is ready to shoot, an additional five (5) minutes will be added to the competition time remaining; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) He will be permitted unlimited sighting shots before he starts the remaining competition shots. 242 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9.3 When a Shot Fails to Register or Display on the Monitor The athlete must immediately inform the nearest Range Officer of the failure. The Range Officer must make a written note of the time of the complaint. One or more Jury Member(s) must go to the firing position. The athlete must be directed to fire one more MATCH shot at his target: If the value and location of this shot is registered and displayed on the monitor:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must be directed to continue the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The value, location and time of firing of this extra shot must be recorded, its shot-number (after including the missing shot) and its value and its shot- location, and the firing point number must be given to the Jury in writing and recorded on the Range Register and a Range Incident Report;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) After the end of that relay, the Procedure for EST Examination will be applied. Using this information and the time of the extra shot and its location, the RTS Jury will determine whether all shots, including the extra shot, are recorded on the computer record;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If all the shots are recorded correctly, then the questioned shot (shot that did not register or display) will be counted in the score of the athlete, as well as the shot fired immediately after (as the “extra” shot), but the last shot fired (extra to the competition) will be annulled;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) If the questioned shot was not located by applying the Procedure for EST Examination or was confirmed as an off-target miss (Note: This means a questioned 10m shot could not be found on the witness strip or target face; a questioned 25m shot could not be found on the backing target, control sheet or backing card or there was evidence that a questioned 50m or 300m shot was an off-target miss), then the questioned shot must be scored as a miss and the last shot fired (extra to the competition) must be nullified; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) If the questioned shot was found or was located in the computer memory, the RTS Jury must determine and count the score of the questioned shot; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) If a questioned 50m or 300m shot is not found, the Jury must decide whether to score the missing shot as a miss and nullify the last shot or, if there is no credible evidence that the questioned shot was an off-target miss, the Jury may conclude that a target system anomaly occurred and count the extra shot in lieu of the missing shot and the last shot fired.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9.4 OR: If the extra shot fired as directed does not register or display and the EST cannot be repaired within five (5) minutes:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: a) The athlete must be moved to a reserve position;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) When he is ready to shoot, an additional five (5) minutes will be added to the competition time remaining and he will be permitted unlimited sighting shots;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) In 10m and 50m Rifle and Pistol Events, the athlete will repeat the two (2) MATCH shots that did not register or display on the previous target used.

chunks.text: 6.10.9.5 OR: In Moving Target Events, the athlete will be permitted two (2) minutes to resume his position and then allowed two (2) additional sighting shots (Rule

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.2). Then he will repeat the two (2) competition shots which did not register or display on the previous target used and fire the remaining shots of the series. The athlete will be credited with the score of all the shots that were EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 243

chunks.text: displayed on the monitor of the first target plus the score of all the properly fired competition shots that were displayed on the second target used. If the two (2) extra shots were later found in the computer record of the previous target they will be annulled.
