chunks.text: 7.5.4.1 Thickness of material - The body and sleeves of the jacket may consist of more than one layer of material, including a thin inner lining, provided that the maximum combined thickness of 2.5mm, (single) or 5mm (double) thickness is not exceeded. (see 7.5.2.1).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.2 Closure - Closure of the jacket must be only by non-adjustable means e.g. buttons or zippers. The jacket must not overlap more than 100mm at the closure (see Jacket diagram). The jacket must hang loosely on the wearer. To determine this, the jacket must be capable of being overlapped beyond the normal closure by at least 80mm, measured from the centre of the button to the outside edge of the button hole. The measurement will be taken with the arms at the sides. A measurement must be made with an overlap gauge with a tension of 6.0kg to 8.0kg. The area surrounding the button hole is limited to a maximum of 12mm, and this area may exceed the permitted 2.5mm thickness. A maximum number of five (5) button holes are permitted to be used at any one time, to close the jacket. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 333

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: NOTE: An 80mm overlap requirement is to make the jacket less tight-fitting against the athletes’ body, especially in the chest area. Buttons can be moved towards the edge of the jacket to comply with the 80mm overlap. If, however, there is insufficient material to allow this movement, it is permitted to extend each buttonhole by using strong cord or laces to form a loop into which the button can be fastened.

However, it is permitted to have one (1) zipper or not more than two (2) straps to gather loose material in the area of the shoulder pad (see Shooting Jacket Measurements, 7.5.4.9). No other zipper or other closing or tightening device is permitted other than those specified in these Rules and Diagrams.

The sleeve must not be placed between the hand or glove and the fore-end of the stock when the athlete is in the shooting position. chunks.text: 6.7.4.2 which prohibits the use of special devices, means or clothing, which immobilizes or unduly reduces the movement of the athlete's leg, body or arms. However, it is accepted that athletes’ need some support to reduce the risk of strain to the upper back and shoulders when holding the rifle ‘on-aim’ in the standing position, which is the reason for the greater stiffness allowance in the upper part of the jacket. Most jackets in current use will not necessarily need tailoring alterations but, when new, will require flexing and manipulation to achieve the required degree of flexibility.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5 Shooting Trousers

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.55.1 Thickness - The trousers, including the lining, must not exceed 2.5 mm in single thickness and 5mm in double thickness at any point where flat surface may be measured. The number of layers of material is irrelevant provided that the permitted thickness is not exceeded.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Height - The top of the trousers must not fit or be worn higher on the body than 50 mm above the crest of the hipbone.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Pockets - All pockets are prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Tightening - The trousers must be loose around the legs. All drawstrings, zippers, or fasteners to tighten the trousers around the legs or hips are prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Waist belt - To support the trousers only a normal waist belt not more than 40 mm wide and 3mm thick or braces (suspenders) may be worn. If a belt is worn in the standing position, the buckle or fastening must not be used to support the left arm or elbow. The belt must not be doubled, tripled etc. under the left arm or elbow.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Waist-band - If the trousers have a waist-band it may not be more than 70mm wide. If the thickness of the waistband exceeds 2.5mm, a waist belt is not permitted. If a waist belt is not worn, the absolute maximum thickness of the waistband is 3.5mm.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) Belt loops - There can be a maximum of seven (7) belt loops, not more than 20mm in width, with at least 80mm between belt loops.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) Closure - The trousers may be closed by one (1) hook and up to five (5) eyes, or up to five (5) adjustable snap fasteners, or similar closure or Velcro that must not be multi-layered. Only one (1) type of closure is permitted. A Velcro closure combined with any other closure is prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) Ordinary trousers - If special shooting trousers are not worn, ordinary trousers may be worn providing they do not give artificial support to any part of the body.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.2 Zippers, buttons, Velcro or similar non-adjustable fasteners or closures, may 336 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: be used in the trousers only in the following places:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) One type of fastener or closure in the front to open and close the trouser fly. The fly must not be lower than the level of the crotch;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Any holes that cannot be closed are permitted; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Only one (1) other fastener is permitted in each trouser leg. The opening (fastener) must not start closer than 70 mm from the top edge of the trousers. It may, however, extend to the bottom of the trouser leg (see Shooting Trousers Measurements 7.5.5.5). One (1) fastener is permitted either in the front of the upper leg or the back of the leg, but not in both places in one (1) leg.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.3 Reinforcements - may be added to both knees of the trousers. Knee reinforcements may have a maximum length of 300mm and must not be wider than half the circumference of the trousers leg. The thickness of reinforcement including the trousers material and any linings must not exceed 10mm in single thickness (20mm double thickness).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.4 Shooting Trousers may be worn in the Rifle Prone events, and any stage of Rifle 3 Position events, Men and Women.

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.55.5 Shooting Trousers Measurements Shooting Trousers must comply with the specifications shown in the drawing: height of trousers 70 — | | | El | |e | 40 1 9] hip bone AD \ i 1 maximum height waist of trousers leg belt width band opening stiffer material allowed above level of crotc] | trouser leg opening 300 mm | |

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.6 Shooting Trousers Stiffness — Trousers may consist of more than one layer of material, including a thin inner lining, provided that the maximum combined permitted single thickness of 2.5mm is not exceeded, or 5mm if it is necessary to measure two total thicknesses (for example a sleeve or a leg) The upper part of the trousers above the level of the crotch may be stiffer than the lower part, subject to the following proviso: The trousers above the level of the crotch must pass the stiffness test when measured with the official stiffness-testing device and achieve a deflection of 3mm within a maximum time of thirty, (30), seconds. The material of both legs below the level of the crotch must pass the same test within fifteen (15) seconds. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 337

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: Stiffness measurements apply to a ‘single’ thickness of the trouser panels irrespective of the number of layers of material used in the construction. l.e. unfolded panels with a maximum thickness of 2.5mm, (see 7.5.2.1). The intention is consistent with that outlined for the Jacket, (7.5.4.10); which is to reduce the stiffness of the leg material to comply with Rule 6.7.4.2, but to retain some support for the lower back and lumbar region to reduce the risk of strain or injury when holding the rifle ‘on aim’ in the standing position.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.6 Shooting Gloves

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.6.1 The total thickness must not exceed 16mm when measuring front and back materials together at any point other than on seams and joints. If an athlete is also wearing a lining glove this must be included in the thickness measurement.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.56.2 The glove must not extend more than 50mm beyond the wrist measured from the centre of the wrist knuckle (see drawing). Any strap or other closure device at the wrist is prohibited. However, a portion of the wrist may be elasticated to enable the glove to be put on, but it must leave the glove loose around the wrist. = < — - { wrist knuckle —i fi

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.7 Underclothing 7571 Clothing worn under the shooting jacket must not be thicker than 2.5mm single thickness or 5mm double thickness. The same applies to all clothing worn under the trousers. Jeans or other ordinary trousers cannot be worn under shooting trousers.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.7.2 Only normal personal undergarments and/or training clothing that does not immobilize or unduly reduce the movement of the athlete’s legs, body or arms may be worn under the shooting jacket and/or trousers. Any other undergarments are prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8 Equipment and Accessories

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.1 Spotting Telescopes The use of telescopes not attached to the rifle to locate shots and judge wind is permitted for 50m and 300m events only.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.2 Slings Maximum sling width is 40mm. The sling must be worn only on the upper part of the left arm and from there be connected to the fore-end of the rifle stock. Slings may be attached to the fore-end of the rifle at a single point only. The 338 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: sling must pass along one side of the hand or wrist only. If the sling is worn such that it forms a loop between the arm and the forward attachment, both halves must be fastened together or attached so that the width does not exceed 40mm where it passes around the hand or wrist. No part of the rifle may touch the sling or any of its attachments except at the sling swivel and hand stop.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.58.3 Rifle Rests The use of a rifle rest for resting the rifle between shots is permitted providing that no part of the stand is higher than the athletes highest shoulder when holding the rifle in a standing shooting position. A stand for resting the rifle must not be placed in front of the shooting table or bench when shooting in the standing position. Athletes must take care when resting or loading the rifle using the Rest, that it does not intrude on the athlete on either side by keeping the rifle within the width of their firing points. For safety while the rifle is on the rifle rest, the athlete must retain a hold on it with his hand.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.84 Shooting Box or Bag The shooting box or bag must not be placed forward of the athlete’s forward shoulder on the firing line, except that in the standing position a shooting box or bag, table, or stand may be used as a rifle rest between shots. The shooting box or bag, table or stand must not be of such size or construction as to interfere with athletes on adjacent points or to constitute a wind break.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.585 Kneeling Roll Only one (1) cylindrically shaped roll is allowed for shooting in the kneeling position. The dimensions are a maximum of 25cm long and 18cm in diameter. It must be made of soft and flexible material. Binding or other devices to shape the roll are not permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.6 Bipod Bipods may be used to support the rifle before and after shooting or during position changes, but bipods, whether fixed or folding, must be removed from the rifle during all MATCH firing times.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.7 Kneeling Heel Pad A separate piece of flexible, compressible material with maximum dimensions of 20cm x 20cm may be placed on the heel in the kneeling position. The kneeling heel pad may be no thicker than 20mm when compressed with the measuring device used to measure Rifle clothing thickness.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.5.88 Visor or Cap A cap or visor may be worn. The cap or visor may extend forward of the athlete’s forehead no more than 80mm. The Cap or visor made with a flexible material may touch the rear sight. A cap or visor that is made of non-flexible and stifffhard material is not allowed to touch the rear sight. Any type of Cap or visor may not be worn in a way that makes it a side blinder, the jury must be able to see the side of the athlete's eye when viewed laterally at the same height from the ground. The original prohibition on caps or visors touching the rear sight was to prevent those being used as a point of reference and to steady the rifle to prevent horizontal rotation. The flexible rubber visors do not offer those advantages and are therefore allowed. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 339

chunks.text: 7.6 SHOOTING EVENT PROCEDURES AND COMPETITION RULES

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.6.1 Shooting Positions

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.6.1.1 Kneeling

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete may touch the firing point surface with the toe of the right foot, the right knee and the left foot;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The rifle may be held with both hands and the right shoulder

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The cheek may be placed against the rifle stock;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The left elbow must be supported on the left knee;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The point of the elbow must not be more than 100mm over or 150mm behind the point of the knee;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) The rifle may be supported by the sling but the fore-end behind the left hand must not touch the shooting jacket;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) No part of the rifle may touch the sling or its attachments;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) The rifle must not touch or rest against any other point or object;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) If the kneeling roll is placed under the right foot or ankle, the foot must not be turned at an angle of more than 45 degrees;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: j) If the kneeling roll is not used, the foot may be placed at any angle. This may include placing the side of the foot and the lower leg in contact with the surface of the firing point or shooting mat.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: k) No portion of the upper leg or buttocks may touch the surface of the firing point or shooting mat at any point;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 1) If the athlete uses the shooting mat he may kneel completely or partially on the mat so that there may be up to three points of contact, (toe, knee, foot). Other articles or padding may not be placed under the right knee. A kneeling roll may be used in conjunction with the mat if required.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: m) Only the trousers and underclothing may be worn between the athlete's seat and heel, except that a kneeling heel pad may be used. The jacket or other articles must not be placed between these two (2) points; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: n) The right hand may not touch the left hand, left arm or the left side of the shooting jacket or sling.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.6.1.2 Prone

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete may lie on the bare surface of the firing point or on the shooting mat;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) He may also use the mat by resting his elbows on it.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The body must be extended on the firing point with the head toward the target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The rifle may be supported by both hands and one shoulder only;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The cheek may be placed against the rifle stock.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) The rifle may be supported by a sling attached to the fore-end in front of the hand stop.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) No part of the rifle may touch the sling or its attachments;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) The rifle must not touch, or rest against, any other point or object; 340 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) Both forearms and sleeves of the shooting jacket forward of the elbow must be visibly raised from the surface of the firing point;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: j) The athlete's sling (left) forearm must form an angle not less than 30 degrees from the horizontal, measured from the axis of the forearm;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: k) The right hand and/or arm may not touch the left arm, shooting jacket or sling; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 1) The jacket sleeve on the supporting arm may be allowed to touch the underside of the fore-end provided that it is not between the glove and the rifle nor giving additional support.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.6.1.3 Standing

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must stand free, without any artificial or other support, with both feet on the firing point surface or on the shooting mat;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The rifle may be held with both hands and the shoulder or the upper arm near the shoulder. The rifle is allowed to touch the jacket across the upper part of the chest*.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The cheek may be placed against the rifle stock;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The right hand may not touch the left hand or left arm. The left hand may not touch the left shoulder. Neither hand nor fingers may touch the left side of the jacket. “The left side of the jacket” is the area to the left of an imaginary vertical line down the centre of the chest.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The left upper arm and elbow may be supported on the chest or on the hip. If a belt is worn the buckle or fastening must not be used to support the left arm or elbow;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) The rifle must not touch or rest against any point or object except in the area permitted by 7.6.1.3.b & d). There must be a clearly visible gap between the rifle and the athlete’s face and rear-sight, including a blinder if attached to the rifle. The width of this gap is deliberately not specified to avoid an athlete being disturbed during match firing by an Official or Jury member taking physical measurements, but the gap must be such that there is no doubt that the rifle, including the rear sight or blinder is not touching any point or object when viewed.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) A palm rest may be used but not in 300m Standard Rifle or 10m Air Rifle events;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) A hand stop/sling swivel is not allowed in this position for 300m Standard Rifle and 10m Air Rifle events;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) In this position, the use of the sling is prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 7.7 RIFLE EVENTS See ISSF RECOGNIZED SHOOTING EVENTS Rule 3.3 and Rule 7.7.4, RIFLE EVENT TABLE.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: 8.4.4.1 See ANNEX B Procedures for conducting Rapid Fire Pistol Ammunition Velocity Tests Manual.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.4.4.2 The ammunition of at least one (1) athlete from each relay must be tested. The Equipment Control Jury will supervise the selection of the athletes to be tested and collect the ammunition to be tested before each 30-shot Qualification stage. Athletes should have at least 50 rounds with them for each stage of competition. A Jury Member must take ten (10) cartridges from the ammunition that the athlete is using, place them in a labelled envelope, seal the envelope and hand it to the testing officer. After the stage is completed, the athlete selected must go to the testing station. The testing officer will load a magazine with three (3) cartridges and fire them in that athlete's pistol and record the muzzle velocity of each cartridge. If the average velocity is under 250.0m/sec, the test must be repeated. If the average velocity of the six (6) shots is less than 250.0m/sec, the athlete must be disqualified.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.4.4.3 Not more than twenty (20) minutes after the end of the qualification stage of the Rapid Fire Pistol event the eight (8) athletes who have qualified for the Final, according to the published results, must report to the velocity testing station with all the ammunition that they will use in finals. If athlete did not present himself for velocity test before the final, he will not be allowed to start and will be ranked 8th and marked DNS in finals results. Samples from ammunition will be taken and a velocity test will be performed. Ammunition will be sealed in the presence of the athlete and will be taken to finals reporting area by the Equipment Control Officer.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: 8.5.1 Only low-sided shoes that do not cover the ankle bone (below the medial and lateral malleolus) are permitted. The sole must be flexible in the entire forward part of the foot;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.5.2 Athletes may use removeable inner soles or inserts in their shoes, but any inserts must also be flexible in the forward part of the foot;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.5.3 An ISSF approved testing device will be used to check sole flexibility;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.5.4 To demonstrate that shoe soles are flexible, athletes must walk normally (heel toe) at all times while on the field of play. A warning will be given for the first offence, a two-point penalty or disqualification will be given for subsequent violations;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: 8.5.5 Shoe Sole Flexibility Measurement Device. The device used to measure shoe sole flexibility must be capable of accurately measuring how many degrees the shoe sole bends while bent with a precise amount of upward pressure; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: 8.5.6 Shoe Sole Flexibility Standard. The soles of athletes’ shoes must bend at least 22.5 degrees when a force of 15 Newton-Meters is applied to the heel area while the shoe is clamped in the testing device. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 359

chunks.text: 8.6.1 Spotting Telescopes The use of telescopes not attached to the pistol to locate shots or judge the wind is permitted in 25m and 50m events only.

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.6.2 Pistol Transport Boxes Athletes may use pistol transport boxes to take pistols and equipment to the shooting ranges. During Finals, pistol transport boxes or equipment bags must not remain on the FOP.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: 8.6.3 Pistol Support Stands Athletes may place pistol support stands or boxes on the bench or table to rest their pistols between shots. The total height of the bench or table with a support stand or box on it may not exceed 1.00m (see Rule 6.4.11.10.c, maximum bench height is 1.00m). During Elimination or Qualification competitions, a pistol transport box (Rule 8.6.2) may be used as a pistol support stand, provided the total height of the bench or table plus the box does not exceed 1.00m. During Finals, a pistol transport box may not be used as a pistol support stand.

chunks.text: 8.7.1 Firing Position The athlete must stand free, without any artificial or other support, with both feet and/or shoes completely within the firing point. The pistol must be held and fired with one (1) hand only. The wrist must be visibly free of support.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.7.2 Ready Position In the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol event, 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol Rapid-fire Stages and 25m Standard Pistol 20sec. and 10sec. series, shooting must start from the READY position (see drawing). In the READY position, the athlete’s arm must point downward at an angle of not greater than 45 degrees from the vertical. The arm with the pistol must not be pointed at the ground within the forward edge of the firing point. After the series begins, the pistol may not rest on the bench or shooting table. The arm must remain in this position while waiting either for the appearance of the target or, when EST are used, for the green light(s) to come on. 360 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.text: 8.7.3 Ready Position Violations A READY position violation occurs when an athlete in the 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol event or in the Rapid-Fire Stage of the 25m Pistol or 25m Centre Fire Pistol event, or in the 20 second or 10 second stages of the 25m Standard Pistol event:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: c) Raises his arm above 45 degrees before the light changes or the targets start to turn.

chunks.text: 8.7.4 Procedures for Ready Position Violations WHEN A READY POSITION VIOLATION OCCURS;

chunks.text: a) The athlete must be warned by a Jury Member and the series must be recorded and repeated;

chunks.text: b) When the series is repeated in the 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol event, the athlete must be credited with the lowest value hit on each target. In all other 25m events, the athlete must be credited with the five (5) lowest value hits in the two (2) series (or three (3) series should a malfunction be involved);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If the fault is repeated in the same stage of 30 shots in the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol event, or in the Rapid-fire Stage of the 25m Pistol or 25m Centre Fire Pistol event, or in the combined 20 second and 10 second stages of the 25m Standard Pistol event, the same procedure must be applied and the athlete must be penalized by a deduction of two (2) points from his score; and d) If a third violation of this Rule occurs, the athlete must be disqualified. chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) In all 25m events, timing must start at the moment the green lights come on (or the targets begin to face) and stop when the red lights come on (or the targets begin to turn away); when EST are used, the green lights are on for the required time +0.1 sec.;

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The turning of the targets or the switching of lights may be controlled by a Target Operator who is located behind the firing line. His position must not disturb the athlete, but it must be within the sight and hearing of the Range Officer. chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If an athlete in Qualification loads his pistol with more cartridges than he is allowed to load (full series or series completion) or he loads more than one (1) magazine on any command “LOAD” he must be penalized by the deduction of two (2) points from his score in that same series. chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: f) “UNLOAD.” In all events, after the series or stage has been completed, the command “UNLOAD” must be giv- en. In any case, immediately upon completing a series (unless there is a pistol malfunction), or when ordered, the athlete must unload the pistol and insert safety flag.

chunks.text: 8.7.6.3 Specific Rules for the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol Qualification Event

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The event is 60 competition shots divided into two (2) stages of 30 shots each. Each stage includes six (6) series of five (5) shots each, two (2) series in eight (8) seconds, two (2) series in six (6) seconds and two (2) series in four (4) seconds. In each series, one (1) shot is fired at each of the five (5) targets within the specified time limit for the series;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Before the beginning of each stage, the athlete may fire one (1) Sighting series of five (5) shots in eight (8) seconds;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) All shooting (Sighting and MATCH firing series) is by command. Both athletes in the same Range Section must fire at the same time, but organizers may have more than one (1) Range Section to fire simultaneously under centralized commands;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If a pistol of any of the athletes firing together has a malfunction, the malfunction series must be re-fired by those concerned in the same time stage with the following regular series. The final series of this stage will be fired immediately after all other athletes firing together have completed this time stage. Each Range Section may operate independently;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Before the Range Officer gives the command “LOAD,” he must call out the series time (i.e. “eight second series,” “six second series,” etc.), or the series time must be indicated in some manner such as using a numbered sign of sufficient size to be visible to the athlete. When the Range Officer gives the command “LOAD,” athletes must prepare themselves for their series within one (1) minute;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) When one (1) minute has expired, the Range Officer will give the command: “ATTENTION” The red lights must be switched on (if paper targets are used, they must be turned to the edge-on position) and the athletes must bring their pistols to the READY position. When EST are used, the red lights will be switched on. After a delay of 7 sec. +/-

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 0.1sec. the green lights will come on for the required time +0.1sec. When paper targets are used, the targets will be turned to the edge-on position. After a delay of 7sec. (+/- 0.1sec.), the targets will be turned to face the athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) Before each series, the athlete must lower his arm and adopt the READY position;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) The green lights come on (if paper targets are used, the targets turn to face the athletes) seven (7) seconds+/- 0.1sec. after the command “ATTENTION;” EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 363

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) Pistols may be raised the moment the green lights come on (or the targets begin to face);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: j) The athlete should fire five (5) shots during each series;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: k) A series is considered as having started after the command “ATTENTION”; every shot fired after that must be counted as a MATCH shot;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 1) After the firing of each series, there should be a pause of at least one (1) minute before the next command “LOAD;” and

chunks.text: 8.8 INTERRUPTIONS AND IRREGULARITIES

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.1 Interruptions in 25m Events and Stages If shooting is interrupted for safety or technical reasons (without being the fault of the athlete):

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If the elapsed interruption time is more than 15min., the Jury must allow one (1) extra sighting series of five (5) shots;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) In the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol and in the 25m Standard Pistol event, if the series is interrupted it must be annulled and repeated. The repeated series must be recorded and credited to the athlete;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) In the 25m Pistol and the 25m Centre Fire Pistol events, the interrupted series must be completed. The completed series must be recorded and credited to the athlete; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) In the Precision Stage the time limit is forty-eight (48) seconds for every shot to be fired to complete the series.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2 Irregular Shots in 25m Events and Stages

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2.1 Too Many Competition Shots Fired (25m) If an athlete fires more MATCH shots on a target than the Pistol Events Qualification Table (Rule 8.11) specifies, or more than one (1) shot at one (1) appearance of the target in a Rapid-Fire Pistol Series, the highest value hit(s) must be disregarded from the score of that target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Two (2) points must also be deducted from the score of that series for each extra shot fired in the series;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) This penalty is in addition to the penalty of two (2) points that may be imposed when an athlete loads more than the authorized number of cartridges; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Two (2) points must be deducted on every occasion if two (2) shots are fired during a single exposure of the target in the Rapid-Fire stages of the 25m Pistol and the 25m Centre Fire Pistol events.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2.2 Too Many Sighting Shots Fired (25m) If an athlete fires more Sighting shots than are provided for in the Pistol Events Qualification Table (Rule 8.11), or are approved by the Range Officer or Jury, he must be penalized by the deduction of two (2) points from the first series of his MATCH score for each excessive sighting shot fired. This penalty is in addition to the penalty of two (2) points that may be imposed when an athlete loads more than the authorized number of cartridges.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2.3 Early Or Late Shots (25m)

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Any shot(s) fired accidentally after the command “LOAD,” but before the start of a MATCH series, must not be counted in the competition and two (2) points must be deducted from the following series. This penalty must not apply in the Sighting series. The athlete who fired accidentally must not continue, but must wait until the other athletes finish that series and then report this to the EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 367

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: Range Officer as if he had a malfunction. The Range Officer will then permit him to continue and repeat the series in the same time stage with the following regular series. The final series of the stage will be fired immediately after all athletes have completed that time stage. If this procedure is not followed and the athlete continues the original series, the accidentally fired shot will be scored as a miss (zero); and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) In a Precision Stage, if a shot(s) is fired after the command or signal “STOP,” that shot must be counted as a miss. If the shot(s) cannot be identified the highest value hit(s) must be deducted from the score of that target and scored as miss(es).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2.4 Crossfires on Sighting Targets (25m) If an athlete fires a Sighting shot on the sighting target of another athlete, he must not be allowed to repeat the shot, but will not be penalized. If it cannot be established clearly and quickly which hit(s) belong to whom, the athlete who is not at fault has the right to repeat the sighting shot(s).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.3 Incorrect Range Commands (25m)

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If, because of an incorrect command and/or action by a Range Officer, the athlete is not ready to fire when the signal to fire is given, he must hold his pistol pointing down range and raise his free hand, and immediately after the series report this to a Range Officer or Jury Member; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If the claim is considered justified, the athlete must be allowed to fire the series; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If the claim is considered not justified, the athlete may fire the series, but must be penalized by the deduction of two (2) points from the score of that series; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If the athlete has fired a shot after the incorrect command and/or action, the protest must not be accepted.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.4 Disturbances Should an athlete consider that he was disturbed while firing a shot, he must hold his pistol pointing down range and immediately inform the Range Officer or Jury Member by raising his free hand. He must not disturb other athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.4.1 IF THE CLAIM IS CONSIDERED JUSTIFIED:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The series (25m Rapid-fire Pistol, 25m Standard Pistol), must be annulled and the athlete may repeat the series; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The shot (25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol) must be annulled and the athlete may repeat the shot and complete the series.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.4.2 IF THE CLAIM IS CONSIDERED UNJUSTIFIED:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If the athlete has finished his series, the shot or series must be credited to the athlete;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If the athlete has not finished his series due to the claimed disturbance, the athlete may repeat or complete the series. Scoring and penalties are as follows;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) In the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol Event the series may be repeated and the score must be recorded as the total of the lowest value hit on each target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) In the 25m Standard Pistol Event the series may be repeated and the 368 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: score must be recorded as the total of the five (5) lowest value hits on the target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) In the 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol Events the series may be completed and the score must be recorded;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) Two (2) points must also be deducted from the score of the repeated or completed series; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) In any repeated series, all five (5) shots must be fired at the target. Any shot(s) not fired or not hitting the target must be scored as a miss(es).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.5 Timing Irregularity Claims

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.5.1 If an athlete considers that the time elapsed between the command specified in the Rules and the green light coming on or the facing of the targets was too fast or too slow, and therefore not according to the time specified in the Rules, he must hold his pistol pointing down range and immediately inform a Range Officer or Jury Member by raising his free hand. He must not disturb other athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If it is found that his claim is justified, he may begin the series again; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If his claim is found not justified, he may fire the series, but a two (2) point penalty must be deducted from the score of that series; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Once the athlete has fired the first shot in the series, such a claim must not be accepted.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.8.5.2 If an athlete considers that the time of the series was too short, he may inform a Range Officer immediately after finishing the series.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The Range Officer and/or Jury must verify the timing of the mechanism; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If itis confirmed that there has been an error, the protesting athlete's series must be annulled and repeated; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If the claim is considered not justified, the result of the series must be credited to the athlete and recorded.

chunks.text: 8.9 MALFUNCTIONS IN 25M EVENTS

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.1 Malfunctions during a sighting series may not be claimed, however, an athlete may clear the malfunction and continue to shoot the unfired shots within the specified time for the sighting series for that event. Only one (1) malfunction (either ALLOWABLE or NON-ALLOWABLE) may be claimed during each MATCH stage(s) of a 25m Pistol event as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Once in each 30 shot stage of the 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol, 256m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol events;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Twice in the 60-shot Standard Pistol match. NOTE: In exceptional cases, where the match is shot in two stages (see Rule 8.7.6.5.h), then only once in each 30 shot stage of the Standard Pistol match.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The appropriate Malfunction Form (RFPM or STDP) must be used to score repeated malfunction series. Malfunction Forms are found in the General Technical Rules, Rule 6.19.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Malfunctions (ALLOWABLE or NON-ALLOWABLE) in 25m Finals will be decided according to 6.17.4.0) or 6.17.5 k). EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 369

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.2 Repairing or Replacing a Broken Gun Should a pistol break or cease to function, the athlete is allowed to repair or replace the pistol. In all cases, the Chief Range Officer must confirm that the pistol cannot function safely and the Jury must be informed.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) An athlete is allowed a maximum of 15min. to repair or replace a pistol in order to resume the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If the repair is likely to take more than 15min., the athlete, at his request, may be granted more time by the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If extra repair time is granted, he will complete the competition at a time and place determined by the Jury or he may continue to fire with another pistol of the same type of mechanism (semi-automatic or revolver) and of the same calibre; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) In the 25m events the Jury must allow one (1) extra sighting series of five (5) shots.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.3 Malfunctions in 25m Pistol Events

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If a shot has not been fired due to a malfunction, and if the athlete wishes to claim a malfunction, he must hold his pistol pointing down range and must retain his grip. Only the tip of the barrel may rest on the bench, if the magazine is not of the type that is loaded from the barrel end, but the magazine must be clearly not touching the bench or hand and immediately inform a Range Officer by raising his free hand. He must not disturb other athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) An athlete may try to correct a malfunction and continue the series, but after attempting any correction, he may not claim an Allowable Malfunction unless the firing pin has broken, or any other part of the pistol is damaged sufficiently to prevent the pistol from functioning.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4 Types of Malfunctions

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.1 ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTIONS (AM) are:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Abullet is lodged in the barrel;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The trigger mechanism has failed to operate;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) There is an undischarged cartridge in the chamber and the trigger mechanism has been released and operated;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The cartridge case has not been extracted or ejected; this applies even if a case catcher is used;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The cartridge, magazine, cylinder, or other part of the pistol has jammed;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) The firing pin has broken, or any other part of the pistol is damaged sufficiently to prevent the pistol from functioning;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) The pistol fires automatically without the trigger being released. The athlete must stop firing immediately and must not continue to use such a pistol without the permission of a Range Officer or a Jury Member. When using electronic scoring targets, the first shot will be scored by the system and this will be credited to the athlete. When using paper targets, should the automatically fired shot(s) hit the target, the hit(s) found highest up on the target must be disregarded before the repeat series. After any repeat series, all the shot(s), except those that were disregarded on the one (1) target concerned, must be included to establish the score; or 370 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) The slide jams or the empty case is not ejected, this applies even if a case catcher is used.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.42 NON-ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTIONS (NAM) are:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete has touched the breech, mechanism or safety catch or the pistol has been touched by another person before being inspected by the Range Officer;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The safety catch has not been released;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The athlete did not load his pistol;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The athlete loaded fewer cartridges than prescribed;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The athlete did not allow the trigger to return far enough after the previous shot;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) The pistol was loaded with the wrong ammunition;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) The magazine was not inserted correctly, or had fallen out during shooting unless this is due to damage to the mechanism; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) The malfunction is due to any cause that could reasonably have been corrected by the athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.3 Determining the Cause of a Malfunction If the external appearance of the pistol does not show an obvious reason for the malfunction and there is no indication, and the athlete does not claim that there may be a bullet stuck in the barrel, the Range Officer must take the pistol without interfering with or touching the mechanism, point the pistol in a safe direction and pull the trigger one time only to determine whether the trigger mechanism had been released.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If the pistol is a revolver, the Range Officer must not pull the trigger unless the hammer is in the cocked position;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If the pistol does not discharge, the Range Officer must complete the examination of the pistol to determine the cause of the malfunction and to decide whether or not the malfunction is allowable; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The Range Officer decides, after inspection of the pistol, that there is an ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION or a NON-ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.4 In the case of a NON-ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION, every shot that is not fired will be scored as a miss (zero). No re-fire or completion is permitted. Only the values of shots fired will be credited to the athlete. The athlete may continue to shoot the remainder of the event.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.5 ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION PROCEDURES - 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol and 25m Standard Pistol

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If an ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION occurs during a 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol Men or 25m Standard Pistol Men series, record the scores of the shots that were fired on first line of the Malfunction Form (Form RFPM or Form STDP); and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete must fire all five (5) shots at the target(s) in any repeat series. After the repeat series, record the scores of all shots fired on the second line of the Malfunction Form; any shots not hitting the target or late shots, fired or unfired, must be scored as zero(s); or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If a second malfunction occurs in the repeat series, record the scores of EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 371

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: the fired shots in the repeat series on the second line of the Malfunction Form. Then add zeros to the line (first series or repeat series) that has scores for the most fired shots to ensure that one line has five scores. These added zeros must be counted in determining the score for that series; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Determine the scores of the five shots to be counted for the series and record them on the third line of the Malfunction Form (“Final Score”): + RFPM: enter the lowest value scores on each of the five targets and total scores. + STDP: enter the five lowest value scores from all recorded shots, including any zeros that were added to one of the two lines, and total those scores.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.6 ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION PROCEDURES - 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol Precision and Rapid-Fire Stages:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The number of shots is recorded and the series may be completed;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Shot(s) to complete the series (series completion) must be fired in the next competition series; in the Precision Stage a time of forty-eight (48) seconds will be allowed for each shot to be fired; in the Rapid-Fire Stage, the series completion must start on the first exposure;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Any shot(s) not fired or not hitting the target must be scored as miss(es) (zero(s);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The five-shot series must be scored in the normal manner; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Use Form IR to report series completion.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.10 FAILURE OF EST OR PAPER TARGET SYSTEMS

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.10.1 Failure of ALL targets on a Range or Range Section

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The expired shooting time must be recorded by the Chief Range Officer and the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) All completed MATCH shots of each athlete must be counted and recorded. In the event of a range power supply failure, this may involve waiting until power is restored to enable the number of shots registered by the target, not necessarily on the firing point monitor, to be established;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) After the targets are repaired and the full range, or Range Section, is in operation, an additional Sighting series and a one (1) minute pause will be given before starting the completion of the series in accordance with the following rules;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol Events. The athletes will COMPLETE the series of five shots in the same way as for an ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION. The athlete should fire the number of shots that had not been recorded by the target when the failure occurred.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) 25m Standard Pistol and 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol Events. If the series was not completed and recorded, it will be annulled and repeated. If the five (5) shots were recorded for any athlete, the series score will be recorded and no repetition will be permitted by that athlete. 372 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.10.2 Failure of a Single Target or Target Group If there is a failure of a single target or group of five targets (25m Rapid-Fire Pistol event) that cannot be repaired immediately, the athlete will be moved to another firing position in the same, or a following relay. After the problem is resolved, a separate sighting series and a one (1) minute pause will be given before the firing of the next series in accordance with the rule above (8.10.1.c).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.10.3 Failure to Register or Display a Shot If there is a complaint concerning failure to register or display a shot on the monitor(s) of 25m Electronic Scoring Target systems, or the monitor shows a zero (0) that was not expected:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) In the Precision Stages of 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol events and in the 150sec. series of the 25m Standard Pistol event, the athlete must immediately (before the next shot) inform the nearest range official of the failure;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete will then be directed to complete the series (remaining unfired shots only) at a time decided by the Jury; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) In the Rapid-Fire Stages of the 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol events, and in the 25m Standard Pistol and 25m RFP men events, the athlete must continue the five (5) shot series and must inform the nearest range official of the failure immediately after the end of the series;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) There will be no repeat series. The score will be determined by the RTS Jury. After the series has been completed, the Procedure for Examination of Electronic Scoring Targets (6.10.8) will be applied. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 ©ISSF 373
