chunks.text: 9.7 TARGETS —- REGULAR, IRREGULAR, BROKEN, HIT, LOST AND NO TARGETS

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.71 Regular Target

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Aregular target is one (1) whole target called by the athlete and released according to the Rules; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Aregular Double is two (2) whole targets called by the athlete and released simultaneously according to the Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.7.2 Irregular Target An irregular target is a target that is not thrown according to the Rules and flies along a path other than that specified in the Rules in angle, elevation or distance. An irregular Double occurs when;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) One (1) or both of the targets are irregular;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The targets are not thrown simultaneously;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Only one (1) target emerges; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Either target emerges “broken.”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 8.7.3 Broken Target

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) A broken target is any target that is not whole in accordance with the General Specifications for Clay Targets (G.T.R. 6.3.6.1); and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Abroken target is a “NO TARGET” target and must always be repeated.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.7.4 “HIT” Target

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Atarget is declared as “HIT” when a regular target is thrown and hit according to the event Rules and at least one (1) visible piece is broken from it;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Atarget that is only “dusted,” but from which no visible piece is seen, is not a “HIT”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Where flash (powder filled) targets are used, a target must also be declared as “HIT” when there is visible emergence of coloured powder after a shot is fired; and 398 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) All decisions regarding “HIT,” “LOST,” “IRREGULAR” or “NO TARGET” targets rest finally with the Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Itis prohibited to pick up a clay target from the range to determine whether or not it was a “HIT.”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.7.5 “LOST” Target Atarget, must be declared “LOST” when:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) It is not hit during its flight within the shooting boundaries;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Itis only dusted and no visible piece is broken from it;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The athlete does not fire at a regular target for which he has called and there is no mechanical or other external reason that has prevented the athlete from firing;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The athlete is not able to fire his shotgun for any reason attributable to the fault of the athlete;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The athlete is not able to fire because he has not released the “safety,” or the “safety” has slipped to “safe”;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) The athlete has forgotten to load;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) If after a malfunction the athlete has opened the shotgun or has touched the safety before the Referee has examined the shotgun; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) It is the third or subsequent malfunction in the same round. 976 “NO TARGET”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) A“NO TARGET” is irrelevant to the competition and must always be repeated;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The Referee must, if possible, call “NO TARGET” before the athlete fires, but if he calls “NO TARGET” after the athlete fires, a “NO TARGET” must be declared regardless of whether the target/s was/were hit or not; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) After a “NO TARGET” is declared the athlete may open the shotgun and reposition him/her self.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8 COMPETITION RULES FOR TRAP

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.1 Conduct of a Round of Trap Each squad member, with sufficient ammunition and all equipment necessary to complete the round, must occupy a shooting station in the order shown on the scorecard. The sixth athlete must stand in the marked area (Station

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 6) behind Station 1 ready to move to Station 1 as soon as the first athlete has shot at a regular target and the result is known. The Referee must take charge and when all preliminary procedures are completed (names, numbers, Assistants Referees, test firing and then viewing of targets etc.) give the command “START.”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.1.1 Method

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) When the first athlete is ready to fire, he must raise the shotgun to the shoulder and call loudly and crisply for the target, after which the target must be thrown at once;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) When the result of the shot(s) is known the second athlete must do likewise, EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 399

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: followed by the third athlete and so on;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) When the athlete has called for the target, it must be released immediately, allowing only for human reaction time to press a button if the release is manual;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Two (2) shots may be fired at each target except that in Finals and any shoot- offs during Finals only one (1) shot may be fired. If an athlete fires two (2) shots, the target will be declared “LOST” whether it was hit or not by either of the shots;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) After athlete No.1 has fired at a regular target, he must prepare to move to Station 2 as soon as the athlete on Station 2 has fired at a regular target; the other athletes in the squad must, on their stations, do likewise in rotation from left to right;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) This whole sequence must continue until all athletes have each shot at 25 targets (2 left, 2 right and 1 centre from each of the five stations); each athlete having a varying random equal distribution of targets.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) Once the round has started an athlete may close the shotgun only after the previous athlete has completed his turn;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) An athlete having shot must not leave the station before the athlete on the right has fired at a regular target and the result is registered, except when the athlete has completed shooting on Station 5; in this case he must turn clockwise and proceed immediately to Station 6, with unloaded shotgun being careful not to disturb the athletes who are on the line as he passes by;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) All shotguns must be carried OPEN and UNLOADED when moving between any stations.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: j) Any athlete who loads his/her shotgun on a fired station before leaving it, or carries his/her shotgun loaded between any stations must be given an initial Warning (Yellow Card); any further occurrences until the end of the Qualification process or the PET may result in Disqualification (Red Card); and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: k) No athlete having shot on one (1) station may proceed towards the next station in such a way as to interfere with another athlete or match officials.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.1.2 Preparation Time Limit

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) An athlete must take his/her position, close the shotgun and call for the target within twelve (12) seconds after the previous athlete has fired at a regular target and has opened the shotgun and the result is registered, or after the Referee has given the command “START;” or “READY”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) In case of non-compliance with this time limit, the penalties provided in the rules will be applied;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Where squads consist of five (5) or less athletes, preparation time must be extended to give the athlete leaving Station 5 sufficient additional time to arrive at Station 1; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) During Qualification Rounds, preparation time limits must be controlled by the Referee. During shoot-offs during Finals, preparation time limits must be monitored by an electronic timing device which must be managed by a Referee selected from among the appointed Competition Referees.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The timekeeper must have sufficient experience on how to use the timing device. 400 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.1.3 Interruptions

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If a round of shooting is interrupted for more than five (5) minutes because of a technical malfunction that is not the fault of an athlete, the squad must be allowed to view one (1) regular target from each machine in the group on which the interruption occurred before the competition resumes.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If a technical malfunction or any other unforeseen situation (example: the control unit is accidentally set at the start of a round to the wrong number of participating athletes) requires a restart of the control unit, scoring must continue from the point where the malfunction or restart commences and no protest regarding the uneven distribution of targets will be considered.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.2 Target Distances, Angles and Elevations

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.2.1 Trap Setting Table Each trap machine must be set before the start of the PET and the competition to one (1) of the Trap Setting Tables 1 - 10 of Rule 9.8.2.3 / 9.20.2 drawn by lot, under the supervision of the Jury Chairperson.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.22 Trap Competition arrangements and settings In a competition, depending upon the number of ranges in use, the squads must be scheduled before the start of the competition under the supervision of the Jury Chairperson and the approval of the Technical Delegate, in such a way that, whenever possible, each squad should shoot:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The same number of times on each range in use;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The same number of times on a particular setting;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Whenever possible the settings used in Unofficial, or Pre-Event Training should be different from those used during the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If the Organizing Committee together with the TD and the Chairperson of the Jury decide that the Trap competition for any group of athletes (e.g.: men, women or juniors) is to be conducted on only one (1) separate range, the settings must be changed after all athletes in this group have completed fifty (50) targets (except in special ISSF competitions, with very small number of participating athletes);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.2.3 Target Limits Targets must be set according to the selected schemes in Tables 1 - 10 (Rule

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.20.2) and within the following limits:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Height at 10m -- 1.5m to 3.0m, as per Trap setting tables, 1-10 with a tolerance of +/- 0.15m;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Angle -- as per Trap setting tables 1-10, with a tolerance of 5°; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Distance -- 76.0m +/- 1.0m (as measured from the front edge of the pit roof).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.24 Trap Setting Procedure Each machine must be set to throw the target as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Adjust angle to the zero (0) degrees, straight forward position;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Adjust spring tension and height at 10m forward of the front edge of the trap pit to obtain the required elevation and distance; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Adjust to required angle as measured from a position immediately above the centre of each machine, on the top of the trap pit roof with the use of a EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 401

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: protractor. c) An ISSF approved Radar Speed Gun System can be used. The System must have data collected for each of the Ranges being used. The Data must include the Type of Machine, the Targets being used in the competition and the Flash Targets being used in the Finals

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.3 Jury Checks

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.3.1 Trial Targets

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Each range must be set before the start of the PET and the competition and the settings must be examined, approved and sealed by the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Each day, after the traps have been adjusted and approved by the Jury, one (1) trial target must be thrown from each machine, in sequence, from each range in use, before the start of the competition (before the start of the first rounds of the day);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) One (1) trial target must also be thrown from each machine, in sequence, from each range in use, in cases where there is a time break between rounds in the competition programme and the athletes cannot observe the targets of the range on which they will shoot their next round.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Trial targets may be observed by the athletes; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) All athletes, Coaches and Team Officials are prohibited from entering the trap pits after the Jury has examined and approved the trap settings (see Rule

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) All athletes, coaches and team officials are prohibited from entering the field of play while juries are examining the schemes and the target settings prior to the start of the PET or the competition, unless permitted by the jury.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) After two consecutive times of a No Target being called by the Referee, the Athlete may ask for a Trial Target to be thrown, provided that the No Target was not fired upon.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) After the Jury have approved the target settings, the CRO is responsible for the security of the Trap Pits.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.4 Trap General Rules

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.8.4.1 Irregular Trajectory Any target flying along a path other than that specified in angle, elevation or distance must be considered irregular.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.84.2 Refused Target An athlete may refuse a target if:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Atarget is not released immediately after the athlete's call;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The Referee agrees that the athlete, after calling for the target, was visibly disturbed by some external cause; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The Referee agrees that the target was irregular. Procedure by Athlete — The athlete refusing a target must indicate this by opening the shotgun and raising an arm. The Referee must then give his decision.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.84.3 A“NO TARGET” target is one that is not thrown according to these Rules: 402 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) A“NO TARGET” decision is always the Referee’s responsibility;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) A target declared a “NO TARGET” by the Referee must always be re peated from the same trap (whether hit or not). However, the athlete may not refuse it even if he considers that it was thrown from another machine in the same group; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) A Referee should attempt to call “NO TARGET” before the athlete fires. However, if the Referee calls “NO TARGET” as, or immediately after the athlete has fired, the Referee’s decision must stand and the target must be repeated regardless of whether the target was “HIT” or not.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.844 A “NO TARGET” target must be declared even if the athlete has fired when:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Abroken or irregular target emerges;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) A target of a distinctly different colour from that of the others being used in the Competition is thrown;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Two (2) targets are thrown;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The target is thrown from a machine in another group;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) An athlete shoots out of turn;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) Another athlete fires at the same target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) The Referee is satisfied that the athlete, after calling for the target, was visibly disturbed by some external cause;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) The Referee detects an initial violation of the athlete’s foot position in a competition; (warning with yellow card).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) The Referee detects an initial violation of the time limit; (warning with yellow card).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: j) The Referee, for any reason, cannot decide whether the target was “HIT” or not, (in such cases the Referee must always consult the Assistant Referees before announcing the decision);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: k) The shot is discharged involuntarily before the athlete has called for the target. However, if the athlete then fires at the target with the second shot, the result must be scored. Also, the athlete must be warned and if the same situation occurs a second or subsequent time in a round, the target(s) shall be declared “LOST”; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 1) The first shot is a miss and the athlete’s second shot misfires due to an allowable malfunction of either the shotgun or the cartridge. In this case the target must be repeated and must be missed with the first shot and hit only with the second shot. If the target is hit with the first shot, it must be declared “LOST.”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.84.5 A“NO TARGET” target must be declared provided that the Athlete has NOT fired when:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Atarget is thrown before the athlete's call;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) A target is not released immediately after the athlete’s call (see Note);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Atarget’s trajectory is irregular (see Note);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d)_There is an allowable malfunction of shotgun or cartridge; or EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 403

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The athlete's first shot misfires due to an allowable malfunction of either shotgun or cartridge and he does not fire the second shot; If the second shot was fired, the result of that shot must be scored. Note: Unless the Referee calls “NO TARGET” before or immediately after the athlete fires, no claim for an irregular target must be permitted if the target was fired upon, when the irregularity claim is based solely upon an alleged “Quick Pull” or an alleged “Slow Pull” or a deviation from the prescribed lines of flight. Otherwise, if the athlete fires the result must be recorded.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.84.6 Atarget must be declared “LOST” when:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Itis not hit during its flight;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) It is only dusted and no visible piece is broken from it;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) An athlete, for no permitted reason, does not shoot at a regular target for which he has called;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) After a malfunction of shotgun or cartridge, an athlete opens the shotgun or moves the safety catch before the Referee has inspected the shotgun;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) An athlete suffers a third or subsequent malfunction of shotgun or cartridge in the same round;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) The first shot is a miss and the athlete fails to fire his second shot because he forgot to place a second cartridge in the shotgun, or because the safety has slipped to the “safe” position by recoil of the first shot;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) The athlete is not able to fire his shotgun because he has not released the safety or has forgotten to load;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) The time limit is violated and the athlete has been warned once already (Yellow Card) in any previous round (Rule 9.15.3.g); or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) The athlete’s foot position is violated and the athlete has been warned once already (Yellow Card) in the any previous round (Rule 9.15.3.9).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9 COMPETITION RULES FOR SKEET

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.1 Conduct of a Round of Skeet The squad must assemble on the range in an area next to Station 1, with sufficient ammunition and all equipment necessary to complete the round. The Referee must take charge and when all preliminary procedures are completed (names, numbers, Assistant Referees, test firing, then show targets, etc.) give the command “START.”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.1.1 Method After the command “START” is given:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The first athlete must move on to Station 1, load the shotgun with one (1) cartridge only, adopt the READY position and call for the target, after which a regular target from the high house must be thrown within an indefinite period varying randomly from zero (0) to a maximum of three (3) seconds; Note: If an electronic-microphone system is used, it must be constructed so as to randomly insert a delay varying from 0.2 to 3.0 seconds. 404 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) When the result of the shot is known, the first athlete shall remain on the station, load with two (2) cartridges, adopt the READY position, and call and fire at a regular double;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) When the results of both shots are known the first athlete must leave the station;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The second athlete must then do likewise, followed by the third athlete and so on until all the members of the squad have each shot the required sequence on Station 1;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The first athlete must then move on to Station 2 and shoot the required number of targets in the required sequence and time, followed in turn by each member of the squad;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) This rotation will continue until all the required stations have been shot by all members of the squad;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) No athlete in the squad may advance to the station before his shooting turn, before the Referee’s order to shoot or before the previous athlete has completed his shooting and has left the station; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) No athlete having shot on one (1) station may proceed towards the next station until all the members of the squad have completed their shooting on the station or in such a way as to interfere with another athlete or impede the duties of the match officials.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.2 Competition Procedures

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.21 Preparation Time Limits. Athletes must call for their targets according to the following time limits:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) After the Referee has given the signal to “START” or after the previous athlete has left the station, the next athlete must occupy the station within maximum ten (10) seconds;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete must stand with both feet entirely within the station boundaries, take his position, load the shotgun, adopt the READY position and call for the target(s) in the required sequence for the station;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The athlete must then call for the next single or double to be fired at from that station within the shortest time possible;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The maximum total time allowed to call for the required sequence for that station is thirty (30) seconds in both Qualification Rounds and Finals after the athlete has occupied the station; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) In case the athlete is shooting two doubles, or one single and one double and he shot the first double or single normally and then something unusual occurs when he calls the second double (visible disturbance, malfunction, no target, etc) the athlete will be allowed 15 seconds to call for the second double.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) During Qualification Rounds, preparation time limits must be controlled by the Referee. During shoot-offs before Finals and during Finals, preparation time limits must be controlled with an electronic timing device managed by the appointed Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) The timekeeper must have sufficient experience with using the timing device. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 405

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.22 Target Shooting Sequence for Qualification Rounds Only one (1) shot may be fired at each target EE —— er— 2 I =rra— ; a — er HE — ; I — re —

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: I —— — I m—

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.2.3 Special Procedures for Station 8: When the squad advances to Station 8, they must stand in their shooting order behind the Referee who should be positioned approximately five (5) meters from Station 8 on an imaginary line drawn between the centres of Station 8 and Station 4. After the Referee has declared “START” each athlete in turn must:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Take position for the high house target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Load the shotgun with one (1) cartridge only;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Adopt the READY position;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Call for the target; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Shoot at the high house target. Then turn clockwise (to the right, in the direction of the target crossing post):

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) Take position for the low house target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) Load the shotgun with one (1) cartridge only;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) Adopt the READY position;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) Call for the target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: j) Shoot at the low house target; and 406 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: k) When the result of this last shot is known, the athlete must leave the station and move to the rear of the line of the athletes who have still to shoot. Each athlete must do the same in succession.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.24 Cartridge Loading Sequence

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) On Station 8 for both the high and low house targets, the shotgun must be loaded with one (1) cartridge only;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) On Station 4 where two (2) single targets are to be shot, two (2) cartridges must be loaded before calling for the first single target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) In case an athlete forgets to load the second barrel in singles on Station 4 (when two (2) single targets are to be shot) and after calling for or shooting at the first target, remembers and either opens his shotgun to load or he raises his hand to ask permission of the Referee to load his shotgun, the target will be declared “LOST;”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) When shooting is interrupted, the shotgun must be opened and be made empty; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) No athlete may turn from the shooting station before his shotgun is open and empty.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.25 Trial Targets Aregular target from each of the high and low houses may be seen by the athletes of each squad:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) From Station 1 immediately prior to the start of their first round on each day of competition;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If the Referee declares “NO TARGET,” on a single target two consecutive times, the Athlete may ask to have one (1) trial target thrown. If the Referee declares “No Target” on a double two consecutive times, the Athlete may ask to have one (1) trial target of doubles, provided the “No Target”, was not fired upon or both or either of the targets of a No Target double were not fired upon.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If a round of shooting is interrupted for more than five (5) minutes because of a technical malfunction that is not the fault of an athlete, before the competition resumes the squad must be allowed to view one (1) regular target from each House.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.26 Sighting On the Ranges Aiming and sighting exercises:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) May be conducted after the Referee has ordered “START” only on Station

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 1. The athlete is permitted (within the allowable time limit) after loading and before shooting to raise the shotgun to the shoulder and sight for a few seconds for both the single target and the double;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete must then adopt the READY position before calling for the target(s);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Prior to the start of the round an athlete is not permitted to make any aiming or sighting exercises with or without the shotgun on any other station; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) during the round, athletes who are not shooting may, without disturbing the other athletes or the Referee, use their hand to track targets while another athlete is shooting. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 407

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.3 Target Distances and Elevations

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Skeet traps must be set before the start of the PET and the competition according to the specifications. (In calm weather conditions targets must carry a distance of 68.00m +/- 1.00m as measured from the face of the house behind Stations 1 and 7). The settings must be examined, approved and sealed by the Jury prior to each day of PET and competition.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) All athletes, coaches and team officials are prohibited from entering the Skeet houses after the Jury has examined and approved the trap settings (see Rule 9.3.c).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) All athletes, coaches and team officials are prohibited from entering the field of play while juries are examining the target settings prior to the start of the PET or the competition, unless permitted by the jury

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Depending upon the number of ranges in use, the squads must be scheduled before the start of the competition under the supervision of the Jury, in such a way so that, whenever possible, each squad should shoot the same number of times on each range in use.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.3.1 Irregular Trajectory Any target flying along a path other than that specified in angle, elevation or distance, in the Rules, must be considered irregular. A target must also be considered irregular in case it does not pass the boundary.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.4 READY Position At the moment the athlete calls and until the target(s) appears, the athlete must stand in the READY position with:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Both feet entirely within the shooting station boundaries;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Holding the shotgun with both hands;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The shotgun stock in contact with the body; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The toe of the stock on or below the ISSF official marker tape and clearly visible to the Referee standing in the correct position.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.4.1 Marker Tape To aid the Referee in controlling the position of the gun the ISSF official marker tape must be permanently affixed to the shooting vest (outer garment).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.4.2 The ISSF official marker tape must be:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) 250mm long, 30mm wide, distinctly yellow in colour, clearly bearing the ISSF logo; not to be faded or torn and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Permanently affixed to the appropriate side of the shooting vest.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.4.3 Marker Tape Check

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Athletes are responsible for ensuring that the marker tape is correctly positioned as per Rule 9.9.4.4 below. The Jury will provide an equipment control consultation service that is available to all athletes starting on the first Pre-Event Training Day so that athletes, if they wish, may have their equipment checked prior to the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) To ensure compliance with ISSF Rules, the Jury will conduct random checks during Competition and any athlete found to be in violation of the rules must be disqualified (see Rule 9.15.5.1). 408 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.9.4.4 The correct position of the marker tape must be checked as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) All pockets of the shooting vest must be empty;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete must stand straight (erect) while holding the right arm (right- handed shooter) in a right-angle position on the side of the body with the lower arm horizontal and the upper arm vertical.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) TWO JURY MEMBERS TO DO THE TEST. One jury member must stand in front of the athlete to see that the athlete has the shoulder down, another jury member must stand on the side of the athlete to see if the elbow is over the hip mark. The athlete will just relax in the shoulder and bend the arm in 90 degrees.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The jury in charge will make sure that the skeet marker tape is at the correct position immediately below the point of the elbow.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) An ISSF seal must then be placed on the end of the marker tape and a small hollow rivet on the front of the mark.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026

chunks.text: 9.95.7 Additional “LOST” Target Rule Applying to Doubles In addition, the following must also apply in the case of doubles:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) When an athlete for no permitted reason fails to fire at the first target of a regular double for which he has called the targets must be declared “LOST” and “LOST,”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) When an athlete for no permitted reason fails to fire at the second target of a regular double for which he has called the first target must be recorded according to the result and the second target must be declared “LOST;”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) An athlete misses the first target of the double and accidentally hits the second target with the same shot; the first target shall be declared “LOST” and the double repeated to determine the result of the second shot only. The athlete must always shoot at both targets in the repeated double(s);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) A shot is discharged involuntarily after the athlete has called, but before the targets appear, the first target must be declared “LOST” and the double must be repeated to determine the result of the second shot only. The athlete must shoot at both targets in the repeated double; For a second or subsequent involuntary discharge in the same round the targets must be declared “LOST” and “LOST” and the Referee must issue a Warning (Yellow Card);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) If an athlete misses the first target in a double and has an allowable EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 411

chunks.text: malfunction on the second shot, the first target must be declared “LOST” and the double repeated to establish the result of the second shot only. The athlete must shoot at both targets in the repeated double;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) If the athlete breaks the first target in a double and has an allowable malfunction on the second shot, the first shot must be declared “HIT” and the double repeated to establish the result of the second shot only. The athlete must shoot at both targets in the repeated double; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: g) If the targets of a regular double are shot in reverse order, both of them must be declared “LOST.

chunks.text: 9.9.5.8 Shooting Out of Turn If an athlete inadvertently shoots out of turn, the result of the shot(s) must be recorded and the athlete given an official Warning (Yellow Card). Any repetition in the same round must result in the target(s) shot at being declared “LOST” and the matter referred to the Jury. The athlete may be Disqualified (Red Card).

chunks.text: 9.10 COMPETITION ADMINISTRATION

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.10.1 Shooting Schedules

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Athletes and Team Officials must be informed of the exact start time, the squad and range schedules and the allocated positions within the squads no later than two (2) hours after the Technical Meeting on the day preceding the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Athletes and Team Officials must be informed of the range schedules for the Pre-Event Training by 18:00 hours on the day before; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If it becomes necessary to change any of the shooting schedules for any reason, the Athletes and Team Officials must be informed immediately by posting the new schedules on the Main Notice Board and the Shotgun Range Scoreboard and distributing them to all participating teams. If necessary, post the new schedules on the info boards of the official hotels.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.10.1.1 Replacement of an Athlete If an athlete has fired a shot in the competition and must withdraw, he may not be replaced. This rule will also apply for competitions composed of several parts or carried out over several days.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.10.1.2 Programme Interruptions Once shooting has started it must continue without interruption according to the programme, except for safety reasons, mechanical breakdowns, poor lighting conditions, extreme weather conditions, or other enforced delays in the programme that would seriously affect the quality of competition. Only the Technical delegate or Chairperson of juries with the Technical Delegate approval, may interrupt the shooting, in the event of heavy rain, storm or lightning or bad visibility conditions (Fog). In emergency situations, the jury on duty may temporarily stop the shooting until the Chairperson of Juries or the Technical Delegate takes the final decision 412 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.text: 9.10.2 Squadding

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.10.2.1 Squad Composition

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) A squad must be composed of six (6) members except when the drawing does not permit a totally even distribution; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Squads of less than five (5) are not permitted except when an athlete is declared “ABSENT” at the commencement of a round or an athlete has to leave a round for any reason or if the organising committee could not provide auxiliary athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.10.2.2 Auxiliary Athletes (Fillers)

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The Organizing Committee should have available athletes of a proficient standard who may be required to act as non-competing auxiliary athletes (Fillers):

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If the squad consists of less than five (5) members drawn by lot, it should be filled with auxiliary athletes (Fillers);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The Organizing Committee may, with the approval of the Jury, also use auxiliary athletes (fillers) to fill squads with only five (5) members; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) These auxiliary athletes should have their scores posted in the normal manner on the official scorecard in order to provide continuity. However, their names and nationality must not be listed on any official document.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The auxiliary must be of the same gender as the original squad

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.10.23 Squadding Draw

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The drawing for the Qualification Rounds must be made so that the athletes of each country are distributed in such a way that no squad will contain more than one (1) athlete from each nation (except in the World Cup Final/Final Tournament of the Year and Olympic Games if necessary);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The allocation of athletes to the squads and positions within the squads must be done by the drawing of lots under the supervision of the Jury Chairperson and the approval of the TD. This may be done with a computer programme suited for this purpose; and ¢) The random selection of ranges and the division of the rounds must be made under the supervision of the Jury Chairperson and the approval of the TD.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.10.24 Squad Adjustments The Jury, in conjunction with the Organizing Committee/RTS Office, and with the approval of the Technical Delegate(s), may adjust the draw, but only to ensure that the requirements of the Squadding Draw (Rule 9.10.2.3) are met.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.10.25 Shooting Order The shooting order of the squads and the shooting order within the squads must also be changed from day to day by the Organizing Committee/RTS Office under the supervision of the Jury. This can be done by either having the squads and the members of each squad shoot in reverse order or by splitting the squads in a manner agreed by the Jury. In the case of a one (1) day competition, the shooting order within the squads may, with the permission of the Jury, be changed from round to round. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 413
