chunks.text: (The man always shoots before the Woman) until the tie is broken according to the following sequence: Station 1 left target, Station 2 right target, station 3 left target, Station 4 right target, Station 5 left target, then Station 1 again this time shooting at a right target and so on. Only one (1) shot is permitted at each target. After shooting, the athlete must move to the rear of the athlete who has yet to shoot. The score of the team is combined.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Skeet Mixed Teams. The athletes must line up behind station 4 in Start number order. They must shoot at a regular double (man shoots first) followed by the second member of the team (woman) who will also shoot at a regular double. The athletes of the other mixed team must than do likewise and each member of the team shoot at a normal double. The mixed team with the lowest number of hits out of 4 shots will be eliminated and will be ranked the lower place, If the tie is not broken, the same procedure will continue on the same station in the same order but with reverse doubles, If the tie is still not broken, the same procedure will continue on the same station in the same order but with regular doubles, and so on until the tie is broken. The score of the team is combined.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.1 When an athlete disagrees with a Referee’s decision regarding a “LOST TARGET/S” or a “NO TARGET/S”, before the next athlete fires, he/she must act immediately by raising an arm, saying “VAR” and requesting the use of VAR to resolve the protest.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.2 Likewise, a coach (who is assigned a seat in the FOP), can initiate a VAR protest before the next athlete fires, by drawing the attention of the Jury in Charge and showing the “VAR” card, which will be given to all coaches inside the FOP before the start of the final. The Jury in Charge must then attract the attention of the Referee and initiate a VAR protest

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.3 After a VAR protest has been initiated, the Referee must immediately command “STOP” and temporarily interrupt the shooting. The referee must ensure that the athletes empty their Shotguns, face the spectator’s area, and form a rectangle outline, indicating a video screen, to show that the protest must be verified using VAR.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.4 The Referee and the Jury in charge will proceed to the VAR Station, where the display screen is located, to review the recorded video. The VAR must be reviewed by both the Jury member and the Referee in charge. They will jointly examine the slow-motion footage to resolve the protest, with the assistance of the VAR System specialist (either a Technician or a Special Jury member) if available. The final decision, after reviewing the video in slow motion, rests with the Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: 9.17.8.5 An athlete or a coach may submit a VAR protest only for himself or on behalf of his own Athletes, not for any other participant in the final.

chunks.text: After the end of the Qualification Rounds, the top 4 teams will qualify for the Final. The final is only (1) stage, consisting of 8 Athletes (4 Teams). Finalists shoot one shot only at each target. The man is always shooting first followed by the woman. After each athlete has shot at a station he must move to the next station to fire in sequence on that station. A timing system to control the 30-second preparation time limit must be used. Each Final consists of a series of target sequences followed by progressive eliminations that continue until the gold and silver medals are decided, as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) After the 8 finalists (4 Teams) complete a round of 12 targets each athlete, (24 targets per team), (one regular double and one reverse double on station 3, one regular double and one reverse double on station 4, one regular double and one reverse double on station 5) The 4th team is eliminated, ranked in 4th place. The 6 remaining finalists (3 Teams) will continue according to their Finals Start numbers.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) After the 6-remaining finalist (3 Teams) complete another round of 12 targets each athlete, (24 targets per team), (one regular double and one reverse double on station 3, one regular double and one reverse double on station 4, one regular double and one reverse double on station 5,) and complete 24 targets/Athlete (48 Targets/Team) the 3rd team is eliminated in 3rd place (Bronze Medal winning team). In case there’s a tie up to and including this stage, the lowest Finals Start number wins. Finals Start Number 1 is the lowest Start Number, Start Number 4 is the highest Start Number.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) After the 4 remaining finalists (2 Teams) shoot at another 4 targets per 442 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: athlete, (one regular double and one reverse double on station 4), and complete 28 targets per athlete, (56 targets per team), the gold and silver medals are decided In case of a tie between 1st and 2nd place teams, there is an immediate shoot- off (9.17.4.3.b) Both team members must participate in the shoot off. Both team members will shoot (The man fires first followed by the woman) to obtain a combined score for the team. Test firing followed by the target showing will be done and finished before the start of the presentation. Total targets: 56 Targets per team.

chunks.text: 9.18.5.1 Coaching Timeout In the Final, while shooting is in progress, Coaches/Team Officials, without disturbing the athletes, may request from the Jury Member in Charge, one (1) Coaching Timeout for a maximum duration of thirty (30) seconds. The Jury Member in Charge will then, at the turn of that team’s athlete(s) to fire, without disturbing the shooting procedure decide when to stop shooting and allow the Coach/Team Official to approach and speak to the his/her athletes, on the shooting station. The other Coach/Team Official may, during this time, also approach and speak to his/her athletes without losing the opportunity for a timeout. The Jury Member in Charge must control the time.

chunks.text: 9.18.5.2 Reporting Times and Cartridge Control

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The members of the four (4) qualified Mixed Teams in the Final or their representatives (Coaches or Team Officials) must report to the Finals Range (at the designated area) for cartridge control at least 30 minutes before the scheduled Start Time of the Final. At this time the Jury will distribute the Finals Start numbers to all the athletes of the four (4) qualified Mixed Teams.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The Equipment Control Jury will instruct the members of each Mixed Team or their representatives (Coaches or Team Officials) to place all of their cartridges in numbered boxes (corresponding to the Start numbers of their Team). The Equipment Control Jury will select cartridges to be checked and seal the boxes in the presence of the Team members or Coach/Team Official and conduct equipment inspections. Cartridge checks must be completed before the presentations.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The members of the Qualified Mixed Teams must present themselves to the Finals Range, 15 minutes, before the start of the Final (Stage 1), for preliminaries and presentation

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) No additional cartridges may be brought to the FOP.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Atwo (2) hit penalty will be deducted from the score of the first series of the first athlete, if any of the Mixed Team's cartridges are not presented 30 minutes before the start of the Final or if either of the Team members does not report 15 minutes before the start of the Final. Any team that does not report at the time of the Presentations will not be allowed to take part in the Final and will be awarded 4th place.

chunks.text: b) After target observation and test firing, the athletes in the Final will assemble in a designated area to the side of the range, to await being called for presentation. The teams will line up in Start number order. The Qualified Teams in Final will enter the field of play (male athlete first — female athlete second) and the announcer will introduce them to the spectators. The Teams must remain facing the spectators until all have been presented, including the Jury Member in Charge and the appointed Referee.

chunks.text: e) At the end of the Final the Gold, Silver and Bronze Medallists are assembled by the Jury Member in Charge, on the field of play for official photographs and announcement, (Rule 6.17.1.14 q).

chunks.text: 9.18.54 Music and Audience Support During the Final, music must be played. The Jury should approve the music selected. Enthusiastic audience support is encouraged and is recommended during the matches.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: a) If the Referee decides that a disabled shotgun, or the malfunctioning of the shotgun or ammunition, is not the fault of the athlete, the athlete must be given not more than three (3) minutes in which to repair the shotgun or obtain another approved shotgun, or replace his ammunition. If this cannot be done within three (3) minutes, the athlete (Mixed Team) must withdraw. After the malfunction is corrected, the Final must continue.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) If a withdrawal of a team occurs during the Final the remaining Mixed Teams will continue, unless only one team remaining, then they must be declared as the winner.

chunks.text: c) AMixed Team is allowed a maximum of two (2) malfunctions during a Final, including any shoot-offs, whether or not there was an attempt to correct the malfunction.

chunks.text: d) Any regular target(s) on which any further malfunction occurs will be declared “LOST” whether or not the athlete attempted to fire.

chunks.text: c) Any other protest by the athlete or coach will be decided by the Finals Protest Jury immediately. The decision of the Finals Protest Jury is final and cannot be appealed.

chunks.text: 10.1 GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.1.1 These Rules are part of the ISSF Technical Rules and apply to all 10m and 50m Moving Target events.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.1.2 All athletes, team leaders and officials must be familiar with the ISSF Rules and ensure that these Rules are enforced. It is the responsibility of each athlete to comply with the Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.1.3 When a Rule refers to right-handed athletes, the reverse of that Rule refers to left-handed athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.1.4 Unless a Rule applies specifically to a men’s or women’s event, it must apply uniformly to both men’s and women’s events.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.2 SAFETY SAFETY IS OF PARAMOUNT IMPORTANCE ISSF Safety Rules are found in Rule 6.2.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.3 RANGE AND TARGET STANDARDS Target and target standards are found in Rule 6.3. Requirements for ranges and other facilities are found in Rule 6.4.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4 STANDARDS FOR 10m AND 50m RIFLES See MOVING TARGET RIFLE SPECIFICATION TABLE (10.14) Any rifle that meets the following standards may be used:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.1 The weight of the rifle and sight together must not exceed 5.5kg.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.2 An adjustable butt-plate is permitted. The curvature of the butt plate (positive or negative) must not exceed a depth or height of 20mm. The butt plate length must not exceed 150mm. Measurement of the depth or height of the butt- plate will be made at right-angles to the Centre-line of the bore of the rifle (see Table). The lowest point of the butt-plate, in its lowest position must not be lower than 200mm below the Centre-line of the bore of the rifle (see Table).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3 Sights The height of the Centre line of the telescope above the Centre line of the bore must not be more than 75mm.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.1 50m Rifles. Any types of sights are permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.2 10m Rifles. Any type of sights are permitted except that optical sights must be non-variable with a maximum of four power (4X) magnification (tolerance = +0.4 x). Examination of magnification power will be done with mechanical or optical devices.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.3 Except when a sight is damaged, through mechanical or optical failure, it may not be exchanged between slow and fast part, before the medal matches, or between the two series of a mixed competition. Sight adjustments during the event are permitted, provided they do not delay the shooting.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.4 Barrel Weights. Only barrel weights within a radius of 60mm from the Centre of the barrel are permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.5 One Rifle Per Event. The same rifle, including the sight, weights and trigger EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 461

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: system, must be used for slow and fast, or first and second part in any event.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: a) The trigger pull weight must be not less than 500 grams;

chunks.text: c) The length of the system measured from the rear of the closed bolt in the discharged position to the foremost end of the system, including any extension (whether part of the barrel or not), must not exceed 1000mm; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: a) The trigger pull weight is unlimited;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) A set trigger must not be used;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The length of the system measured from the rear of the mechanism to the forward end of the system, including any extension (whether part of the barrel or not), must not exceed 1000mm; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Pellets of any shape, made of lead or other soft material, with a calibre of

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.5.1 Athletes are responsible for ensuring that all items of equipment used by them comply with these Rules. The Equipment Control Section must be open to inspect athletes’ equipment from the Official Training Day until the last day of Moving Target competition. Athletes are encouraged, if they wish, to bring their equipment for an Equipment Control check before the competitions to be sure they comply with these Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.4.5.2 Random post-competition checks will be made of all equipment items to ensure compliance (6.7.9).

chunks.text: 10.5.1.2 The correct position of the Marker Tape must be checked as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.6.1 Duties and Functions of the Chief Range Officer A Chief Range Officer must be appointed for each event on a specific range. The Chief Range Officer is:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) In charge of all Range Officers and range personnel and is responsible for the correct conduct of the shooting event and, where centralized control is exercised, responsible for giving all range commands;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Responsible for ensuring the co-operation of all range personnel with the Jury; EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 463

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Responsible for resolving any irregularities which other Range Officers cannot resolve;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Responsible for the rapid correction of any equipment failures and for making available the necessary experts and material to operate the range. A repair service expert must be at the Chief Range Officer's immediate disposal at all times. For cases that exceed the capabilities of the repair service, additional provisions must be made;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Responsible for the efficient and rapid scoring of all targets in co-operation with the Chief RTS (Results, Timing and Scoring) Officer; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) If necessary, the Chief Range Officer participates in the drawing of lots for the assignment of firing points.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.6.2 Duties and Functions of the Assistant Chief Range Officer If the competition is being shot on several ranges, an Assistant Chief Range Officer should be appointed. He also substitutes for the Chief Range Officer during his absence.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.6.3 Duties and Functions of the Range Officer Range Officers are responsible to the Chief Range Officer for the orderly operation of a particular range. They work closely with the Jury. The Range Officer:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Calls the athletes and announces the preliminary result of the series;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Checks the names and bib numbers of athletes to ensure that they correspond with the start list, Range Register and small scoreboards. If possible, this must be completed before the start of the Preparation Time;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Gives the necessary competition commands;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Continually watches the READY and shooting positions;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Is responsible for the coordinated work of the Register Keeper (when using paper targets) and other range officials;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) Supervises the correct operation of the targets;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) Receives protests and passes them on to a Jury Member; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) Records all disturbances, disciplinary actions, malfunctions, additional sighting shots, repeats, etc. on the Register Keeper's score card.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.6.4 Duties and Functions of the Register Keeper — Paper Targets

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Examines the entries on the range assignment list and score cards to ensure that the names of the athletes, bib numbers, range numbers and nations agree;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Writes down the indicated score and compares this with the TV monitor when it is in use; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Make entries on score cards in such a way that the RTS Office can identify if the target moves to right or left.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.6.5 Duties and Functions of the Line Officer

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The Line Officer must be located so he can observe the readiness of the athlete and is able to hear the athlete’s “READY” command;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) He must be able to observe the score keeping system after each shot, 464 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: see the result of scoring, and at the same time observe the signal to start the target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) He operates the starting button, the stop button, and the switch to change from slow to fast; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If no electronic programme switch is provided for the mixed event, the necessary switching must be executed under a plan approved by the Jury.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.6.6 Duties and Functions of the Pit Officer — Paper Targets A Pit Officer and an assistant must be stationed at each side of all ranges used during the competition. Depending on the system used, target changing can be done with one pit officer and an assistant if adequate safety baffles are available. The pit officer or his assistant is responsible for changing the target during the standard rhythm time. The pit officer is responsible for:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Ensuring that the correct targets are attached to the frame in the specified sequence;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Correct positioning of the targets or repair Centres, correctly applying patches to cover bullet holes, establishing the rhythm of score indicating, etc.;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Examining the target after each shot and ensuring that every shot is correctly signalled for both value and location;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) Ensuring that the target is facing in the correct direction before each shot;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Giving bullet holes close to a scoring ring the lower value when indicating the score;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) Removing targets from the frame at the conclusion of each stage and place them in a secure container to await transfer to the RTS Office;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) Target couriers must transmit targets and report sheets to the RTS Office at least after every second athlete finishes firing;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) Covering sighting shots on 50 m targets with black patches;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) Each series begins with four 4 sighting shots. In 50 m disciplines, if the athlete does not shoot the sighting shots, black patches must be stuck on the corresponding targets outside the rings; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: j) Competition shot holes on 50m targets must be covered with transparent patches. Only the outer part of shot holes which are close to a scoring ring should be covered to assist the RTS Office in scoring. The last hit on each target must remain uncovered.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.6.7 Specific Rules For 10m Events Depending on the system used, target changing can be done with one Pit Range Officer and an assistant if adequate safety baffles are available. The Pit Range Officer or his assistant is responsible for changing the target during the standard rhythm time.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.6.8 Technical Officers — Electronic Scoring Targets (EST) Technical Officers may be appointed by the Official Results Provider to operate and maintain EST systems. They may offer advice to Range Officers and Jury Members, but must not make any decisions regarding the application of these rules. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 465

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7 SHOOTING EVENT PROCEDURES AND COMPETITION RULES

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.71 Positions

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.1.1 Until the moment that any part of the target becomes visible in the opening, the athlete must remain in the READY position, holding the rifle with both hands in such a way that the lower tip (toe) of the butt-plate is equal to or below the mark on the shooting jacket. The mark must be visible to a Jury Member or Range Officer while the athlete is in the READY position.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.1.2 The Shooting Position is standing without support. The rifle butt-plate must be held against the shoulder (upper right chest) and supported only with both hands. The left arm (right arm for left-handed athlete) must not rest on the hip or the chest. The athlete must take a position in relation to the bench, table, or wall in such a way that it is clearly visible that they do not give him any support whatsoever. The use of a sling is not permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.1.3 The perfomance is the time when the target is visible in the opening. The timing of it must start when the leading edge of the target appears and stop when the leading edge of the target reaches the opposite wall. Target can move either “fast” or “slow”

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.2 10m and 50m Events — Programmes

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.2.1 10m and 50m 30 + 30 shots (Men, Women, Men Junior, and Women Junior):

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) 4 sighting shots and 30 shots slow, each in 5.0 seconds (+0.2 seconds); and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) 4 sighting shots and 30 shots fast, each in 2.5 seconds (+0.1 seconds).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.2.2 10m and 50m 40 shots Mixed (Men, Women, Men Junior, and Women Junior):

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The event will be fired in two (2) series. Consisting of four (4) sighting shots (two (2) slow and two (2) fast from each side) and 20 mixed; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Each mixed serie must have 10 slow and 10 fast from each side, arranged in such a way that the athlete must fire an equal number of each speed from each side. They must be mixed in such a manner that it is unlikely the athlete can anticipate whether the next is slow or fast. There must not be more than five (5) continuous (combined right and left) ones at the same speed.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.2.3 All events can be conducted in either one (1) or two (2) days, depending on the number of entries in the competition. If an event is conducted in two (2) days, one (1) complete series must be conducted each day.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.2.4 Categories (Men/Women or Men Junior/Women Junior) can be combined as open category, if there are not enough competitors to reach the minimum requirement for a Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3 Competition Rules

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.1 a) Every athlete must shoot the entire competition on the assigned range.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Any change in range assignments may be made only if the Jury decides that there are different range conditions such as light conditions;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If the event is conducted in one (1) day, the order of shooting for the second stage must remain the same as the order of shooting for the first stage; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If the event is conducted over two (2) days the athlete in the lowest ranking position at the end of the first day shoots first on the second day, and the 466 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: athlete in the highest-ranking position at the end of the first day shoots last on the second day.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.2 Before the start of the competition, the first athlete must be given the opportunity to dry fire a full series in the event being shot. If the first athlete does not wish to dry fire a full series, it is still necessary to run a full series.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.3 At ISSF Championships, the Organizing Committee must open the day's competition by having a test athlete (someone not in the competition) shoot a full series commencing at the official start time, so that the first athlete may complete the dry firing series under competition conditions.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.4 Only the next athlete in succession may dry fire, at a specially marked point on the firing line (see Rule 6.4.15).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.5 The competition series always starts from the right to left. Only one shot may be fired each time the target moves through the area of fire.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.6 Indication of Shots

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Different methods for indicating the score and location of hits may be used. The method used must allow the athlete to be certain of the score and location of the shot;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Television or similar monitoring devices that indicate scores and hit locations are permitted for any competition and are compulsory in ISSF Championships;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The athlete is not required to use the television monitor. If he does not use it, he must accept the alternative method of indicating scores and hit locations; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If an athlete observes a discrepancy between the monitor and the alternative method of indicating scores and hit locations, he may request the signal to be repeated, but he is not entitled to another shot even if the first signal was in error. If a repeat signal is requested, this must be before shooting again.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.7 Preparation Time After the athlete is called to the shooting station, he must be given a preparation time of two (2) minutes before the first “READY” is to be given.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4 Firing Procedures

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) When the athlete has finished his preparation on the range, he must call “READY” before each sighting shot and also before the first shot of the series;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The Range Officer must start the target immediately. If the target does not appear in four (4) seconds after the order to start is given or after completion of the indication of the score, the Range Officer must stop the shooting and make sure that the range equipment and the athlete are ready, after which he will start the target again;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If the target is started before the athlete has called “READY,” he should refrain from shooting. However, if he shoots, the result must be scored;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If the Range Officer finds that the athlete delays unnecessarily before calling “READY” or taking the READY position, the following action will be taken. In the case of the first occurrence, he will be given a Warning (Yellow Card) for delay of competition. On the second occurrence a two (2) point EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 467

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: Deduction (Green Card) will be given. Any subsequent violation could result in Disqualification (Red Card) by the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) After completing the sighting shots, the athlete may pause for up to 60 seconds to adjust his sight. The MATCH series will then be started;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) After each shot, the score and location of each shot hole must be shown for at least 4 seconds. The end of the indication of the score is always the signal to the athlete for the continuation of the series;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: g) Itis necessary to set a constant rhythm (time cycle) and system in the time taken to indicate the score, the method to indicate the score and the method to change targets;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: h) In 50m MATCH firing, following the completion, the marking and signalling must be completed and the target available to move in not more than 12 seconds, and the athlete must be ready for the target to be released in not more than 18 seconds;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: i) In 10m MATCH firing, following the completion of a shot, the signalling and target changing must be completed and the target available to move in not more than 18 seconds, and the athlete must be ready for the target to be released in not more than 20 seconds;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: j) The Range Officer and the Jury Members must control carefully the 18 and 20 second timings and immediately penalize an athlete who does not comply with this rule;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: k) When the athlete shoots and the shot is not on the target and he later claims that he was not ready when the target started it will be recorded as a miss and he will not be permitted to re-shoot;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 1) The timing for the 18 second (50m) and 20 second (10m) time limits begins when the target disappears at the end of each time moving. The timing stops when the athlete is in the ready position;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: m) The Jury must verify the correct timing of the targets during the competition; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: n) If the target is started from the wrong side or tail first, it must be cancelled and repeated, even if the athlete has fired.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.1 In case anything should occur that might be dangerous, disturb the athlete, or otherwise interfere with the competition, the Range Officer must stop the shooting with the command “STOP.” Should the athlete fire at the moment of the command, he is entitled to have the shot cancelled if he requests it.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.2 If a series is interrupted for more than 5 minutes or the athlete is moved to another firing point, he may ask for 2 additional sighting shots (4 sighting shots in the mixed event). In such a case the Range Officer must announce “SIGHTING SHOTS” and the score keepers must be informed. These sighting shots must begin from the same side from which the series is to be continued after the interruption. If no sighting shots are requested, the series resumes where it was interrupted.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.3 If an athlete should be unable to fire, a miss must be scored, unless the Rules that entitle the athlete to a re-shoot apply.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.4 If the Range Officer neglects to stop the shooting when the respective Rules apply, the athlete may raise his arm and call “STOP” provided he has not caused the situation himself. The Range Officer must stop the shooting 468 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: at once. If the Range Officer finds the action of the athlete justified, he may continue shooting after a check of the situation according to Rules respectively. If the athlete is not justified, the Range Officer must give the command to repeat and the athlete must be penalized by deducting two (2) points from the value of that shot.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.5 Misses

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Every shot prior to the appearance of the competition target must be scored as a miss;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The target will be started without a repeated shot and the miss marked as “Z” on the target, on the score card and on an incident report;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Hits outside the scoring rings must be scored as zero(es) and recorded as “X” on the target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If the athlete does not shoot, the shot is scored as zero and recorded as *“-" on the target;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) Shots not hitting the target are scored as zero(es) and recorded as “Z" on the target; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) Skid shots and ricochets must be scored as zero(es).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.6 Misses and Penalties in 10m Events:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must not discharge propellant gas from his rifle. For the first such offence, two (2) points will be deducted (Green Card) from the score of the next competition shot. For the second offence, the athlete must be disqualified (Red Card) from further competition;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Any release of the propelling charge, after his first competition target is in place, without a hit on the target will be scored as a miss; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) ltis the responsibility of the athlete to ensure his air or gas rifle is fully charged with propellant air or gas prior to commencing the competition. If during the competition he has insufficient propellant air or gas to continue, he will be allowed a maximum of five (5) minutes to renew the supply. He may then continue the series but without any additional sighting shots.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8 MEDAL MATCH RULES

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.1 A 10m Moving Target Medal Match may be conducted as the second phase in the 10m Moving Target Men, Women, Men Junior or Women Junior events.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.2 The full 10m Moving Target Men, Women, Men Junior or Women Junior course of fire must be completed as a Qualification for a Medal Match.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.3 The four (4) highest scoring athletes in the Qualification advance to the Medal Match. Their start position in the Medal Match is determined by their rank in the Qualification.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.4 Ties for the second and fourth place in the Qualification will be broken according to shoot-off rules.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.5 All qualifiers for the Medal Match start at zero (0). No Qualification scores carry forward into the Medal Match.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.6 Medal Match qualifiers must report ready to shoot on the range 10 minutes before the start time.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.7 In the Medal Match, the first place athlete in the Qualification will compete EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 469

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: against the fourth place athlete; the second place athlete in the Qualification will compete against the third place athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.8 An introduction of the athletes must be made.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.9 The Medal Match will be conducted on either two (2) or four (4) ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.10 If there are only two (2) ranges, the first relay will be held with the athletes ranked first and fourth.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.11 If there are four (4) ranges, the athletes ranked first and fourth are on adjacent ranges and second and third are on the other ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.12 The preparation time is one (1) minute followed by two (2) sighting shots, one left and one right (fast). The first sighting shot is on command.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.13 All competition shots are on command in fast (2.5 seconds).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.14 Scoring is in decimals. The athlete with the highest score in each match on each shot receives one point. If there is a tie between a pair, no athlete receives a point.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.15 The athlete who receives six (6) points or more with a difference of two (2) points is the winner of the match.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.16 The losers of the two (2) semi-final matches will compete for bronze medal in the same way as above

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.8.17 The winners of the semi-final matches will compete for gold or silver medals in the same way as above.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.9 INFRINGEMENTS AND DISCIPLINARY RULES

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.9.1 The athlete must not exceed the preparation time of two (2) minutes without justification, or wait longer than 60 seconds after the conclusion of sighting shots to begin competition shots. After 30 additional seconds, the target must be started and the result counted whether the athlete is in the shooting position or not.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.9.2 If an athlete does not report when he is due to start the competition the Range Officer must call his name out loud three (3) times within one (1) minute. If the athlete fails to appear, he must have a new shooting time set by the competition officials and two (2) points must be deducted from his total score. If, however, the Jury is convinced that the reason the athlete was late was beyond his control, no penalty will be enforced.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.9.3 An athlete who violates the Rules concerning the READY or shooting position must be given a Warning (Yellow Card) after the first violation. On the second occurrence a two (2) point DEDUCTION (Green Card) will be given. Any subsequent violation must result in DISQUALIFICATION (Red Card).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.10 MALFUNCTIONS

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.10.1 If the athlete has a malfunction with his rifle or ammunition in the Qualification round, the rifle must be placed on the bench or table without further touching it. The Range Officer must be called and shown the malfunction. The Range Officer must interrupt the series and start a timer to determine the length of the interruption. Malfunctions in Medal Matches may not be claimed.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.10.2 If the Range Officer determines, after examining the rifle and ammunition, that 470 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: the malfunction was not caused by the athlete, the shot may be repeated.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.10.3 The athlete must not be considered at fault if:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The rifle is found in a discharged condition, the chamber is found to contain a cartridge of the same type the athlete is using, the cartridge shows a clear impression of the firing pin and the bullet has not left the barrel; or,

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The reason for not shooting was caused by a malfunction of the rifle which is not likely to have been caused by the athlete or could not reasonably have been prevented by him.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.10.4 The athlete must be considered at fault if:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) He or she has not placed the rifle on the bench or table;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) He or she changed something on the rifle before placing it on the table;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The safety catch was not released;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) The breech was not closed all the way;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: e) The rifle was not loaded; or

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: f) The rifle was loaded with the wrong kind of ammunition. If the Range Officer determines that the malfunction was caused by the athlete, a miss must be scored.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.10.5 After the interruption due to a malfunction of the rifle or ammunition, the Range Officer may order the repair of the rifle or a change of ammunition. If the malfunction can be repaired within five (5) minutes, the shooting may be continued. If the repair will take longer than five (5) minutes, the athlete has the right to continue shooting immediately with another rifle or to withdraw to repair his rifle. The Range Officer, with the consent of the Jury, must then decide when the athlete may continue his series, either with the repaired rifle, or with another rifle if a repair is impossible. The series must be continued from the point of interruption.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.10.6 The Range Officer should continue as if the athlete did not withdraw in order to allow the next athlete to complete his dry firing.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.10.7 Faulty Sights

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If the athlete discovers during his or her sighting shots that a faulty sight cannot be corrected by adjustment, the Jury can agree to a change of the sight, if a second sight is available;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) After the change the athlete must receive sighting shots;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The athlete must not receive a repeat or additional sighting shots if the examination by the Range Officer shows that the sight mount was not properly tightened; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) If the sight becomes loose during a competition series because it was not properly tightened, all shots must be scored.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.11 FAILURE OF 10m EST SYSTEMS

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.11.1 If there is a failure of ALL targets on a range - also applicable to conventional ranges:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The actual time must be recorded by the Chief Range Officer and the Jury; EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 471

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) All completed MATCH shots fired by each athlete must be counted and recorded. In the event of a range power supply failure, this may involve waiting until power is restored to enable the number of shots registered by the target, not necessarily on the firing point monitor, to be established; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) After the failure is rectified and the full range is in operation the athletes will be allowed a one (1) minute preparation time to allow them to resume their positions. The time for recommencing is to be announced over the loudspeaker system at least five (5) minutes beforehand. At the end of the preparation time, the athletes will be allowed four (4) sighting shots (2 left ; 2 right). These sighting shots must begin from the same side from which the series is to be continued after the interruption. After the sighting shots a 30 second pause will be allowed. After the sighting shots and pause the series will resume where it was interrupted.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.11.2 In the event of the failure of a Single Target If a single target fails to function the athlete will be moved to another target where the same procedure stated in Rule 10.11.1, ¢ will apply.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.11.3 Complaint concerning failure to register or display a shot on the monitor of an electronic scoring target system.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must immediately inform the nearest range official of the failure. The range official must make a written note of the time of the complaint. One or more Jury Members must go to the firing position; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete will be directed to fire one more MATCH shot at his target. The athlete must call “READY.” The procedure of a complaint concerning a failure to register or display a shot stated in the Technical Rules (6.10.8) will apply.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos

chunks.text: 10.12 TIE-BREAKING

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.121 Individual Ties in 50m and 10m Events Ties for athletes with perfect scores will not be broken.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.12.1.1 Ties for places 1 — 3 and below:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) If two (2) or more athletes shoot equal scores, ties for the first three (3) individual places must be decided by a shoot-off to be arranged by the Jury. This shoot-off consists of two (2) sighting shots (one (1) left — one (1) right) and two (2) competition shots (one (1) left — one (1) right) in 2.5 seconds (fast) on command for all competition shots; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) In the event of a further tied score the shoot-off will continue until the tie is broken.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.12.1.2 Rules for Shoot-offs

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The shoot-off must begin as soon as possible after the protest time has expired. If the shoot-off is not held at a prearranged time that was publicly announced, the athletes involved must remain in contact with the Chief Range Officer pending an announcement as to time and place;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Athletes with tied scores will be allocated adjacent firing points by the drawing of lots under the supervision of the Jury. If more athletes have equal scores, the firing sequence will also be determined by the drawing of lots. When several athletes are tied for more than one ranking place, the tie for the lowest ranking position will be broken first, followed by the next ranking higher position until all ties are broken; 472 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If an athlete fails to appear for a shoot-off, he will be ranked last in this shoot-off. If two (2) or more shoot-off athletes fail to appear they will be ranked according to Rule 10.12.1.3 for Individual Ties ranking from 4th place; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) During the shoot-off, malfunctions and other irregularities must be treated according to these Rules, but only one (1) malfunction is allowed during the breaking of the tie and any re-shoot or completion will take place immediately.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.12.1.3 Ties for 4th place and lower, if not resolved by any Shoot-off, must be decided as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) 10m Events. Any remaining ties for fourth (4th) place and lower are ranked according to tie-breaking Rule 6.15 (i.e., highest number of inner tens, highest score on the last series, next to the last series, etc.);

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) For 50m Moving Target 30 + 30. Any remaining ties for fourth (4th) place and lower are ranked according to the highest total of the fast part; and if ties remain by comparing the lowest value shot(s) in the total competition for the tied individuals (the athlete with the lowest value shot(s) is declared the loser); if any ties remain, the athletes must have the same ranking; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) For 50m Moving Target Mixed. Any remaining ties for fourth (4th) place and lower are ranked according to the highest total of the second stage; and if ties remain by comparing the lowest value shot(s) in the total competition for the tied individuals (the athlete with the lowest value shot(s) is declared the loser); if any ties remain, the athletes must have the same ranking.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.122 Team Ties Team Ties in 10m Events / 50m Events Ties in team events must be decided by totaling the results of all members of a team and applying these Tie-Breaking steps.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The highest total number of inner tens;

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The highest total score on the last series, then the next to the last series etc.; and

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) If any ties remain, total scores will be compared on shot-by-shot basis using inner tens, beginning with the last shot, then the next to the last shot etc.

chunks.text: 10.13.4 Number of participants in each team Ateam consist of two (2) athletes from each nation. One man and one woman (juniors or seniors or mixed). A maximum of three (3) teams per Nation is allowed. No mixed nation teams are allowed.

chunks.text: 10.13.6 Position The two members of the team shoot at the same range. The man stands on the left side and the woman on the right side. Dry firing from the second member is not permitted.

chunks.text: 10.13.7.1 Shooting event procedures - Qualification stage

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) The event will be fired in one series of 8 sighting shots (4 sighting shots for each shooter) and 40 competition shots (mixed; 20 for each team member).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) The sighting shots: Both team members alternately; 2 shots each per time, starting with the men (2 men, 2 women, 2 men 2 women).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) The Competition: Both team members alternately; 20 shots for each team member, starting with the men (2 man, 2 women, 2 man, 2 women, ...).

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: d) No dry- firing allowed for the next team in line preparing for their series.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.13.7.2 Ranking in qualification The ranking in qualification stage will be the combined results of the two team members. The perfect score in the qualification is 400 points.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.13.7.3 Tie in qualification stage Rule ISSF 10.8.4 for Medal Match is used. The team decides which athlete shoots the tie breaking shots. The tie will be fired according to the rule

chunks.text: 10.13.8 Medal Match The four highest scoring teams in Qualification advance to the Medal Match.

chunks.text: 10.13.8.1 Rules for the Medal Matches The Medal Matches will be conducted as per ISSF Rule 10.8, if no other way stated in the rules here below.

chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: 10.13.8.2 Commands for Medal Matches Before the sighting shots the team will have one minute preparation time. Sighting shots: - ‘For the sighting shots load’ - ‘Attention’ - ‘3-2-1 START’ - The next sighting shots are up to the Athletes - STOP, end of sighting shots Competition: - ‘For the first competition shots load’ - ‘Attention’ - ‘3-2-1 START’ 474 EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF

chunks.text: 10.13.8.3 Shooting event procedures - Medal Matches and scoring

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: a) Semi-finals The teams compete in the Medal Matches only in fast. The members of the same team shoot at the same range. The Medal Matches will be conducted on two ranges. Four (4) sighting shots (1 going to left for man, 1 going to right for woman, 1 left man and 1 right woman) will be fired. Both Athletes are loading at the same time. A command for every competition shot is given. Scoring is in decimals. The competition starts with 2 shots (1 left men and 1 right women). The team with the highest total score of the 2 shots receives one point. If there is a tie between the teams, no team receives a point. The team who reaches six points or more with the difference of two points is winner of the match.

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: b) Semi-Final Procedure The winner of the semi-finals will compete for the Gold/Silver medal The losers of the semi-finals will compete for the Bronze medal

chunks.title: ISSF_Regras_2026_julho PT-BR e Anexos
chunks.edition: ISSF Edition 2025, Second Print 07/2026; effective 1 July 2026
chunks.text: c) Gold/Silver Match and Bronze Match The teams compete in the Medal Matches in fast. The members of the same team shoot at the same range. The Medal Matches will be conducted on two ranges. Four (4) sighting shots (1 going to left for man, 1 right woman, 1 left men and 1 right women) will be fired. Both Athletes are loading at the same time. A command for every competition shot is given. Scoring is in decimals. The competition starts with 2 shots (1 left men and 1 right women). The team with the highest total score of the 2 shots receives one point. If there is a tie between the teams, no team receives a point. The team to reach six points or more with the difference of two points is winner of the match. EDITION 2025 (Second Print 07/2026) Effective 1 July 2026 © ISSF 475
