chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1 PURPOSE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.1 THE ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.2  Promotes and guides the development of the shooting sport, without discrimination of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, gender, sexual orientation, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.3  Strengthens bonds of friendship and collaboration between shooting associations of all nations, Continental Confederations, other sport organizations and bodies according to the Fundamental Principles of Olympianism as defined in the Olympic Charter.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4 For achievement of its purposes the ISSF in particular

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.1  Co-operates with the IOC and the Organizing Committees of the Olympic Games in carrying out the organization of the shooting sport events and, as delegated by the IOC, supervises and controls all technical arrangements;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.2  Organizes World Championships, World Cups and other international competitions for ISSF recognized events for juniors and seniors;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.3  Encourages and supervises other international championships and competitions that include ISSF recognized events, upon request of the Organizers;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.4 Recognizes shooting sport disciplines and events;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.5  Supports the efforts of Member Federations to further develop the shooting sport in their respective country/ies;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.6  Grants support to Member Federations and individual athletes whose performances in international shooting competitions particularly contributed to the achievement of the Federation’s purposes;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.7 Establishes official Rankings;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.8 Issues Regulations and Rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.9 Licences Judges and Coaches;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.10 Develops and promotes methods and programmes of education;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.11 Researches scientific and medical principles;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.12 Publishes official communications;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.13  Awards distinctions to those who have contributed to the achievement of the Federation’s purposes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.2 ISSF HEADQUARTERS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.2.1  The ISSF Headquarters is located in Munich, Federal Republic of Germany.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.2.2  The ISSF must be registered under the laws of the country in which the Headquarters is located.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.2.3  Any change in the location of the Headquarters must be approved by the General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3 MEMBERSHIP

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.1  The ISSF must be composed of those National Shooting Organizations that are members of their National Olympic Committees and recognized by the EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 9 respective National Olympic Committee (NOC) as the sole governing body of the shooting sport related to ISSF recognized events in the country.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.2  The (NOC) of the country must be recognized by the International Olympic Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.3  Membership is open to one Member Federation from each country or territory which is governed by a NOC recognized by the IOC.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.4  Countries with two Member Federations recognized prior to 1989 may retain dual membership if both of the Member Federations are members of their (NOC) according to Article 1.3.1.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.5  Member Federations must not belong to other International Shooting Associations which include events defined in the ISSF Regulations and must not participate in the championships of such International Shooting Associations, except when authorized by the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.6  Membership fees are due on January 1st of each year and must be paid within ninety (90) days.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.7  Membership may be full or associated. Unless the Constitution indicates otherwise, the term Member(s) comprises both Full Members and Associate Members. RIGHTS OF THE MEMBERS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.8.1  To submit proposals for consideration by ISSF Bodies including the General Assembly;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.8.2  To take part in the ISSF competitions with their athletes in accordance with the ISSF Regulations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.8.3  To submit applications for the organization of the World Championships and other ISSF recognized competitions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.8.4  To exercise all other rights granted to them by this Constitution and regulations and decisions made by the respective ISSF body. ADDITIONAL RIGHTS OF FULL MEMBERS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.9.1  To vote on any items in the General Assembly;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.9.2  To propose candidates for the election of any function within the ISSF bodies and committees. OBLIGATIONS OF THE MEMBERS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.10.1  To comply with this Constitution and Regulations as well as decisions made by the respective ISSF;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.10.2  To take part in the ISSF competitions with their athletes in accordance with the ISSF Rules and Regulations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.10.3  To meet the responsibility as Host Federation entrusted with the organization of the World Championships and other ISSF competitions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.10.4  To encourage shooting practice and participation in competitions in disciplines and events recognized by the ISSF;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.10.5  To regularly organize national shooting sport competitions in ISSF recognized events in Senior and Junior categories and provide the ISSF with the results upon request. 10 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF ADDITIONAL OBLIGATIONS OF FULL MEMBERS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.11.1  To pay the annual membership fee and any other financial obligations established by ISSF Rules and Regulations in due time;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.11.2  To take part with its athletes in at least two ISSF competitions per year, which includes Continental Championships, Continental Games and other international competitions organized by the Continental Confederations. REQUIREMENTS FOR MEMBERSHIP

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.1  Applicants for membership must submit all documents in the official working language English to the ISSF Headquarters:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.2  Details of their foundation and organization including a list of members of the statutory bodies of the applicant;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.3  A copy of their Constitution/Statutes and of the minutes of the last General Assembly;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.4  Certification of recognition and affiliation as required in 1.3.1.and 1.3.2;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.5  A copy of a registration certificate under the laws of the applicant’s country;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.6  A copy of their Anti-Doping Regulations which must be in conformity with the ISSF Anti-Doping Regulations and the World Anti-Doping Code;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.7  Copies of Result books of the national shooting sport competitions for Seniors and Juniors in the previous two years, or a link to results published on the applicant’s official website;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.8  A written declaration whereby the applicant undertakes to observe the ISSF Constitution and all regulations (including Code of Ethics) as well as to recognize decisions taken by the competent ISSF bodies. After affiliation to ISSF the Member Federation has the obligation to integrate the content of this declaration into a provision of the Member Federations’ Constitution/Statutes. The Council may therefore set an appropriate deadline for a Member Federation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.9  Associated Membership may be granted to a National Shooting Organization in case it is needed for this National Shooting Organization to be recognized by the respective NOC according to article 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 of this Constitution, or when it would allow the National Shooting Organization, that has applied for the ISSF Membership with all necessary documents, to participate in competitions and events supervised by the ISSF before a Full Membership is decided.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.12.10  In case an application for membership is denied by the Council, the decision may be appealed to the General Assembly. MEMBERSHIP STATUS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.13.1  Every two years (starting from 1st January 2022) or upon request the Executive Committee may review the fulfilment of the Membership requirements and obligations by the Member Federations with respect to their current Membership status and propose the Council to decide whether any Member Federation should be transferred to another Membership status.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.13.2  The Member under review will be invited to present its position to the Executive Committee and the Council. SUSPENSION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.14.1  A Member Federation may be temporarily suspended if, in the opinion of the Executive Committee, this Member Federation has committed a breach of this EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 11 Constitution or if such Member Federation does not meet the requirements for ISSF Membership anymore.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.14.2  A suspended Member Federation may not exercise its membership rights. The ISSF Executive Committee may allow athletes of a suspended Member to participate in ISSF Competitions under the ISSF Flag.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.14.3  Any suspension must be submitted to the Council within two months for consideration as to whether or not the Member Federation should be excluded, or the suspension lifted or continued.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.14.4  The Member Federation concerned will be invited to present its position to the Executive Committee and/or the Council, before any final decision on its suspension will be taken. EXCLUSION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.15.1  A Member Federation may be excluded by the Council if it seriously breaches this Constitution.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.15.2  The Member concerned will be invited to present its position to the Council.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.15.3  A Member Federation may be excluded by the Council, if it loses its status as the sole governing body of the shooting sport related to ISSF recognized events in the country.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.15.4  The exclusion must be supported by at least two-thirds of the valid votes cast. WITHDRAWAL OF MEMBERSHIP

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.16.1  Membership with ISSF may be withdrawn in writing to the Secretary General which must arrive at least by 31st October in order to be valid for the next year.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.16.2  The Secretary General will inform the Executive Committee which will confirm the withdrawal, as well as the date of validity, in writing.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4 ISSF BODIES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1  The ISSF conducts its work through the following bodies and individual positions:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1.1  General Assembly;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1.2  Council;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1.3  Executive Committee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1.4  President;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1.5  Vice-Presidents;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1.6  Secretary General;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1.7  Athletes Committee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1.8  Other Committees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1.9  Integrity, Ethics and Safeguarding Unit

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.2  While individual members of ISSF Bodies may bring knowledge, skill and expertise from the Member Federation from which they are drawn, they must perform their duties as a member of an ISSF Body in an impartial and independent manner, serving only in the interests of the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.3  All members of the ISSF Bodies must promote the interests of the ISSF and support the decisions taken by its bodies. 12 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.4  A person can only be elected or appointed to one position. Ex-officio positions remain unaffected by this provision.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.5  All persons elected to any ISSF Body serve on an honorary basis and without salary but can be reimbursed for expenses. The following election procedures apply to elections of members of ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.6  Bodies except the Athletes Committee:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.6.1  A candidate for election to any position in an ISSF Body must have the support of his/her Member Federation. The nomination must be submitted to the Secretary General in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the meeting in which the election takes place.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.6.2  All members of the Council, the Executive Committee, the ISSF President, Vice- Presidents as well as Committee Chairpersons are elected for a four-year term of office. Such mandate starts after the election during the General Assembly and ends before the new elections in the next General Assembly in the fourth year of the mandate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.6.3  All ISSF Body members may only serve twelve (12) consecutive years in the same elective position.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.6.4  The age limit for nomination of any candidate is seventy-five (75) years as of the date of the election.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.7  Members of any ISSF Body shall not take part in the deliberation of any matter or point of issue involving specifically the Member Federation which has nominated them as candidate and/or to which they are affiliated, if they changed to another Member Federation after being elected, or in any other case in which a conflict of interest exists.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5 DECISION MAKING

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5.1  Unless otherwise prescribed in this Constitution, a valid decision is taken within any of the aforementioned ISSF Bodies, if the request is supported by a simple majority of the valid votes cast. Abstentions shall not be counted. In the event of a tie, the chairperson of the ISSF Body in question shall have the casting vote.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5.2  Such decisions are taken by open vote unless a request for secret ballot is supported by at least one-third (1/3) of the members present within the corresponding ISSF Body.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5.3  Any decision shall come into force with immediate effect, unless otherwise decided.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5.4  Elections must be executed by secret ballot. In case the number of candidates is equal to the number of vacancies, the competent elective body of ISSF may decide to proceed otherwise and hold elections by open vote or by acclamation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5.5  In respect of elections to any of the aforementioned ISSF bodies, the candidate(s) shall be elected in the first ballot, if supported by a simple majority of the valid votes cast (i.e. more than half of the valid votes cast) in the order of received votes. If not enough candidates receive a simple majority, there shall be a second ballot executed. In the second ballot candidates shall be elected by relative majority. In the event of a relevant tie in one ballot, those candidates in question go for a further ballot in which the candidate with a simple majority of the valid votes cast is elected. If the tie is repeated, the chairperson responsible for the election in question shall determine the elected candidate by the drawing of lots. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 13

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5.6  Only ballots that contain votes for as many candidates or fewer as there are vacancies are valid. Ballots with incorrect names indicated, discriminating words or unclear declarations are considered as invalid.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5.7  The General Assembly may agree, by a simple majority of the valid votes cast to take decisions by electronic voting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6 GENERAL ASSEMBLY

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.1  The General Assembly is the supreme authority of the ISSF. It is either the ordinary General Assembly to be held every two years or an extraordinary General Assembly upon decision of the Council or a written request of at least one-third (1/3) of the Member Federations having voting rights.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.2  The General Assembly consists of:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.2.1  The ISSF Member Federation represented by a maximum of two (2) delegates per Member Federation. If two Member Federations represent one country, only one (1) delegate per Member Federation is admissible; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.2.2  Members of the Council, the Executive Committee, and the Secretary General have consultative powers only (no voting right), unless they officially represent a Member Federation at a General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.3  Only the President, the Vice-President, the Secretary General, the Executive Director or Executive Committee/Board members can represent their Member Federation at the General Assembly. Participation forms for delegates must reach the Secretary General at least seven (7) working days prior to the opening of the General Assembly. All delegates representing the Member Federations must provide documented proof of their appointment as a delegate of that Member Federation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.4  Each Member Federation that represents one country has two (2) votes. Member Federations that represent one (1) country together with a second Member Federation, have one (1) vote each. Representation of members by proxy is not allowed. The ISSF shall cover the expenses for one delegate per Member Federation to attend the General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.5  The ordinary or extraordinary General Assembly is chaired by the President.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.6  After the official opening of the ordinary or extraordinary General Assembly, the Secretary General must conduct the roll call of voting powers, establish the voting list and announce the total number of eligible votes to the General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7  The General Assembly has the powers assigned to it by the Constitution, in particular to:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.1  Elect Scrutinizers for General Assembly votes and elections;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.2  Approve the agenda;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.3  Appoint the minutes committee on proposal of the Executive Committee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.4  Approve reports;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.5  Receive and approve the Auditors’ report;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.6 Approve the final balances and the financial report;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.7  Discharge the President and the Executive Committee of liability for their acts in fulfilling their role as ISSF bodies; 14 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.8  Handle requests of Member Federations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.9  Adopt and modify the Constitution;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.10  Elect ISSF’s President, the Vice- Presidents, five (5) members of the Executive Committee, and the Chairpersons of the Committees with the exception of the Chairperson of the Athletes Committee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.11  Grant the title of “Honorary Member” and “President of Honour” on proposal by the Executive Committee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.12  Approve the membership fee; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.7.13  Declare the dissolution of the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.8  The ordinary General Assembly meets once every two (2) years in a place chosen by the Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.9  The agenda is prepared by the Secretary General and approved by the Executive Committee. Member Federations may forward their own proposals for the agenda to the Secretary General in writing in English and with a short explanation as well as any supporting documents no later than ninety (90) days prior to the opening of the General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.10  The date, time and place for the General Assembly is determined by the Executive Committee and notice must be given to the Member Federations at least one-hundred and twenty (120) days in advance. The final agenda with the supporting documents must be sent to the Member Federations and the Council at least sixty (60) days prior to the date of the General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.11  Decisions by the ordinary or extraordinary General Assembly are restricted to items on the final agenda. Items, excluding amendments to this Constitution, may be added to the agenda by the Council upon approval by a two-third (2/3) majority vote in the General Assembly. However, during the meeting no new item may be added on to the agenda, except when unanimously agreed by all Member Federations present.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.12  An extraordinary General Assembly shall be held within six (6) months of receipt of a valid written request by the Secretary General. The Executive Committee shall decide on the date, time and place of the extraordinary General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.13  To take valid decisions, the ordinary or extraordinary General Assembly must have at least a quorum of presence of one-third of its Member Federations with the right to vote.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6.14  The minutes of the General Assembly shall be sent to the Member Federations promptly after approval by the Council in its first meeting following the General Assembly excluding the Council meeting dedicated to the elections of the Committee members on the next day after the General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7 COUNCIL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.1  The Council may hold ordinary or extraordinary meetings.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.2  The Council consists of the following members, representing both the male and the female gender (minimum 4 per male and female gender, respectively):

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.2.1  The Executive Committee members;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.2.2  The Chairpersons of the following Committees (2): Statutes and Eligibility, Medical,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.2.3  Representatives of the Continental Confederation according to Article 1.24.7. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 15

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.3  The Council has the powers assigned to it under this Constitution and other Regulations and Rules, in particular the following:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.3.1  To establish or amend Regulations and Rules upon recommendation by the Executive Committee or any other Committee to the extent such competence has not been assigned to the General Assembly or the Executive Committee according to this Constitution. This includes in particular the competence to amend, create and approve: a) General Regulations, b) Anti-Doping Rules, c) Code of Ethics, d) Eligibility Rules; e) Disciplinary Regulations f) Safeguarding Regulations

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.3.2  To appoint replacements in case a vacancy in any of the ISSF bodies occurs; any replacement shall serve for the remaining term of office;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.3.3  To elect members of the Committees for a two-(2)-year term with the exception of the members of the Athletes Committee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.3.4  To approve minutes of the General Assembly;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.3.5  On proposal from an Ad-Hoc Awards Committee, to approve award distinctions for outstanding service;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.3.6  To acknowledge Committee reports.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.3.7  To decide on Membership matters; Council meetings:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.4.1  The ordinary Council meeting is held once a year upon proposal of the President. Members must be informed at least sixty (60) days prior to the meeting about the date, time and place of the meeting as well as of the draft agenda prepared by the Secretary General. Any Council member may forward their own proposals for the agenda in writing in English and with a short explanation as well as any supporting documents no later than forty (40) days prior to the Council meeting to the Secretary General. The final agenda (including all supporting documents) must be submitted to the Council members no later than thirty (30) days prior to the meeting by the Secretary General.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.4.2  The Council shall meet online if requested by the Executive Committee. For online meetings, the Council may decide on diverting provisions with regards to the time limits as set out in Article 1.7.4.1 of this Constitution.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.5  At any meeting, the Council may take decisions when more than half (1/2) of its members are present. Proxy voting is not allowed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.6  For urgent matters, as decided by the President and/or Secretary General, the decisions may be taken by postal or electronic vote with a two-third (2/3) majority of the members who take part in the voting by casting their votes. The quorum of such vote must be 1/2 of the members. Such decisions are put into the minutes of the next Council meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.7.7  Upon proposal of the Executive Committee, the Council may suspend or expel a member of the Executive Committee, the Council or a Committee as well as 16 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF any official or athlete, if such a member, official or athlete seriously violates this Constitution, Regulations, the ISSF Code of Ethics or decisions of the ISSF. A majority of three-fourths (3/4) of the members who cast votes is required to suspend or expel such a member. The quorum of such vote must be 1/2 of the members.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8 EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.1  The Executive Committee consists of the following members:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.1.1  The ISSF President (1);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.1.2  Four Vice- Presidents (4); elected by the General Assembly represented by both male and female gender:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.1.3  The Chairperson of the Technical Committee and the Chairperson of the Athletes Committees (2);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.1.4  Five (5) representatives of the Continental Confederations (one from each Continent) according to Article 1.24.7;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.1.5  Five (5) ordinary members elected by the General Assembly representing both male and female gender.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2  The Executive Committee has the powers assigned to it under this Constitution and other Regulations and decisions by the General Assembly or Council, in particular the following:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.1  To ensure that decisions of the General Assembly and the Council are put into effect;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.2  To appoint and dismiss the Secretary General on proposal of the President;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.3  To discharge the Secretary General of liability for his/her acts as Secretary General on a yearly basis;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.4  To appoint the ISSF Treasurer from the members of the Executive Committee with the responsibility to manage the financial assets of the ISSF;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.5  To appoint an additional member to the Executive Committee representing the Member Federation of the host of the next Olympic Games on proposal of this Member Federation for the term of the Olympic Cycle as well as to dismiss the member. For the purposes of this provision, Olympic Cycle means the period commencing on the day after the closing ceremony of the Summer Olympic Games until the closing ceremony of the succeeding Summer Olympic Games. Upon beginning of the new Olympic Cycle, the new member to the Executive Committee shall be appointed in the first meeting of the Executive Committee of that Olympic Cycle;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.6 To amend, create and approve:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Technical Rules for shooting events,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Events that are recognized by the ISSF,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Commercial Rights and Sponsorship Rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) To adopt guidelines and procedures for ISSF bodies in line with this Constitution and the ISSF Regulations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.7  To designate a review committee to examine proposals to the General Assembly;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.8  To decide the hosts of the ISSF supervised competitions, including the ISSF EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 17 World Championships and to decide on the substitution of a Member Federation as the host of an ISSF Championship in the case that the selected host is unable to fulfil its duties;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.9  To designate delegates, representatives and juries for ISSF competitions and the Olympic Games;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.10  To decide on the dates, time and place of the ISSF General Assemblies;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.11  To decide about the design and use of the ISSF logos and emblems;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.12  To approve yearly preliminary budgets and balances;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.13  To establish, the “Regulations for the Participation in the Shooting Events of the Olympic Games” to be submitted to the IOC for approval;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.14  To provisionally accept applicants for associated membership;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.15  To temporarily suspend a Member Federation, if such Member Federation does not meet the requirements for ISSF membership anymore, or in case such Member Federation has violated this Constitution or any other ISSF Rules or Regulations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.16  To set up ad-hoc Committees and Commissions for a limited period of time and/ or for specific tasks and to determine the number of its members;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.17  To act on matters not assigned either to the General Assembly or the Council;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.2.18  To have the power to decide on all matters not covered in this Constitution. Such decisions are to be made in accordance with the relevant IOC Regulations. If no such regulations exist, the Executive Committee shall decide according to their duty to act fairly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.3  Executive Committee meetings:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.3.1  The Executive Committee will hold meetings at least twice a year. Executive Committee Members must be informed at least sixty (60) days prior to the meetings about date, time and place of the meeting as well as the draft agenda as approved by the President and elaborated by the Secretary General. Any Executive Committee member may forward their own proposals for the agenda in writing in English and with a short explanation as well as any supporting documents no later than forty (40) days prior to the meeting to the Secretary General. The final agenda (including all supporting documents) must be submitted to the Executive Committee members no later than thirty (30) days prior to the meeting by the Secretary General.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.3.2  The Executive Committee shall meet online if requested by the President. For online meetings, the Executive Committee may decide on diverting provisions with regards to the time limits as set out Article 1.8.3.1 in this Constitution.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.4  At any meeting, the Executive Committee may take decisions when more than half (1/2) of its members are present. Proxy voting is not allowed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.8.5  For urgent matters, decisions may be taken by postal or electronic vote with a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the valid votes cast. The quorum of such vote must be 1/2 of the members. Such decisions are put into the minutes of the next Executive Committee meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9 PRESIDENT

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1  The President of the ISSF:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.1  Provides leadership and direction to the ISSF; 18 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.2  Represents the ISSF and presides over all its activities;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.3  Represents the ISSF in international sports organizations and in all legal matters with the right for single representation of the ISSF;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.4  Acts on behalf of the ISSF as circumstances require;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.5. Chairs the meetings of the General Assembly, of the Council as well as of the Executive Committee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.6  Ensures the proper observance of the Constitution and ISSF Regulations, Rules as well as the decisions taken under them;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.7  Supervises the execution of decisions and activities of ISSF Bodies;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.8  Ensures that the decisions taken by the Executive Committee are put into effect;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.9  To propose the appointment and dismissal of the Secretary General to the Executive Committee

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.10  Ensures that ISSF’s obligations towards its Member Federations are fulfilled;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.9.1.11  Performs special assignments on request of the Executive Committee or Council.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.10 VICE PRESIDENTS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.10.1  The ISSF has four (4) Vice Presidents elected by the General Assembly represented by both male and female gender.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.10.2  The Vice Presidents:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.10.2.1  Support and assist the President and carry out duties assigned by the Council, the Executive Committee, or the President;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.10.2.2  A Vice President may be appointed by the President to convene and chair the General Assembly, the Council or the Executive Committee meetings;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.10.2.3  In case no such appointment has been made, the Vice President appointed by the Executive Committee replaces the President when he cannot anymore execute his duties due to an accident, illness, etc.; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.10.2.4  When present at any ISSF Championship or activity, a Vice President is the highest ISSF representative and authority after the President.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11 SECRETARY GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.1  The Secretary General is the head of administration of the ISSF, supervising all tasks performed at the ISSF Headquarters.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.2  The Secretary General has the powers assigned to him by this Constitution, other Regulations and in particular the following:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.2.1  Represents the ISSF in all legal matters with a single representation of the ISSF;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.2.2  Supervises and coordinates administrative services and activities, including overseeing all ISSF competitions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.2.3  Ensures the implementation, documentation and archiving of all decisions taken by the General Assembly, the Council and the Executive Committee as well as the Committees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.2.4  Reports on the activities of ISSF Headquarters at each meeting of the General Assembly, the Council and of the Executive Committee; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 19

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.2.5  Appoints and dismisses the staff working in the ISSF Headquarters;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.2.6  Attends meetings of the General Assembly, the Council, the Executive Committee as well as the Committees with voice but without vote;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.2.7  Fulfils ISSF administrative responsibilities that include conducting ISSF correspondence, preparing circular letters and reports and mailing summons to meetings;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.2.8  Performs special assignments on request of the Council, of the Executive Committee, or the President.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.11.3  The Secretary General shall receive an appropriate salary for his services.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12 ISSF COMMITTEES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1  The ISSF has the following Committees with its number of members in addition to the Chairperson:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.1  The Technical Committee (12 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.2  The Athletes Committee (9 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.3  The Rifle Committee (7 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.4  The Pistol Committee (7 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.5  The Shotgun Committee (7 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.6  The Moving Target Committee (7 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.7  The Target Sprint Committee (5 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.8  The Judges Committee (7 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.9  The Coaches Committee (7 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.10  The Statutes and Eligibility Committee (7 members),

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.11  The Medical Committee (at least 7 members), and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.1.13  The E-Sports, E-Games and Technological Innovations Committee (5 Members)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.2  The male gender and female gender must be represented in all Committees by at least two members, respectively.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.3  Members of the Committees may act as judges for ISSF Championships Juries, if the Executive Committee assigns them to do so and if they hold the appropriate licence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.4  The Committees act as advisory bodies within the ISSF. They shall assist, support and advise ISSF Bodies with respect to all matters assigned to them according to the provisions below. The ISSF Bodies shall obtain recommendations from the Committee competent to the relevant matter.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.5  The Executive Committee approves the Terms of References for each Committee. In such provisions, they may also define the decision-making power of such a Committee in writing and without affecting the powers of the General Assembly, the Council as well as the Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.5.1  Membership in the Committees is personal and representation by proxy is not permitted. While Committee members bring knowledge, skill, and expertise from the National Federations from which they are drawn, they must act in an impartial and independent manner, serving only in the interests of ISSF. 20 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.5.2  The Chairpersons and the Members of the Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun, Moving Target, Target Sprint and E-Sports, E-Games & Technological Innovations Committee should have the necessary knowledge and experiences of their respective discipline.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.5.3  The Chairpersons and the Members of the Judges Committee must be holders of a current Judges Licence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.5.4  The Chairpersons of the Judges, Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun, Moving Target and Target Sprint Committees are ex officio members of the Technical Committee.

chunks.text: 1.12.6  The Chairpersons of the Committees:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.6.1  Shall report concerning Committee meetings and activities in the next meeting of the Council;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.6.2  May advise ISSF bodies in urgent matters without a meeting of the members of the respective Committee. In such cases, the Chairpersons shall inform their Committee members about the advice given; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.6.3  Shall designate a recording secretary for each meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

The agenda as well as all supporting documents should be sent to the participants at least thirty (30) days prior to the meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.8  At any meeting, a Committee may take decisions when more than half (1/2) of its members are present. Proxy voting is not allowed. The Chairperson will cast the deciding vote in case of a tied vote.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.9  Minutes of Committee meetings are for internal ISSF use only and may not be published or distributed without the approval of the Secretary General.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.12.10  Minutes of Committee meetings must be sent to the Secretary General who forwards them to the Council.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.13 TECHNICAL COMMITTEE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.13.1  The Technical Committee shall:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.13.1.3  Coordinate and review proposals from the Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun, Moving Target and Target Sprint Committees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.text: 1.14 ATHLETES COMMITTEE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.1  The Athletes Committee consists of 10 (ten) members comprising the Chairperson and nine (9) members of which three (3) are from shotgun, three (3) EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 21 from rifle and three (3) from pistol. Six (6) members are elected by the athletes (two (2) of each discipline). Three (3) members are appointed by the Executive Committee (one (1) of each discipline) considering the representation of the Continental Confederations pursuant to Article 1.14.3 and the number of votes received by the athletes. The Chairperson shall be elected by and from among the nine (9) members of the Athletes Committee. After the election of the Chairperson the athlete with the highest number of votes corresponding to the Chairperson’s discipline shall be adapted as tenth (10th) member of the Athletes Committee. Further details on the electoral rules shall be set out in the procedural regulations concerning the Athletes Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.2  The Athletes Committee must have at least four male members and four female members, respectively, as they are registered in the ISSF Athletes registration domain.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.3  The Athletes Committee shall consist of at least one athlete from Member Federations of every Continental Confederation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.4  The Athletes Committee’s duties include:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.4.1  Gathering information and opinions from athletes on their needs and problems with regard to the Olympic Games and major ISSF Competitions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.4.2  Consulting with athletes in the evaluation of the rules and regulations of the shooting sports and subsequently provide feedback to the ISSF;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.4.3  Establishing contacts and coordinating activities with the Athlete Committees of the IOC, NOCs, Continental and National Federations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.4.4  Participating in working groups, to ensure the best possible conditions for the training, accommodation and living conditions for the athletes as well as for the conduct of the ISSF competitions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.4.5  Engaging with the Integrity, Ethics and Safeguarding Unit when necessary and participating in any initiative which promotes the safeguarding of all athletes and shooting sport activities, both in competition and out of competition, which should all be free from harassment and abuse;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.4.6  Engaging actively with initiatives and projects that protect and support clean athletes on and off the field of play;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.4.7  Establishing a direct link between athletes within the ISSF;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.4.8  Reporting through its Chairperson to the Executive Committee and Council concerning its meetings and activities.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.5  The Council will establish further election and other procedural regulations for the Athletes Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.6  A representative member of the Athletes Committee may attend meetings of other ISSF Committees with voice but without vote.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.14.7  The provisions established for the Committees also apply to the Athletes Committee

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.21.1.4  Promote the development of e-sports and e-games in connection to shooting sport.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.text: 1.24 CONTINENTAL CONFEDERATIONS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.1 The purpose of the Continental Confederations is to maintain, to strengthen and to develop the sport of shooting in accordance with the Constitution and the Regulations of the ISSF and to strengthen the bonds of friendship and good relations among the Member Federations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.2 ISSF recognizes the Continental Confederations which are composed of National Federations belonging in principle to same territory of a Continent.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.3 Each Federation may only belong to one single Confederation. A change of Confederation is subject to the approval of the parties involved including the ISSF Council.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.4 The relationship between ISSF and the Confederation is regulated by specific ISSF Regulations or by contract.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.5 ISSF recognizes the following five Continental Confederations: - African Shooting Sport Federation (ASSF) - Shooting Confederation of the Americans (CAT) - Asian Shooting Confederation (ASC) - European Shooting Confederation (ESC) - Oceania Shooting Confederation (OSC)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.6 The objectives of the Continental Confederations are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.6.1 To promote the shooting sport within its territory in a spirit of peace, understanding and fair play, without any discrimination on account of politics, gender, religion, race or any other reason;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.6.2 To maintain good relations with and cooperate with the ISSF for the promotion and development of the shooting sport;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.6.3 To organize Continental Championships on regular basis;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.6.4 To organize ISSF competitions in agreement with the ISSF Executive Committee; To encourage the promotion of traditional Regional Championships and other major shooting competitions within the Continent;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.6.5 To maintain relations between the National Member Federations in order to promote the development of shooting sport within the Continent; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 25

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.6.6 To promote the exchange of experience by organizing lectures, debates, conferences or courses in close collaboration and in line with the ISSF policies;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.6.7 To participate in realization of the ISSF development and educational programmes;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.6.8 To promote the knowledge of the shooting sport through mass media.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.7 The Continental Confederations must be represented in the ISSF Executive Committee and in the Council according to the following formula which determines the respective number of continental representatives for the electoral term:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.7.1 Continental Confederation with up to 15 ISSF Member Federations – 1 Executive Committee member

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.7.2 Continental Confederations with 16-25 ISSF Member Federations – 1 Executive Committee member and 1 Council member

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.7.3 Continental Confederations with 26-35 ISSF Member Federations – 1 Executive Committee member and 2 Council members

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.7.4 Continental Confederations with 36-45 ISSF Member Federations – 1 Executive Committee member and 3 Council members

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.7.5 Continental Confederations with 46 and more ISSF Member Federations – 1 Executive Committee member and 4 Council Members

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.8  All representatives of the Continental Confederations in the Executive Committee and Council must be associated with different ISSF Member Federations and be elected by respective statutory bodies of the respective Continental Confederation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.9  Both genders must represent a Continental Confederation in the Council in case it may have more than two members in the Council.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.10  The respective statutory body of a Continental Confederation may substitute its representative in the ISSF Executive Committee and the Council at any time but only once for the remaining term of office of the Executive Committee and the Council.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.24.11  The Continental Confederations must submit reports on their activities to each meeting of the Council.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.text: 1.26 FINANCIAL POLICY

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.26.1 The financial year runs from January 1st to December 31st.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.26.2 The yearly Preliminary Budgets and Balances must be approved by the Executive Committee upon proposal of the Secretary General.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.26.3 In each meeting of the Executive Committee, the Secretary General must report on the financial status of the ISSF. 26 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.27 LANGUAGES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.27.1 The following seven languages are recognized as the official languages of the ISSF during meetings: English, French, German, Russian, Spanish, Chinese and Arabic. The Executive Committee may permit the use of other languages in the meetings and the General Assemblies.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.27.2 However, English is the permanent working language in which the Constitution, the regulations, rules and minutes as well as legal or official communications must be provided and published. The resolution of disputes must be conducted in the English language. The matters to be proposed for discussions at the General Assemblies must be sent by the Member Federations to the President or the Secretary General in the English language only.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.27.3 In World and Continental Championships, the language of the host country may be used in the programme, instructions, announcements, etc. in addition to English.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.27.4 Simultaneous translation into English, French and Spanish must be provided at General Assemblies. Simultaneous translation into Russian, German, Chinese and Arabic may be also provided at the General Assemblies upon request at least ninety (90) days before the General Assembly of at least five (5) Member Federations. The Organizing Committee of the General Assemblies may add any language for simultaneous translation at their own cost.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.27.5 In the case of disagreement in the interpretation of documents, the English text shall prevail.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.28 RESOLUTION OF DISPUTES Any final decision rendered by the ISSF may be submitted exclusively to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in Lausanne, Switzerland, which will resolve the dispute definitively in accordance with the Code of sports-related arbitration. The language of the proceedings shall be English. The time limit for the appeal to be filed is twenty-one days after the reception of the decision concerning the appeal. Any decision taken by CAS will be final and binding on all parties concerned.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.29 ALTERATION OF THE CONSTITUTION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.29.1 Proposals must be submitted to the Secretary General at least three (3) months before the General Assembly and distributed to the Member Federations and Council at least two (2) months before the General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.29.2. The General Assembly may only adopt changes in the Constitution if at least half of all Member Federations with voting rights are present. In order to be valid, any change needs at least the support of two-thirds (2/3) of the valid votes cast.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.30 DISSOLUTION OF THE FEDERATION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.30.1 A demand for dissolution of the Federation must be received six (6) months before the General Assembly and mailed to all Member Federations and the Council five (5) months before the General Assembly.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.30.2 The dissolution of the Federation must be approved by a three- quarters (3/4) majority in the General Assembly at which at least half (1/2) of all Member Federations with voting rights are represented. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 27

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.31 REGISTRATION OF THE FEDERATION ACCORDING TO ARTICLES 2.2

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.31.1 The Federation has its Headquarters in Munich, Germany, and is legally registered under the name: “International Shooting Sport Federation, registered society (ISSF)” (Internationaler Schiess- Sportverband, eingetragener Verein, ISSF) by the Amtsgericht Muenchen, Registergericht VR 10152.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.31.2 The Federation observes, exclusively and without reservation, beneficial purposes according to the section “Tax aid and abet” of the Tax laws of Germany. It acts selflessly and observes primarily non-profit making purposes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.31.3 Funds of the Federation may only be used for constitutional purposes. Members receive no financial gain from the Federation. No person must be privileged by expenditures which are contrary to the purposes of the Federation or by disproportionately high compensations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.31.4 In case of dissolution of the Federation or suspension of the tax exception by the German Government, any remaining assets must be given to the National Olympic Committee with the injunction for exclusive use for beneficial purposes for the international shooting sport.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.31.5 Alterations to this Constitution and dissolution of the Federation must be reported to the Finance Office of the place of registry.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.34.1 All decisions taken according to the previous version of the Constitution will stay effective until they are realized or changed. All persons elected to any ISSF Body before this version of the Constitution became effective must complete their term of office. All amendments decided in the General Assembly on November 30th, 2024 in Rome, ITA, shall become effective immediately, except indicated otherwise and except all changes in respect to the composition of ISSF Bodies which shall become effective for and as of the first elections after 30th November 2024.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.text: 2.1 STATEMENT OF PRINCIPLE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.1 Every person elected to a position in any ISSF body serves solely in the interest of, and is responsible to the Federation. In performing his responsibilities he must ensure that all provisions of the Constitution, General Regulations and other rules of the ISSF will therefore be given priority in all decisions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.2 All persons elected or appointed to the ISSF serve on an honorary basis and without salary.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.3 By accepting election or appointment everyone agrees to devote the time necessary to accomplish the duties required by their position.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2 DESCRIPTION OF FUNCTIONS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2.1 President Objectives Successful leadership and direction of the ISSF ensuring a balanced promotion of all sections and activities of the amateur shooting sport and also observing the needs of tradition and development. Principal Duties and Responsibilities Convenes and presides over Assemblies and meetings according to the Constitution. Supervises the execution of decisions; activities of ISSF bodies; ensures the proper observance of the Constitution, General Regulations and other rules. Ensures that the ISSF obligations to Member Federations, Continental Confederations, Organizing Committees and International or National Sport Organizations are fulfilled. Represents the ISSF in legal matters in conjunction with the Secretary General. Acts on behalf of, or represents, the ISSF, as circumstances require. Authority Acts as Chairperson of the General Assembly, the Council and the Executive Committee. Acts in urgent cases on matters not provided for in the Constitution or General Regulations. Such actions, however, require subsequent approval by the

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: Council or Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2.2 Vice Presidents Objectives Support and assist the President in leading and directing the ISSF. Principal Duties and Responsibilities As delegated by the President, convene and preside at ISSF meetings in the President’s absence or at his request. Carry out duties assigned by the Council or Executive Committee or as requested by the President. Perform special assignments or assist and supervise specific parts of ISSF activities on a permanent basis on request of the Executive Committee or the President. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 31 Authority Act on behalf of the President in his absence or on his request.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2.3 Secretary General Objectives Operates the Headquarters for efficient conduct of all ISSF business. Principal Duties and Responsibilities Represents the ISSF in legal matters together with the President. Acts as ISSF Treasurer. Represents the President at his request. As set-out in 1.11.2.6 the Secretary General can attend meetings of all Committees but does not have a vote, this includes the Executive Committee. Performs duties defined in description of Headquarters operations. Authority Full authority over all ISSF employees. For further details see description of Headquarters operations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2.4 Members of the Committees Objectives Assistance, support and advice to the Council and the Executive Committee in all matters assigned to them. Principal Duties and Responsibilities All Committees of the ISSF shall deal with all matters within their field of interest as an advisory body and shall be responsible for the technical and other activities assigned to them by the Constitution or the Council and the Executive Committee. All members of the Committees act and vote as independent members and not as representatives of their National Federations. Each Chairperson must designate his substitute in the event of his absence, and a Recording Secretary for each meeting. Authority Each Chairperson represents his Committee in the Council. The Committee Chairperson may act on behalf of his Committee in urgent cases, and on request of the President, Secretary General, the Council, or the Executive Committee. He must inform his Committee members of any action taken.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.3.1 Frequency The ISSF Committees meet as stated in the Constitution, on request of the President, Secretary General, the Council, or the Executive Committee, or on request by a Committee Chairperson. 32 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF If possible, meetings shall be scheduled in conjunction with World Championships or other important shooting sport events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.3.2 Notices Notices for Committee meetings will be sent by the Secretary General. For this purpose, the Chairperson must submit the agenda, documents and any other information for the meeting early enough to permit mailing of the notices at least two (2) months in advance of the meeting date.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.3.3 Recording Secretary The Chairperson must appoint a Recording Secretary for each meeting. The Recording Secretary will prepare minutes, which must be signed by the Chairperson after agreement by the members who attended. The minutes must be submitted to the Secretary General within two (2) months of the meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.3.5 Quorum and Voting Procedure A quorum in Committee meetings is 50 % of the members (including the Chairperson), unless otherwise stated in the Constitution. Proxy voting is not permitted. Each member of the Committee has one (1) vote. The Chairperson in the case of a tie, shall cast the deciding vote. All decisions are taken by open ballot, except when a secret vote is requested by 50 % or more of the members present. A postal vote may be conducted in the interval between meetings. When a postal vote is required, the Chairperson must send to each member (and a copy to the ISSF Headquarters) a clear statement of the question to be voted upon, with a request that each member must return his vote before a stated date. Within eight (8) days of closing the postal vote, the Chairperson must send a report and the result of the vote to the ISSF Headquarters. A non-response will be taken to signify an affirmative vote.

chunks.text: 2.5 ISSF HEADQUARTERS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5.1 The ISSF Headquarters, under direction of the Secretary General, conducts the business of the ISSF. Correspondence, preparation of circular letters and reports, preparation and mailing of summons to meetings are, among others, the duties of the Headquarters.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5.2 All work, communications and decisions arising from the Constitution or action by the General Assembly, the Council and the Executive Committee is carried out as a matter of course by the Headquarters under supervision of the Executive Committee. The Secretary General is directly responsible to the President for operation of the Headquarters.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5.3 All affairs related to finances such as accounting and ISSF budget preparation are performed by the ISSF Headquarters. The President of the ISSF is kept currently informed as to the state of affairs and must give his approval on all important matters. A short financial report is presented at each meeting to the Council and the Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5.4 The President, Council Members and Executive Committee Members will all receive a copy of documents concerning any matter of special importance.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5.5 The Secretary General is the employer of all who work in the Headquarters of the ISSF. This will be in conformity with the labour laws in effect at the headquarters of the ISSF, with regard to all related matters. The Executive Committee and the Council will be informed of all current important personnel matters at their next meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5.6 The Secretary General will work independently, within the limits of his authority. In his capacity as Secretary General, and as a member of the Executive Committee, he has the right and duty at all times to coordinate the work of the various ISSF bodies. He is responsible for covering the financial obligations of the ISSF while remaining within the budget. The direction of the transactions and entering into contracts with other organizations, sporting or otherwise, commercial firms, etc. are within the usual authority of the Secretary General; however, the President and the ISSF bodies concerned must be made aware of all such transactions or contracts. 34 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 3 GENERAL REGULATIONS EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 35

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1.1  The General Regulations of the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) govern shooting sport competitions (Championships) according to Articles

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1.4.1, 1.1.4.8 and 1.1.4.9 ISSF Constitution.
