chunks.text: 3.2 ISSF CHAMPIONSHIPS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.1  ISSF Championships are divided in three categories concerning the requirements for Organizers and the conditions that they have to fulfil: Those requirements are specified in the Guidelines for Organizing ISSF Championships (A separate Manual, available at the ISSF Headquarters). Level 1 - World Championships - World Championships Rifle/Pistol - World Championships Shotgun - Final Tournament of the Year - World Cups with Olympic Quota Places allocation - Continental Championships/Continental Games with Olympic Quota Places allocation Level 2 - World Cups - World Championships Moving Target - World Championships Juniors - Youth Olympic Games Qualifying competitions - Continental Championships Level 3 - Grand Prix tournaments - Other competitions organized according to the ISSF Rules and Regulations

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.2  The ISSF Championships are organized by Member Federations that are chosen by the Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.3 World Championships

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.3.1  World Championships for all events must be organized every four years, two years after the Olympic Games. In other years, with the exception of the year in which the Olympic Games take place, separate World Championships for Shotgun as well as Rifle and Pistol events must be organized. World Championships Juniors for all events must be organized every two years in the year of the Olympic Games and the second year after the Olympic Games (even numbered years). Continental Championships should be organized at least every two (2) years as decided by the respective Continental Confederations. [As of 1 January 2025 (i.e., relevant for World Championships to be organized starting from the year 2025) the following provision applies]: EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 37

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.3.2  World Championships for all events among Men and Women must be organized every four years, two years after the Olympic Games. In other years, with the exception of the year in which the Olympic Games take place, separate World Championships for Shotgun as well as Rifle and Pistol events among Men and Women must be organized. World Championships Juniors for all events among Men Junior and Women Junior must be organized every two years in the year of the Olympic Games and the second year after the Olympic Games (even numbered years). In other years (uneven numbered years), separate World Championships Juniors for Shotgun as well as Rifle and Pistol events among Men Junior and Women Junior must be organized. Continental Championships should be organized at least every two (2) years as decided by the respective Continental Confederations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.4 Application for ISSF Championships A Member Federation desiring to organize an ISSF Championship must submit its application to the Secretary General at least one (1) month in advance of the Executive Committee meeting where the host federation will be chosen.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.4.1  The application should include:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) An official statement from the appropriate government agency and/ or National Olympic Committee, indicating the support to be given to the organization of the Championships;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A statement that all the requirements of the ISSF Constitution will be observed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) A statement that the organizing federation will invite all ISSF Member Federations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) A description of the existing or proposed shooting ranges and other necessary facilities that must meet ISSF requirements;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Information regarding the proposed organization, cost of accommodation, time of transportation to and from ranges, transportation fees for transfer airport – official hotel – airport and any training fees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) A statement listing the events the Federation proposes to include in the programme.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.5  If no application is received, or if the Federation selected to organize the World Championships withdraws, the Executive Committee must select another Federation to organize the World Championships. Or, if no single Federation can be found, select neighbouring Federations to organize the World Championships together in separate groups of events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.6  Withdrawal is only possible with the approval of the Executive Committee. Unapproved withdrawal is subject to the assessment of a fine, or the suspension of membership or the suspension of participation at ISSF Championships for a certain time to be decided by the Council.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3 ISSF EVENTS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.1  Events recognized by the ISSF in Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun, Moving Target and Target Sprint disciplines are: 38 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF Name of Event 10m Air Rifle 50m Rifle 3 Positions 50m Rifle Prone 300m Rifle 3 Positions 300m Rifle Prone 300m Standard Rifle 10m Air Pistol 25m Pistol 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol 25m Centre Fire Pistol 25m Standard Pistol 50m Pistol Trap Skeet 10m Moving Target 10m Moving Target Mixed 50m Moving Target 50m Moving Target Mixed Target Sprint

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.2  The ISSF recognizes individual, Mixed Team, Team and Open events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.2.1  Individual events are events in which individual athletes of the same gender compete against each other.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.2.2  Mixed Team events are for the Teams with two members, one of each gender.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.2.3  Team events are for Teams with three (3) members of the same gender. Only full Teams of three (3) athletes will be ranked in the Team results list.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.2.4  Open events are individual events with athletes of both genders competing together in one event.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.3  Formats of the ISSF recognized events must be approved by the Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.4  New events can be added to the list of ISSF recognized events after the following conditions have been met:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.4.1  the appropriate ISSF Committee develops rules for the event,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.4.2  the Executive Committee (Article 1.8.2.5 ISSF Constitution) approves the rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.5 Olympic Events (ISSF recognized events included in the programme of the Olympic Games by the IOC) Olympic Events are conducted in accordance with Rifle, Pistol and Shotgun Technical rules approved by the Executive Committee in accordance with Article 1.8.2.12 of the ISSF Constitution. Each Olympic event has a “Qualification” round and a “Final.” EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 39

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.6 Programme of the ISSF Championships

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.6.1  The programme of the ISSF Championships is composed of the ISSF recognized events and must be approved by the Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.6.2  The mandatory events of the respective ISSF Championship programme are determined by the Executive Committee and additional events may be included upon proposal by the Organizers. The list of mandatory events approved by the Executive Committee can be found at the start of section 6 General Technical Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.6.3  If 300m Rifle events cannot be included, the Executive Committee should choose a national federation to organize a separate 300m Rifle World Championship in the same year as the World Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.6.4  If Moving Target events cannot be included, the Executive Committee should choose a national federation to organize a separate Moving Target World Championship in the same year as the World Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.6.5  In all ISSF Championships a “Qualification” round and the “Final” are conducted in the Olympic events in Individual, Mixed Team, and Team events that are part of the respective Championship’s programme.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3.7 Events included in the programme for a Continental Championship are decided by the Continental Confederation concerned, however they can only be ISSF recognised events that are listed as such in Rule 3.3.1 and must be submitted for approval to the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4 RANKING SYSTEM

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4.1  The ISSF establishes official Rankings for each ISSF event that determine the placing of athletes according to their achievements in the ISSF Championships during a designated time frame.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4.2  The ISSF Ranking system is established by the Executive Committee. The current ISSF Ranking system can be found on the ISSF website and is updated on a monthly basis.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5 ADMINISTRATION AND CONTROL OF THE ISSF CHAMPIONSHIPS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.1 General

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.1.1  After the host of the ISSF Championship is approved by the Executive Committee, the ISSF and the respective National Federation must sign the Host Federation Agreement (HFA) within 30 days after the approval.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.1.2  Every National Federation that earns the right to host the ISSF Championship must create an Organizing Committee responsible for administrating and delivering the Championship according to ISSF General Regulations, the HFA and the Guidelines for Organizing ISSF Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.1.3  The National Federation and the Organizing Committee must work in close cooperation with the ISSF Headquarters and the Technical Delegate/s.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.2 To coordinate the cooperation with Organizers of the ISSF Championships and to control the fulfilment of all the obligations for the preparations of the competitions by the Organizers, the ISSF Executive Committee appoints one (1) or two (2) Technical Delegates. 40 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.2.1  In order that the Technical Delegates can carry out these responsibilities, they must be invited at the expense of the Organising Committee to the site of the Championships at least once, 10 to 12 months before the Championship, and again, not less than three (3) days before the official arrival day.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.2.2  Technical Delegates must have experience of officiating at major ISSF Championships and shall not be members of the federation(s) hosting the respective ISSF Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.3  To control the fulfilment of the ISSF General Technical Rules during the competitions and to guarantee the objective outcome of official results and rankings, a Competition Jury must be appointed for all ISSF Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.3.1  Members of the Competition Jury must be approved by the Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.3.2  The Competition Jury must include judges with experience of officiating at major ISSF Championships in respective disciplines, result production and equipment control.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.3.3  The exact number of the Competition Jury members depends upon the level of the ISSF Championship, the competition schedule, and the existence of sufficient numbers of experienced range officers, supporting officials and referees provided by the Organizers.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.3.4  All members of the Competition Jury must have a valid respective ISSF Judges licence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.3.5  The Chairperson of the Competition Jury is personally responsible for the objective outcome of all results and rankings at the ISSF Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.3.6  Technical Delegates are authorized to create a Jury of Appeal, if necessary.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.3.7  The Jury of Appeal must consist of three (3) to five (5) members, including a Chairperson. One (1) member should be from the national federation organizing the Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.4  The travel expenses of the Technical Delegates (TD) is borne by the Organising Committee, TD’s have the right to a “Business Class” flight if the flight time exceeds 3 hours. Jury members and other ISSF appointed officials travel expenses are borne by the Organizing Committee up to a maximum of €1,500. A per diem of €50,00 per day is paid by the ISSF. The costs for accommodation of the Technical Delegates, Jury Members and the ISSF appointed officials or staff are borne by the Organizing Committee. The costs for the local transportation of the Technical Delegates, Jury Members and other ISSF appointed officials or staff are borne by the Organizing Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6.1.2  Upon any proposal of the Organizers and approval of the Executive Committee the number of Trap and Skeet ranges for Qualification can be lower than indicated in 6.4.1, but a Final Range must be provided.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6.2 Result Production

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6.2.1  The competitions venue must be equipped in accordance with the official ISSF General Technical Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6.2.2  Electronic target systems, of makers and models approved by the ISSF must be used for Rifle and Pistol events Qualification and Final stages at all ISSF Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6.2.3  The ISSF Technical Delegates are responsible for examining the ranges and other facilities to ensure that they meet ISSF standards and are suitable for conducting Championships. The Technical Committee will provide checklists in accordance with the ISSF Rules and Regulations for use by the Technical Delegates in examining the ranges and facilities (available from ISSF Headquarters).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6.2.4  Ranges to be used for World Championships should be completed one (1) year in advance. If the range is not completed, the detailed plans, construction schedule and financial plan must be submitted to the Secretary General one (1) year in advance, and the range must be completed three (3) months in advance.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7 PARTICIPATION AND ISSF ATHLETES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.1  Only ISSF Member Federations may participate in the ISSF Championships. Member Federations participating in Continental Championships and Continental Games must be members of the Continental Confederation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.2  An ISSF Member Federation that is not accepted as a member by its own Continental Confederation, or is not allowed to participate in its own Continental Championships, may be invited by another Continental 42 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF Confederation to participate in its Continental Championships and Continental Games with the right to awards and records.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.3  Team officials participating in ISSF Championships must abide by the ISSF Rules and Regulations

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4 ISSF Athletes

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.1  To participate in any of the ISSF Championships all athletes must obtain an ISSF ID Number and sign an “Athlete’s Declaration”.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.2  Any athlete must be a national of the country he/she represents.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.3  All disputes relating to the determination of the country which an athlete may represent shall be resolved by the ISSF Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.4  An athlete who is a national of two (2) or more countries at the same time may represent either one (1) of them, as he may select. However, after having represented one (1) country in the Olympic Games or in any ISSF Championships, he may not represent another country unless he meets the conditions set forth in paragraphs below that apply to persons who have changed their nationality or acquired a new nationality.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.5  An athlete who has represented one (1) country in the Olympic Games or in any ISSF Championship, and who has changed his nationality or acquired a new nationality, may participate in ISSF Championships to represent his new country provided that at least three (3) years have passed since the athlete last represented his former country. This period may be reduced or even cancelled, with the agreement of the Federations concerned and the ISSF Executive Committee, which takes into account the circumstances of each case.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.6  If an associated State, province or overseas department, a country or colony acquires independence, if a country becomes incorporated within another country by reason of a change of border, if a country merges with another country, or if a new NOC is recognized by the IOC, an athlete may continue to represent the country to which he belongs or belonged. However, he may, if he prefers, elect to represent his country or be entered in ISSF Championships by his new Federation when recognized by the ISSF. This particular choice may be made only once.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.7  Furthermore, in all cases in which an athlete would be eligible to participate in ISSF Championships, either by representing another country than his or by having the choice as to the country which such athlete intends to represent, the ISSF Executive Committee may take all decisions of a general or individual nature with regard to issues resulting from nationality, citizenship, domicile or residence of any athlete, including the duration of any waiting period.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.8  The period following naturalization may be reduced or even cancelled with the agreement of the two (2) National Federations concerned and the final approval of the ISSF Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.9  Once an athlete has participated with an ISSF ID number in an ISSF Championship, this ID will NEVER be changed. In case of a change of nationality, the data associated with the ISSF ID number must be corrected but the ID itself will not change.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.10  An official declaration of eligibility for each athlete will be required from the Member Federation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.11  Age of ISSF Athletes There is no age limit for participation in ISSF Championships. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 43

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.12 Juniors Athletes will remain as Juniors until the 31st December of the year in which they become 21 years of age. Any athlete born between the 1st January and the 31st December, will cease to be a Junior on the 31st December of that year. Juniors may participate in all ISSF Championships and the Olympic Games as members of their national team.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.13  The final ranking at the ISSF Championships can be established showing Juniors but an athlete can be part of the final ranking in one category only.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.14  Events for Juniors should be chosen from the recognized ISSF events, or be events designed to support the development of junior athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.4.15  Events for Juniors should be included in Continental Championships by decision of the Continental Confederation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5 The number of participants in the ISSF Championships

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.1  The number of participants from each nation is determined by the ISSF Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.2  In the World Championships each nation can enter a maximum of three (3) athletes in Individual events, two (2) Mixed Teams in respective Mixed Team events and one (1) Team in the respective Team events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.3  In the World Championships, each nation can enter a maximum of six (6) Junior athletes in Individual Events. A maximum of three (3) athletes of one nation (the three top ranked after Qualification) may proceed to the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.4  In the other ISSF Championships each nation can enter a maximum of five (5) athletes in individual events but only three (3) of them can be registered to compete in the Final for the medals. The other two (2) can only compete for the ranking points.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.5  Any of the athletes entered in an ISSF Championship can be registered for the Mixed Team and Team events while respecting the number of Mixed Teams and Teams allowed to be entered by one nation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.6  Replacements of the athletes may be made only in the Team events, but only from those already registered for this Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.7  When events for Juniors are scheduled in the World Championships, the number of athletes allowed per event is the same as in the World Championship Juniors.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.8  In World Championships, juniors may participate in the men’s and the women’s competitions, but in one (1) category only at the same Championships (place and dates).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.9  If there is no particular junior event in a Championship, juniors may participate in this event as a member of the national team, even if they participate in another junior event in the same Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.5.10  The participating federation is responsible for the travel and living expenses of team members. The Organizing Committee must provide transportation from the local airport or railway station to the official hotels and from the official hotels to the range. The cost for transfer from the airport(s) to the official hotels and back may be charged when approved by the Executive Committee of the ISSF. 44 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.text: 3.8 COMPETITION PROCEDURES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.1  The ISSF General Regulations and the applicable current ISSF General Technical Rules and respective rules for the disciplines will govern the conduct of events in all ISSF Championships. Programmes

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.2.1  The Preliminary Programme prepared by the Organizing Committee must be submitted by the Technical Delegate to the ISSF Secretary General for examination at least 8 months prior to the Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.2.2  The schedule for the mandatory events of the World Championships should not exceed sixteen (16) days. At the option of the Organizing Committee, the ranges may be opened for additional training days before official training begins.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.2.3  The Final Programme prepared by the Organizing Committee must be submitted by the Technical Delegate for approval by the ISSF Secretary General at least 6 months prior to the Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.2.4  The General Information letter prepared by the Organizing Committee must be distributed among the Member Federations upon approval by the Technical Delegate at least 5 months prior to the Championship. Entries

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.3.1  Preliminary Entries Each national federation entering the Championship must submit a preliminary entry to the Organizing Committee. The preliminary entry must list all individual, Mixed Team and Team events in which the national federation will participate. Preliminary entries must be received by the Organizing Committee at least thirty (30) days before the official arrival day. Any Preliminary entry sent after this date will be entered on a waiting list according to the date of the receipt of the entry and it may be that the participation is only possible if targets/places are available. The Organizing Committee must inform the Nations in question of any such change immediately after these entries are received.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.3.2  Final Entries Final Entries must be entered in the ISSF Online Registration System directly to the ISSF before midnight (Munich time) of the 30th day before the official arrival day. The final entry must list the names and ID Numbers of all athletes. The final entry must list the names and dates of birth of all officials with their function. All Final entries must be completed at least three (3) days before the official arrival day.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.3.3  Any additional entries received after the deadline of three (3) days before the official arrival day will be rejected by the ISSF Online Registration System and the athlete may not participate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.3.4  Replacement of a registered athlete by another already registered athlete for that Championship is permitted. This change can only be made before12:00 pm (noon) on the day before the Pre-Event Training for that event. Fees

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.4.1  Entry fees must be paid to the Organizing Committee upon request.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.4.2  The following Entry fees are applicable (amounts in Euro): EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 45

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) World Championships and World Cups: - Individual entry – 170; - Mixed Team – 170; - Team – 170; - Official – 50.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) World Championships Juniors: - Individual entry – 170; - Mixed Team – 170; - Team – 170; - Official – 50.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Grand Prix tournaments: - Individual entry – 170; - Mixed Team – 170; - Team – 170; - Official – 50.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.4.3  A reasonable fee for training that is not part of the Championship’s schedule may be charged when approved by the Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.4.4  Any federation reducing the number of athletes and / or officials after the Final Entry Deadline is obligated to pay all applicable fees and costs including entry fees according to the number of athletes and entries on the Final Entry Forms originally received. If the applicable fees and costs are not paid no member of that federation may participate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.4.5  Any entry requested and accepted after the final entry deadline will incur a late entry fee of 220 Euro for each athlete entered in each event.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.4.6  The Entry fees for the Continental Championships are established by the Continental Confederations. Information to be sent to ISSF Headquarters by the Organizer/the

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.5  Organizing Committee

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.5.1  Copies of all invitations, programmes and entry forms for all ISSF Championships must be sent to the Secretary General.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.6 Doping Control Doping control at all ISSF Championships must be done in all events and categories as specified in the ISSF Anti-Doping Rules. Olympic Games

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.7.1  The athletes’ participation quota at the Olympic Games in established by the IOC.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.7.2  The Qualification system is established by the ISSF Executive Committee and approved by the IOC.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.7.3  The ISSF supervises the Olympic Games through one (1) or two (2) Technical Delegates approved by the ISSF Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.7.4  In order that the Technical Delegates can carry out their responsibilities they must be invited at the expense of the Organizing Committee to the site of the Olympic Games at least two times in the years leading up to the Games, one of which must be 10 to 12 months before the Games. This is in addition to any Test Event and the Games themselves where the TDs are to arrive not less than five (5) days before the Opening Ceremony. 46 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.7.5  Programmes, schedules, forms and other details must be received by the ISSF, checked and agreed with the Organizing Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.7.6  Entries in the Olympic Games must be made using the procedures specified in the ISSF General Regulations except that schedules or special procedures established by the ISSF or IOC will prevail.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8.7.7  Anti-Doping Control in the Olympic Games will be conducted according to the procedures established by the IOC. Anti-Doping Control in all ISSF Championships will be conducted in all events and categories according to procedures established by the ISSF Anti-Doping Regulations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9 PROTOCOL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9.1  The holding and the format of an opening and closing ceremonies at ISSF Championships are guided by the applicable ISSF Guidelines for Organizing ISSF Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9.2  In the ISSF Championships the Organizing Committee must award:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9.2.1  Championship medals in gold, silver and bronze colours to the first three (3) individual event winners. A minimum of 15 athletes in individual events or 10 athletes in junior individual events must participate in order that individual medals shall be awarded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9.2.2  Championship medals in gold, silver and bronze colours to each member of the first three (3) Mixed Team events winners. A minimum of ten (10) Mixed Teams in each of the events must participate in order that Mixed Team medals shall be awarded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9.2.3  Championship medals in gold, silver and bronze colours to each member of the first three (3) Team events winners. A minimum of five (5) Teams in each event must participate in order that Team medals shall be awarded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9.3  If the above-mentioned minimums of participants are not reached, the event will be declared an “International Championship” of the nation which organized the competitions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9.4  A commemorative medal, of a different design from the Championship medals shall be given by the Organizing Committee to each athlete, team official, judge and delegate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9.5  The design of all official awards and the official symbol must be submitted to the Secretary General for approval by the Executive Committee at least two (2) months in advance.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.9.6  A Medal Ceremony must be held for each Championship event, at which the flags of the first three (3) winners in Individual, Mixed Team or Team must be raised while the anthem of the winner’s nation is played.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.10 RECORDS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.10.1  Records may be established in all recognized ISSF events in the Olympic Games and all ISSF Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.10.2  ISSF recognizes Olympic records, World records and Qualification World records.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.10.2.1  Olympic records are records established at the Olympic Games

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.10.2.2  World records are records established during a Final in any ISSF Championship. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 47

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.10.2.3  Qualification World Records can be established in Qualification) and Eliminations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.10.3  The ISSF will issue a World Record diploma to individual athletes, Mixed Team or Team members who establish a Record.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.10.4  The Technical Delegate(s) must submit reports for recognition of all Records.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.11 MEDIA RELATIONS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.11.1  The Media Coverage, Broadcasting and Advertising Rights of all ISSF World Championships, World Cups and other ISSF official events (General Assemblies, Congresses, etc.) are the property of the International Shooting Sport Federation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.11.2  Press, radio and television services must be given all cooperation and assistance to ensure the free flow of public information and communication. Necessary facilities including telecommunications, must be available prior to and during the Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.11.3  Provisions for interviews, photography and other media requirements will be made by the Organizing Committee to ensure that media personnel have access to athletes and team leaders; provided that such arrangements do not inconvenience the individual(s) concerned. Media representatives may communicate with athletes through their respective team leaders.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.12 GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.12.1  Alterations of the General Regulations may only be made by the Council in accordance with Article 1.7.3.1.a) ISSF Constitution.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.12.2  Upon approval, alterations become effective upon publication on the ISSF Website.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.13.2  The annexes to the General Regulations may not contravene the General Regulations.

chunks.text: Championships and World Cups The ISSF General Assembly chooses World Championship organizers in accordance with the ISSF General Regulations, 3.2.3. An ISSF Member Federation that wants to organize a World Championship must submit a proposal to the Secretary General one (1) month in advance of the General Assembly where the organizing federation will be chosen. Applicants must complete an Application for an ISSF World Championship and submit it to the Secretary General with all required documentation. The Executive Committee chooses World Cup organizers in accordance with the ISSF General Regulations 3.2.4. An ISSF Member Federation that wants to organize a World Cup or World Cup Final must submit a proposal to the Secretary General not later than 31 December, three (3) years before the year in which the World Cup is to be organized. Applicants must complete an Application for an ISSF World Cup and submit it to the Secretary General. PREAMBLE In accordance with the ISSF Constitution, the objectives of the ISSF are to promote and encourage the development of the shooting sport throughout the world, to provide drug- free sport and to promote and encourage the development of international relations. The purpose of this Code is to guarantee that the objectives of the ISSF will be executed in a fair manner, without improper interference, and to sanction incidents that damage the image of ISSF activities or bring them into disrepute. ISSF members, continental organizations, teams, officials and athletes shall participate in ISSF Championships and activities in accordance with the standards of ethics, fair play and sportsmanship established by the ISSF Statutes, Rules and Regulations and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: by this Code. This Code provides basic standards for fair play and moral behaviour and procedures for judging and sanctioning violations of those standards. With the following regulations the ISSF adopts its own code of ethics based on the principles and rules of the IOC Code of Ethics. Furthermore, acknowledging the danger to sports integrity from the manipulation of sports competitions, ISSF restates its commitment to safeguarding the integrity of sport, including the protection of clean athletes and competitions as stated in the Olympic Agenda 2020. Therefore, ISSF with these regulations also implements the new IOC Olympic Movement Code on the Prevention of the Manipulation of Competitions. The Definitions used in version 2016 of such IOC Code also apply to the following rules. These Ethics Rules had been amended by decision of the ISSF Executive Committee in its meeting on February 21, 2017. For enforcement of this Code, the ISSF will establish an Ethics Committee. 1 SCOPE OF APPLICATION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1 SCOPE OF APPLICABILITY This Code shall apply to conduct that damages the integrity and reputation of sports and in particular to illegal, immoral and unethical behaviour.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.2 PERSONS COVERED This Code shall apply to all officials and employees of the ISSF, ISSF member federations, the Continental Shooting Sport Confederations, as well as to athletes, coaches and other participants in ISSF activities.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3 APPLICABILITY IN TIME This Code shall apply to conduct whenever it occurred including before the passing of the rules contained in this Code. However, no individual shall be sanctioned for breaching this Code on account of an act or omission which would not have contravened the Code applicable at the time the breach was committed. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 65 Neither may they be subjected to a sanction greater than the maximum sanction applicable at the time the breach occurred. This shall, however, not prevent the Ethics Committee from considering the conduct in question and drawing any conclusions from it that are appropriate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4 SCOPE OF THE CODE, CUSTOM, DOCTRINE AND JURISPRUDENCE During all its operations, the Ethics Committee may draw on precedents and principles already established by sports doctrine and jurisprudence. 2 RULES OF CONDUCT

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1 DUTIES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.1 General Rules of conduct Persons bound by this Code are expected to be aware of the importance of their duties and associated obligations and responsibilities. Persons bound by this Code are obliged to respect all applicable laws and regulations, as well as ISSF Statutes, Rules and Regulations, and decisions taken by the competent ISSF bodies to the extent applicable to them. Persons bound by this Code shall behave in a dignified manner and act with complete credibility and integrity. They shall respect universal fundamental ethical principles that include:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Respect for the Olympic spirit, which requires mutual understanding with a spirit of friendship, solidarity and fair play;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Respect for principles of universality, political neutrality and autonomy of the Olympic Movement;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Respect for international conventions on protecting human rights insofar as they apply to the Olympic Games and ISSF Championship activities and which ensure in particular: • respect for human dignity; • rejection of discrimination of any kind on whatever grounds, be it race, colour, sex, sexual orientation, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status; • rejection of all forms of harassment, be it physical, professional or sexual, and any physical or mental injuries;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) ensuring the participants’ conditions of safety, well-being and medical care favourable to their physical and mental equilibrium. Persons bound by this Code may not abuse their position in any way, especially to take advantage of their position for personal or private aims or gains.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.2 Duty of fair behaviour / sportsmanlike behaviour Persons bound by this Code are expected to behave in a fair way and shall in particular refrain from any form of cheating including, but not limited to doping, manipulation of equipment or scores to give an advantage to an athlete or to a team, falsification or alteration of documents indicating false age, nationality, gender or other information, with the purpose of obtaining unfair advantage for an official, an athlete or a team. 66 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.3 Loyalty Persons bound by this Code have a duty of loyalty to the ISSF and its members. Therefore, they shall in particular refrain from any act of indiscretion, insubordination or partiality.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.4 Integrity of competitions Persons bound by this Code shall not take part in, either directly or indirectly, or otherwise being associated with betting, gambling, lotteries and similar events or transactions connected with shooting competitions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.5 Other ethical offences Other ethical offences, including the improper or illegal manipulation of equipment testing, ammunition testing, scoring decisions or competition results, illegal access to systems and data, committed by persons bound by this Code may be considered independent of any action taken or not taken by ISSF Competition Juries.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.6 Forgery and falsification Persons bound by this Code are forbidden from forging a document, falsifying an authentic document or using a forged or falsified document.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1.7 Duty of disclosure, cooperation and reporting Persons bound by this Code shall immediately report any potential breach of this Code to the ISSF Secretary General or send an email to ethics@issf- sports.org. At the request of the Ethics Committee, persons bound by this Code are obliged to contribute to clarifying the facts of the case or clarifying possible breaches and provide the evidence requested for inspection.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2 UNDUE ADVANTAGE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2.1 Conflicts of interest When performing an activity for the ISSF, or before being elected or appointed, persons bound by this Code shall disclose any potential conflicts of interest that could be linked with their prospective activities. Conflicts of interest arise if persons bound by this Code have, or appear to have, private or personal interests that detract from their ability to perform their duties with integrity and in an independent manner. Private or personal interests include gaining any possible advantage for the persons bound by this Code for themselves, members of their family, relatives, friends and acquaintances. Any such conflict shall be immediately disclosed and notified to the body or organization for which the person bound by this Code performs his duties. If an objection is made concerning an existing or potential conflict of interest of a person bound by this Code, it shall be reported immediately to the organization for which the person bound by this Code performs his duties for appropriate measures. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 67

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.3 OFFERING AND ACCEPTING GIFTS AND OTHER BENEFITS Persons bound by this Code may only offer or accept gifts or other benefits to and from persons within or outside ISSF, or in conjunction with intermediaries or related parties as defined in this Code, which

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) have symbolic value;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) are not given to influence a decision, voting behaviour or any other act that is related to their official activities or that falls within their discretion;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) do not create any undue pecuniary or other advantage; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) do not create a conflict of interest. Any gifts or other benefits not meeting all of these criteria are prohibited. Requests for guidance should be addressed to the Secretary General.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.4 BRIBERY AND CORRUPTION Persons bound by this Code must not offer, promise, give or accept any undue pecuniary or other advantage for the execution or omission of an act that is related to their official activities. Such acts are prohibited, regardless of whether carried out directly or indirectly through, or in conjunction with, intermediaries or related parties as defined in this Code. Any such offer must be reported in writing to the Secretary General and any failure to do so shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with this Code. Persons bound by this Code are prohibited from misappropriating ISSF assets, regardless of whether carried out directly or indirectly through, or in conjunction with, intermediaries or related parties, as defined in this Code.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5 NON-DISCRIMINATION Persons bound by this Code may not offend the dignity or integrity of a country, private person or group of people through contemptuous, discriminatory or denigrating words or actions on account of race, skin colour, ethnic, national or social origin, gender, language, religion, political opinion or any other opinion, wealth, birth or any other status, sexual orientation or for any other reason.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.6 PROTECTION OF PHYSICAL AND MENTAL INTEGRITY Persons bound by this Code shall respect the integrity of others involved. They shall ensure that the personal rights of every individual whom they contact and who is affected by their actions is protected, respected and safeguarded. 3 PREVENTION OF MANIPULATION The following conduct as defined in this Article constitutes a violation of this Code:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1 BETTING Betting in relation either:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) to a Competition in which the Participant is directly participating; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) to the Participant’s sport; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) to any event of a multisport Competition in which he/she is a participant.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2 MANIPULATION OF SPORTS COMPETITIONS An intentional arrangement, act or omission aimed at an improper alteration of the result or the course of a Competition in order to remove all or part of 68 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF the unpredictable nature of the Competition with a view to obtaining an undue Benefit for oneself or for others.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3 CORRUPT CONDUCT Providing, requesting, receiving, seeking, or accepting a Benefit related to the manipulation of a Competition or any other form of corruption.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4 INSIDE INFORMATION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4.1  Using Inside Information for the purposes of Betting, any form of manipulation of Competitions or any other corrupt purposes whether by the Participant or via another person and/or entity.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4.2  Disclosing Inside Information to any person and/or entity, with or without Benefit, where the Participant knew or should have known that such disclosure might lead to the information being used for the purposes of Betting, any form of manipulation of competitions or any other corrupt purposes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4.3  Giving and/or receiving a Benefit for the provision of Inside Information regardless of whether any Inside Information is actually provided.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5 FAILURE TO REPORT

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.1  Failing to report to ISSF or a relevant disclosure/reporting mechanism or authority, at the first available opportunity, full details of any approaches or invitations received by the Participant to engage in conduct or incidents that could amount to a violation of this Code.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5.2  Failing to report to ISSF or a relevant disclosure/reporting mechanism or authority, at the first available opportunity, full details of any incident, fact or matter that comes to the attention of the Participant (or of which they ought to have been reasonably aware) including approaches or invitations that have been received by another Participant to engage in conduct that could amount to a violation of this Code.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6 FAILURE TO COOPERATE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6.1 Failing to cooperate with any investigation carried out by ISSF in relation to a possible breach of this Code, including, without limitation, failing to provide accurately, completely and without undue delay any information and/or documentation and/or access or assistance requested by ISSF as part of such investigation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6.2  Obstructing or delaying any investigation that may be carried out by ISSF in relation to a possible violation of this Code, including without limitation concealing, tampering with or destroying any documentation or other information that may be relevant to the investigation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7 APPLICATION OF ARTICLES 3.1 to 3.6

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.1  For the determination of whether a violation has been committed, the following are not relevant:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Whether or not the Participant is participating in the Competition concerned;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The outcome of the Competition on which the Bet was made or intended to be made; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 69

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Whether or not any Benefit or other consideration was actually given or received;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The nature or outcome of the Bet;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Whether or not the Participant’s effort or performance in the Competition concerned were (or could be expected to be) affected by the acts or omission in question;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Whether or not the result of the Competition concerned was (or could be expected to be) affected by the acts or omission in question;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Whether or not the manipulation included a violation of any ISSF rule;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7.2 Any form of aid, abetment or attempt by a Participant that could culminate in a violation of this Code shall be treated as if a violation had been committed, whether or not such an act in fact resulted in a violation and/or whether that violation was committed deliberately or negligently. 4 DISCIPLINARY MEASURES, SANCTIONS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.1 GENERAL Breaches of this Code or any other ISSF Statutes, Rules and Regulations by persons bound by this Code are punishable by one or more of the following sanctions:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) warning;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) fine;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) return of awards;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) disqualification;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) suspension;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) expulsion;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) ban on entering a competition or a venue;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) ban on taking part in any shooting-related activity. The Ethics Committee may decide that the notification of a case be made to the appropriate law enforcement authorities.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.2 INVESTIGATIONS The Participant who is alleged to have committed a violation of this Code must be informed of the alleged violations that have been committed, details of the alleged acts and/or omissions, and the range of possible sanctions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.3 BURDEN AND STANDARD OF PROOF The ISSF shall have the burden of establishing that a violation has been committed. The standard of proof in all matters under this Code shall be the balance of probabilities, a standard that implies that on the preponderance of the evidence it is more likely than not that a breach of this Code has occurred.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.4 CONFIDENTIALITY The principle of confidentiality must be strictly respected by the ISSF during all the procedure; information should only be exchanged with entities on a need to know basis. Confidentiality must also be strictly respected by any person concerned by the procedure until there is public disclosure of the case. 70 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.5 DETERMINATION OF THE SANCTION The sanction may be imposed by taking into account all relevant factors in the case, including the offender’s assistance and cooperation, the motive, the circumstances and the degree of the offender’s guilt. The Ethics Committee shall decide the scope and duration of any sanction. Sanctions may be limited to a geographical area or to one or more specific categories such as a competition. Unless otherwise specified, the sanction may be increased as deemed appropriate if a breach has been repeated. Where more than one breach has been committed, the sanction shall be based on the most serious breach, and increased as appropriate depending on the specific circumstances. 5 LIMITATION PERIOD As a general rule, breaches of the provisions of this Code may no longer be prosecuted after a lapse of ten years. The limitation period, when applicable, shall be prolonged if proceedings are opened and/or suspended. 6 PROCEDURES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1 ETHICS COMMITTEE The Ethics Committee consists of a Chairperson and two additional members. The members of the Ethics Committee are appointed by the Executive Committee in case a complaint according to 6.2 below has been filed. The members of the Ethics Committee must be independent and may not hold a position in the ISSF or any ISSF member federation. The Ethics Committee is to be composed in such a way that the members, together, have the knowledge, abilities and specialist experience that is necessary for the due completion of their tasks. The Chairperson and at least one other member shall be qualified to practise law. Members of the Ethics Committee must disclose to the Chairperson or the ISSF Secretary General any situation or fact that may establish a conflict of interest between themselves and the case under investigation. Such disclosure must be made immediately after the inquiry is opened or immediately after the situation or fact in question arises. Any person being subject to investigations of a potential breach of this Code, or declaring a conflict of interest, may not be part of the Ethics Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: In such cases, or if a member of the Ethics Committee is unable to act, the Executive Committee must appoint a person acting as a replacement.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2 RULES FOR PROCEDURES Any complaints, charges or guidance relating to a breach of ethical principles and rules should be addressed in writing to the Secretary General or to ethics@ issf- sports.org. The Secretary General shall inform the Chairperson in order to summon the Ethics Committee. The Ethics Committee shall decide whether to conduct an inquiry or to dismiss the complaint. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 71 When conducting an inquiry regarding a complaint or charges, the Ethics Committee may: • Request written information or documents from the parties concerned; • Hear the parties concerned, with or without the presence of legal counsel, as determined by the Ethics Committee; • Decide to hear witnesses as determined by the Ethics Committee or at the request of the parties concerned; • Conduct investigations in the field by designating one (1) or more of its members or another person to represent the Committee; • Designate one (1) or more experts to assist the Ethics Committee in its inquiry. In the absence of a consensus, decisions of the Ethics Committee shall be

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: taken by majority of members present. 7 APPEALS Decisions by the Ethics Committee may be appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne, Switzerland, (“CAS”) which will resolve the dispute definitively in accordance with the Code of sports-related arbitration. The time limit for appeal is twenty-one days after the reception of the decision concerning the appeal. 8 MUTUAL RECOGNITION Subject to the right of appeal, any decision in compliance with this Code by an International Sporting Organisation shall be recognised and respected by the ISSF. Athletes or team participating in ISSF Championships have a right to protest when competitions are not conducted according to ISSF Rules and Regulations. ISSF rules for filing and deciding protests are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.  Protests filed at ISSF Championships must be decided according to ISSF Rules and Regulations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.  Competition Juries (3.5.3) are responsible for receiving and deciding all protests;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.  The Jury of Appeal (3.5.3.7) is responsible for making final decisions on all appeals against protest decisions by Competition Juries. Decisions by the Jury of Appeal may not be appealed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.  During Finals round competitions, the Competition Jury shall supervise the Finals and make any decisions required by ISSF Rules and Regulations that do not involve protests. If a protest is made during a Final, a Finals Protest Jury is responsible for making an immediate decision regarding the protest. Finals Jury decisions may not be appealed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.  For Finals round competitions where protests must be decided immediately, a combined Finals Protest Jury consisting of two (2) members of the Competition Jury plus one (1) member of the Jury of Appeal must be designated by the Technical Delegate and the appropriate Jury Chairperson.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.  In a Finals round no score protest is permitted except for a failure to indicate a shot. In such cases one (1) member of the Classification Jury must also be included;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.  Rules and forms for filing protests or appeals are specified in the General Technical Rules, 6.16 and 9.17. ISSF protest rules provide for verbal protests that can be submitted and decided on the ranges immediately, for written protests to be decided by the appropriate Jury and for appeals of Jury decisions to be decided by a Jury of Appeal. The rules also provide for scoring protests to be decided by the RTS Jury with decisions on scoring protests not subject to appeal. The protest rules further provide that in Finals round competitions, the Finals Jury shall make immediate decisions on any protests and that such decisions may not be appealed; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.  In the case of protests involving conflicts between the ISSF Constitution, ISSF General Regulations or Technical Rules, the ISSF Constitution shall take precedence over the ISSF General Regulations or Technical Rules and the ISSF General Regulations shall take precedence over the Technical Rules. In conflicts involving IOC Rules, the IOC Rules shall prevail. 74 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF Article 3.13.3.8, Annex “TA” Guidelines for Training Academy BACKGROUND Special ISSF training courses for coaches were approved by the Executive Committee in

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1992. The diploma courses were designed for national coaches from Member Federations to achieve an international coaching qualification. In March 2024, a new ISSF Academy was established for all educational needs of ISSF, including and starting with the Coach Courses. 1 ISSF Academy authority ISSF Academy is the supreme body of ISSF Coach Education. The ISSF Coach Licences will be granted after having successfully passed the respective level Coach Course provided by ISSF Academy. ISSF Academy may cooperate with high level shooting academies and grant (after evaluation process and written Licence agreement) an academy to execute shooting Coach Courses and deliver Course Diplomas under supervision of ISSF Academy. The database of the successful participants shall be delivered to ISSF Academy, which gives out the Coach Licences. ISSF Member Federations may ask for tailored Coach Courses from ISSF Academy. Based on a written agreement between the Federation and ISSF Academy, these courses may be executed by the ISSF Academy coaches.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1 The ISSF Academy Board The ISSF Academy Board regularly monitors the fulfillment of the Academy’s tasks, educational objectives and the development of the Academy in accordance with its long- term objectives. In addition, the Board: • establishes the Academy’s ethical values and policies and monitors their implementation, • monitors management’s communication to the shareholders and the supportive partners and, where appropriate, discusses the development of the shooting family reactions, • reviews annually the basic plans of the Academy and the objectives derived from it for the planning period, • supports the Academy leadership as appropriate. 2 Coach ‘A’ Course and Licence Coaches seeking ‘A’ level Licence are professionals. They work mainly for their national federation or other international federation. They travel with their athletes to international competitions and are entitled to enter all the ISSF events and finals. They contribute to the sport by educating new coaches. Course ‘A‘ is a hybrid course that includes a research assignment before joining the

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: contact phase of the course. The contact phase of the course, which lasts 5-7 days, is carried out in conjunction with the ISSF major competition for all disciplines. The main theme of the course is winning - coaching athletes to reach grand finals and win competitions. During the course, research papers will be presented and evaluated. Monitoring of personal development plans will also be part of the course. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 75 During the ‘A’ course, there will be live and online lectures, group discussions, individual presentations and practical exercises related to the live final competitions. Prior to the course, coaches participating in the course will be required to collect personal feedback on their coaching environment and use this feedback to develop individual development plans before the end of the course. The language of the course is English. A prerequisite for admission to the ‘A’ course is that the participant must be permanently involved in coaching and be applying for or undertaking a full-time role as an Olympic

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: shooting coach. The role of the ISSF Academy Coach also opens up after successful participation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1 Terms of graduating ‘A’ Licence Basic route to the coach ‘A’ Licence is the educational path through the ISSF Academy. Active role as a shooting coach is a basic demand to access the ‘A’ level education. Merit-based route to the coach ‘A’ Licence demands proven achievements, support from the national federation and approval process of the ISSF Academy Board. The proven achievements include:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1) H  aving obtained the Level ‘B’ ISSF Coach Licence and having actively coached international level athletes for at least four consecutive years with the role of National Coach.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2) H  aving achieved the qualification of an athlete to the Olympics with the role of National Coach\Team Coach for at least two editions of the Games.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3) H  aving had an athlete qualify for an Olympic final with the role of National Coach\Team Coach.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4) H  aving coached a Youth National team with the role of National Junior Coach\Junior Team Coach and having won a medal in a Junior World or Continental Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5) H  aving achieved at least three individual or Mixed Team medals in WCH or WCF or WC with the role of National Coach\Team Coach.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6) L  ong-term work for the ISSF Academy or another shooting academy will be seen as an additional merit. A coach applying for a merit-based coaching ‘A’ Licence must submit the application and all necessary documents to the ISSF Academy through the national federation. The ISSF Academy will provide guidance to federations on this process. The deadline for applications is the last day of October each year. The ISSF Academy Board processes the applications at its meeting at the end of the year. 3 Coach ‘B’ Course and Licence Coaches applying for a ‘B’ level Licence are typically semi-professional. They typically work for their national federation and have athletes they personally coach on the national team. They can travel with their athletes to international competitions and are entitled to participate in ISSF events and finals with their athletes. B Course is a hybrid course, utilizing an e-learning platform, but having also a one close contact week located in a multi-discipline shooting training center. The main theme of the ‘B’ Course is how to build a professional training environment for the athletes. The close

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: contact week will be organized in close cooperation with the Confederations. During the ‘B’ Course, there will be live and online lectures, group discussions, individual learning sessions and practical exercises at the shooting range around the main theme of the course. Prior to the course, the participating coaches are required to collect personal feedback on their own coaching environment and use this feedback to develop individual development plans before the end of the course. The course language is English. 76 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF A prerequisite for access to the ‘B’ course is that the participant is actively involved in coaching after the ‘C’ course. This is a prerequisite for access to the ‘B’ course. The workload for a participant in the ‘B’ course is 60 hours, including online pre-course assignments before the contact phase. By the end of the ‘B’ Course, participants will select a research topic, approved by the Academy. The research paper will be one part of the assignments before joining the ‘A’

chunks.text: 3.1 Terms of graduating ‘B’ Licence Basic route to the coach ‘B’ Licence is the educational path through the ISSF Academy combined with active role as a shooting coach. Merit-based route to the coach ‘B’ Licence demands proven achievements, support from the national federation and approval process of the ISSF Academy Board. The proven achievements include:

chunks.text: 4) Long-term work for the ISSF Academy or another shooting academy will be seen as an additional merit. A coach seeking for the merit-based coach ‘B’ Licence must provide an application with all the appropriate documents to the ISSF Academy via National Federation. The ISSF Academy will give the instructions of this process to the Federations. Deadline of these applications is the last day of October annually. ISSF Academy Board will handle the applications in the end of a year in their meeting. 4 Coach ‘C’ Course and Licence Coaches seeking for ‘C’ level Licence are typically in the beginning of their coaching career and they contribute locally to the shooting club or regional level activities. ‘C’ Course is an online course. ‘C’ Course will last 12 weeks and demands approximately 50 hours work from the participant to pass the tasks given during whole course. There will be live online lectures, recorded lectures, and seminars during the course. Provided reading materials support tasks given in the course. Some tasks will be shared among the

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: learning group by using the learning platform. ‘C’ Course main content is about the relevant sport science in shooting. Beside mental and physical training, nutrition, sleep and life balance, much room will be given to coach behaviors and development as a coach through feedback. There are several digital books available as well. One part of the ‘C’ course is also deeper understanding about shooting techniques and training programming. The goal is to reach a holistic understanding of shooting performance. Important part of the learning process is the Coach Diary, that every participant will use throughout the course as a learning memory. On the other hand, the participants will evaluate the course frequently and give their feedback to further develop the course. Successful participation of the course will be rewarded with the ISSF Academy Coach ‘C’ Certificate. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 77 5 Coach ‘D’ Course and Licence Coaches applying for a Level ‘D’ Licence are typically early in their coaching careers and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: are involved locally at the shooting club or regional level. The ‘D’ course is an online course tailored separately for rifle, pistol and shotgun. The ‘D’ course lasts 12 weeks and requires approximately 50 hours of work from the participant to complete the tasks assigned throughout the course. Live online lectures are held almost every week. These lectures are recorded for participants who for some reason cannot attend the live session. In addition to other tasks, it is typical for participants to visit the shooting range once a week. The tasks are distributed among the learning group using a learning platform. The introduction and the first week of the ‘D’ course provide the participant with a framework for the chosen discipline. The Olympic values, combined with our own values, point the way to good coaching behaviors. Safety always comes first. Anti-doping issues and the prevention of all forms of harassment are part of this framework. The main content of the ‘D’ course deals with shooting technique. It is the basis of the coach’s basic knowledge. From the coach’s point of view, there is also support content
