chunks.text: covering mental and physical training and other essentials. At the end of the ‘D’ course, each participant will have a personal feedback session with the academy instructor. An important part of the learning process is the Coach diary, which is used by each participant as a learning memory throughout the course. On the other hand, participants often evaluate the course and provide feedback to further improve the course. Successful participation in the course will be rewarded with the ISSF Academy Coach ‘D’ Certificate. The ISSF Academy can organize tailored ‘D’ Courses for ISSF Member Federations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1. Terms of graduating ‘D’ Licence The route to the Level ‘D’ ISSF Coach Licence is the educational path through the ISSF Academy combined with a fresh role as a shooting coach.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6. Course application process There are two routes to apply for the Coach Courses. Individual coaches can apply via Academy webpage (www.issf-academy.com). The Member Federations can nominate persons to participate the courses. Before the course starts, the Academy shall confirm the list of participants with the Member Federations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7. Delivery of the course diplomas and ISSF Coach Licences After successful participation at a course, ISSF Academy will deliver the course diplomas electronically to the participants. After approval of an ISSF Coach Licence, ISSF Academy will update the ISSF Coach database. There is a plan to transfer the identification and update process of the Licences to an ISSF Coach Application.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8. Coach Licence administrative costs. The ISSF Academy administrative cost of registering a Coach Licence, updating the datafiles and delivering the diplomas and Licences is 70€ until the Coach APP is available. 78 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF Article 3.13.3.9, Annex “J”: Guidelines for Judges Licences 1 GENERAL 80 2 ACQUISITION OF A LICENCE 80 3 VALIDITY AND EXTENSION OF THE LICENCE 81 4 EXPIRATION OF A LICENCE 82 5 UPGRADING 84 6 SPECIAL ADMINISTRATIVE PROCESS FOR THE ISSUANCE OF JUDGES’ LICENCES 85 7 ASSIGNMENT OF JUDGES 85 8 ELECTRONIC SCORING TARGET COURSES 86 9 INSTRUCTORS’ LICENCE 87 10 APPLICATION FORMS FOR LICENCES 88 SPECIAL NOTE: In the context of this Annex, the word “Judge” refers to an accredited ISSF Judges’ Licence holder. chunks.text: Jury duties at specified Championships. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 79 1 GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1  For the achievement of its purposes the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF), Licences judges to supervise shooting competitions and to ensure the fair and equal treatment of all competitors (see 1.1.4 ISSF Constitution). Judges must be experienced and fully conversant with the current versions of the ISSF Rules and Regulations plus the relevant Technical Rules for the Shooting discipline concerned in order to Advise, Supervise and Assist if necessary.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.2  The ISSF issues judges’ Licences as confirmation of qualification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3  Judges’ Licences are divided into two (2) categories.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.1  Category “A” authorizes the holder to act as an official Jury member at all shooting competitions, for which the Licence is valid with respect to the disciplines included, including the Olympic Games and World Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3.2  Category “B” Licence authorizes the holder to act as an official Jury member in all shooting competitions, for which the Licence is valid with respect to the disciplines included, except the Olympic Games and the World Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4  The ISSF issues judges’ Licences for the following disciplines:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.1  Rifle shooting (1)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.2  Pistol shooting (2)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.3  Shotgun shooting (3)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.4 Moving Target shooting (4)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4.5 Target Sprint (5) 1.4.6 Electronic Scoring Target Control (6) 1.4.7 Referee (7) 1.4.8 The ISSF can issue judges’ Licences for one (1) or more discipline(s), but only following successful completion of official ISSF courses in each of the disciplines.No.1 (Rifle), No.2 (Pistol), No.3 (Shotgun), No. 4 (Moving Target) No.5 (Target Sprint) and No.7 (Referee). However, No.6 (Electronic Scoring Target Control) is only issued after successful completion of an official ISSF course on that specific subject. 1.5 The ISSF Headquarters and the Chairperson of the Judges Committee maintain a list of all the Licence holders. 1.6 Licence holders may only act as Jury Members for the Olympic Games and the World Championships if they have been designated by the Executive Committee of the ISSF. For World Cups Jury Members will be nominated by the ISSF Secretary General and the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges Committee, and approved by the Executive Committee. For Continental and Regional Games and Championships they must be designated by the Continental or Regional Confederations, who in turn must forward this

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: designation to the ISSF for ratification and authorization. Continental and Regional designations must have full endorsement prior to the event to ensure official recognition has been granted. 2 ACQUISITION OF A LICENCE.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1 The applicant must have the necessary capability and experience as a judge, in particular with a clear understanding and expression of the English language. 80 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2 ISSF Judges’ Licences are not granted to active athletes who still participate in competitions where world records may be established. If the holder of a judges’ Licence wishes to participate as an athlete, his licence will be suspended. He may subsequently apply to re-activate it if still valid or apply for a new licence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.3 For the acquisition of an ISSF Judges’ Licence, preparatory instruction and training is necessary. The applicants should possess a National judges’ Licence of the highest level issued by their National Federation, or must have equivalent experience as a national judge and as a range official. For acquisition of a Judges’ Licence in the shotgun discipline, applicants must first be in possession of a valid Shotgun Referees Licence and have experience of at least one (1) year as a Referee at International/Regional/National competitions. Proof of this must be provided.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.4 Applicants must also have achieved the pass-standard in the General Aspects and the Shooting Discipline Parts of an official ISSF Judges’ course within the previous two (2) years.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5 An applicant’s National Federation must sign the completed official ISSF Judges’ application form (see form at end of Guidelines) to confirm the contents and support the application. The National Federation must then send it to the ISSF Headquarters.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.6 Applications should be submitted as soon as possible, but no later than 31 December each year for Licences to be issued in the following year. In order that applicants are not disadvantaged by any time considerations, once applications are received by ISSF Headquarters, the Chairperson of the Judges’ Committee will endeavour to authorize the issue of Licences or upgrades as soon as possible. This does not negate the requirement for the Judges’ Committee to approve and confirm the granting of these Licences at their annual meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.7 The ISSF Judges Committee will evaluate and approve, where appropriate or postpone applications during its annual meeting which will usually be held towards the end of January each year.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.8 After approval, the ISSF Headquarters will issue the Licences. To be valid they must be signed by the ISSF Secretary General and the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges’ Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.9 These Licences are sent to the National Federations for delivery to the Licence holders.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.10 A fee of Euro 50.00 must be paid for a new Licence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.11 Approval of initial applications will result in the issue of a “B” category Licence. Category “A” Licences are only issued following further experience with assessment before upgrading. 3 VALIDITY AND EXTENSION OF THE LICENCE.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1 All ISSF Judges’ Licences are issued for a period of five (5) years.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2 After expiration of this period, the Licence can be renewed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3 The National Federation must submit all requests for renewal to the ISSF Headquarters accompanied by a completed Renewal Form (see form at end of Guidelines).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4 In special circumstances, the ISSF Technical Committee, and Judge Committee can also confirm that the applicant has obtained experience as a EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 81 Jury Member in International or regional level competitions during the previous five (5) year period and act as the Nominating authority for renewal of a Judges Licence. The renewed licence, in that situation, should be sent to the Continental Confederation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5 The National Federation must confirm that the applicant has obtained experience as a Jury Member in international, regional or national level competitions during the last five (5) year period.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6 The current Licence should not be returned when applying for a renewal, though it will cease to be valid after the expiry date. Applications for renewal should be submitted at least three (3) months before expiry.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.7  The Chairperson of the Judges’ Committee in co-operation with the ISSF Headquarters will deal with all renewals. Renewed Licences will be returned to the National Federation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.8 A fee of Euro 25.00 will be charged for each renewal. 4 EXPIRATION OF A LICENCE.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.1  When an ISSF Judge’s Licence expires after five (5) years, Licence holders will be taken off the ISSF list if not renewed by application within two (2) years. In such a case any future Licence must be applied for in accordance with the acquisition of a Licence, including attendance at course(s). Licences renewed late within the two (2) years will only be valid for five (5) years from the previous expiry date.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.2  Once a licence has expired for more than two (2) years, the licence holder must follow a refresher training course to validate the licence renewal for five (5) years.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.3  The Licence holders’ National Federation, at any time, has the right to apply for cancellation of an ISSF Judge’s Licence. The Licence holder may be taken off the list, in such a case the Licence should be returned to the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.4  A judge’s Licence may be cancelled if a holder does not fulfil his duties as a judge or harms the interest or reputation of the ISSF. The holder will be taken off the ISSF list and the Licence must be returned to the ISSF. All ISSF Judges’ Licences remain the property of the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.5  Judges’ Courses.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6  Only courses that have been approved and recognized by the ISSF will be considered as official training courses for judges. The location and dates of such courses are to be agreed with the Secretary General and C h a i r p e r s o n of the Judges’ Committee. Once agreed, the Chairperson of the Judges’ Committee and the Secretary General will appoint a qualified ISSF Instructor, from the approved list of ISSF Instructor licence holders, to deliver each course. Instructors will not normally be appointed from the host country. After authorisation by the ISSF Judges’ Committee, the ISSF will publish the annual courses programme by January of that year. Applications for recognition must be submitted to the ISSF Headquarters using the form “Application for Judges Courses” (available on ISSF web site). The application must be sent to ISSF at least 3 months before the date of the intended course. All applications and subsequent publication of courses must include the following details:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6.1 Where the course will be held; 82 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6.2 The dates of the course;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6.3 The name(s) of the shooting disciplines that will be covered;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6.4 The name(s) of the ISSF Instructor. The name of the course coordinator and, if different, of the person who is to conduct the instruction on the General Aspects of the Rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6.5 What expenses will be met by the National Organizer; English language is mandatory. The ISSF Licence will not be granted if obtained with any other language.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6.6 From which National Federation(s) the Participants will come; Normally, applications will be considered when received from other National Federations within the same Continent, but cannot be guaranteed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.7 The basis for ISSF Judges’ courses is the “ISSF Training Guidelines”. A copy of this document will be issued by the ISSF to the course coordinator of every approved course. The objective is to ensure that applicants for ISSF Licences have a proper understanding of the Rules, and their application, in respect of the disciplines for which they seek to be Licenced; also, to ensure applicants have a proper understanding of the Constitution, General Regulations, Terms of Reference, Eligibility and Anti-Doping Regulations, etc applicable to all disciplines. Separately, applicants for Licences must possess practical experience gained from officials’ duties within their National Federation. Normally, applicants for ISSF Judges’ courses should already possess the highest National Licence as a range official; where nations do not have a national Licence system the applicants must possess equivalent practical experience.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.7.1 Every part of the course should be opened with the explanation of the purpose and the content of the course, followed by the duties and decision making processes required to make a good judge.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.7.2 During the course the ISSF General Regulations and Constitution of the ISSF, etc… must be covered and a test conducted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.7.3 The “Rifle” discipline must also include 50m and 10m Pistol shooting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.7.4 If a separate course is held for 25m Pistol shooting, 10m and 50m Pistol shooting must also be included.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.7.5 Shotgun, Moving Target, Target Sprint and Electronic Scoring Target disciplines are treated separately.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.8 The name of the instructor(s) must be submitted to the ISSF and confirmed. The Organizer can propose instructors to the ISSF for approval, or can request that suitable instructors be provided.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.8.1 When there is only one (1) instructor, the different disciplines must be dealt with in succession. This must be done according to a training schedule so that the participants can become familiar with the content of a course and can make arrangements for participating in the different sections.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.8.2 If there are instructors for the various disciplines the opening of the course, and lectures on the Constitution and the General Regulations, should be given to everyone together. The participants can then separate for the individual disciplines.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.8.3 The organizer must pay the costs for travelling, accommodation, meals and local transportation for the instructor(s). EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 83

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.9 Courses should last a minimum of three (3) days and this must be extended if more than one discipline is to be treated in succession.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.10 The organizer is responsible for providing a training room with adequate facilities for efficient instruction, and for the comfort of those attending.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.11 A maximum of 15 participants are permitted per instructor.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.11.1 The participants should possess a good background of practical experience as officials before attending a course. Participants with little experience must obtain practical experience under the guidance of an experienced judge in a series of national competitions before applying for an ISSF Judges’ Licence. They must speak and understand English.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.11.2 The organizer should publish details of the course as early as possible. The announcement should include all details about dates, times, accommodation, meals, local transportation, costs and any further important information.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.11.3 Every participant must be given a registration form to be filled in with his name, address and date of birth. The participant must further indicate his experience and any special knowledge he has acquired during competitions in which he acted as an official, and the qualifications obtained in his National Federation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.11.4 Only participants entered by a National Federation will be accepted. Inexperienced people should not be allowed to participate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.12 Participants who complete the course satisfactorily, including knowledge of the General Aspects will be issued with an ISSF Diploma. ISSF certificates of attendance will not be issued, but organizers are encouraged to provide host Federation certificates of attendance for those not achieving the Diploma standard.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.13 The ISSF Diploma does not guarantee the issue of an ISSF Licence; it only certifies the satisfactory completion of the official course.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.14 At the end of the course the instructor must write and submit a short report, using the form “Report Official ISSF Judges Course” with a list of those attending and those completing the course to the standard required for an ISSF Licence (i.e. those having received a Diploma), stating for which disciplines they passed. Where possible the report should indicate whether the individuals already possess sufficient practical experience, or whether further practical experience appears appropriate before an ISSF Licence is granted. The report must be sent as soon as possible to the ISSF Headquarters for the attention of the ISSF Secretary General and the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.15 Official recognition of judges’ courses will be decided by the ISSF Secretary General and the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.16 National Shooting Federations are encouraged to run courses for national judges’ Licences, following the material provided for official ISSF courses.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.17 National Federations not having suitably qualified ISSF Licence holders to conduct courses for National judges’ Licences are also encouraged to request assistance from the ISSF Secretary General or the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges Committee. 84 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 5 UPGRADING.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1  The basis for upgrading of a “B” judges’ Licence to an “A” judges’ Licence is the experience acquired as the judge over a number of years:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.1 A minimum period of four (4) years recent experience is required as an active “B” Licence holder; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.2 The applicant must have officiated in at least five (5) international competitions, in the last six (6) years, which have a minimum of five (5) participating nations, at least three (3) must be ISSF or WSPS Championships. For at least two (2) appointments the applicant must have been a Jury Member, but if not more, the other three (3) appointments must have been as a Chief Range Officer, Chief Referee, Chief of RTS or Chief of Equipment Control. An upgrading based only on the required period of time, but on inadequate further experience at championships, will not be granted; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.3 For Rifle, Pistol and Moving Target disciplines “A” Licence upgrades, the applicant must be in possession of a valid ISSF EST Licence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.4 They must have passed an ISSF Judge’s course held in English language. They should demonstrate that they have extensive experience in serving on competition juries (ISSF or WSPS).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.2 Accordingly, Applications for upgrading should be made to the ISSF Headquarters. When an upgrading is approved by the Judges committee, the ISSF Headquarters will issue a new ISSF Licence valid for 5 years and this will be sent to the National Federation in the same way as for other Licence issues.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.3 A fee of Euro 15.00 is charged for an upgrading.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.4 Additional disciplines will only be added to an existing Licence (“A” or “B”) after the recent satisfactory completion of an official ISSF course for that discipline. Applications will be dealt with in the same way as applications for new Licences (as opposed to renewals) by the ISSF Judges Committee at its annual meeting. Those approved will receive new Licences. Where an “A” Licence is already held, the additional discipline will be added at that level. 6 SPECIAL ADMINISTRATIVE PROCESS FOR THE ISSUANCE OF JUDGES’ LICENCES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1 In exceptional cases an ISSF Judge’s Licence can be issued or upgraded when it is necessary to ensure there are sufficient qualified personnel at events where world records may be established. For example, when a change of venue is necessary, or when any change of a previously assigned judge is necessary.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2 The National Federation must submit an application.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3 The applications will be considered and decided by the ISSF Secretary General together with the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4 Licences issued in this way will be included in the list of Licence holders. At the next meeting of the ISSF Judges Committee the Chairperson must inform the Committee of any Licences granted in this way.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.5 Licences issued in this way must only be given to well qualified individuals. The usual standards must be met; only the administrative process is changed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6 A Judges licence holder can have only one country designation change during their lifetime. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 85 7 ASSIGNMENT OF JUDGES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1 The nomination and designation of the Jury Members is made according to the Constitution of the ISSF. It is recommended and all appointed Jury members are encouraged to take out their own individual travel and medical insurance prior to deploying on an assignment, this is in addition to any ISSF insurance.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1.1 The Secretary General and the Chairperson of the Judges Committee of the ISSF will nominate to the Executive Committee the required number of Jury Members and substitutes for World Championships, Olympic Games and for World Cups and Grand Prix in accordance with the Guidelines. The Executive Committee designates the Juries for the World Championships and Olympic Games and approves the list for the World Cups and Grand Prix.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1.2 The Continental and Regional Confederations recognized by the ISSF should nominate and designate the Jury Members for their Championships and Games. Where Olympic quota places are distributed, these designations must be endorsed and ratified by the ISSF prior to the start of the event. Only with such ISSF authorization will jury appointments be granted official recognition and status.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1.3 The Organizing Committee, or the Organizing Federation, is responsible for the designation of Jury Members for other international championships and national championships held under the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.2 All Jury Members must hold the applicable current ISSF Judges’ Licence with EST Licence for all competitions where world records may be established. At all other championships held under the ISSF Rules, the Jury Members should hold valid ISSF Judges’ Licences and EST Licence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.3 In championships where world records may be established, Team Leaders, Officials, Coaches and Athletes must not be members of a Jury. If possible one (1) Member, but not usually the Chairperson, must be from the National Federation organizing the championships. These host nation judges must be approved by the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4 In all other championships, team officials should not be members of a Jury.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5 It is desirable that senior officials participating in the organizing of major competitions should possess an appropriate ISSF Licence. Particular tasks and duties for which ISSF Licences should be held are: Chief Range Officer, RTS Chief, Chief Referee, Chief of Equipment Control.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.6 Range Officers, RTS Officers, Referees and Equipment Control Officers should also be encouraged to undertake official training with a view to obtaining ISSF Licences.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.7 Competition Officials designated by the Organizing Committee must not be members of any Juries at the same championships. 8 ELECTRONIC SCORING TARGET COURSES Background

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.1.1 Special courses for Electronic Scoring Target (EST) Control Licences were approved by the Executive Committee in 1998. These courses provide education about the underlying principles involved, and the procedure for dealing with score-protests and with scoring problems that may be encountered.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.1.2 These courses are designed for holders of ISSF Judges’ Licences in the shooting disciplines of Rifle, Pistol and Moving Target as the scoring and 86 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF ranking rules for these disciplines must be known already as well as the ISSF Statutes, Rules and Regulations plus the relevant Technical Rules for the shooting disciplines concerned.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.1.3 Judges’ EST Control Licences are of one (1) category – depending upon the category “A” or “B” of the shooting discipline Licence held.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.1.4 A course fee fixed by the Executive Committee is payable by each student registering for an Official ISSF course for the first time. This covers the preparation of detailed notes issued to students, and the cost of issuing a handbook, plus future updating as EST equipment is improved, and the Licence when issued.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.1.5 Students may attend courses on more than one (1) occasion; to update their knowledge and to improve their result to gain an EST Licence, if they do not already have one; no further fee is payable.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.2 As for all official ISSF courses, official recognition of judges’ courses for Electronic Scoring Target Control will be decided by the ISSF Secretary General and the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.2.1 Instructors for these courses are chosen from those having achieved a high standard on a previous course and having considerable practical experience.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.2.2 Assistant Instructors, with similar qualifications, also may be designated depending upon the number of students attending.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.2.3 An ISSF Test Paper is provided, together with all supporting test material to conduct a Final Test.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.2.4 The completed Test Papers are returned to the ISSF for formal marking to ensure a uniform standard is set as the basis for the recommendations for EST Licences.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.2.5 Students are given an indication of their result after the official marking. On the recommended course programme, the answers are discussed with the class, so that students gain a idea of where they may have been wrong.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.3 Electronic Scoring Target Control Licences (Category 6)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.3.1 The results are provided to the ISSF Judges Committee annually and the issue of Licences is made after a decision by that committee. No specific application is required, and no separate fee is payable. 9 INSTRUCTORS LICENCE.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.1 The instructors must be highly qualified, be holders of a valid ISSF “A” licence and have regularly conducted and delivered previous courses. Instructors should have attended and passed the ISSF “A” Licence Instructors Workshop and where deemed appropriate acted as an assistant instructor prior to appointment themselves.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.2 The “Instructor’ Licence, authorises the holder to act in all situations as described for “A” Licence holder and for EST instructor licence the holder must have previously passed the EST course with an “A” Grade. The Shotgun instructor licence must have an “A” Licence and confirmed experience as a referee. In addition, Judges in this category are permitted to instruct and conduct official ISSF judge’s courses and Shotgun Referee Courses. In order to achieve this level, selected judges need to have successfully attended an ISSF Instructors Workshop. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 87

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.3  The Judges Committee or the Continental Confederations must nominate their own candidate to participate at the instructor’s workshop, depending on their requirement and need for instructors.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4  The ISSF Instructors workshop will be organised by the ISSF Secretary General and ISSF Judges’ committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5 The ISSF Education programme will be developed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.6  The same support material in English for the Judges’ training course will be given to the instructors.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.7  The support material will explain the objective of the Judges’ training, rules intent and application and will include practical situational and awareness training. 10 APPLICATION FORMS FOR LICENCES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1  For the achievement of its purposes the International Shooting Sport Federation Licences Shotgun Referees to act at ISSF supervised shooting competitions and to ensure the fair and equal treatment of all competitors (ISSF General Regulations). Referees must be experienced and fully conversant with the current versions of the ISSF Shotgun Rules for the respective events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.2  The ISSF issues Shotgun Referees’ licences as confirmation of qualification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3  The ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence is of one (1) category and can be issued in the events Trap (T), and Skeet (S), but only following successful completion of an official ISSF International Shotgun Referees’ Course for all these events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4  The ISSF Headquarters and the Chairperson of the Judges’ Committee maintain a list of all the International Shotgun Referees’ licence holders, in consultation with the Chairperson of the Shotgun Committee. ACQUISITION OF AN INTERNATIONAL SHOTGUN REFEREES’ LICENCE 2 

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1  The applicant must have the necessary capability and experience as a Referee and must be able to speak English.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2  ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licences are not granted to active athletes who still participate in competitions where world records may be established. If the holder of an Shotgun Referees’ licence wishes to participate as an athlete, he must return the licence to the ISSF Headquarters for cancellation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.3  For the acquisition of an ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence, preparatory instruction and training is necessary. The applicants should possess a national Shotgun Referees’ licence of the highest level issued by their National Federation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.4  For the acquisition or renewal of an ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence, the applicant must have passed an eyesight examination.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5  An applicant’s National Federation must sign the completed official ISSF Shotgun Referees’ application form to confirm the contents and support the application. The National Federation must then send it to the ISSF Headquarters with the original eyesight examination form. See forms at the end of these Guidelines.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.6  Applications should be submitted as soon as possible, but no later than 31 December each year for licences to be issued in the following year. In order that applicants are not disadvantaged by any time considerations, once applications are received by ISSF Headquarters, the Chairperson of the Judges’ Committee will endeavour to authorize the issue of licences as soon as possible. This does not negate the requirement for the Judges’ Committee to approve and confirm the granting of these licences at their annual meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.7  The ISSF Judges’ Committee will evaluate and approve appropriate applications, if necessary, with help from the ISSF Medical Committee during its annual meeting. Any queries will be referred to the Shotgun Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.8  After approval, the ISSF Headquarters will issue the Shotgun Referees’ licences. To be valid they must be signed by the ISSF Secretary General and the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges Committee. 2.9 These licences are sent to the National Federations for delivery to the licence holders.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.10  A fee of Euro 50.00 must be paid for a new licence. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 95 VALIDITY AND EXTENSION OF THE LICENCE 3 

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1  All ISSF International Shotgun Referees’ licences are issued for a period of five (5) years.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2  After expiration of this period, the licence may be renewed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3  The National Federation must submit all requests for renewal to the ISSF Headquarters accompanied by a completed Renewal Form (see form at end of Guidelines).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4  The current licence should not be returned when applying for a renewal, though it will cease to be valid after the expiry date. Applications for renewal should be submitted at least three months before expiry.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5  The Chairperson of the Judges’ Committee in co-operation with the ISSF Headquarters and the Chairperson of the Shotgun Committee and in some cases also with a member of the Medical Committee will deal with all renewals. Renewed licences will be returned to the National Federation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.6  A fee of Euro 25.00 will be charged for each renewal. EXPIRATION OF A LICENCE 4 

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.1 When an ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence expires after five (5) years, licence holders will be taken off the ISSF list if not renewed by application within two years. In such a case any future licence must be applied for in accordance with the Acquisition of a licence, including attendance at course(s).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.2  Once a licence has expired for more than two (2) years, the licence holder must follow a refresher training course to validate the licence renewal for five (5) years.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.3 The licence holder’s National Federation, at any time, has the right to apply for cancellation of an ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence. The licence holder may be taken off the list, in such a case the licence must be returned to the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.4 A Shotgun Referees’ licence may be cancelled if an eyesight test shows the licence holder does not meet the required standard any longer, or if a holder does not fulfil his duties as a Referee, or harms the interest or reputation of the ISSF. The holder will be taken off the ISSF list and the licence must be returned to the ISSF. All ISSF International Shotgun Referees’ licences remain the property of the International Shooting Sport Federation. SHOTGUN REFEREES’ COURSES 5 

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1  Only courses that have been approved and recognized by the ISSF will be considered as official training courses for Shotgun Referees. Applications for recognition must be submitted to the ISSF Headquarters using the form “Application for Shotgun Referees’ Courses” (available from ISSF Headquarters). If a course is required in exceptional circumstances at short notice, then the application must be sent to ISSF at least three (3) months before the date of the intended course. All applications and subsequent publication of courses must include the following details:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.1  Where the course will be held;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.2  The dates of the course;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.3  English Language is mandatory;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.4  From which National Federation(s) the Participants will come; Normally, applications will be considered when received from other National Federations 96 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF within the same Continent, but cannot be guaranteed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.5  Name of the Instructor recognised by ISSF Judges’ Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1.6  The expenses that will be met by the National Organiser; (should be equivalent with 5.2.2)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.2  The basis for ISSF Shotgun Referees’ courses is the ISSF Shotgun Referees’ Training Guidelines (as prepared and maintained by the Shotgun Committee). The objective is to ensure that applicants for ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licences have a proper understanding of the Rules, and their application, in respect of the events for which they seek to be licenced as Shotgun Referees. Applicants for ISSF Shotgun Referees’ courses must already possess the highest National licence as a Shotgun official.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.2.1  Every part of the course should commence with an explanation of the purpose and the content of the course, followed by the duties of a Shotgun Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.2.2  The Organizer must pay the costs for travelling, accommodation, meals and local transportation for the instructor(s).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.3  Courses should last a minimum of four (4) days.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.4  The Organizer is responsible for providing a training room with adequate facilities for efficient instruction, and for the comfort of those attending.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.5  A maximum of 15 participants are permitted per instructor.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.5.1  The participants should possess a good background of practical experience as a Shotgun official before attending a course. Participants with little experience must obtain practical experience under the guidance of an experienced Referee in a series of national competitions before applying for an ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.5.2  The Organizer must publish details of the course as early as possible. The announcement must include all details about dates, times, accommodation, meals, local transportation, costs and any other important information.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.5.3  Every participant must be given a registration form to be filled in with his name, address and date of birth. The participant must indicate his experience and any special knowledge he has acquired during competitions in which he acted as an official, and the qualifications obtained in his National Federation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.5.4  Only participants entered by National Federations will be accepted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.6  Participants who complete the course satisfactorily will be issued with ISSF diplomas. ISSF certificates of attendance will not be issued, but organizers are encouraged to provide them.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.7  The ISSF Diploma does not guarantee the issue of an ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.8  At the end of the course the instructor must write and submit a report, using the form “Report Official ISSF Shotgun Referees’ Course” with a list of those attending and those completing the course to the standard required foran ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence stating for which they passed. Where possible the report should indicate whether the individuals already possess sufficient practical experience, or whether further practical experience appears appropriate before an ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence is granted. The report must be sent as soon as possible to the ISSF Headquarters for the attention of the ISSF Secretary General and the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges’ Committee. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 97

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.9  National Federations must request for the ISSF to appoint an instructor licence holder to conduct official ISSF Courses under the terms above and are encouraged to request assistance from the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges’ Committee. Instructors will not normally be appointed from the host country EYESIGHT CERTIFICATES FOR SHOTGUN REFEREES 6 

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1  To ensure that Shotgun Referees are able to carry out their duties in a fair and impartial manner, they must have good eyesight. Accordingly, all Shotgun Referees must have passed an eye and vision examination made by an ophthalmologist or other appropriate medical practitioner.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2  The form shown at the end of these Guidelines must be submitted with the application for a licence. The certificate must not be older than three (3) months when the licence application or licence renewal application is made.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3  All Shotgun Referees must be in possession of an eyesight certificate, which is not more than two (2) years old, when undertaking the duties of a Shotgun Referee at any ISSF competition. Such certificates must be checked by the Chief of Referees before any competition commences.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4 Eyesight Standards

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1  Visual acuity must be 0.7 (equal to 6/9 and 20/30) or better in each eye with or without correction.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.2  The night vision must not be impaired.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3  The colour vision must be normal.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4  There must be no diplopia (double vision).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.5  The binocular visual field must be normal.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.6  Diabetes or any pathological eye conditions that may cause a substantial deterioration in visual acuity or visual field within four (4) years must be notified to the ISSF in order to give the ISSF the possibility to require further investigations or to decide a shorter period of licence validity.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.5  In case of any impairment to the vision of any Shotgun Referee, the Referee must not be allowed to undertake duties until his eyesight is again certified to be at least the minimum standard. SPECIAL ADMINISTRATIVE PROCESS FOR THE ISSUANCE OF 7  SHOTGUN REFEREES’ LICENCES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1  In exceptional cases an ISSF Shotgun Referees’ licence can be issued when it is necessary to ensure there are sufficient qualified personnel at events where world records may be established. For example, when a change of venue is necessary, or when any change of a previously assigned Referee is necessary.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.2  The National Federation must submit an application.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.3  The applications will be considered and decided by the ISSF Secretary General together with the Chairperson of the ISSF Judges’ Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4  Licences issued in this way will be included in the list of licence holders. At the next meeting of the ISSF Judges’ Committee the Chairperson must inform the Committee of any licences granted in this way.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5  Licences issued in this way must only be given to well qualified individuals. The usual standards must be met; only the administrative process is changed. 98 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF APPLICATION FORMS FOR SHOTGUN REFEREES’ LICENCES AND 8  EYESIGHT EXAMINATION FORM AND CERTIFICATE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.1  To simplify the administration of licence issue, the attached forms must be used when applying for a Shotgun Referees’ licence.

Free facilities for firearms and equipment manufactures to service their products must be made available. Firms may rent space for displays at venues where ISSF supervised events

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: and meetings are held. Proposals for promotional and advertisement programmes that involve ISSF participation or endorsement can be submitted by firms. Each programme requires a specific agreement. The ISSF may grant a licence to use the official emblem of the ISSF. This will permit greater promotion of the shooting sport. Advertisers’ requests, specifying detailed proposals and terms, must be submitted to the ISSF Secretary General, who will present them for consideration by the ISSF Executive Committee. All income must be deposited in the ISSF accounts. 2 Public Relations with Media The ISSF intends to have the best possible public relations with the press, radio and TV services in order to achieve extensive media coverage of ISSF Championships and events. To support successful media relations, Organizing Committees must coordinate with the ISSF Communication Manager and provide: •  a press room at the shooting ranges with all modern telecommunication systems, free internet service, telephone, duplication facilities and other appropriate resources;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: • a responsible person to be in charge of the media; • areas where interviews and press conferences can be held with officials, athletes and coaches; • procedures to permit media access to the shooting ranges during the competition for filming and reporting; • procedures to give media personnel reasonable access to athletes and team leaders. 104 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 3 Public Relations with the Community The ISSF desires to establish good relations with members of the public in all communities where ISSF Championships, events and meetings are conducted. In all ISSF Championships, events and meetings, the laws, rules and ecological regulations of the community must be respected. The shooting sport, in the tradition of the Olympic Spirit, must work to create goodwill among all persons. Further details are available in the “Guidelines for Organizing ISSF Championships” and “Guidelines for the Organization of the Media Work”. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 105

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: Article 3.13.3.12, Annex “B” Guidelines for Media Coverage, Broadcasting and Advertising 1 All details about commercial rights including Media Coverage, Broadcasting and Advertising of all ISSF Championships and other ISSF official events (General Assemblies, Congresses etc.) are the property of the International Shooting Sport Federations and further specified in the “ISSF Eligibility, ISSF Commercial Rights and ISSF Sponsorship/Advertising Rules” within this Rule Book. 2 Details about Media Coverage and Broadcasting can be found in the “Guidelines for the Organization of Media Work” available at ISSF Headquarters. 106 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF Article 3.13.3.13, Annex “AC” Athletes Committee Preamble This Annex AC shall set out general provisions regarding the Athletes Committee, its aims and objectives, its structure and composition, the election and appointment of its members and chairperson as well as convening of meetings. This Annex AC shall be read in conjunction with the Athletes Committee Election Regulations which foresees specific

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: provisions on the election and appointment of the Athletes Committee members. 1 AIMS AND OBJECTIVES OF THE ATHLETES COMMITTEE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1  To gather information and opinions from athletes on their needs and problems with regard to the Olympic Games and ISSF Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.2  To voice opinions and make recommendations on these topics and forward them to the relevant bodies of the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3  To establish contact and coordinate activities with the Athletes Committees of other international federations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4  To participate in working groups, to ensure the best possible conditions for the training, accommodation and living conditions for the athletes as well as for the conduct of the competitions at the major international championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5 To support the fight against drugs and doping.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.6 To establish a direct link with the athletes within the ISSF. 2 STRUCTURE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1  The ISSF Athletes Committee must be composed of a Chairperson and nine (9) members, six (6) of them elected by the athletes participating in the ISSF World Championships which are held every four (4) years and three (3) members appointed by the ISSF Executive Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2  In addition to the six (6) elected athletes, three (3) additional athletes (one (1) of each discipline) will be appointed by the ISSF Executive Committee as equal members of the committee in order to guarantee a balance between continents, genders and disciplines.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.3  The elections by the athletes will be held during the World Championships on site or online.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.4  The appointment of three (3) additional members by the ISSF Executive Committee will follow in a meeting after the athletes have elected the six (6) committee members.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.5  To qualify as a candidate, an athlete must never have been found guilty of a doping offence and must have participated in either the last Olympic Games or in the previous or present World Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.6  The Chairperson shall be elected by and from among the nine (9) members of the Athletes Committee. After the election of the Chairperson the athlete with the highest number of votes corresponding to the Chairperson’s discipline shall be adapted as tenth (10th) member of the Athletes Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.7  Athletes Committee members may be re-elected/re-appointed/re-adapted. The term of office shall be in accordance with Article 4.6.3 ISSF Constitution limited EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 107 to a maximum of three (3) consecutive terms of four (4) years provided that the other eligibility criteria as outlined under Article 3.1 of the Election Regulations for the ISSF Athletes Committee are met during the whole term of office.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.8  The Chairperson will become a member of the Executive Committee and will participate in all meetings of the Executive Committee as a representative of the athletes with full voice and vote.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.9 The ISSF Athletes Committee may hold one (1) or two (2) meetings per year. 3 ELECTION PROCEDURE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1  The Nominations Form for Athletes Committee nominees shall be submitted by the ISSF Member Federations to the ISSF Headquarters via email as stated on the Nominations Form no later than one (1) month prior to the opening of the ISSF World Championship/Championships at which the elections are held (if elections are held at more than one ISSF World Championship as determined by the ISSF Executive Committee, the deadline shall end on the date/time one (1) month prior to the opening of the ISSF World Championship whichever is scheduled earlier in the electoral year) as stated on the published Nominations Form. Each Member Federation has a right to nominate only one candidate for election for the Athletes Committee. The Member Federations must indicate on the Nominations Form the shooting discipline of the nominee which she/he shall represent in the Athletes Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2  The ISSF Headquarters will establish a list of all nominated candidates including a brief biography. This list will be published on the ISSF website.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3  With the accreditation of all participating athletes in the World Championships, each athlete entered in the men or women categories will be issued a voting card (either paper or online/digital) showing all candidates and the information on the voting procedure. For online elections, eligible voters will receive a secure digital voting link together with the voting list and instructions on how to cast their vote online.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.4  Each athlete may only vote for a maximum of six (6) candidates (up to two (2) of each discipline) from the voting list.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.5  The two candidates from each discipline with the highest number of votes shall be elected as Athlete Committee members, resulting in six (6) members elected. In case of tie vote the athlete with the higher ISSF ranking at the end of election period shall be elected or/and the athlete who rounds out the gender balance. 4 APPOINTMENT OF THREE ADDITIONAL MEMBERS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.1  The ISSF Executive Committee will appoint three (3) additional members to the Athletes Committee at its next meeting following the election of athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.2  The appointment will be conducted by a selection using the list of all candidates for the election.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.3  After this meeting, the Chairperson of the Athletes Committee will be elected according to Article 2.6 of this Annex. 5 FINANCIAL SITUATION OF THE COMMITTEE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1 In general, the ISSF Member Federation that nominated the elected member has the responsibility of supporting the athlete’s participation in committee meetings according to the Guidelines to the Constitution. 108 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.2 The ISSF Executive Committee will decide on any financial support for the purpose of the meeting and will fix the amount of the daily allowance for each athlete participating in the meeting. 6 METHOD OF COMMUNICATION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1 There will be an official website for the ISSF Athletes Committee within the framework of the ISSF website. The internet can be one of the communication tools.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2 Announcements will be made in the ISSF NEWS magazine. 7 REMARKS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1 Athletes elected or appointed to the Athletes Committee must be aware of their responsibilities as representatives of the athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.2 They must make every effort to attend all meetings.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.3 They should be motivated to contribute to the shooting sport and the Olympic Movement.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4 They should also be responsible for the education of young athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5 They should be educated in respect of positions as representatives, or officials, in both international and national federations during the duration of their appointment as members of the Athletes Committee EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 109 Election Regulations for the ISSF Athletes Committee Preamble Article 14 ISSF Constitution establishes the ISSF Athletes Committee’s composition, its duties and rights. Pursuant to Article 14.5 ISSF Constitution, the Council will establish further election regulations for the Athletes Committee. 1 Composition In accordance with Articles 14.1-3 ISSF Constitution, the composition of the Athletes Committee shall be as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.1 The Athletes Committee consists of 10 (ten) members comprising the Chairperson and nine (9) members of which three (3) must have competed or still compete in shotgun, three (3) in rifle disciplines and three (3) in pistol disciplines.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.2 Six (6) members are elected by the athletes (two (2) of each discipline) in accordance with the procedures as outlined under Article 4.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.3 Three (3) members are appointed by the Executive Committee (one (1) of each discipline) among the remaining candidates running for election considering the gender balance in accordance with Article 1.4, the representation of the Continental Confederations pursuant to Article 1.5 and the number of votes received by the athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.4 The Athletes Committee must have at least four (4) members of each gender.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.5 The Athletes Committee shall consist of at least one athlete from Member Federations of every Continental Confederation. 2 Date and Place of Election

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.1 The election of the six (6) members (two (2) of each discipline) of the Athletes Committee to be elected by the athletes exclusively takes place every four years in the second year of the Olympic cycle at and during the ISSF World Championships in events included in the program of the next Olympic Games. Elections may be conducted online, if decided by the ISSF Executive Committee. Information about the voting procedure, including details for participation in online voting, will be provided to eligible voters in good time.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.2 In the year of election, the ISSF Executive Committee shall determine at least 90 days in advance the specific ISSF World Championships at and during which the elections shall be conducted. The ISSF Executive Committee may also set the period and platforms for online elections, ensuring that eligible voters can participate in the election.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3. Eligibility provisions

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1 In order to be eligible to be elected to the Athletes Commission, a nominee shall:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1.1 be an active athlete or have participated in a shooting competition as defined under 3.1.3,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1.2 have never been sanctioned, or currently under investigation, by the competent body of any national, regional or international sport association for a major disciplinary, ethical or anti-doping offence, 110 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1.3 have participated in either the ISSF World Championships where the previous Athletes Committee elections took place or in at least one of the ISSF Championships following such ISSF World Championships prior to his/her nomination or participates in an ISSF World Championships where election(s) take place and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.1.4 be at least eighteen (18) years old.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2 Athletes are eligible to participate in the Athletes Committee elections if, they:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.1 are at least eighteen (18) years old; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.2.2 participate in the ISSF World Championships at which the elections are held (if elections are held at more than one ISSF World Championships as determined by the ISSF Executive Committee and participation in both World Championships, voting is only allowed at one of these two occasions).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.3 The ISSF Executive Committee approves the composition of the Athletes Committee in its first meeting after the election process has been completed. From thereon, Athletes Committee members shall serve for a term of office until the next elections of the Athletes Committee have been held and approved by the ISSF Executive Committee. Athletes Committee members may be re-elected/re-appointed/re-adapted. The term of office shall be in accordance with Article 4.6.3 ISSF Constitution limited to a maximum of three (3) consecutive terms of four (4) years provided that the other eligibility criteria as outlined under Article 3.1 are met during the whole term of office.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4. Procedural provisions

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.1 Nominations The Nominations Form (see Annex 1) for Athletes Committee nominees shall be submitted by the ISSF Member Federations to the ISSF Headquarters via email as stated on the Nominations Form no later than one (1) month prior to the opening of the ISSF World Championship/Championships at which the elections are held (if elections are held at more than one ISSF World Championship as determined by the ISSF Executive Committee, the deadline shall end on the date/time one (1) month prior to the opening of the ISSF World Championship whichever is scheduled earlier in the electoral year) as stated on the published Nominations Form. Each Member Federation has a right to nominate only one candidate for election for the Athletes Committee. The Member Federations must indicate on the Nominations Form the shooting discipline of the nominee which she/he shall represent in the Athletes Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.2 List of candidates The ISSF Headquarters will establish a list of all nominated eligible candidates. This list will also be published on the ISSF Website.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.3 Voting

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.3.1 Every athlete eligible to cast a vote in accordance with Article 3.2 may vote for a up to six (6) candidates (up to two (2) of each discipline) from the voting list. Proxy is not allowed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.3.2 The election shall be conducted by secret ballot on site or online, depending on the decision of the ISSF Executive Committee. The online voting system shall be designed to ensure confidentiality and security of the votes. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 111

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.3.3 The voting process on site will be supervised by two scrutineers, one of each gender, to be appointed by the ISSF Executive Committee. For online voting, a designated team of digital scrutineers will be responsible for overseeing the voting process, ensuring that all votes are cast securely and confidentially.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.4 Members elected The two candidates from each discipline with the highest number of votes shall be elected as Athlete Committee members, resulting in six (6) members elected. In case of tie vote the athlete with the higher ISSF ranking at the end of election period shall be elected or/and the athlete who rounds out the gender balance.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.5 Appointment Procedure Three (3) members shall be appointed by the ISSF Executive Committee in accordance with Article 1.3 at its first meeting after the Athletes Committee elections.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6 Election of the Chairperson and adopted member

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6.1 The Chairperson shall be elected by and from among the nine (9) members of the Athletes Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.6.2 After the election of the Chairperson the athlete with the highest number of votes from the election results pursuant to Section 2 corresponding to the Chairperson’s discipline shall be adopted as the tenth (10th) member of the Athletes Committee mandatorily taking into account Articles 1.4 and 1.5.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5. Final Provisions

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.1 The provisions of the ISSF Constitution concerning the Committees shall additionally apply (see Article 14.7 ISSF Constitution) without prejudice to the more specific constitutional provisions governing the Athletes Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 5.2 These regulations shall come into force upon approval of the ISSF Council in accordance with Article 14.5 ISSF Constitution and may be amended by the ISSF Council. 112 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF Annex 1 Nomination form for candidates ‘Member of the ISSF Athletes Committee’ All proposals have to be received by the ISSF Headquarters by no later than … Please return by email to office@issf-sports.org ISSF Member Country Federation Family Name First Name ISSF ID Number Date of birth: Day Month Year Address City Country Street Phone Email Athlete pursuant to Article 3.1.1 Election Regulations in the following disciplines Rifle  Pistol  Shotgun  Running Target 
