chunks.text: 6.1 GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1.1 Objective and Purpose of ISSF Rules The ISSF establishes Technical Rules for the shooting sport to govern the conduct of shooting events recognized by the ISSF (ISSF General Regulations, 3). The objective of ISSF Technical Rules is to achieve uniformity in the conduct of the ISSF Championships and those Competitions authorised by the ISSF. Olympic Games shooting events are authorised by the IOC. They apply to shooting sport throughout the world and to promote the development of the sport.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) ISSF General Technical Rules include rules for range construction, targets, scoring and specific competition procedures for all shooting disciplines. Discipline Rules apply specifically to the five (5) shooting disciplines: Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun, Moving Target and Target Sprint;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) ISSF General Technical and Discipline Rules are approved by the ISSF Council in accordance with the ISSF Constitution;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) ISSF General Technical and Discipline Rules are subordinate to the ISSF Constitution and the ISSF General Regulations; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) ISSF General Technical and Discipline Rules are approved to be effective for a period of four (4) years beginning on 1 January of the year following the Olympic Games. Except in special situations, ISSF Rules are not changed during this four (4) year period.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1.2 Application of ISSF General Technical and Discipline Rules

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) ISSF Championships are shooting sport competitions in the Olympic Games, World Championships, World Cups, World Cup Finals, Continental Championships, Continental Games, Junior World Championships and Junior World Cups that are supervised by the ISSF in accordance with the ISSF General Regulations, 3.2.1, and these Rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The ISSF, with the approval of the Executive Committee, may designate other competitions that fulfil ISSF standards for supervision (i.e. Technical Delegate, Juries, doping control, entry procedures, results management, etc.) as competitions where Minimum Qualification Score/Ranking Points Only (MQS/ RPO) scores may be obtained and where World Records may be established, for instance, Grand Prix competitions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) ISSF General Technical and Discipline Rules must govern all ISSF Championships;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The ISSF recommends that ISSF Rules should also be used to govern regional, national and other competitions that are not ISSF Championships, but where ISSF events are on the programme;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) All competition officials, athletes, coaches and team leaders must be familiar with the ISSF Rules and must ensure that they are enforced;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) It is the responsibility of every athlete to comply with these Rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) When a Rule refers to right-handed athletes, the reverse of that Rule applies to left-handed athletes; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Unless a Rule applies specifically to a men’s or women’s event, it must apply uniformly to both men’s and women’s events. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 189

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Where diagrams and tables in these rules contain specific information, the specific information in these diagrams and tables has the same authority as the numbered rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1.3 Scope of ISSF Technical Rules ISSF Technical Rules include:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Rules for the preparation and organization of ISSF Championships;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Rules that apply to all shooting disciplines or more than one shooting discipline (General Technical Rules); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Rules that apply to one shooting discipline (Special Technical Rules).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1.4 Uniform Standard for Equipment and Clothing Shooting is a sport where equipment and clothing play critical roles in the conduct of the sport. Athletes must use only equipment and clothing that complies with ISSF Rules. Any gun, device, equipment, accessory or other item that may give an athlete an unfair advantage over others and that is not specifically mentioned in these Rules, or that is contrary to the spirit of these Rules, is prohibited. ISSF Rules for equipment and clothing are strictly enforced (see 6.7.9) to ensure that no athletes have equipment, clothing or accessories that give them an unfair advantage over other athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1.5 Organization and Supervision of ISSF Championships

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1.5.1 ISSF Supervision. The ISSF Executive Committee appoints ISSF Technical Delegates, Jury Members and technical officials for every ISSF Championship in accordance with 1.8.2.6 and 3.4. These appointments include:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Technical Delegate(s);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Competition/Equipment Control/RTS Juries;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) A Jury of Appeal may be appointed, otherwise the Technical Delegate can appoint a Jury of Appeal as and when required.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) An Official Results Provider responsible for providing and operating the electronic technology necessary for the management of entries, athletes’ results, competition operations, results presentation and results archiving.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The ISSF may appoint International Referees to assist local Referees.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.1.5.2 Organizing Committee. An Organizing Committee must be formed for every ISSF Championship in accordance with 3.4.1. The Organizing Committee is responsible for the preparation, administration and conduct of the shooting competitions. The Organizing Committee must, in cooperation with the ISSF, appoint:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Chief Range Officer(s), Range Officers, a Chief of Referees and Referees, as appropriate, who are responsible for the actual conduct of the shooting events;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A Chief RTS (Results Timing and Scoring) Officer and necessary assistants to establish a RTS Office responsible for entries, accreditation, scoring and results operations during the Championship;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) A Chief of Equipment Control and appropriate Equipment Control Officers who are responsible for Equipment Control operations; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) All other staff necessary to fulfil their responsibilities as an ISSF Championship Organizer. 190 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2 SAFETY SAFETY IS OF PARAMOUNT IMPORTANCE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.1 General Safety Rules

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.1.1 ISSF Rules establish specific safety requirements that must be applied in all ISSF Championships. ISSF Juries and Organizing Committees are responsible for safety.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.1.2 Necessary and special safety regulations for ranges differ from country to country so additional safety rules may be established by the Organizing Committee. Juries, range officials, team officials and athletes must be advised of any special safety regulations in the competition programme.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.1.3 The safety of athletes, range workers, officials and spectators, requires continued and careful attention to gun handling. It is the duty of range officials to enforce gun safety and the duty of athletes and team officials to apply all gun safety and gun handling rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.1.4 Safety precautions shall also include: Safe food, hand washing and potable water availability for all attendees at the event; athletes and range officials schedules must be managed to ensure the prevention of heat exhaustion or hypothermia.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.1.5 The ISSF may refuse to accept the entry of an athlete in a competition if it has substantial information from competent authorities that such an athlete presents a serious threat to the safety of others on a shooting range.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.1.6 In the interest of safety, a Jury Member, Referee or Range Officer may stop shooting at any time. Athletes and team officials must immediately notify Range Officers, Jury Members or Referees of any situation that may be dangerous.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.1.7 An Equipment Control Officer, Range Officer or Jury Member may pick up an athlete’s equipment (including a gun) for control without his permission, but in his presence and with his knowledge. However, immediate action must be taken when a matter of safety is involved.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.2 Gun Handling Rules

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.2.1 To ensure safety, all guns must be handled with maximum care at all times. Guns must not be removed from the firing line during training or competition except with the permission of a Range Officer.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.2.2 Safety flags constructed of fluorescent orange or a similar bright material must be inserted in all rifles and pistols at all times except when safety flag removal is authorized by these rules. To demonstrate that air guns are unloaded, safety flags (safety lines) must be long enough to extend through the full length of the barrel. Safety flags for all other guns must have a probe that inserts into the chamber (breech end of barrel) to demonstrate that the chamber is empty. Shotgun actions must be open to demonstrate that they are unloaded. Even when shotguns are on a rack.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Safety flags must be inserted in all Rifles and Pistols that are not in gun cases or boxes before athletes are called to the line, when leaving a firing point, after firing is completed and when personnel must go forward of the firing line. In Finals, safety flags may not be removed until Preparation and Sighting Times start. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 191

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If a safety flag is not used as required by this rule, or a Shotgun is not open, a Jury Member must give a WARNING with instructions to insert a safety flag in the gun or to open the Shotgun; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the Jury confirms that an athlete refuses to use a safety flag, or to open a Shotgun, as required by this rule and after being warned, the athlete must be disqualified (DSQ).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.2.3 While athletes are on their firing points, their guns must always be pointed in safe directions. The action or breech must not be closed until the gun is pointing downrange in a safe direction toward the target area.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.2.4 When placing a gun down to leave the firing point or when firing is complete, or when a shotgun round is completed, guns must be unloaded with actions (bolt or locking mechanism) open and safety flags inserted. Before leaving a firing point, or the shooting range, the athlete must confirm and the Range Officer or Referee must verify that there is no cartridge or pellet in the gun’s chamber, barrel or magazine and a safety flag is inserted, or the Shotgun is open.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.2.5 If the athlete boxes or cases his gun or removes it from the firing point without having it checked by a Range Officer, he may be disqualified if the Jury determines that a significant safety violation is involved.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.2.6 During firing, the gun may be put down (not held) only after the cartridge(s) and/ or magazine are removed and the action or the Shotgun is open. Air guns must be made safe by opening the cocking lever or loading port.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.2.7 When any personnel are forward of the firing line, or the shooting stations, handling guns is not permitted, safety flags must be inserted and Shotguns must be unloaded and open. If it is necessary for a Jury member, Range Officer or Technical Officer to go forward of the firing line during training, competition or a Final, this must be authorized and controlled by the Chief Range Officer (CRO) and any movement forward of the firing line may only be permitted after all guns have safety flags inserted, or in the case of Shotguns, they must be unloaded and open.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.2.8 In the range, when guns are not on the firing points or shooting stations, they must always be in their cases, or in the gun rack, unless otherwise authorized by a Range Officer, Referee or Jury.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.3 Range Commands

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.3.1 Chief Range Officers, Referees, or other appropriate range officials, are responsible for giving the commands “LOAD,” “START,” “STOP,” “UNLOAD” and other necessary commands. Range Officers or Referees must ensure that the commands are obeyed and that guns are handled safely.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.3.2 Guns and their magazines may only be loaded on the firing point, shotguns at the shooting station, and after the command “LOAD”, “START” or “READY” is given. At all other times, shotguns, guns and magazines must be kept unloaded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.3.3 Only one cartridge may be loaded in a Rifle or 50m Pistol event if it has a magazine. If a 5-shot Air Pistol is used in a 10m Air Pistol event only one pellet may be loaded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.3.4 A gun is considered loaded when a cartridge, pellet, a magazine with cartridges or and empty shotgun cartridge contacts a gun. No one may place a cartridge or pellet or magazine with cartridges in or on a gun or its chamber or barrel until the command “LOAD” is given, or until the athlete is in his shooting station and is his turn to fire. 192 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.3.5 If an athlete fires a shot before the command “LOAD” or “START” is given, or after the command “STOP”, or “UNLOAD” is given, he may be disqualified if safety is involved.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.3.6 When the command or signal “STOP” is given, shooting must stop immediately. When the command “UNLOAD” is given, all athletes must unload their guns and magazines, and make them safe (to unload air guns ask the Range Officer for permission). Shooting may only resume when the command “START”, or “READY” is given again.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.4 Additional Safety Requirements Dry Firing is the release of the cocked trigger mechanism of an unloaded

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.4.1  cartridge gun or the release of the trigger mechanism of an air or gas gun fitted with a device which enables the trigger to be operated without releasing the propelling charge (air or gas). Dry firing and aiming exercises are permitted only on the firing line or in a designated area and direction in accordance with these rules. If an athlete is found to be dry firing in a non designated area, or wrong direction, he may be disqualified for safety reasons with the majority decision of the Jury. Jury members must always make sure that athletes are not test firing in any non-designated dry firing areas.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.4.2 It is the athlete’s responsibility to ensure that any air or CO2 cylinder is still within its validity date. This may be checked by Equipment Control.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.5 Hearing Protection

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.5.1 All athletes, range officials and other persons in the immediate vicinity of the 25m, 50m and 300m firing lines and all Shotgun ranges must wear ear plugs, ear muffs, or similar ear protection. Notices must be prominently displayed and hearing protection must be available for all persons in the range areas. Hearing protection incorporating any type of sound-enhancing or receiving devices may not be worn by athletes or coaches on the FOP. Competition officials may wear sound-enhancing hearing protection devices or other communication devices on the FOP. Hearing impaired athletes may wear sound-enhancing devices with the approval of the Jury.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.5.2 If a shotgun athlete is found in his shooting station ready to shoot without the hearing protection, The athlete will receive a warning by the referee in charge (yellow card) for the first violation and for the second violation during any round in the competition or PET, a deduction of 1 Target will be imposed (green card) by the referee in charge (The first target hit in the round will be LOST).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.2.6 Eye Protection All Shotgun athletes must wear shatterproof shooting glasses or similar eye protection while shooting. See Rule 9.2.7 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 193

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3 TARGETS AND TARGET STANDARDS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.1 General Target Requirements

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.1.1 Targets used in ISSF Championships may be either electronic scoring targets (EST) or paper targets for Rifle and Pistol events or clay targets (normal or flash) for Shotgun events. Note: Specific Rules for paper target operations are now available in the Annex to these Rules, Rules for Paper Target Scoring.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.1.2 All targets used in ISSF Championships must comply with the scoring ring, dimension or other specifications given in these rules and must be approved by the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.1.3 Random checks during the competition will be done by an ISSF representative or by the ISSF TD.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.2 Electronic Scoring Target Requirements

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.2.1 Only EST tested and approved by the ISSF must be used.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.2.2 The accuracy requirement for EST is to score shots to an accuracy of at least one-half of one decimal scoring ring. The tolerances given for scoring ring sizes on paper targets are not applicable to EST.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.2.3 All EST target units must provide a black aiming area corresponding in size to the black areas of the respective competition targets (Rule 6.3.4) and a non- reflective, contrasting white or off-white area surrounding the aiming area.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.2.4 Scores recorded by EST must be determined according to scoring ring dimensions for competition targets (Rule 6.3.4).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.2.5 Every shot hitting an EST must have its result with its location and value displayed on a monitor placed on the firing point.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.2.6 10m EST must use a paper strip or other form of witness strip to allow a determination that a shot fired did, or did not, hit the target.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.2.7 A printout of each athlete’s results from a memory source other than the main EST system computer (back-up memory) must be available immediately during and after a competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.2.8 When EST are used, the targets must be checked to ensure the targets are scoring correctly under normal conditions of use before each ISSF Championship under the supervision of the Technical Delegate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.3 ISSF Target Standards Targets must comply with the scoring ring dimensions, tolerances and specifications in this rule.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.3.1 Rifle and Pistol targets may be scored in full ring values or, if ESTs or electronic paper target scoring machines are used, in decimal ring values. Decimal ring scores are determined by dividing the scoring area for one full ring into ten equal scoring rings that are designated with decimal values starting with zero (i.e. 10.0, 9.0, etc.) and ending with nine (i. e. 10.9, 9.9, etc.);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.3.2 Rifle and Pistol Elimination and Qualification Round competitions are scored in full ring values, except that in ISSF Championships, Elimination and Qualification Round competitions for 10m Air Rifle Men and Men Junior, 10m Air Rifle Women and Women Junior, 50m Rifle Prone Men and Men Junior and 50m Prone Women and Women Junior, 10m Air Rifle Mixed Team and Mixed Team Junior events must be scored in decimal values. 194 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.3.3 Rifle and Pistol Finals, Rifle Mixed Team Qualification and Finals and Pistol Mixed Team Finals are scored in decimal values, except that 25m Pistol Finals use hit- miss scoring with hit zones based on decimal values established by these Rules.

chunks.text: 6.3.5 Target Control Systems For Rifle and Pistol events, target marking and control systems must be used to facilitate the conduct of competitions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.5.1 EST Target Control Systems Backing Targets, Backing Cards and Control Sheets are used as control systems for ESTs (see diagram). 204 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.5.2 Backing Targets for 50m and 300m ESTs To locate cross-shots, backing targets must, if possible, be placed 0.5m – 1.0m behind the targets. The exact distance between the target and the backing target must be measured and recorded and, as far as possible, be the same for all targets.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.5.3 Backing Targets for 25m ESTs

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Backing targets must be used for all 25m Pistol events to assist in the identification of shots that may have missed the targets;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Backing targets must, at a minimum, cover the entire width and height of the 25m frames (5 targets). They should be located a uniform distance of one (1) meter behind the competition targets. They must be continuous, or on adjoining frames, without any spaces between them, to register any shots between competition targets;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Backing targets for 25m ESTs must be made of non-reflecting paper of a neutral colour similar to the colour of the target; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) For 25m events, new backing targets must be provided for each athlete for each stage.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.5.4 Control Sheets for 25m ESTs The area immediately behind the ESTs must be covered by control sheets. New control sheets must be provided for each athlete for each stage. If the location of any shot hole is outside of the control sheet, the geometric relation between the shot holes on the control sheet and the backing card must be noted before the control sheet is removed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.5.5 Backing Cards and Control Sheets for 50m and 300m ESTs A backing card must be affixed to the rear of all 50m and 300m ESTs. Smaller, replaceable control sheets should be affixed to the backing cards. The control sheets or backing cards must be renewed and collected after each relay. If the location of any shot hole is outside of the control sheet, the geometric relation between the shot holes on the control sheet and the backing card must be noted before the control sheet is removed. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 205

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.3.6 Clay Targets for Shotgun Events Diameter: 110mm (±1mm). Height: 25mm to 26mm. Weight: 105g (±5g). The colour of the targets may be all black, all white, all yellow, or all orange; The target colour must be clearly visible against the range background under all normal light conditions. The same colour and same make of targets must be used for training. The clay target colour must be specified in the programme of each ISSF Championship with Shotgun events. Clay targets used in all ISSF supervised Championships and Competitions must be approved by the ISSF and will be eco-friendly targets that comply with appropriate international standards (contact ISSF Headquarters for details).

chunks.text: 6.3.6.2 “Flash” Targets

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) In Shotgun Finals, “Flash” targets containing coloured, non-toxic powder that contrasts with the range background must be used.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) In Shotgun Qualification Rounds, “Flash” targets containing ISSF approved non-toxic, coloured powder may be used.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If a target of the same external colour as those used in the competition, but containing the incorrect coloured powder, is inadvertently thrown, the results of any shot at that target must be recorded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.text: 6.4 RANGES AND OTHER FACILITIES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1 General Requirements

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.1 Requirements for minimum range sizes for ISSF Championships are given in Rule 3.6.1. While those requirements are the minimum, the practical requirement for Shotgun World Championships and large World Cups is that five (5) ranges are recommended. For large Rifle/Pistol World Cups, 80 10m and 80 50m firing points are recommended.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.2 A separate Rifle/Pistol Finals Range is required for World Championships and the Olympic Games. The ISSF recommends that a separate Finals Range be available for World Cups.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.3 Continental Confederations must establish minimum range requirements for Continental Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.4 Trap and Skeet ranges may be combined. If possible, Trap and Skeet Finals should be conducted on the same Range.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.5 The area used by athletes, officials and spectators on Rifle and Pistol ranges must be covered to provide protection from sun, wind and rain. This protection must not give a significant advantage to any firing point or part of the range.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.6 The ISSF recommends that all new ranges be accessible to disabled persons. Existing ranges should be adapted to make them accessible to disabled persons.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.7 It is recommended that ranges used for World Championships and Olympic Games be completed at least one (1) year in advance.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.8 Electronic target systems (EST) of makes and models approved by the ISSF must be used for Rifle and Pistol Eliminations, Qualifications and Finals in the Olympic Games, ISSF World Championships and in ISSF World Cups. Electronic target systems must include monitors or video boards that display individual shots and scores for spectators as well as displays that show ranked incomplete results during the competitions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.9 Technical Delegates are responsible for examining the ranges and other facilities to ensure that they comply with ISSF Rules and are prepared for the conduct of the Championship. Technical Delegates should use the Checklist for Technical Delegates to examine the organization, ranges and facilities (available from ISSF Headquarters). EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 207

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.1.10 A Technical Delegate may approve small deviations from specifications in ISSF Rules that do not conflict with the intent and spirit of ISSF Rules, except that no deviations in shooting distances or target specifications are allowed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.2 General and Administrative Facilities The following facilities must be provided on or near the shooting ranges: a) Athlete rest areas;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Changing rooms for athletes near the Finals and Qualification Ranges;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Meeting rooms for use by ISSF officials and Juries;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Rooms for Organizing Committee offices and administration;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) A room with adequate storage for RTS (results, timing and scoring) operations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Control rooms on each range for RTS (results, timing and scoring) and results provider operations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Dry firing or warm-up areas for all rifle, pistol and shotgun ranges;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) All 10m Ranges must have a supply of compressed air that is accessible to athletes and coaches; compressed air tanks must be securely fastened to a wall or other structure so they cannot be tipped over;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) One Main Scoreboard for posting official results and notices, and smaller Range Scoreboards on each range for posting competition schedules and preliminary results; a scoreboard should also be placed in the athletes rest area;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) An armoury for secure arms storage;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) An equipment control testing area, with changing rooms;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) A gunsmith’s shop with suitable work benches and vices;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: m) Free facilities for firearms and equipment manufacturers to service their products;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: n) An area for commercial displays should be available; a fee may be charged for such displays;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: o) A restaurant or facilities for safe food service and refreshments;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: p) Adequate toilet and hand washing facilities;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: q) Wireless Internet and email communication services; separate internet services must be provided for operations (results services, ISSF TV, administration) and for the public;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: r) A Medal Ceremony area or a portable Medal Ceremony podium and backdrop that can be set up on the Finals Range;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: s) Facilities for media, radio and television representatives;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: t) Facilities for Anti-Doping testing, with toilets;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: u) Appropriate medical facilities; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: v) Parking facilities.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: w) Athlete’s preparation area near the shotgun final range 208 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3 General Standards for 10m, 25m, 50m and 300m Rifle and Pistol Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.1 New 25m, 50m and 300m outdoor ranges should be constructed in such a way that the sun is behind the athlete as much as possible during the competition day. The range design must ensure that there are no shadows on the targets.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.2 Ranges must have a line of targets and a firing line. The firing line must be parallel to the line of targets.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.3 The design and construction of the range may provide the following features:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a). The range may, if necessary, be surrounded by safety walls;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Protection against the exit of accidental or unaimed shots from the range may be provided by transverse baffle systems between the firing line and the line of targets;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c). 10m ranges must be indoor ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) 25m and 50m ranges should, whenever possible, be outdoor ranges, but may, exceptionally, be indoor or closed ranges if required by legal or climatic conditions; or Finals Hall.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) 300m ranges should have at least 285m open to the sky;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) 50m ranges should have at least 35m open to the sky;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g). 25m ranges should have at least 12.5m open to the sky; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) 25m and 50m Finals ranges may be indoor or outdoor ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.4 There must be sufficient space behind the firing points for the range officials and the Jury to perform their duties. There must also be a space provided for spectators. This area must be separated from the area for athletes and officials by a suitable barrier located at least 7.0m behind the firing line.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.5 Each range must be equipped with a large clock (a countdown clock is recommended) at each end of the range where the time can clearly be seen by athletes and officials. The Finals Range preparation area must also have a clock. Range clocks must be synchronized with results computers so that all timing devices show the same time. Rifle and Pistol Finals Ranges must have a count- down timer that shows the time remaining for each shot. Shotgun Ranges must have a count-down timer to use in controlling preparation times.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.3.6 Target frames or mechanisms must be marked with numbers (starting from the left) corresponding to their firing point number. The numbers must be large enough to easily be seen by persons with normal vision under normal conditions. The numbers should be of alternating and contrasting colours. On 25m targets, each group of five (5) targets must be lettered, starting with the A group on the left. 25m targets must also be individually numbered using numbers 11-20 for the targets in groups A and B, numbers 21-30 for groups C and D, etc.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4 Wind Flags for 50m Ranges and 300m Rifle Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.1 Rectangular wind flags, which indicate air movements on the range, should be made of a cotton or polyester material weighing approximately 150 g/m². Wind flag height must correspond with the central area of the bullets’ flight paths without interfering with the bullet flight paths or athletes’ views of the targets. The colour of the wind flags must contrast with the background. Dual colour or striped wind flags are permitted and recommended. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 209

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.2 Wind Flag Dimensions and Locations Ranges Distances Size of Flag 50m Ranges 10m and 30m 50mm x 400mm 300m Ranges 50m 50mm x 400mm 100m and 200m 200mm x 750mm

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.3 On 50m ranges, wind flags are to be placed at fixed distances from the firing line, on imaginary lines separating each firing point and its corresponding target from the adjacent points and targets. Flags must be placed on the athlete’s side of any safety baffle supports.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.4 If a 50m range is also used as a 10m enclosed range the 10m wind flags must be placed far enough down range so that they give an accurate indication of the wind.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.5 On 300m ranges, wind flags are to be placed at the above distances from the firing line on imaginary lines separating every fourth (4th) firing point and its corresponding target from the next point and target. Flags must be placed on the athlete’s side of any safety baffle supports.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.6 Athletes must check the wind flags before the Preparation and Sighting Time starts to be sure they do not obscure their targets. Only Range Officers or Jury Members may reposition wind flags.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.4.7 Private wind indicators and the repositioning of wind flags by athletes are prohibited. 210 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.5 Shooting Distances

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.5.1 Shooting distances must be measured from the firing line to the target face.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.5.2 Shooting distances must be as exact as possible, subject to the following allowable variations. 10m Range ±0.05m 25m Range ±0.10m 50m Range ±0.20m 300m Range ±1.00m 10m Moving Target Range ±0.05m 50m Moving Target Range ±0.20m

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.5.3 In combined 50m Rifle, Pistol and Moving Target ranges, the allowable variation can be increased to +2.50m for Moving Target. The opening must be accordingly adjusted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.5.4 The firing line must be clearly marked. The range distance must be measured from the target line to the edge of the firing line nearest to the athlete. The athlete’s foot or, in the prone position the athlete’s elbow may not be placed on or in front of the firing line.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.6 Target Centre Locations Target centre locations must be measured to the centre of the ten (10) ring.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.6.1 Height of Target Centres Target centres must be within the following heights when measured from the level of the firing point floor: Range Standard Height Variation Allowable 10m 1.40m ±0.05m 25m 1.40m +0.10m/-0.20m 50m 0.75m ±0.50m 300m 3.00m ±4.00m 10m Moving Target 1.40m ±0.05m 50m Moving Target 1.40m ±0.20m All target centres within a group of targets or range must have the same height (±1cm). EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 211

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.6.2 Horizontal Variations for Target Centres on 300m, 50m and 10m Rifle and Pistol Ranges Target centres at 300m, 50m, and 10m must be oriented on the centre of the corresponding firing point. Horizontal deviations from a centre line drawn perpendicular (90 degrees) to the centre of the firing point are: Range Maximum variation from centre in either direction 10m 0.25m 50m 0.75m 300m 6.00m

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.6.3 Horizontal Variations for Firing Points on 50m and 10m Moving Target and 25m Pistol Ranges The centre of the firing points must be located as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) For Rapid-Fire ranges, according to the centre of the group of five (5);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) For Moving Target ranges, according to the centre of the opening; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c)The centre of the firing point must be oriented on the centre of the corresponding target or opening. Maximum horizontal deviations from a centre line drawn perpendicular (90 degrees) to the centre of the target or opening are: Range Maximum variation in either direction 10m Moving Target 0.40m 25m 0.75m 50m Moving Target 2.00m

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.7 General Firing Point Standards for Rifle and Pistol Ranges The firing point must be stable, rigid and constructed so that it does not vibrate or move. From the firing line to approximately 1.20m rearward, the firing point must be level in all directions. The remainder of the firing point must either be level or may slope to the rear with a few centimetres drop.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.7.1 If shooting is done from tables, the tables must be approximately 2.20m long and 0.8m to 1.00m wide, rigid, stable and removable. Shooting tables may slope to the rear a maximum of 10cm.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.7.2 Firing Point Equipment. Firing points must be equipped with:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) A bench or stand, 0.70m – 1.00m high; rifle athletes may not place any item or material on the table to change its height;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A mat for shooting in the prone and kneeling positions. Athletes must not alter shooting mats provided by the range. The front portion of the mat must be of a compressible material not more than 50mm thick, and approximately 50cm x 80cm in size and measuring not less than 10mm when compressed with the measuring device used to measure the thickness of Rifle clothing. The remainder of the mat must have a maximum thickness of 50mm and a 212 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF minimum thickness of 2mm. The minimum overall size must be 80cm x 200cm. An alternative of two mats is permitted, one thick and one thin, but together they must not exceed the dimensions indicated. The use of private mats is prohibited;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) A chair or stool for the athlete on Qualification ranges; no chairs or stools for athletes may be placed on or near the firing points on Finals ranges;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) On new ranges, wind screens forward of the firing line are not recommended, but when necessary to ensure that wind conditions are as equal as possible throughout the range, wind screens may be used; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) When it is necessary to install dividing screens on the 300m firing line, they should be made of transparent material on a light frame. Screens should extend at least 50cm forward of the firing line, and be approximately 2.00m high.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.8 Firing Point Standards for 300m Ranges The size of the firing point must not be less than 1.60m wide x 2.50m long. The width of the firing point may be reduced only if any dividing screens are constructed so that an athlete in the prone position can place his left leg in an adjacent firing point without disturbing that athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.9 Firing Point Standards for 50m Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The firing point must be a minimum of 1.25m wide x 2.50m in length and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If the firing point is also used for 300m shooting, the firing point must be a minimum of 1.60m wide.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.10 Range and Firing Point Standards for 10m Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The firing point must be a minimum of 1.00m

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The nearest edge of the bench or stand must be placed 10cm forward of the 10m firing line; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the firing point is also used for 50m shooting, the firing point must be a minimum of 1.25m wide.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11 Range and Firing Point Standards for 25m Pistol Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.1 Roofs and screens of 25m ranges must provide the athlete with adequate shelter from wind, rain, sun and ejected cartridge cases.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.2 The firing point must be roofed or covered at a minimum height of 2.20m above the level of the firing point.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.3 25m ranges must be divided into sections that are composed of two (2) groups of five (5) targets. Two (2) of five (5) targets are one bay.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.4 In 25m events, athletes must be squadded with one athlete in each group of five (5) targets for the Rapid-Fire Pistol event, and with four (4) (targets 1-2- 4-5), three (3) (targets 1-3-5) or exceptionally five (5) (all targets) athletes in a group of five (5) targets for the 25m Pistol, 25m Centre Fire Pistol and 25m Standard Pistol events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.5 25m ranges may be either open or divided by protected walkways. In open ranges, target officers move from the firing line area to the targets. Protected walkways, if used, must allow range staff to safely move to and from the target line. When protected walkways are used, a secure safety control system must be available. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 213

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.6 Range Sections should be capable of being operated centrally and of being operated independently.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.7 Firing point or shooting station dimensions must be: Event Width Depth 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol 1.50m 1.50m 25m Pistol 25m 1.00m 1.50m Centre Fire Pistol 1.00m 1.50m 25m Standard Pistol 1.00m 1.50m

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.8 Firing points must be separated by small transparent screens that protect athletes from ejected cartridge cases and permit visibility of athletes by officials. The screens must be placed or hung next to the pistol locations and be large enough to prevent ejected cartridge cases from hitting other athletes. The screens must not obscure the officials’ and spectators’ views of the athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.9 45-degree reference lines should be placed on range walls or section dividers to the left or right of the firing points.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.10 Each firing point must be provided with the following equipment:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) A removable or adjustable bench or table, approximately 0.50m x 0.60m in size and 0.70m to 1.00m high;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) In Qualification competitions, athletes may place items or support stands on a table to increase the table to a maximum height of 1.00m;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) In Finals competitions, pistol athletes may place an adjustable support stand (8.6.3) on the table provided the total table height with stand does not exceed

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.0m; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) A chair or stool for the athlete on Qualification ranges; no chairs or stools for athletes may be placed on or near the firing points on Finals ranges;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.11.11 Function Firing Range. A specially designated and supervised function firing range, without targets, must be provided for athletes to test guns.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.12 Exposure Times for 25m Pistol Events are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol: 8, 6 and 4 seconds;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) 25m Standard Pistol: 150, 20 and 10 seconds; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol Rapid-Fire Stage: Facing for three (3) seconds for each shot, alternating with an edge-on face away time of seven (7) seconds (±0.1 second).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.13 Standards for 25m Electronic Scoring Target Systems When electronic scoring targets are used, the timing equipment must be set to add a total of 0.3 seconds to each established scoring time. This includes the established firing time +0.1 second (tolerance) plus an after-time of +0.2 second. The after-time ensures that shots that would have been valid skid- shots on paper turning targets, are scored according to the same standard on electronic targets. The green lights remain on for the required time +0.1 sec. and the electronic target must continue to record and score valid shots for an additional 0.2sec. after-time. Many 25m EST systems now have both the red and green light display positioned at the top of the target frame. 214 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.14 Indoor Range Light Requirements (Lux) Type of Indoor General Lighting Target Lighting Range Recommended Minimum Minimum Recommended 10m 500 1500 >1800 10m RT 500 1000 >1000 25m 500 1500 >2500 50m 500 1500 >3000 Finals Ranges must have a minimum general lighting of 500 lux and minimum of 1000 lux on the firing line. For new ranges lighting of about 1500 lux on the firing line is recommended.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.14.1 All indoor ranges must have artificial illumination providing the necessary amount of light without glare or distracting shadows on the targets or firing points. The background area behind the targets must be a non-reflecting, light even neutral colour.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.14.2 Measuring target illumination on targets with external lighting must be done with the measuring device held at the level of the target and pointed toward the firing point (A). Measuring target illumination on targets with internal lighting must be done by measuring reflected light from the target face. Approved EST systems that display the target aiming mark on an LED screen will have much lower light levels when measuring the target illumination.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.14.3 Light measurements can also be done in Lumen, especially LED lighting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.14.4 Measuring general range illumination must be done with the measuring device held at the firing point (B1) and midway between the firing point and the target line (B2) with the device directed toward the ceiling illumination. Indoor Range Light Measuring EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 215

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15 Standards for Moving Target Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.1 The range must be so arranged that the target moves horizontally in both directions across an open area with a constant speed. This area, where the target may be fired upon, is called the “opening”, wich the target is moving over.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.2 The protective walls on both sides of the opening must be of such a height that no part of the target is visible until it reaches the opening. The edges must be marked with a colour differing from that of the target. If a sled wider than the target is used, the effective target area shall be clearly marked in such a way that the moment at which the target becomes fully visible or completely obscured is unambiguous.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.3 Targets for 50m are placed on a trolley or target carrier. The trolley may move on rails, cable, or a similar system and must be moved by a driving unit which can be regulated accurately for speed. Targets for 10m are not changed for left and right.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.4 The shooting station must be arranged so that the athlete is visible to spectators. The shooting station must be protected from rain. The athlete should also be protected from sun and wind if this does not prevent spectators from seeing him.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.5 The shooting station must be at least 1.00m wide and aligned with a centre - line perpendicular to the target. The dry firing position must be located to the left of the shooting station. The shooting station must be screened on both sides with separating partitions so the athlete is not disturbed by dry firing or other extraneous influences. The separating partition between the firing point and the dry firing point must not be longer than to allow the dry firing athlete to watch the READY position of the competition athlete by observing the muzzle movement of his rifle.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.6 In front of the athlete there must be a bench or a table 0.70m – 1.00m high.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.7 Behind the athlete there must be a place for the Range Officer and at least one member of the Jury. The Register Keepers must be located either behind or at the side of the shooting station.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.8 Moving times for the targets are: Slow: 5.0 seconds, +0.2 seconds – 0.0 seconds Fast: 2.5 seconds, +0.1 seconds – 0.0 seconds Timing should preferably be done by using an electronic timer that is started and stopped by switches mounted on the rail. If this method cannot be used, timing may be done by using three (3) stop watches operated by three different persons. The middle (median) of the three (3) times must be counted. If the moving time is found to be less or more than that specified, range personnel or the Jury must regulate the time to within the specified moving time standards. If the timer is built into the starting control, the timing must be examined by the Jury and sealed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.15.9 Timing must be electronically controlled and continually displayed for inspection by athletes and officials. Any deviation must be corrected immediately. 216 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.16.1 Special Standards for 50m Moving Target Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) There must be a vertical wall on both sides of the opening for the protection of operating personnel and scorers;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) There must be an embankment behind the opening. In front of the opening there must be a low wall to conceal and protect the target carrying mechanism; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The visible length of the target track must be: 10.00m (+0.05m/-0.00m) as seen from the firing point. This must be considered when measuring the opening since the distance between the visible corner of the wall and the target increases the distance over which the target is visible.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d)Wind flags are not permitted for 50m Moving Target. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 217

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.16.2 Standards for 10m Moving Target Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If target changing and shot evaluation is done behind the target carrier, there must be sufficient protection for operating personnel and scorers. The target changing and evaluation must be supervised by a member of the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Behind the opening there must be a backstop to stop pellets and prevent ricochets. The target carrying mechanism must be protected by a front cover plate;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The visible length of the target track must be: 2.00m (+0.01m/-0.00m) as seen from the firing point. This must be considered when measuring the opening since the distance between the visible corner of the wall and the target increases the distance over which the target is visible;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Two shooting stations may be installed and used alternately, to save time. In this case, the two firing points must not deviate from the standards; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) When electronic scoring targets are used, the timing equipment must be set to give the nominal exposure times plus 0.1 second. This should ensure that the earlier appearance of the EST aiming mark is allowed for.

chunks.text: 6.4.17 General Standards for Shotgun Venues

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.17.1 Shotgun venues in the Northern Hemisphere should be laid out so shooting is toward a north to north-easterly direction. Venues in the Southern Hemisphere should be laid out so shooting is toward a south to south-easterly direction. These arrangements place the sun to the back of the athlete and on the target as much as possible.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.17.2 10m Ranges Where necessary and feasible, new Shotgun venues must be constructed with a reasonably level shot fall zone that is free of obstacles (a minimum of 90m from the front edge of the trap station), to permit mechanical salvage and the recovery of lead pellets. Net systems may also be installed to capture lead pellets.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.17.3 When Shotgun venues include more than one range, ranges must be identified, starting on the left, with letters (A, B, C, etc.) or numbers (1, 2, 3, etc.),.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.18 Standards for Trap Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.18.1 The Trap Pit The trap pit must be constructed so that the upper surface of the roof is on the same elevation as the surface of the shooting stations. Interior measurements of the trap pit should be approximately 20m from end to end, 2.00m from front to rear, and 2.00m to 2.10m from the floor to the underside of the roof. These dimensions will allow freedom of movement for working personnel and sufficient storage space for targets (see Figures).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.18.2 Distances Between Trap Pits The distance between the centre of machine fifteen (15) on Range A and the centre of machine one (1) on Range B must not be less than 35m. For pre- existing ranges with a distance less than 35m, as specified above, the Jury may reduce the throwing angles of the settings of machine 13 of Range A, and machine three (3) of Range B, if necessary, to prevent those targets from crossing over, into the target flight path of the adjoining range and disturbing those athletes. 218 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.18.3 The Traps (Target Throwing Machines) Each trap pit must have 15 traps attached to the front wall of the pit. The traps must be divided into five (5) groups of three (3). The centre of each group must be indicated only by a painted mark on the top of the roof which must be positioned so that it must indicate the point above the centre trap of each group at which a target must emerge when set to throw at zero (0) degrees. The painted mark must be in the form of an isosceles triangle (the length, the sides of the triangle must be between 0.40m ± 0.05m). The triangle must be positioned with its base in line with the edge of the roof of the trap pit. The distance between the traps within each group must be equal, from 1.00m to

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.10m. The distance between the centre traps of adjacent groups should be

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3.00m to 3.30m. For existing ranges this may be 3.00m to 6.00m.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) In the case of use of machines with left-hand (clockwise) rotation of throwing arms the distance between the left side (viewed from behind) and the centre machine in each group may be reduced to less than the prescribed 1.00m to

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1.10m (see also Rule 6.4.19.3).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The traps must be installed in the pit so that the pivot point of the throwing arm is 0.50m (±0.10m) below the top surface of the roof of the trap pit and set back 0.50m (±0.10m) from the front edge of the roof when the trap is set at the 2m elevation. This is defined as the Throwing Point. Traps may be fully automatic (self-loading and cocking), semi-automatic (hand loaded and self- cocking), or manual (hand loaded and cocked). Each trap must be provided with a means of sealing its elevation angle, and main spring tension after these have been inspected and approved by the Jury. All traps must be provided with a means of making target throwing settings on a precise setting. All traps which are hand loaded must have two stops fixed to them. The stops are necessary to prevent accidental or deliberate movement of the target forward or backward on the throwing arm, thus changing the preset directions of the target. Each trap must have the elevation and angle sectors marked in increments of 10 degrees.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The traps must be released by an electric-manual or electric-microphone system. The control system must be placed in such a position that the puller can clearly see and hear the call of the athlete. The release devices must guarantee equal distribution of targets to each athlete in a series of 25 targets. This distribution must be: ten (10) targets to the right, ten (10) targets to the left and five (5) targets to the centre. With the correct distribution, in a series of 25 targets, each group of traps must throw two (2) targets from the left trap, two (2) from the right trap and one (1) from the centre trap as the athletes progress from station 1 to 5. The 15 machines in each shooting range must be of the same make and model, no mixture of machines at the same range is permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The five (5) shooting stations must be arranged on a straight line at a distance of 15m ± 0.05m to the rear of the front edge of the trap pit. Each station must be prominently marked with a square 1.00m x 1.00m which is centred on a line perpendicular to the line of shooting stations and extending through the painted mark which indicates the zero (0) degree exit point above the middle machine in each group of three. A sixth station must be marked about 2.00m to the rear and slightly to the left of Station 1 where athlete number 6 may take his position. In the Final Range, two additional waiting stations (7 & 8) to be positioned 1m behind station 6. All EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 219 eight (8) shooting stations may have a table or bench where the athletes can place their extra cartridges and other equipment. The stations must be firm and level in all directions. Each station must have at the front right and left hand corners a block of wood, piece of carpet or rubber about 15cm square or round upon which the athlete may rest his shotgun.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) For Trap Finals, medium intensity coloured lamps must be fitted to each microphone stand at a height of 40cm to 75cm to indicate when the microphone is live. The lamp system must be constructed to indicate a pause (microphone dead) of 5-25 seconds after each athlete has shot at a predetermined number of targets. At the end of the pause, the Referee must command “READY” and the athlete next to shoot must have a further 12 sec. preparation time to call for the target.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) 3.00m to 4.00m behind the line of shooting stations a path must be provided for mandatory use by the athletes moving from station 5 to stations 6, 7 or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8. Athletes must not pass between the path and the shooting stations. A wire, rope or other suitable barrier is to be erected 7.00m to 10.00m behind the return walkway. No spectators are to be allowed within this barrier. The Referee and Jury Members are responsible for enforcing this rule. The shooting stations, Referee stand and operator stand should have adequate protection from sun and rain, except that Finals ranges should, if possible, be open. 220 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.text: 6.4.19 Standards for Skeet Ranges

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.19.1 A Skeet field consists of two houses (high house and low house) and eight (8) shooting stations. Stations 1 through 7 are arranged on a segment of a circle with a 19.20m radius and a base chord of 36.80m (with a tolerance of ±0.25m) which is 5.50m from the centre point of the circle which is marked by a stake.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The centre of the circle which is marked by a stake also marks the base of the target crossing point.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Station 1 is located at the left end of the base chord and station 7 at the right end when standing anywhere on the segment of the circle and facing the centre stake. Stations 2 through 6 are located on the segment of the circle at points equidistant from each other (the distance between the centre of the front of the stations 1 and 2, 2 and 3, etc., is 8.13m ±0.05m on chord). Stations 8 and 4 are located at the centre of the base chord (see Figure).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Shooting stations 1 through 7 are 0.90m ±0.05m x 0.90m ±0.05m square, with two sides parallel to a radius of the circle drawn through the station marker (centre of the station). Shooting station 8 is rectangular, 0.9m ±0.05m wide by 1.85m ±0.05m long, with its long sides parallel to the base chord. The location of each shooting station must be accurately indicated. The markers for shooting stations 1 through 7 are on the centre of the side nearest the target crossing point. The marker for shooting station 8 is on the centre point of the base chord. All eight (8) shooting stations must be on the same level, within ±0.05m difference in elevation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.19.2 Target Distances, Angles and Elevations

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Each house must contain a clay target throwing machine in a fixed position. The throwing arm of the target throwing machine in the high house, when in a horizontal position, should be 2.80m ±0.10m above the level of station 1 and the throwing arm in the low house should be 0.80m ±0.10m above the level of station 7. The two target throwing machines must be of the same make and model.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Targets thrown from the high house must emerge at a point 0.90m ± 0.05m behind the station marker 1 (measured along the extended base chord) and 3.05m ±0.05m above the level of the station. Targets thrown from the low house must emerge at a point 0.9m ± 0.05m behind station marker 7 (measured along the extended base chord) (moved 0.75m ± 0.05m to the exterior of the base chord) and 1.05m ± 0.05m above the level of station 7.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Targets properly released must pass through a circle 0.90m - 0.95m in diameter, located 4.60m ±0.05m above the centre point.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) In calm weather conditions targets must carry a distance of 68.00m ±1.00m as measured from the face of the house behind stations 1 and 7. If the correct distance cannot be verified by measurement, the Jury will decide the trajectory of the targets.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The shooting boundaries of stations 1 to 7 are 40.30m ±0.10m from the face of each house. For station 8 the shooting boundary is determined by the crossing point between a straight line running from station 4 to station 8 and the target crossing point. Suitable markers must be placed on the target flight path, at points 40.30m ±0.1m from both the high house and the low house, to indicate the shooting boundaries. Similar markers must be placed at 67.00m and 69.00m to indicate the distance a regular target must fly. The tops of these distance markers should indicate the ground level. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 223

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) A safety shield must be installed at the opening of each trap house so that the trap operator is not visible to an athlete on any station. This precaution is mandatory as a safety measure to protect the operator from possible injury from direct or ricocheting shot, and the athletes from broken targets emerging from the opening of the trap house. A wire, rope or other suitable barrier is to be erected 10.00m to 13.00m behind Station 4 and parallel to the base chord. No spectators are allowed within this barrier. The Referee and Jury Members are responsible for the enforcement of this Rule.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) The traps must be released by an electric-microphone system (see note below) with a timer device which must be installed so as to allow the operator to see and hear the athletes. For all ISSF Championships the use of a timer is mandatory. This must provide for the release of the targets within an indefinite period of time, varying from instant release up to a maximum of three (3) seconds after the athlete has called for his target. The release device must be designed so that only one (1) button (or switch) can be used to release double targets.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Note: If an electro-microphone system is to be used, it must be so constructed as to randomly insert a delay varying from 0.2 to 3.0 seconds.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) A coloured lamp must be fitted to the outside of both high and low houses. The lamps must light immediately on the athlete’s call and extinguish when the target(s) are thrown. The lamps must be clearly visible to the Referee. The lamp must be installed on the side of the skeet house which faces the spectator area at a height of 2.20m – 2.80m on the high house and 1.60m –

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2.00m on the low house.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.19.3 An openable or a mobile net must be fitted in between the ranges to reduce the possibility of any broken pieces flying from one range to another, these nets will be opened during the target checking by the juries and will be kept closed during shooting unless there is a machine breakdown and the jury need to confirm that the machine had been set well and that the target is regular and according to the rules. This net should be a minimum of 8m high and 8m wide. 224 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.4.19.4 Skeet Range Layout All new Skeet ranges must comply with these specifications. Skeet ranges constructed before 2013 with stations 1 and 7 facing the opposite target house will continue to be accepted for ISSF Championships. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 225
