chunks.text: 6.5 GAUGES AND INSTRUMENTS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Each Organizing Committee must provide a complete set of gauges and instruments for Equipment Control during ISSF Championships;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A detailed list of Equipment Control Instruments that are required for conducting Equipment Control tests and the requirements and specifications for those instruments is available from ISSF Headquarters;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The ISSF Technical Delegate or the Chairperson of the Equipment Control Jury must examine and approve all gauges and instruments prior to the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Calibration test equipment for use in examining Equipment Control instruments is available from ISSF Headquarters and must be used to calibrate testing instruments before each day of testing and when a disqualification is considered during post-competition testing (Calibration Report Forms are available from ISSF Headquarters); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The measuring devices used to test the thickness, stiffness and flexibility of athletes’ clothing must be constructed according to this rule (see Rule 6.5.1 below) and be approved by the ISSF Technical Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.5.1 Thickness Measurement Device The device used to measure the thickness of clothing and shoes must be capable of measuring to one-tenth of a millimetre (0.1mm). Measurements must be taken with a 5.0kg weight applied. The device must have two (2) circular flat surfaces facing each other, each 30mm in diameter. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 227

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.5.2 Stiffness Measurement Device The device used to measure the clothing stiffness must be capable of measuring to one tenth of a millimetre (0.1mm) and have the following dimensions: A Measuring cylinder = 60mm diameter B Measuring weight = 1000g (including grip and measuring plate C) C Measuring plate = 20mm diameter D Digital display indicating 0.1mm E The rounding of the edges on the measuring plate (C) and measuring cylinder (A) must not be more than 0.5 mm radius as a maximum. Stiffness measurements must be made with the fabric/material laid flat, without stretching, on measuring cylinder “A;” and • Measuring weight “B” presses measuring plate “C” onto the fabric/material on measuring cylinder “A.” 228 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.5.3 Shoe Sole Flexibility Measurement Device The device used to measure shoe sole flexibility must be capable of accurately measuring, in degrees, the shoe sole flexibility under a precise amount of upward pressure (NM).

chunks.text: 6.6 CHAMPIONSHIP ADMINISTRATION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1 Championship Programme and Schedule The administration of ISSF Championships shall be carried out in accordance with this Rule, except that the administration of Olympic and Continental Games Shooting Championships shall be carried out in accordance with the charter and regulations of the IOC or the appropriate Continental NOC organization. Official Championship Programme. The office of the ISSF Secretary

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.1  General will provide a standardized Championship Programme and coordinate the preparation of an Official Championship Programme with each Organizing Committee to be finalized in November of the year before the Championship. The Official Championship Programme, including invitations, schedules, the official symbol or logo and entry forms will be posted on the ISSF website and the Organizing Committee must publish the Official Programme and send it to all ISSF Member Federations as soon as possible after it is finalized. It is recommended the ISSF Technical Delegate with the organising committee produce the general information and publish it online a minimum of 6 months before the start of the championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.2  Official Schedule. The office of the ISSF Secretary General, the Organizing Committee and the Technical Delegate appointed for the Championship must prepare a detailed Official Schedule for each Championship. Championship schedules should include an official arrival day, at least one day of Official Training, or Pre-Event Training (PET) the necessary competition days and an official departure day. World Championship schedules, including Official Training days and the opening and closing ceremonies, should not exceed 20 days. Ranges may be open for additional Unofficial Training before the Official Training Day (PET) at the option of the Organizing Committee and the ISSF. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 229 Official Schedules must provide dates and times for Opening Ceremony,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.3  unofficial Training, Pre-Event Training, Elimination Relays, Qualification Relays or Rounds for Shotgun, Technical Meeting, Equipment Control availability, Finals Reporting Times, Finals and Medal Ceremonies. When creating Programmes for ISSF Championships, a minimum period of one and a half hours must be allowed between end of Qualification and Final Reporting time. Schedule changes, as approved by the Technical Delegate, must be made as soon as possible after the Final Entry Deadline and distributed to all participating delegations. Entry Status and Limits. National Federations may enter a maximum of three

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.4  (3) athletes per nation per event who are competing for awards (in-competition) in ISSF Championship events. In addition, in World Cups, the Organizing Committee may accept a maximum of two additional athlete entries per nation, per event, that may compete for Ranking Points Only (RPO), Olympic MQS status (MQS only) or participate out-of-competition (OOC), however, RPO, MQS or OOC status is only possible if there are more than three (3) starts in an event for that country. Maximum Entry. The Organizing Committee and Technical Delegate

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.1.5  must establish the Maximum Entry (range capacity) for each event on the programme. Final entries that exceed the maximum entry for an event will be placed on a waiting list and will only be accepted if entry spaces become available before the Late Entry Deadline.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.2 Technical Meeting A Technical Meeting conducted by the Competition Director and Technical Delegate(s) must be scheduled on the day before the first competition day to inform team leaders about competition details and any schedule changes. A separate Technical Meeting may be arranged for shotgun events if more advantageous for arriving teams.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.3 Training Official Training. Official Training will be allocated within the programme if

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.3.1  time permits. Pre-Event Training (PET). Pre-Event Training must be provided for every

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.3.2  individual event on the programme, before Elimination or Qualification for that event starts. For Rifle, Pistol and Moving Target individual events, each athlete must be allowed to train on his allocated competition target for a minimum of 40 minutes per relay (30 minutes per relay for Rapid-Fire Pistol, 15 minutes per athlete for Moving Target) on a day before the event, where ever possible. This is in addition to the Official Training day(s) in the programme (for Shotgun, see Rule 9.6.2.1). If Mixed Team events follow comparable individual events, Pre-Event Training with open target allocations may be scheduled for these events when time is available in the schedule. If PET for Mixed Team events is provided for in the programme, this should be for a minimum of 30 minutes. Unofficial Training. In addition to Official Training and scheduled Pre-Event

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.3.3  Training, athletes should be given additional Unofficial Training opportunities when the shooting ranges are available, this will usually also be on Arrival Day.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.3.4 Electronic training/tracking devices Electronic training/tracking devices must not be used during Pre-Event Training or competition (elimination, qualification, finals), but may be allowed during official and unofficial training. 230 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.4 Entries and Entry Confirmation National Federations must submit entries to the ISSF Online Registration Service by the Final Entry Deadline 30 days before the official arrival day (Rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Late Entries may be submitted until three days before the official arrival day if an additional penalty is paid and entry spaces are available (Rule 3.8.3.3);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Entry Confirmations and the payment of applicable fees to the Organizing Committee, together with Entry Verification Forms must be completed by team leaders upon arrival (Rule 3.8.4.1); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Entry Changes can only be made in accordance with Rule 3.8.3.4. Entry Changes must be completed not later than 12:00pm (noon) on the day before the Pre-Event Training for a particular event.

chunks.text: 6.6.6 Principles for Firing Point Allocation in Rifle and Pistol

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The allocation of athletes to firing points and relays in Qualification must be done by random under the supervision of the Technical Delegate with a computer programme designed for this purpose.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The allocation of athletes to firing points in the Final will also be by random, as Rule 6.17.1.2.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Whenever draws are used to determine firing positions the Technical Delegate must approve the range constraints to be taken into account; the Technical Delegate may approve the squadding of MQS-only, RPO and OOC athletes in specific sections of a range.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Individual athletes and teams (nations) should be able to shoot under conditions that are as nearly equal as possible;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Athletes from the same nation should not be allocated adjacent firing positions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Athletes from the same nation should be divided as equally as possible between relays;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) If there are more athletes than targets in Air Rifle or Air Pistol events, targets must be distributed by drawing lots for two (2) or more relays;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) If more than one relay is used in team competitions, team members must be distributed equally between the relays; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 231

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) If a Rifle competition lasts for more than one day, all athletes must fire an equal number of shots in the same position or positions each day; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) When a Pistol event is divided into two (2) stages or days, all athletes must finish the first stage before the second stage or day may begin. All athletes must fire an equal number of series on each day of a two-day competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.6.1 Elimination Events for Outdoor 50m and 300m Ranges If the number of athletes exceeds the useable capacity of the range, an Elimination must be conducted. This requirement may be waived by the Technical Delegate when required by schedule limitations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Any Elimination must be over the complete course of fire; Scores attained in Elimination will be used for any athletes Team Events results entered in that event.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) All athletes are squadded at random.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Elimination relays should be scheduled on the day before the Qualification is scheduled;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Qualification athletes must consist of a proportionate number of highest- ranking athletes from each Elimination relay, taking the number of starts on the start-lists into account. The number of athletes who qualify must be announced at the Technical Meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Formula: The usable number of firing points is divided by the total number of athletes on the start-lists multiplied by the number of athletes on the start- list for each relay to give the number of athletes going forward from the to the Qualification, e.g. 60 firing points and 101 athletes: 1st relay: 54 athletes = 32.08 ≈ 32 athletes forward; 2nd relay: 47 athletes =

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 27.92 ≈ 28 athletes forward;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) When Eliminations are required, team members/nations must be equally divided between the Elimination relays. Team scores are taken from these relays;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) If insufficient targets are available to allocate two team members from each team to the first relay and the remaining member from each team to the second relay, then it will be necessary to have three relays with one member from each team on each relay;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) An athlete who does not qualify must not be allowed to participate further in the event; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) If there are tied scores for the last places in an Elimination the order of rank will be determined according to tie breaking rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) If an Elimination is not scheduled in Junior World Cups and multiple relays are scheduled, Team Leaders must be allowed to designate their athletes who will be squadded on the first and subsequent relays.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) In 50m 3-Position event qualification, if only one Relay, then the top 8 will proceed to the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The second 30-shot stage must begin only after all athletes complete the first 30-shot stage. If there are fewer athletes than are necessary to completely fill all relays, the allocation of firing points should be done so that gaps are left in the last relays of the first and second stages; 232 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) For the 2nd stage, firing point allocation will be in order of ranking according to scores fired in the first 30-shot stage, with the lowest ranked athletes shooting in the first relay, except that if both stages are shot on the same day, then the start list for the second stage should be the same as for the first stage. Start positions within each relay will be decided by a random draw.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.6.6.3 Schedules and Squadding -- 25m Pistol Women The event may be scheduled to take place on one or two days. If possible, the event should be scheduled to take place on two days with the rapid-fire stage and Final taking place on the second day. If the event is scheduled over two days, the PET before the first day should be for the precision stage. There should be a second PET on the first competition day, after the precision stage, for the rapid- fire stage.

chunks.text: 6.7 COMPETITION CLOTHING AND EQUIPMENT

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.1 The ISSF establishes specific standards for competition clothing and equipment that athletes may use in ISSF Championships and for Equipment Control testing to check those standards in order to safeguard the principles of equal and ethical competition where no athlete can gain an unfair advantage over other athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.2 Athletes are responsible for ensuring that all items of equipment and clothing used by them in ISSF Championships comply with ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.3 All athletes’ equipment is subject to checks by the Equipment Control Jury and an Equipment Control Section established by the Organizing Committee as well as by the respective Competition Juries.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.4 Standards for Clothing and Equipment

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.4.1 Rules governing specific equipment used by athletes in a particular discipline are found in the Rules for that discipline.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.4.2 The use of any special devices, means or clothing, including the use of Kinesio, medical or similar taping, which immobilizes or unduly reduces the movement of the athlete’s legs, body or arms, is prohibited for Rifle, Pistol and Moving Target athletes in order to ensure that athletes’ performance skills are not artificially improved.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.4.3 Radios, iPods, or any similar type of sound producing or communication systems are prohibited on the FOP during competition and training, except when they are used by competition officials.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.4.4 Mobile phones and other electronic communication devices are not permitted on the field of play.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.4.5 At official ISSF events and championships where TV broadcast is in place, all finalists in 10m and 50m rifle and pistol events must have Live Aiming devices fitted to their firearms. The fitting of these devices is to take place in the Finals Call room prior to each final, assisted and overseen by ISSF RTS and Sport Presentation technical officers and officials. Sufficient time must be allowed for this fitting to take place and support provided to athletes by trained staff and officials. These devices are a vital ingredient for TV broadcasting, and EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 233 the graphic presentation of the Sport and athlete skills sets; every facility must be extended to ensuring the technical implementation of this service at ISSF events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.5 ISSF Dress Code It is the responsibility of athletes, coaches and officials to appear on the ranges dressed in a manner appropriate for a public sports event. Clothing worn by athletes and officials must comply with the ISSF Dress Code. See 6.20 for the full ISSF Dress Code.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.6 Equipment Control

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.6.1 The Organizing Committee must establish an Equipment Control Section to perform equipment control checks under the supervision of the Equipment Control Jury. An Equipment Control checking service must be available to all athletes so that they may have their equipment checked prior to the competitions. To ensure compliance with ISSF Rules, the Equipment Control Jury and Equipment Control Section must conduct random post-competition testing (6.7.9).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.6.2 Equipment Control Procedures

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Organizing Committee must inform team officials and athletes where and when they may have their equipment inspected prior to or during the competitions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Equipment Control Section must be open to provide voluntary inspections for athletes’ equipment, starting with the Official Training Day and continuing through the last day of Rifle-Pistol-Moving Target competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) ISSF calibration test equipment must be used to check testing instruments before each day of testing and when a disqualification is considered during post-competition testing;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Athletes are encouraged to bring any items of equipment to the Equipment Control Section for checking if they are not certain if they will pass a post- competition check;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The Equipment Control Section must ensure that all Rifle shooting jackets, shooting trousers and shoes are identified with a seal bearing a unique serial number that is registered to the athlete. The seal must be designed so that it cannot be removed without breaking the seal. Seals previously issued for one-time- only clothing inspections fulfil this requirement. Jackets, trousers and shoes with no seal must be checked for compliance with ISSF Rules and have seals affixed to them that are registered for the athlete. The Equipment Control and Rifle Juries will use the jacket, trouser and shoe seals to conduct random checks for compliance with Rule 7.5.1.2;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The Equipment Control Section must keep a register of all items that they check, with the name of the athlete, the make (manufacturer), serial number and calibre of each gun checked on an Equipment Control Card;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) The Equipment Control Section must ensure that all pistols have been registered on the ISSF database and a card issued to the athlete. Pistols that have not yet been registered or recorded must be checked for compliance with ISSF Rules and be registered to the athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) It is the athlete’s responsibility that any air or CO2 cylinder is within manufacturer’s validity date (maximum of ten (10) years); this may be checked by Equipment Control and advisory recommendations may be given; 234 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) One copy of the Equipment Control Card is given to the athlete who must retain this card with his equipment at all times. If an athlete loses his Equipment Control Card, there is a EUR 10.00 fee to replace it; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) If a Rifle clothing item is resubmitted for a second or subsequent test during the same Championship, a reinspection fee of EUR 20,00 will apply. No item of clothing may be submitted to Equipment Control more than three times. If an item does not pass on the third occasion this must not be used in competition and doing so will result in disqualification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) For skeet athletes, one seal will be kept at the rear of the skeet marker tape, and one small hollow rivet at the front.

chunks.text: 6.7.7 Bib (Start) Numbers and Items Worn by Athletes

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.7.1 All athletes must be provided with a Bib Number (Start Number) to wear on the back of the outer garment above the waistline during the entire competition. Bib Numbers must display the athlete’s allocated number for that Championship, family name, initial and nation (IOC abbreviation only). If a flag of the nation is used, it must be placed to the left of the IOC abbreviation. The height of the letters in names should be as big as possible, but no letters or numbers may be less than 20mm (for Shotgun, see 9.12.2, 9.12.3).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.7.2 Bib Numbers and Finals Start Numbers. Must be worn by all athletes, on their backs and above the waist, at all times while participating in Pre-Event Training and all stages of competition. If the Bib Number is available and not worn, the athlete may not compete. New Finals Start Numbers will be issued at Reporting Time prior to Shotgun Finals and 25m RFP Finals. Finals Start numbers will not be worn for other Rifle & Pistol Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.7.3 All athletes must comply with ISSF Eligibility, ISSF Commercial Rights and ISSF Sponsorship/Advertising Rules. These rules govern such matters as emblems, sponsorship, advertising and commercial markings on clothing together with controls and sanctions. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 235

One Front Blinder to cover the non-aiming eye that is not more than 30mm

chunks.text: 6.7.9 Post-Competition Testing

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.9.1 Post-competition checks must be conducted after Elimination and Qualification competitions according to procedures specified in the “ISSF Equipment Control Guidelines.” The Equipment Control Jury is responsible for supervising the conduct of all post-competition checks. Judges of the same gender as the athletes must be available for clothing and taping checks. Failure of the following specific post-competition checks must result in disqualification (DSQ):

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Rifle: Shooting clothing, underclothing, taping and rifle specifications (trigger weighing when applicable);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Pistol: Shoes, taping, trigger weighing, pistol dimensions and grips (8.12), ammunition velocity checks and the weighing of bullets where applicable;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Shotgun: See Shotgun Rules; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Moving Target: Rifle weight, telescope power (10m), trigger weight (50m10.4.3.6 a) and marker tapes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) All disciplines: Failure to report for a post-competition check after being given written notice to report.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.9.2 If an athlete fails a post-competition check, the Chairperson of the Equipment Control Jury or one other Equipment Control or Competition Jury Member must confirm that the test was performed correctly and that the athlete is disqualified. The confirmation procedure must include using ISSF calibration testing equipment to confirm that the testing instruments are measuring accurately.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.9.3 Appeals against a post-competition test disqualification may be submitted to the Jury of Appeal. The Jury of Appeal must decide if the test was performed correctly, but it may not repeat the test. The Jury of Appeal can overturn a post- competition check disqualification only if it finds that the test was performed incorrectly. 236 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.9.4 Targeted testing (selection of athletes on a non-random basis) may be done when a Jury has credible evidence that an athlete has altered or attempted to alter his gun, clothing or equipment.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.9.5 In all Post Competition targeted testing, following a Qualification, all Finalists in Rifle and Pistol events must also be tested. (Top 10 athletes to allow for DSQ’s). This is in addition to any testing carried out in the Finals Preparation area.

chunks.text: 6.8 COMPETITION JURY DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS Juries are responsible for advising, assisting and supervising the competition officials appointed by the Organizing Committee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Competition Juries (Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun, Moving Target and Target Sprint) supervise the conduct of events in their respective disciplines;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) RTS (Results, Timing and Scoring) Juries supervise scoring and results operations; and produce the Competition Results Book in cooperation with the Official Results Provider.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Equipment Control Juries supervise the testing of athletes’ clothing and equipment.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) VAR System. Jury (In case VAR is used) is responsible for functioning and controlling the VAR system, he will be designated to operate the monitor as needed during finals. He will oversee the system’s operation and ensure its proper use in accordance with established protocols.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.1 Range Officers, RTS Officers and Referees appointed by the Organizing Committee and the ISSF are responsible for the actual conduct of the competitions while Juries act in an advisory and supervisory capacity. The Range Officers and Juries are mutually responsible for conducting the training and competitions in accordance with ISSF Rules and must ensure that these Rules are enforced in a fair and equitable manner during the competitions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.2 All Jury Members must wear the official ISSF approved Jury vest when on duty. Jury vests can be purchased from ISSF authorised supplier. It is recommended that all Range Officers wear a distinctive vest or other means of identification (preferably in green colour) when on duty. It is recommended that all Target Officers or other personnel who must go forward of the firing lines to perform their duties wear a vest in a fluorescent colour or high visibility armbands.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.3 Before the beginning of the competition, the Competition Juries must examine the shooting ranges and check the organizational arrangements and organization of operating personnel, etc., to ensure that they conform to ISSF Rules. Jury checks should be done in coordination with any earlier checks made by the Technical Delegate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.4 Jury Members must continuously observe the shooting positions and the equipment of the athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.5 Jury Members have the right to examine the guns, equipment, positions, etc., of the athletes at any time, during training and competitions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.6 During training and competitions, Jury Members are responsible for checking athletes clothing and equipment for compliance with ISSF Sponsorship/ Advertising Rules (4.4-4.7 and 6.7.7.3); EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 237

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.7 During competitions, Jury Members should not approach an athlete while he is firing a shot (or series of shots in Rapid-Fire events), or in his shooting station, unless a safety issue requires immediate action.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.8 A majority of the Jury must always be present on the range during competitions so that, when necessary, the Jury can meet and make decisions immediately.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.9 Jury Members have the right to make individual decisions during competitions, but should confer with other Jury Members and Range Officers or Referees when any doubt exists. If a Team Official or Athlete does not agree with the decision of an individual Jury Member, a decision of the majority of the Jury may be requested by making a written protest.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.10 Jury Members must be completely impartial in making decisions, regardless of the nationality, racial, religious, ethnic or cultural identity of any athletes who are involved.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.11 Juries must deal with any protest(s) that are submitted to the Jury in accordance with ISSF Rules. After consultation with the Range Officers or Referees and others directly concerned, the Jury must rule on any protest.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.12 A Jury must delay the start of a Final if a protest involves athletes who could, depending upon the protest decision, qualify for the Final. The RTS Jury may release a Final Start List if a protest does not involve athletes who could qualify for the Final. Official Final Results cannot be released until all protests and appeals are decided.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.13 A Jury must decide all cases that are not provided for in the ISSF Rules. Such decisions must be made within the spirit and intent of ISSF Rules. Any such decisions must be included in a Jury Chairperson’s Report that is submitted to the Technical Delegate after each Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.14 Athletes and Team Officials must not be members of a Jury. Jury Members must not advise, coach or assist athletes beyond the scope of the ISSF Rules at any time during the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.15 The Jury Chairperson is responsible for directing Jury schedules and activities for ensuring the presence of sufficient member(s) of the Jury at all times, including all Official and Pre-Event Training.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.8.16 The Jury Chairperson must prepare a report on Jury decisions and actions to be submitted to the ISSF Secretary General through the Technical Delegate as soon as possible after the Championship.

chunks.text: 6.9 ORGANIZING COMMITTEE COMPETITION OFFICIALS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.9.1 Chief Range Officer (CRO) Duties and Functions A Chief Range Officer (CRO) must be appointed for each range, (Only one CRO for all shotgun ranges). The CRO is in charge of all Range Officers (RO) and range personnel and is responsible for the correct conduct of the shooting event. The CRO is responsible for giving all range commands and for ensuring the cooperation of range personnel with the Jury. The CRO is responsible for the rapid correction of any equipment failures and for making available the necessary experts and supplies to operate the range. It is strongly recommended that an Assistant CRO be appointed to serve as a backup for the CRO, especially in maintaining range documentation and Range Incident Reports (Form IR) regarding events and irregularities that occur during the competition. 238 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.9.2 Range Officer (RO) Duties and Functions (not in Shotgun). A Range Officer (RO) must be appointed for each Range Section or for each ten (10) firing points. Range Officers must:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Be responsible to the CRO for the conduct of the competition in the target section entrusted to them;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Check the names and Bib Numbers of athletes to ensure that they correspond with the start list;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Ensure that the athletes’ guns, equipment and accessories have been examined and approved;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Check athletes’ shooting positions and equipment and advise the Jury of any possible violations;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Ensure that the commands of the CRO are followed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Take necessary actions regarding a malfunction, protest, disturbance, or any other matter arising during the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Receive verbal protests and immediately report them to a Jury Member;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Record all irregularities, disturbances, penalties, malfunctions, cross-fires, extra time allowed, repeated shots authorized, etc. on Range Incident Report Forms (IR) and on the target or printer strip as appropriate; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Refrain from any conversations with athletes or from making other comments regarding scores.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.9.3 Chief RTS (Results, Timing and Scoring) Officer (CRTSO) Duties and Functions The CRTSO must be appointed for each Championship. He is in charge of all RTSO and Entry and Results Personnel. The CRTSO is responsible for the correct conduct of all scoring and results operations at the Championships.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.9.4 RTS Officers (RTSO) Duties and Functions (not in shotgun). One RTSO should be appointed for each range that is used for Qualification competitions. The RTSOs are responsible for working with the RTS Jury, Competition Jury, ROs and Official Results Provider to facilitate the conduct of scoring and results operations on their ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10 EST COMPETITION OPERATIONS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.1 EST Technical Officers

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) EST Technical Officers are responsible for operating and maintaining the Electronic Scoring Target equipment;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) EST Technical Officers may advise Range Officers and Jury Members, but they must not make any decisions regarding the application of ISSF Rules; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) EST Technical Officers are designated by the Official Results Provider or the Organizer and must be persons with special training in EST operations and electronic competition management systems (computer software).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.2 Target Officers

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Target Officers are appointed by the Organizing Committee to assist in the operation and maintenance of EST: EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 239

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Before each relay of each event, Target Officers must ensure that there are no shot holes on the white surface of the target and that all shot marks on the frame are clearly indicated;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) During competitions, Target Officers patch Backing Targets and Backing Cards and change the Control Sheets; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Backing Targets, Backing Cards and Control Sheets must not be patched or changed until after all scoring is completed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.3 Jury Member Duties – Electronic Scoring Targets

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.3.1 Member(s) of the RTS Jury must be present on the ranges to supervise scoring and results operations and assist in the resolution of any questions or protests relating to scoring. Members of the Competition Jury must assist in cases where actions or decisions need to be taken and there are only two or fewer RTS Jury Members available.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.3.2 Before each relay of an event, a Jury Member must inspect the electronic scoring targets to confirm that:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) There are no shot holes on the white surface of the target;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any shot marks on the frame are clearly indicated;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Control Sheets are renewed; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The Backing Cards and Backing Targets have no shots outside of the central area that is covered by the Control Sheet.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.4 Shooting on Electronic Scoring Targets

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Athletes must familiarize themselves during training with the control buttons that alter the target presentation on the monitor screen (ZOOM) and that change from a Sighting target (SIGHTING) to a Match target (MATCH);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) In 10m, 25m and 50m single position events, changing from Sighting to MATCH shots is under control of range personnel. If any athlete is in doubt, he must ask a Range Officer for assistance;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) In 3-Position events, after athletes complete the kneeling or prone positions, changing from MATCH to Sighting and back to MATCH is the responsibility of the athlete. Athletes may fire unlimited Sighting shots before starting MATCH firing shots in the prone and standing positions. No additional time is allowed for these Sighting shots. If an athlete inadvertently fails to switch from MATCH to Sighting after changing positions, any shots recorded as extra shots in the previous position must be nullified and the target must be reset to Sighting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) It is not permitted to obscure the athlete’s monitor-screen or any part of the screen. The whole screen must be visible to the Jury and range personnel;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Athletes and range officials must not touch the printer control panels and/ or printout before the end of the relay or event, except when authorized by the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Athletes should sign the printout (next to the score total) before leaving the range to identify their score.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) When an athlete fails to sign the printout a Jury Member or range official should initial this printer strip to allow it to be sent to the RTS Office. 240 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.5 Target Scoring Complaints During Sighting Shots If an athlete complains during sighting shots about the correct recording or evaluation of the shot(s), the Jury may offer to move him to another firing point.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete will be given appropriate extra time;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Jury will, as soon as possible, examine the sighting shot(s) on the original firing point by applying the Procedure for EST Examination; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If this subsequent examination confirms that the target on the original firing point provided correct results, the athlete will be penalized with the DEDUCTION of two (2) points from the lowest value shot of his first competition series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.6 Failure of the Paper or Rubber Band to Advance If the Jury confirms that the problem causing an athlete complaint is because the paper or rubber band is not advancing properly:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete will be moved to a reserve position;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) He will be permitted unlimited sighting shots to be taken within the time remaining for the event plus any additional time granted;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) He will repeat the number of MATCH shots determined by the Jury plus the number of shots necessary to complete the event;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) After the relay, the RTS Jury will decide which shots are to be counted from each target; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The athlete will be credited with the scores of all shots that were correctly displayed on the monitor of the first target, plus the scores of all MATCH shots fired on the second target that were necessary to complete the course of fire.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.7 Protest Concerning a Shot Value If a shot registers and displays, but the athlete protests the value indicated in accordance with Rule 6.16.5.2:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) After the relay, the detailed printer results (LOG-Print) must be generated by the Technical or Range Officers for all firing lanes on which complaints or protests have been made, and for the immediately adjacent lanes, before the target systems are reset for the next relay;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) After the completion of the relay, the Procedure for EST Examination will be applied;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Any non-indicated or incorrectly indicated shot must be scored by the RTS Jury; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If the RTS Jury determines that a protested shot was scored correctly, a two (2) point penalty will be applied (6.16.5.2.c).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8 PROCEDURE FOR EXAMINING ELECTRONIC SCORING TARGETS FOLLOWING A SCORE PROTEST OR COMPLAINT

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.1 If there is a score protest, complaint or no indication of a shot, etc., a Jury Member must collect the following items (the number of the firing point and the orientation of the card, sheet or target, the relay and series and the time of collection must be noted on each):

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Control Sheet (25m / 50m). If the location of any shot hole is out of the area of the Control Sheet, the geometric relation between the shot holes on the EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 241 Control Sheet and the Backing Card must be made before the Control Sheet is removed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Backing Card (25m / 50m / 300m);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Backing Target (25m);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The black paper strip (10m);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The black rubber band (50m);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The Range Incident Report;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) The LOG print; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) The data record from the electronic scoring target computer (if necessary).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.2 A Jury Member must examine the face of the EST and the frame and record the location of any shots outside the black aiming mark.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.3 No CLEAR LOG must be made before the RTS Jury has given permission.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.4 The number of shot holes must be counted and their location taken into account.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.5 Jury Members must examine these items and then make independent assessments before a formal Jury decision is made.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.8.6 A Jury Member must supervise any manual intervention of the control computer results (e.g. the recording of penalties, corrected scores after malfunctions etc.).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9 EST FAILURE These Rules apply to 10m, 50m and 300m EST. For procedures concerning 25m EST failures, see Rule 8.10. For procedures concerning Moving Target EST failures, see Rule 10.11.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9.1 When ALL Targets on a Range Fail

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The time of failure and the expired shooting time must be recorded by the Chief Range Officer and the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) All completed competition shots of each athlete must be counted and recorded. In the event of a range power supply failure, this may involve waiting until the power supply is restored to enable the number of shots registered by the target, not necessarily on the firing point monitor, to be established; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) After the failure is rectified and the full range is in operation, an additional five (5) minutes will be added to the competition time remaining. The time for recommencing is to be announced over the loudspeaker system at least five (5) minutes beforehand. Athletes must be allowed to resume their position in the five (5) minutes before the competition restarts. Unlimited sighting shots must be allowed during the remaining shooting time, but only before competition shots are resumed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9.2 When a SINGLE Target Fails

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the EST cannot be repaired within five (5) minutes, the athlete must be moved to a reserve position;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) When he is ready to shoot, an additional five (5) minutes will be added to the competition time remaining; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) He will be permitted unlimited sighting shots before he starts the remaining competition shots. 242 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9.3 When a Shot Fails to Register or Display on the Monitor The athlete must immediately inform the nearest Range Officer of the failure. The Range Officer must make a written note of the time of the complaint. One or more Jury Member(s) must go to the firing position. The athlete must be directed to fire one more MATCH shot at his target: If the value and location of this shot is registered and displayed on the monitor:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must be directed to continue the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The value, location and time of firing of this extra shot must be recorded, its shot-number (after including the missing shot) and its value and its shot- location, and the firing point number must be given to the Jury in writing and recorded on the Range Register and a Range Incident Report;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) After the end of that relay, the Procedure for EST Examination will be applied. Using this information and the time of the extra shot and its location, the RTS Jury will determine whether all shots, including the extra shot, are recorded on the computer record;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If all the shots are recorded correctly, then the questioned shot (shot that did not register or display) will be counted in the score of the athlete, as well as the shot fired immediately after (as the “extra” shot), but the last shot fired (extra to the competition) will be annulled;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) If the questioned shot was not located by applying the Procedure for EST Examination or was confirmed as an off-target miss (Note: This means a questioned 10m shot could not be found on the witness strip or target face; a questioned 25m shot could not be found on the backing target, control sheet or backing card or there was evidence that a questioned 50m or 300m shot was an off-target miss), then the questioned shot must be scored as a miss and the last shot fired (extra to the competition) must be nullified; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) If the questioned shot was found or was located in the computer memory, the RTS Jury must determine and count the score of the questioned shot; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) If a questioned 50m or 300m shot is not found, the Jury must decide whether to score the missing shot as a miss and nullify the last shot or, if there is no credible evidence that the questioned shot was an off-target miss, the Jury may conclude that a target system anomaly occurred and count the extra shot in lieu of the missing shot and the last shot fired.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9.4 OR: If the extra shot fired as directed does not register or display and the EST cannot be repaired within five (5) minutes:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must be moved to a reserve position;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) When he is ready to shoot, an additional five (5) minutes will be added to the competition time remaining and he will be permitted unlimited sighting shots;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) In 10m and 50m Rifle and Pistol Events, the athlete will repeat the two (2) MATCH shots that did not register or display on the previous target used.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.10.9.5 OR: In Moving Target Events, the athlete will be permitted two (2) minutes to resume his position and then allowed two (2) additional sighting shots (Rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.2). Then he will repeat the two (2) competition shots which did not register or display on the previous target used and fire the remaining shots of the series. The athlete will be credited with the score of all the shots that were EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 243 displayed on the monitor of the first target plus the score of all the properly fired competition shots that were displayed on the second target used. If the two (2) extra shots were later found in the computer record of the previous target they will be annulled.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11 COMPETITION PROCEDURES (SEE ALSO 6.17, FINALS COMPETITION PROCEDURES)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.1 Rules for 10m and 50m Rifle, 300m and Pistol Events

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.1.1 Preparation and Sighting Time Athletes must be called to the line at least 25 minutes before the published START time of the event, allowed 10 minutes to setup their equipment, and then allowed 15 minutes Preparation and Sighting Time before MATCH firing starts to make their final preparation and fire unlimited sighting shots.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Preparation and Sighting Time must be timed to end approximately 30 seconds before the official starting time for MATCH firing.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Sighting targets must be visible at least 10 minutes before the Preparation and Sighting Time starts;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Athletes may not place their guns and equipment on their firing points until the Chief Range Officer has called the athletes to the line;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If there is more than one relay, each relay must be allowed the same amount of time to bring their equipment to the firing line;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) After the Chief Range Officer calls athletes to the line, they are permitted to handle their guns, dry fire (safety flags may be removed for dry firing) or carry out holding and aiming exercises on the firing line before the Preparation and Sighting Time starts; in Finals, athletes may not remove safety flags or dry fire until the Preparation and Sighting Time starts;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Pre-competition checks by the Jury and Range Officers must be completed during the 10 minutes before the Preparation and Sighting Time starts;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) The Preparation and Sighting Time begins with the command “PREPARATION AND SIGHTING TIME…START;” No shot may be fired before the command “START;”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) An athlete who fires a shot or shots before the “START” command for the Preparation and Sighting Time may be disqualified if safety is involved. If safety is not involved (6.2.3.5), the first competition shot must be registered as a miss (0);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) After 14 minutes, 30 seconds have elapsed in the Preparation and Sighting Time, the Chief Range Officer must announce “30 SECONDS.”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) At the end of the Preparation and Sighting Time, the Chief Range Officer must command “END OF PREPARATION AND SIGHTING…STOP.” There must be a brief pause of approximately 30 seconds when the Target Technician will reset the targets for MATCH firing; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) If an athlete fires a shot after the command “END OF PREPARATION AND SIGHTING…STOP” and before the “MATCH FIRING…START” command, the shot must not be counted as a MATCH shot and a two (2) point penalty must be applied to the first competition shot. 244 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) Malfunctions will be governed according to ISSF Rule 6.13. No additional time will be allowed for an equipment malfunction, but the Jury may allow additional sighting shots on return to the firing line if the malfunction is repaired, but all shots must be fired within the original time allowed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.1.2 START of MATCH Firing

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) When all targets are reset for MATCH firing, the Chief Range Officer will command “MATCH FIRING…START.” MATCH firing is considered to have started when the CRO has given the command “START;”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Every shot fired after the start of MATCH firing must be recorded as a MATCH shot, however, dry firing is allowed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) After the start of MATCH firing, no further sighting shots are allowed, except for position changes in 50m and 300m Rifle 3-Position events (see Rule 7.7.3) or when permitted by the Jury in accordance with these Rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Any further sighting shot(s) fired in contravention of this rule must be scored as miss(es) in the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The CRO must inform athletes by loudspeaker of the time remaining at both ten (10) minutes and five (5) minutes before the end of the competition time;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) A shot or shots that are not fired during the MATCH firing time must be scored as miss(es) on the last competition target(s), unless the CRO or a Jury Member has authorized extra time; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) If, during MATCH firing on 10m ESTs, the Jury directs an athlete to move his position laterally (sideways) within his firing point by 30 cm or more, the athlete may be offered additional sighters and 2 minutes additional time before he resumes MATCH firing.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.1.3 “STOP” COMMAND The competition must stop at the command “STOP.”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If a shot(s) is fired after the command “STOP,” that shot(s) must be scored as a miss; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If the shot(s) cannot be identified, the best hit(s) must be deducted from the score of that target and scored as miss(es).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.2 Specific Rules for 10m Air Gun Events

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.2.1 If an athlete releases the propelling charge prior to the Preparation and Sighting Time he must be given a WARNING (Yellow Card) for the first violation and a DEDUCTION (Green Card) of two (2) points from the lowest value shot of the first MATCH series for the second and subsequent violations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.2.2 Any release of the propelling charge, after MATCH firing starts, without a hit on the target will be scored as a miss. Dry firing without release of the propelling charge is permitted except during Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.2.3 If an athlete wishes to change, or to fill, a gas or air cylinder, he must leave the firing point to do so, after obtaining permission from the Range Officer. No extra time is allowed to change or fill a gas or air cylinder during a competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.2.4 The gun may only be loaded with one (1) pellet. When a gun is accidentally loaded with more than one (1) pellet:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the athlete is aware of the situation, he must raise his non-shooting hand to indicate to a Range Officer that he has a problem. A Range Officer must EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 245 then supervise the unloading of the gun and no penalty will be incurred. No extra time will be allowed for this; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If the athlete is unaware of the situation and fires two pellets at the same time, he must report this to a Range Officer. If there are two (2) hits on the target, the score of the higher value shot will be counted and the second shot will be annulled. If there is only one (1) hit on the target, this will be counted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.3 Interruptions in 10m Events, 50m Rifle and Pistol Events and 300m Rifle Events

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.3.1 If an athlete must stop firing for more than three (3) minutes through no fault of his own and this interruption was not caused by a malfunction of his gun or ammunition, he may demand extra time equal to the amount of time lost, or the time remaining when the interruption occurred, plus one (1) minute, if during the last five (5) minutes of the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.3.2 If an athlete is interrupted for more than five (5) minutes through no fault of his own and this interruption was not caused by a malfunction of his gun or ammunition, or if the athlete is moved to another firing point, he may have additional unlimited sighting shots at the beginning of his remaining shooting time together with any time extension granted plus an additional five (5) minutes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Range Officers or Jury Members must ensure that a complete explanation is recorded on a Range Incident Report; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any extension of time allowed by the Jury or Range Officers must be documented, stating the reason on a Range Incident Report.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.4 Late Arrival By Athlete If an athlete arrives late for a competition, he may participate but will not be given any extra time. If an athlete arrives after the Preparation and Sighting Time, no additional sighting time will be given but sighting shots are allowed. When it can be proven that an athlete’s late arrival was due to circumstances beyond his control, the Jury must grant extra time, including time for Preparation and Sighting if this does not delay the start of the Final or disrupt the overall shooting programme. In this case the Jury will determine when and on which firing point the late athlete may start.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.5 Irregular Shots -- Too Many Shots in an Event or Position If an athlete in a 10m, 50m or 300m event fires more shots in the event or position than are provided for in the programme, the extra shot(s) must be annulled on the last competition target(s). If the shot(s) cannot be identified, the highest value shot(s) must be annulled on the last competition target. The athlete must also be penalized by a deduction of two (2) points for each excessive shot fired, deducted from the lowest value shot(s) in the first series.

chunks.text: 6.11.6 Crossfires

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.6.1 Crossfires of competition shots must be scored as misses.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.6.2 If an athlete crossfires a sighting shot on the sighting target of another athlete no penalty is incurred.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.6.3 If an athlete crossfires a sighting shot on the MATCH target of another athlete, he must be penalized by the deduction of two (2) points from his own score deducted from the first series. 246 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.6.4 If an athlete receives a confirmed crossfire shot and it is impossible to determine which shot is his, he must be credited with the value of the highest undetermined shot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.6.5 If there are more hits on an athlete’s MATCH target than are provided for in the programme, and if it is impossible to confirm that another athlete(s) fired the shot(s), the hit(s) of the highest value must be nullified. Apply rule 6.11.5

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.6.6 If an athlete wishes to disclaim a shot on his target, he must report this immediately to a Range Officer.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.6.7 If the Range Officer confirms that the athlete did not fire the disputed shot(s), he must make the necessary entry on a Range Incident Report and on the Range Register and the shot must be annulled.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.6.8 If the Range Officer cannot confirm beyond all reasonable doubt that the athlete did not fire the disputed shot(s), the shot(s) must be credited to the athlete and must be so recorded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.6.9 The following must be considered as reasons to justify the annulment of a shot:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If a Range Officer confirms by his observation of the athlete and the target that the athlete did not fire the shot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If a missing shot is reported by another athlete or a Range Officer at approximately the same time, and from within the neighbouring two or three firing points; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) When using 300m EST with shot sensors, crossfires should not register on the recipient’s target, but an indication will be received at the control centre. The firer, whose target does not receive the expected shot, will be given a miss (zero) and an indication that he has cross-fired.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.11.7 Disturbances If an athlete claims that he was disturbed while firing a shot, he must keep his gun pointed downrange and immediately inform the Range Officer or Jury Member. He must not disturb other athletes. If the claim is considered justified, the shot(s) must be annulled and the athlete may repeat the shot(s) or series. If the claim is not considered justified, the shot(s) must be credited to the athlete and he may continue shooting; no penalty will be applied.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Observing preliminary and official bulletins, scores and announcements;

chunks.text: f) Receiving official information and informing team members; and

chunks.text: g) Representing the team at all official activities.

chunks.text: 6.12.4 The Athlete is responsible for:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Reporting to his firing point or shooting range, ready to shoot, at the correct time, with equipment that complies with these rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Taking his firing position on his designated firing point so that he does not disturb adjacent athletes; and

chunks.text: c) Conducting himself so that he does not disturb or adversely affect the performances of other athletes. chunks.text: 6.12.5 Coaching During Any Event

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.12.5.1 In all events, non-verbal coaching is allowed, the written word is non-verbal, as is sign language but with no audible sound, otherwise while on the firing line, an athlete may speak only with Jury Members or range officials. Coaching during training is permitted, this includes PET, but such coaching must not disturb other athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.12.5.2 Starting from the ISSF World Championship in 2026, only Coaches with a valid ‘A’ or ‘B’ ISSF Coach licence and registered as team officials, can be present on the field of play during PET, Eliminations, Qualification and permitted to be seated on the Finals range during Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.12.5.3 If an athlete wishes to speak with his Coach or Team Official during an Elimination or Qualification, the athlete must unload his gun and leave it in a safe condition on the firing line with the action open and a safety flag inserted. An athlete may leave the firing line only after notifying a Range Officer and without disturbing other athletes. This applies only to Rifle & Pistol, not Shotgun.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.12..5.4 If a coach or team official wishes to speak with a team member on the firing line, the team official must not contact the athlete directly or talk with the athlete while he is on the firing line. The team official must obtain permission from a Range Officer or Jury Member, who will call the athlete from the firing line, or the shooting station.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.12..5.5 If a team official or athlete violates the rules concerning coaching, a warning must be issued the first time. In repeated cases, two (2) points must be deducted from the athlete’s score and the team official must leave the vicinity of the firing line.
