chunks.text: 6.12.6.1 Deciding Open and Concealed Violations The Jury must decide violations according to these standards:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) In the case of an open violation of the Rules, a Warning (Yellow Card) must first be given so the athlete may have an opportunity to correct the fault. Whenever possible, the warning should be given during training or the Preparation and Sighting Time. If the athlete does not correct the fault as instructed by the Jury, two (2) points must be deducted from his score (First two (2) hit targets in the round where the second violation occurs). If the athlete still does not correct the fault after receiving a Deduction (Green Card), Disqualification (Red Card) (DSQ) must be imposed; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) In the case of a concealed violation of the Rules, when the fault is deliberately concealed, Disqualification (Red Card) (DSQ) must be imposed; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If, when asked to give an explanation for an incident, an athlete consciously and knowingly gives false information, two (2) points must be deducted (The first two (2) hit targets from the last round fired before he had been questioned). or in serious cases, disqualification may be imposed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.12.6.2 In cases of a violation of ISSF Rules or the instructions of Range Officers or Jury, the following penalties may be imposed on the athlete by a Jury Member or the Jury. Penalties for Rule violations in Shotgun events will be decided by the Jury, the Chief of Referees and the Referee, in accordance with Rule 9.16.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Warning (Yellow Card). A warning must be expressed in terms that will leave no doubt that it is a Warning and the yellow card must be shown. However, it is not necessary to precede other penalties with a warning. The warnings must be recorded on a Range Incident Report and noted on the Range Register A warning may be given by an individual Jury Member or Referee. Any warning given must be carried forward for any further similar violation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Deduction (Green Card). A deduction of points from the score may be given by an individual Jury Member or Referee, by showing a Green Card with the word “Deduction.”. In most cases, a deduction of two (2) points will apply, but exceptions are shown in the relevant Rule, e.g. for late shots or dry firing in Finals. Deductions must be recorded on a Range Incident Report Form, marked on the printer strip or scorecard in shotgun, noted on the Range Register and immediately reported to the RTS Jury. Deductions do not necessarily need to be preceded by a Warning.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Disqualification (Red Card) (DSQ). An athlete must be disqualified (DSQ) for failure to pass a post-competition check (6.7.9.1) or for a violation of Shotgun Rule 9.4.1.1 or 9.4.3.2.d. Disqualification for any other reason may only be given by the decision of a majority of the Jury. The disqualification of an athlete is expressed by the Jury by showing a Red Card with the word “Disqualification.” If an athlete is disqualified during any phase of an event (Elimination, Qualification or Final), the results for that athlete for all phases of that event must be deleted and the athlete must be listed at the end of the results list with an explanation regarding why the athlete was disqualified.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Unsportsmanlike Behaviour (DQB). If an athlete is disqualified for a serious safety violation or for the physical or verbal abuse of a competition official or another athlete (Rule 6.12.6.4) as decided by a majority of the Jury, all results for that athlete for all events in the Championship must be deleted and the explanation(s) must indicate DQB. 258 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Anti-Doping Violation (AD-DSQ). If an athlete is disqualified for an anti- doping violation, all results for that athlete for all events in the Championship must be deleted and the explanation(s) must indicate AD-DSQ.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Penalties should be expressed both with a verbal explanation and with the display of yellow, green or red cards. The size of penalty cards should be approximately 70mm x 100mm.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) A team, of which a member has been disqualified, must not be ranked and must be shown in the result list with the remark “DSQ.”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) When there is a penalty or disqualification, a Jury Member must provide or approve remarks for the Results Lists to explain the penalty or disqualification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.12.6.3 Serious Safety Violations If the Jury determines that an athlete has handled a gun or violated a safety rule in a dangerous manner, the athlete must be disqualified (DSQ) (see

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.12.6.4 Physical or Verbal Abuse of a Competition Official or Athlete An athlete or team official who makes verbal abuse or physical contact with a Jury Member, Referee, Range Officer, other competition official or another athlete by grasping, pushing, shoving, striking or similar means may be excluded from further participation in a Championship. Any such act of physical o r v e r b a l abuse must be reported to the C h a i r p e r s o n of the Jury responsible for supervising that area of activity. One or more witnesses or physical evidence must confirm the act of alleged abuse. The Jury must then decide whether the athlete or team official may be excluded from that Championship. A decision to exclude may be appealed to the Jury of Appeal (6.16.6). If the Jury or Jury of Appeal concludes that the act of abuse was of such a serious nature that further sanctions are warranted, they may, in addition to excluding the athlete or team official from the current championship also refer the case to the ISSF Ethics Committee (3.12.3.5, Annex “CE”) for further consideration.

chunks.text: 6.13 MALFUNCTIONS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.1 A malfunction occurs when a gun fails to fire a projectile when the trigger is pulled.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.2 Malfunctions may be either ALLOWABLE or NON-ALLOWABLE.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.2.1 Allowable Malfunctions are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) A cartridge fails to fire;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A bullet or pellet is lodged in the barrel; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The gun fails to fire or function properly and the trigger mechanism has been released.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.2.2 Non-Allowable Malfunctions are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete has opened the action of his gun;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The safety was engaged;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The athlete did not properly load his gun;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The athlete did not pull the trigger; or EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 259

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The malfunction is due to any cause that could reasonably have been corrected by the athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) When electronic trigger is used, the battery fails.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.3 If an athlete has a gun or ammunition malfunction, he may repair it and continue shooting or, if the malfunction was an ALLOWABLE malfunction, he may continue shooting with another gun of the same type and calibre that complies with these Rules. The replacement gun will be subject to targeted testing.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.4 No extra competition time is allowed to repair or replace a gun after any malfunction in 10m, 50m and 300m Rifle or Pistol Elimination or Qualification Rounds, but the Jury may allow an athlete to fire additional sighting shots after repairing or replacing a malfunctioning gun if the malfunction was ALLOWABLE.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.5 Specific rules concerning malfunctions in 25m Pistol events are found in Rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.6 Specific rules concerning malfunctions in Finals are found in Rules 6.17.1.6,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.7 Specific rules concerning malfunctions in shotgun are found in Rules 9.11.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.8 Range Officers, Referees or Jury Members must ensure that malfunctions are documented on Range Incident Reports or Malfunction Score Computation Forms and in the Range Register.

chunks.text: 6.14 SCORING AND RESULTS PROCEDURES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.1 The RTS Office must publish Preliminary Results on the Range Scoreboard as soon as possible after each relay and stage and completion of each event.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.2 Official Final Results must be published on the Main Scoreboard after the Protest Time has expired. Results Distribution: The organizer must provide for the distribution of

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.3  Preliminary and Official Final Results to all match officials, participating teams and media. This may be done by distributing paper or electronic (see 6.6.5 b, Sustainability Option) Results Lists.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.4 After each ISSF Championship, The Official ISSF Results Provider will produce an electronic (on-line) Official Results Book. The Official Results Book for each Championship must contain:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) A table of contents;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) A list of Entries by Country

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The Competition Schedule;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) A list of Medallists by name;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) A list of Medals by Country by number;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) A list of New and Equalled Records; and 260 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) All final results in the standard ISSF order of events as follows: 1) Men‘s 10m, 50m and 300m rifle events; 2) Men‘s 10m, 25m and 50m pistol events; 3) Men‘s Trap and Skeet; 4) Men‘s 10m and 50m Moving Target events; 5) Men’s Team Events; 6) Women‘s 10m, 50m and 300m Rifle events; 7) Women‘s 10m and 25m Pistol events; 8) Women’s Trap, and Skeet events; and 9) Women‘s 10m Moving Target Events; 10) Women’s Team Events; 11) Mixed Team 10m, 25m, 50m, 300m, Trap and Skeet.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.4.1 These lists must contain the full names as used in the ISSF ID Numbers: Family name (in capital letters), full given name (first letter only capitalized), Bib Numbers and the Nation (official IOC abbreviation) of each athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.4.2 The following abbreviations must be used in results lists when appropriate: DNF Did not Finish DNS Did not Start DSQ Disqualified DQB Disqualification for Unsportsmanlike Behaviour WR New World Record in a Final QWR New Qualification World Record EWR Equalled World Record in a Final EQWR Equalled Qualification World Record WRJ New World Record Junior in a Final QWRJ New Qualification World Record Junior EWRJ Equalled World Record Junior in a Final EQWRJ Equalled Qualification World Record Junior OR New Olympic Record in a Final EOR Equalled Olympic Record in a Final QOR Qualification Olympic Record EQOR Equalled Qualification Olympic Record MQS Minimum Qualifying Score RPO Ranking Points Only OOC Out of Competition

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.5 The Official Final Results must be verified and signed by a Member of the RTS Jury to confirm its accuracy.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.6 All irregularities, penalties, misses, malfunctions, extra time allowed, repeated shots/series or the annulment of shots, etc., must be clearly marked and recorded on a Range Incident Report and the Range Register, printout by a Range Officer and/or Jury Member and the scorecard for shotgun. Copies of completed Range Incident Reports (Form IR) must immediately be forwarded to the scoring and results office. At the end of each competition, the RTS Jury must examine the results to confirm that all malfunction calculations and any penalties are correctly recorded in the results list. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 261

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.7 Deductions from Rifle, Pistol and shotgun scores must always be made in the series/round in which the violation occurred. If general deductions are involved, they must be made from the lowest value MATCH shot(s) in the first series of the stage where the deduction applies.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.8 The RTS Jury must check the ten (10) best individual and three (3) best team results prior to approving the Final Results List. When EST are used, this check must be done by comparing scores recorded in the main computer with scores from the printout or an independent memory source (Rule 6.3.2.7) plus all manual score interventions documented by Incident Reports (IR) or malfunction forms.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.9 WORLD RECORDS World Records will be established in all ISSF Championships in accordance with General Regulations, Art.3.10 (see also 6.1.2.b) in all ISSF events where gold medals are awarded. Any Records can only be established by athletes competing for awards (in competition). Athletes with RPO, MQS only or OOC status cannot establish any records

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.9.1 Olympic Records (OR) may only be established in the Olympic Games.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.9.2 World Records Junior (WRJ) for recognized non-Olympic events will be established by using total results in those events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.9.3 Qualification World Records (QWR) and Qualification World Records Junior (QWRJ) will be established by using total results in Qualification competitions in all Olympic events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.14.9.4 When a World Record is established in an ISSF Championship, the report Procedures for Verification of World Records (Rule 3.12.3.6, Annex R) must be completed and forwarded to ISSF Headquarters by the Technical Delegate.

chunks.text: 6.15 TIE-BREAKING

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.15.1 Individual Ties in 10m, 25m, 50m and 300m Events All tied scores will be broken for 10m, 25m, 50m, and 300m events by applying the following Rules:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The highest number of inner tens;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The highest score of the last ten (10) shot series working backward by 10- shot series in full ring scoring (not inner tens or decimals) until the tie is broken;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If any ties remain, scores will be compared on a shot-by-shot basis using inner tens (i.e. an inner ten outranks a 10 that is not an inner ten) beginning with the last shot, then the next to the last shot, etc.;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If any ties remain, and EST are used, scores will be compared on a shot-by- shot basis using decimal ring scores beginning with the last shot, then the next to the last shot, etc.;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) If any ties remain, the athletes must have the same ranking and must be listed in Latin alphabetical order using the athlete’s family name;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) When decimal scoring is used for 10m Air Rifle or 50m Rifle Prone Elimination or Qualification events, ties will be broken by the highest score of the last ten shot series, etc. (decimal scores) and then by comparing decimal scores on a shot-by-shot basis beginning with the last shot, then the next to last shot, etc. 262 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.15.2 Ties in Shotgun Events (see Shotgun Rule 9.14)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.15.3 Ties in Moving Target Events (see Moving Target Rule 10.12)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.15.4 Ties in Olympic Events with Finals If there is a tie to be eligible for Rifle or Pistol Finals from the Qualification, the tie will be broken by Rule 6.15.1. If there is a tie to be eligible for Shotgun Finals from the Qualification, the tie will be broken by Rule 9.15.1.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.15.5 Ties in Team Events Ties in team events, including ties in the Qualification stage of Mixed Team events, must be decided by totalling the results of all members of a team and following the procedures for breaking individual ties.

chunks.text: 6.16 PROTESTS AND APPEALS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.1 All Protests and Appeals are to be decided in accordance with ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.2 Verbal Protests

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.2.1 Any athlete or team official has the right to protest a condition of the competition, decision or action of a competition official immediately and verbally to a Referee, Range Officer or Jury Member on the following matters:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) An athlete or team official considers that the ISSF Rules or the competition programme were not followed in conducting the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) An athlete or team official does not agree with a decision or action by a competition official, Referee, Range Officer or Jury Member;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) An athlete was impeded or disturbed by other athlete(s), competition official(s), spectator(s), member(s) of the media or other person(s) or cause(s);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) An athlete had a long interruption in shooting caused by range equipment failure, the clarification of irregularities or other cause(s); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) An athlete had irregularities regarding shooting times, including shooting times that were too short.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.2.2 Referees, Range Officers and Jury Members must consider verbal protests immediately. They may take immediate action to correct the situation or refer the protest to the full Jury for a decision. In such cases, a Referee, Range Officer or Jury Member may stop the shooting temporarily if necessary.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.3 Written Protests Any athlete or team official who does not agree with the action or decision taken on a verbal protest may protest in writing to the Jury. Any athlete or team official also has the right to submit a written protest without making a verbal protest. All written protests must be submitted to a member of the appropriate Jury not later than 20 minutes after the matter in question, or after the end of the round where the incident occurred and the protest fee becomes payable. Written Protests and Appeals must be submitted on the ISSF Protest Form (see Protest Form at 6.19).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.4 A Protest Fee becomes payable when a written Protest or Ap- peal is submitted to a Jury member, as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Protest: 50,00 EUR;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Appeal of Protest Decision: 100,00 EUR; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 263

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Protest Fee becomes payable when a completed Protest Form is delivered to a Jury Member and must be paid to the Jury Member or Organizing Committee as soon as possible; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Protest and Appeal fees must be returned if the Protest or Appeal is upheld, or will be retained by the Organizing Committee if the Protest or Appeal is denied.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.5 Scoring Protests Decisions by the RTS Jury on the value or number of shots on a target are final and may not be appealed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.5.1 Scoring Protest Time All scoring or results protests must be submitted within 10 minutes after Preliminary Results are posted on the Range Scoreboard (Rule 6.4.2.i). The time when the Scoring Protest Time ends must be shown on the Range Scoreboard, when Preliminary Results are posted. The location to which any score protest must be made must be published in the Official Programme.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.5.2 EST Score Protests If an athlete protests the value of an indicated shot on an EST, the protest will only be accepted when it is made before the next shot or series (25m events) is fired or within three (3) minutes after the last shot, however, this requirement does not apply in case of a failure of the paper or rubber band to advance or other target failures.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If a protest is made concerning the value of a shot, the athlete will be requested to fire another shot at the end of the competition, so that this extra shot may be counted if the protest is upheld and the correct value of the disputed shot cannot be determined;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If the RTS Jury determines that a protested shot scores within two (2) decimal rings of the value of an indicated shot, the protest must not be upheld;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the protest concerning a shot value, other than zero (0) or failure to register, is not upheld, a two (2) point penalty from the score of the disputed shot will be awarded and the protest fee must be paid;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The team official or athlete has the right to know the resolution of the disputed shot; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Shots on 50m EST with an indicated value of 9.5 or higher may not be protested in Elimination or Qualification Rounds; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Score protests regarding the value or number of shots are not permitted in Finals (Rule 6.17.1.7).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.6 Appeals If there is a disagreement with a Jury decision, the matter may be appealed to the Jury of Appeal, except that decisions by a Finals Protest Jury (6.17.1.10

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) and decisions by the RTS Jury on the value or number of shots (6.16.5) are final and may not be appealed. Such appeals must be submitted in writing by the team leader or a representative not later than 30 minutes after the Jury decision has been announced. The decision of the Jury of Appeal is final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.16.7 Copies of all decisions regarding written protests and appeals must be forwarded by the Technical Delegate(s) to the ISSF Secretary General together with his Final Report for review by the appropriate Section and Technical Committees. 264 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.text: 6.17 INDIVIDUAL FINALS IN OLYMPIC RIFLE AND PISTOL EVENTS General Finals Competition Procedures. These procedures apply to Finals

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1  in all 10m, 25m and 50m Rifle and Pistol Individual events. Procedures applicable to specific events are shown as follows: Rule 6.17.2 - 10m Air Rifle and 10m Air Pistol, Men and Women Rule 6.17.3 - 50m Rifle 3-Position Men and Women Rule 6.17.4 - 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol Men Rule 6.17.5 - 25m Pistol Women Rule 6.18 – 10m Rifle and Pistol Mixed Team events Separate procedures apply to Shotgun events, as shown in Section 9.17 Qualification for Finals. All athletes entered in an event will fire the

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.1  Qualification course (Rule 3.3.5 and 3.3.6.5) to determine the finalists for that event. The eight (8) highest-ranking athletes in the Qualification advance to the Finals in all Olympic events

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.2  Start Positions. Start positions in Finals are assigned according to a random draw that is done automatically by the computer when the Finals Start List is produced. 10m and 50m firing points must be labelled R1-A-B-C-D-E-F-G- H-R2. Targets for 25m Pistol Women Finals must be labelled A-B-R1-C-D/E-F- R2-G-H. The reserve targets are designated R1 and R2. Targets for 25m Rapid Fire Pistol will be designated A-B / C-D. Reporting and Start Times. The Start Time for a Final is when the CRO

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.3  begins the commands for the first MATCH shot/series. Athletes must report to the Finals Range Preparation Area at least 30 minutes before the Start Time. A two (2) point/hit penalty will be deducted from the score of the first MATCH shot/series if the athlete does not report on time. For 25m events a two (2) HIT penalty will be deducted from athletes first two (2) hits. Athletes must report with their equipment including sufficient ammunition to complete the Final, competition clothing and a national team uniform that is appropriate to wear in the Medal Ceremony. The Jury must confirm that all finalists are present and that their names and nations are correctly recorded in the results system and on the scoreboards. Juries must complete equipment checks during the reporting period as soon as possible after the athlete reports. During Finals security measures should be put in place to ensure the security of all equipment and athletes belongings left within the Preparation area.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.4  Late Arrival. Any finalist who does not report to the preparation area within 10 min. after the Reporting Time may not start and will be recorded as the first eliminated athlete and shown as DNS. If a finalist does not report, the first elimination will begin with the seventh place. Scoring. Qualification scores entitle an athlete to a place in a Final, but do not

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.5  carry forward. Scoring in Finals starts from zero (0) in accordance with these rules. A deduction or penalty must be applied to the score of the MATCH shot/ series where the violation occurred. No score below zero (0) will be recorded (e.g. 3-1 point deduction = 2, 0-1 point deduction = 0). Malfunctions, 10m and 50m Finals. If a finalist has an ALLOWABLE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.6  malfunction (Rule 6.13.2) during a single shot, a maximum of one (1) min. will be given to repair the malfunction or replace the gun, after which the athlete will be directed to repeat the shot. If a finalist has an ALLOWABLE malfunction in a 5-shot or 10-shot series and the malfunction can be repaired or the gun replaced within one (1) min., any shots fired in that series will be counted and EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 265 the athlete will be permitted to complete the series within the time remaining when the malfunction was claimed plus additional time equal to the time required to repair the malfunction, but not exceeding one (1) min. Finalists may have only one ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION per Final. Score Protests. Score protests regarding the value or number of shots are not

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.7  permitted in Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.8 EST Complaints During Finals

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If a finalist complains that his target failed to register a shot during Sighting shots, the athlete must be directed to fire another shot at that target. If that shot registers, the Final will continue. If that shot does not register or if there is a complaint regarding the failure of a paper/rubber strip to advance, the CRO must command “STOP…UNLOAD” for all finalists and the athlete with the malfunctioning target must be moved to a reserve target. As soon as that athlete is in position on a spare target, the CRO will give all finalists two (2) minutes preparation time and then restart the Preparation and Sighting Time for the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If there is a complaint concerning an unexpected zero (0) (missing shot) during a MATCH shot/series, the Jury (Jury Member-in-Charge, second Competition Jury Member and one RTS) must determine whether the missing shot actually was a miss (0) or if the target malfunctioned (the Jury may direct the CRO to stop firing so they can examine the target). Unless the Jury finds credible evidence that the shot missed the target, it shall direct the athlete to fire another competition shot (10m/50m), 25m Pistol Women series completion (one shot) or a 25m Rapid-Fire Men series. If the extra competition shot registers, the value of that shot shall be counted in lieu of the unexpected zero (missing shot) and the Final shall continue. In a 25m Rapid-Fire Men Final, the score of the repeat series shall count in lieu of the hit total of the original series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the shot fired on a target that had the unexplained miss does not register, the athlete must be moved to a reserve target (25m RFP to another target group). In 10m or 50m Finals, the athlete who was moved to a reserve target must be given two (2) minutes Preparation and Sighting Time. The athlete who is moved must, on command, be allowed to fire the missing competition shot, series completion or refire series (25m RFP) before competition firing continues for all athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) During any delay in competition firing, other finalists are permitted to do aiming exercises and dry fire. If the total delay to resolve the unexplained miss issue is longer than five (5) minutes, all athletes in 10m and 50m Finals must be given two (2) minutes Sighting time before competition firing resumes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) In a 50m Three-Position Event, if there is a complaint of an unexpected zero (0) (missing shot) during the twenty-two (22) minutes MATCH/shot series, the following procedure will apply: • The Jury member in Charge must immediately note the athlete’s remaining time and instruct him to fire one (1) additional shot on the same target. • If the additional shot is successfully registered, its score shall be counted and the unregistered shot shall be disregarded. No additional time will be allowed. • If the additional shot is not registered, the Jury shall immediately instruct the athlete to move to a reserve target, with assistance from the Range Officer, taking care to ensure that other finalists are not disturbed. The athlete’s Coach is allowed to approach and speak to his athlete whilst he is moving and preparing to shoot. 266 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF • Once established in his new position, the athlete will be allowed to complete all remaining kneeling, prone and standing sighting shots in the time that

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: remained when his target malfunction occurred, plus an additional two (2) minutes. The Jury Member in Charge will remind him of his maximum remaining time. • Whilst the affected athlete is being moved and completing his remaining shots, the original twenty-two minutes for the remaining Finalists will probably have expired. The CRO will command; “STOP, except for the athlete on firing point ‘X’”. Those athletes will be permitted to perform aiming exercises and dry firing whilst waiting for the affected athlete to complete his remaining Match shots and Standing preparation. That process should take a maximum time of seven (7) minutes. • When the repositioned athlete’s remaining time has expired, he will be commanded to stop. All athletes will then be allowed two (2) minutes to fire Sighting shots in the Standing position to prepare for the first series of Match shots. The Final will then continue as normal.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.9 Finals Range Equipment. Finals Ranges must be equipped with electronic scoreboards that display ranked results for competition officials, athletes, coaches and spectators; a countdown clock visible to finalists and a speaker system. If a count-down clock is not visible to all finalists, all controlled times must be shown on monitors clearly visible to all finalists. Chairs must be provided for Jury Members on duty, Range Officers, coaches and eliminated athletes who withdraw from the firing line. A table or bench must be provided on which athletes can place their equipment before entering the Finals range or if they withdraw from the firing line.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.10 Finals Officials. The conduct and supervision of Finals must be done by the following personnel:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) CRO. An experienced Chief Range Officer with an ISSF A or B Licence must conduct Finals;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Competition Jury. The Competition Jury must supervise the conduct of Finals. The Jury Chairperson must designate himself or one Jury Member as the Jury Member-in-Charge;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) RTS Jury. One member of the RTS Jury must be present to oversee the Finals’ results process;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Finals Protest Jury. One member of the Jury of Appeal, the Jury Member-in- Charge and one other member of the Competition Jury, as designated by the Technical Delegate and Jury Chairperson, shall act as the Finals Protest Jury and must decide protests if any are made during a Final; no appeals against Finals Protest Jury decisions are permitted;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Range Officer (RO). One or two experienced Range Officer(s) will assist the CRO by checking guns for safety, escorting finalists and their coaches to and from the FOP and handling any malfunction claims during the Final;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Technical Officer(s). The Official Results Provider appoints the Technical Officer(s) to prepare and operate the ESTs and the graphic display of results and to consult with the Juries regarding any technical problems;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Announcer. An official designated by the ISSF or Organizing Committee must work with the CRO and be responsible for introducing finalists, announcing scores and providing information to spectators; and EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 267

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Sound Technician. A qualified technical official must be available to operate the sound and music system during the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.11 Finals Production and Music. The conduct of Finals must use colour, lighting, music, announcements, commentary, staging and CRO commands in a complete production that portrays the athletes and their competitive performances in the most appealing and exciting ways to spectator and television audiences.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.12 Presentation of Finalists. After the Command “Athletes to the Line”, athletes will enter one at a time, as the Announcer introduces them by giving the name, nation and brief information about each Finalist. The Announcer must also introduce the CRO and Jury Member-in- Charge.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.13 Protests in Finals

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Any protests in a Final must be verbal and immediate. Protests are made by the athlete or his coach holding up his hand;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) There is no protest fee for a protest in a Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Any protest must be decided immediately by the Finals Protest Jury (3.12.3.7, 6.16.6 and 6.17.1.10.d.). A decision by the Finals Protest Jury is final and may not be appealed; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If a protest in a Final is not upheld, a penalty of two points or two hits must be deducted from the score of the shot or series relating to the protest.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.1.14 Finals Rules and Procedures.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) ISSF General Technical Rules or the Technical Rules for each event apply in all cases not covered by Rule 6.17.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Reporting and equipment set-up. After reporting to the Preparation Area, finalists or their coaches must be allowed to place their guns and equipment on their firing points at least 20:00 min. before the Final start time. Gun cases and equipment containers must not be left on the FOP. Aiming exercises are not permitted at this time. Athletes must then return to the Preparation Area, ready to be called to the firing line for their presentation and warm-up period. Coaches will take their allocated seats on the field of play.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Call to the line. An NTO will direct athletes to line up close to the Finals Range ten (10) minutes before the published START time. When Rifle finalists are called from the Preparation Area to the firing line, they must walk to the line fully dressed with trousers and jackets closed. The CRO will announce “ATHLETES TO THE LINE”. See Rule 7.5.2.3 regarding ‘walking’.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Safety flags. After finalists are called to the line, they may handle their guns, get into firing positions and do holding or aiming exercises but they may not remove safety flags or dry fire until the “PREPARATION AND SIGHTING TIME…START” command or “PREPARATION BEGINS NOW” (25m Pistol) command.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Dry firing. In Finals, dry firing is permitted only during a Preparation and Sighting Time, Changeover and Sighting Times or a Preparation Period. Dry firing, at any other time must be penalized with a one (1) point deduction in 10m and 50m Finals and a one (1) hit deduction in 25m Pistol Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Early loading. No finalist is permitted to load a rifle or pistol until the CRO gives the command “LOAD” or “START“. This means that for the Preparation and Sighting Time, where there is no “LOAD” command, “START” is also an 268 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF authorization to load. Loading is defined as bringing a cartridge or pellet or magazine with cartridges into contact with the gun (see 6.2.3.4).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Holding and aiming exercises. In Finals, holding and aiming exercises are permitted from the time finalists are called to the line (“TAKE YOUR POSITIONS” command) until the “STOP… UNLOAD” command at the end of the Final is given, except that holding and aiming exercises may not be done during the presentations. For 25m RFPM final, holding exercises are per 6.17.4.h. and 6.17.4.q

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Firing before START or LOAD command. If a finalist in a 10m, 25m or 50m Final loads and fires a shot before the “PREPARATION AND SIGHTING TIME…START” command or before the “FOR THE SIGHTING SERIES… LOAD” command, he must be disqualified.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Firing after STOP command. If a finalist fires a shot after the “PREPARATION AND SIGHTING TIME… STOP” command or the “CHANGE-OVER AND SIGHTING TIME…STOP” command and before the “START” command for the next competition series, the shot must not be counted as a MATCH shot and a two (2) point penalty must be applied to the first MATCH shot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) 25m Pistol – early firing. If a finalist in a 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol Men Final fires a shot before the green light for a series comes on, but after the series has started, the entire series must be scored as score of four remaining shots and 1 Hit penalty is applied. If a finalist in a 25m Pistol Women Final fires a shot before the green light for a shot comes on but after series has started, that shot will be scored as a miss and a one (1) hit penalty will be deducted from the score of the series. Series is considered started after command ATTENTION. If a shot is fired before series is started the shot must not be counted as a competition shot and one (1) HIT must be deducted from the score of the repeated or completed series. Athlete which fired accidentally must not continue but must act as in 8.8.2.3. If the procedure is not followed, and the athlete continues the original series, the score will be the same as if the series has already started

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) 10m Rifle & Pistol – early firing. If an athlete in a 10m Final fires a shot after the ‘’LOAD” command but before the “START” command the shot will be scored as a miss.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) Firing extra shot. If a finalist fires an extra shot in a series or single shot time, the extra shot must be nullified and a two (2) point/hit penalty must be applied to the last correct shot/series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: m) Firing inadvertently. If a finalist who is not involved in a shoot-off or malfunction completion/refire loads and fires a shot that shot must be nullified. There is no penalty for this inadvertent mistake.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: n) Safety flags - must remain inserted in finalists’ guns until the Preparation and Sighting Time starts. Safety flags must be inserted during the presentation and when an athlete is eliminated or the Final concludes. Athletes who are eliminated during a Final must place their guns down on the firing point, bench or equipment box (3-Position Finals) with actions open and muzzles pointed downrange, with safety flags inserted. A Range Officer must check all guns to make sure safety flags are inserted. Medal winners may pose with their guns immediately after the Finals, but no guns may be removed from the firing points until safety flags are inserted and checked by a Range Officer. If an athlete inadvertently fails to insert a safety flag, a Range Officer is authorized to correct the fault and insert a safety flag. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 269

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: o) Coaching. Non-verbal coaching is permitted during all Finals. Verbal coaching is permitted in 25m RFPM final at the loading areas only.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: p) Incorrect commands. If a Finals CRO in either an individual or mixed team Final gives an incorrect command, such as failing to start a relay correctly or calling STOP before all athletes have fired or completed firing, the following procedure must take place: If a Finals CRO in either an individual or mixed team Final gives an incorrect command during a single series, shots already fired must be counted. The CRO must reset the time clock to the original time limit and give new commands to allow the athlete(s) who did not start or were unable to complete firing, to fire their remaining shots. If a Finals CRO in either an individual or mixed team Final gives an incorrect command during a multi-shot individual or mixed team series, shots already fired must be counted. The Jury-Member-in-Charge must determine how much time was remaining at the time STOP was commanded, add 60 seconds to that time and instruct the CRO to restart and complete the series so athletes who have shots remaining can fire. If any athlete misunderstands this procedure and accidentally fires too many

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: shots, any extra shots must be nullified and incur no penalties.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: q) Presentation of Medallists. After the CRO declares “RESULTS ARE FINAL,” the Jury Member in Charge must assemble the three medallists on the FOP and the Announcer must recognize the medal winners by announcing: “THE BRONZE MEDAL, REPRESENTING (COUNTRY), GOES TO (NAME)” “THE SILVER MEDAL, REPRESENTING (COUNTRY), GOES TO (NAME)” “AND THE GOLD MEDAL, REPRESENTING (COUNTRY), GOES TO (NAME)”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: r) Malfunctions. Only one (1) malfunction will be allowed for each athlete throughout the Final. Athletes may be allowed one (1) minute to repair or replace a malfunctioning firearm to permit the Final to continue without unnecessary delay.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: s) Music. During the Final, music must be played which should be approved by The Technical Delegate. Enthusiastic audience support is encouraged and recommended during all Final stages.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: t) Penalties. Any penalties will be applied according to ISSF rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: u) Irregular cases. ISSF General Technical Rules will apply to matters not mentioned in the above paragraphs. The Jury will decide irregular or disputed matters according to General Technical Rules for each event.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: v) National identification (dress code). Athletes must wear shooting clothes consistent with the ISSF Dress Code, (Rule 6.20). Rifle athletes must display their national identification on their shooting jackets as follows: The national flag of the country, or the 3-letter identifier as determined by the IOC on the pocket that faces towards the audience or on the lower back of the jacket. 270 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.2 FINALS – 10m AIR RIFLE AND 10m AIR PISTOL, MEN AND WOMEN NOTE: Timings in this rule are provided as guidelines. For detailed timings for the conduct of Finals, check the “Commands and Announcements for Finals” documents that are available from ISSF Headquarters.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Final consists of two (2) series of five (5) MATCH shots each fired in a FINALS FORMAT time of 250 sec. per series (5 + 5 shots). This is followed by fourteen (14) single MATCH shots each fired on command in a time of 50 sec. Eliminations of the lowest scoring finalists begin after the 12th shot and continue after every two shots until the gold and silver medals are decided. There are a total of twenty-four (24) shots in the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) SCORING Scoring in Finals is done with tenth-ring (decimal) scoring. Cumulative total scores in a Final determine final rankings, with ties broken according to shoot-off scores. Deductions for violations occurring before the first MATCH shot will be applied to the score of the first MATCH shot. Deductions for other penalties will be applied to the score of the shot where the violation occurred.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Finalists or their coaches must be allowed to place guns and equipment on EQUIPMENT SET-UP their firing points not less than 20 min. before the Start Time. TIME 20:00 min before

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The CRO will call finalists to the firing line approximately ten (10) minutes WARM-UP PERIOD before the Start Time by commanding “ATHLETES TO THE LINE.” Athletes Approx. 10:00 min will enter one at a time and be introduced as they walk to their allocated firing before. point and must stand facing the audience. The Announcer will then introduce the CRO and Jury Member in Charge. After all introductions have been made the CRO will announce “TAKE YOUR POSITIONS”. After 30 seconds for Rifle and 10 seconds for Pistol, the CRO will start a combined Preparation and Sighting Time by commanding “FIVE (5) MINUTES PREPARATION AND SIGHTING TIME…START.” During this time, finalists may fire unlimited sighting shots. At 30 sec. before the end of the Preparation and Sighting Time, the CRO will command “30 SECONDS.” After five (5) minutes, the CRO will command “STOP…UNLOAD.” No score announcements are made during sighting shots. The Targets and Scoreboard must be cleared for MATCH shots. After 60 sec., the CRO will begin commands for the first MATCH series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The CRO will command “FOR THE FIRST COMPETITION SERIES… 1st COMPETITION LOAD.” After 5 sec., the CRO will command “START.” Finalists have 250 STAGE sec. to fire five (5) shots. 2 x 5 Shots At 250 sec. or after all finalists have fired five (5) shots, the CRO will Time limit: 250 sec. command “STOP.” for each series Immediately after the command “STOP,” the Announcer will give 15-20 Competition firing sec. of comments on the current ranking of the athletes and notable scores. starts at 0:00 min. Individual shot scores are not announced. Immediately after the Announcer finishes, the CRO will command “FOR THE NEXT COMPETITION SERIES, LOAD.” After 5 sec., the CRO will command “START.” At 250 sec. or after all finalists have fired five (5) shots, the CRO will command “STOP.” The Announcer will again comment on the athletes and their scores and explain that single shots will begin and that after each second shot, the lowest ranking finalist will be eliminated. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 271

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Immediately after the Announcer finishes, the CRO will command “FOR THE 2nd COMPETITION NEXT COMPETITION SHOT, LOAD.” After 5 sec., the CRO will STAGE command “START.” SINGLE SHOTS Finalists have 50 sec. to fire each shot. 14 x 1 Shot At 50 sec., or when all athletes have fired a single shot the CRO will Time limit: 50 sec. for command each shot “STOP” and the Announcer will give comments about the Finalists and their scores. Immediately after the Announcer finishes, the CRO will command “FOR THE NEXT COMPETITION SHOT, LOAD.” After 5 sec., the CRO will command “START.” This sequence will continue until 24 total shots (two 5-shot series and 14 single shots), are fired. At the end of the 24th shot, the CRO will command “STOP…UNLOAD.” A Range Officer must verify that gun actions are open with safety flags inserted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) ELIMINATIONS After all Finalists have fired twelve (12) shots, the lowest ranking athlete is eliminated (8th place). The lowest ranked finalists will continue to be eliminated as follows: After 14 shots – 7th place After 16 shots – 6th place After 18 shots – 5th place After 20 shots – 4th place After 22 shots – 3rd place (bronze medal winner is decided) After 24 shots – 2nd and 1st places (silver and gold medal winners are decided)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) If there is a tie for the lowest ranking athlete to be eliminated, the tied athletes TIE-BREAKING will fire an additional tie-breaking single shot(s) until the tie is broken. For the tie-breaking shot, the CRO will immediately announce the family names of the tied athletes and command them to fire the tie-breaking shot(s) with the normal firing procedure.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) FINALS After the two (2) remaining finalists fire their 24th shots, and if there are no COMPLETION ties or protest, the CRO will command “STOP…UNLOAD” and the declare “RESULTS ARE FINAL.” The Jury must assemble the three medallists on the FOP and the Announcer will immediately recognize the bronze, silver and gold medal winners according to 6.17.1.14 q. 272 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.17.3 FINALS – 50m RIFLE 3-Position MEN AND WOMEN )a The Final consists of 10 MATCH shots in each of the Kneeling and Prone FINALS FORMAT positions, fired in that order, in a total time of twenty-two (22) minutes. When finished firing Match shots in the Prone position, athletes must change to the Standing position and may fire unlimited sighting shots in any time remaining. Athletes are responsible for changing their targets from Match to Sighters when changing positions. No changing of clothing is allowed, but zippers and other fastenings may be adjusted as required. Athletes will then fire two (2), 5-shot series of shots on command in the Standing position in 250 seconds each series. The two (2) lowest ranking finalists are eliminated after 10 (2 x 5) shots. The Final continues in the Standing position with single-shots on command, each fired in 50 seconds. After every shot the athlete with the lowest ranking is eliminated until two (2) athletes remain to fire the last shot and decide the gold medal winner. There are a total of 35 shots in the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: RANGE EQUIPMENT Athletes will be provided with a box in which to place all equipment required to change for the three positions, including extra ammunition. These boxes must be placed at the rear of each firing point. Before returning to the firing line after changing their equipment, athletes must place all unused equipment in their box to keep the firing point clear. If an athlete inadvertently leaves equipment on the firing point and adopts the next position, a Range Officer may assist by discretely placing the equipment in the box before Match firing starts. Shooting mats will be provided for each athlete to use as desired, which must be placed at the back of each firing point when the athlete takes the Standing position. A Range Officer may assist by tidying or collecting the unused mats.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) SCORING Scoring is done with tenth-ring (decimal) scoring. Cumulative total scores in the Final determine final rankings, with ties broken according to i) (below. Deductions for violations occurring before the first competition shot will be applied to the score of the first competition shot. Deductions for other penalties will be applied to the score of the shot where the violation occurred.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Athletes or athletes’ coaches must be allowed to place rifles and equipment EQUIPMENT SET-UP on the firing points not less than 20 minutes before the Start Time. All rifle TIME accessories and equipment needed to complete position changes must be 20:00 min before kept in a single container that remains at the back of the athlete’s firing point during the Final. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 273

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) PREPARATION The CRO will call finalists to the firing line approximately ten (10) minutes AND SIGHTING before the Start Time by commanding “ATHLETES TO THE LINE.” Athletes KNEELING POSITION will enter one at a time and be introduced as they walk to their allocated Approx. 10:00 min. firing point and must stand facing the audience. The Announcer will then before introduce the CRO and Jury Member in Charge. After all introductions have been made the CRO will announce “TAKE YOUR POSITIONS”. Finalists must get into the kneeling position and may do holding or aiming exercises, but they may not remove safety flags or dry fire. After thirty (30) seconds, the CRO will start a combined Preparation and Sighting Time by commanding “FIVE MINUTES PREPARATION AND SIGHTING TIME…START.” After this command, finalists may remove safety flags, dry fire and fire unlimited sighting shots. No score announcements are made during sighting shots. At 30 sec. before the end of the Preparation and Sighting Time, the CRO will

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: command “30 SECONDS.” After five (5) min., the CRO will command “STOP”. Athletes must remain in the kneeling position whilst the targets are reset to MATCH by the EST Technical Officer. A Range Officer must check that all targets have been correctly reset and indicate that to the CRO. .

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) MATCH FIRING The CRO will command, “FINALISTS HAVE TWENTY-TWO MINUTES TO KNEELING AND FIRE TEN SHOTS IN EACH OF THE KNEELING AND PRONE POSITIONS PRONE AND PREPARE FOR THE STANDING POSITION”. After five (5) secs., the CRO will command “MATCH FIRING START.” Finalists must fire ten (10) Match shots in the Kneeling position, insert their safety-flags, change to the Prone position and fire unlimited sighting shots, then fire ten (10) Match shots. After finishing those ten shots they must insert safety flags and change to the Standing position. They may then fire unlimited sighting-shots in the time remaining before the CRO commands “STOP” at the end of the 22 minute Match Firing time. They must be ready to start Match firing in the Standing position when the CRO gives the commands; Safety flags must be inserted and barrels always kept pointing down-range when changing positions. Finalists are responsible for changing their targets from Match to Sighters and back to Match at the appropriate times. Athletes are not permitted to change clothing on the FOP or remove shooting

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: jackets or trousers when changing positions, but zippers and buttons may be undone as required. They must make their own adjustments to rifles and move their own equipment during shooting and transitions. This includes picking up any dropped equipment from the floor of the FOP, for example retrieving a breech flag. A two point penalty, (green card), may be applied if an athlete requires any assistance if they are unable to complete those tasks for themselves whilst on the FOP.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) CRO COMMANDS After seventeen (17) minutes, the CRO will announce, “FIVE MINUTES”. After 21 minutes and 30 seconds, the CRO will announce, “THIRTY SECONDS”. After twenty-two minutes, the CRO will command, “STOP”. 274 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) MATCH FIRING After 30 seconds. the CRO will command “FOR THE NEXT COMPETITION STANDING SERIES…LOAD”. After 5 secs., “START”. Athletes have 250 seconds to fire each 5-shot MATCH series. After 250 seconds the CRO will command “STOP”. The Announcer will make some brief comments about the ranking and any other relevant information including the fact that at the end of the next series, the two lowest ranking athletes will be eliminated. x 5-shot series 2 The same command procedure and sequence of announcements will continue until the athletes have completed two (2) 5-shot series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) ELIMINATION The two (2) lowest-ranking finalists are eliminated after the second standing series, (30 shots total, 8th and 7th places). The Announcer will recognise those athletes who are eliminated and comment on the ranking so far. Immediately after the Announcer finishes, the CRO will command, “FOR THE NEXT COMPETITION SHOT…LOAD”, 5 secs, “START”. The remaining six finalists will fire a single shot in a maximum time of 50 seconds. Shot time countdown information must continue to be available for all Single shot series athletes. At 50 seconds, or after all finalists have fired a single shot, the CRO will command “STOP”. This sequence and appropriate commands will continue until all finalists have fired a single shot, after which the lowest ranked athlete will be eliminated. The Announcer will recognise the athlete (6th place) and make further relevant comments. The remaining five finalists will continue firing single shots on command, with the lowest ranked being eliminated after each shot, as follows: After 32 shots – 5th place After 33 shots – 4th place

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: After 34 shots – 3rd place (bronze medal winner decided) After 35 shots – 2nd and 1st places (silver and gold medals decided)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i)TIE-BREAKING If there is a tie for the lowest ranking athlete to be eliminated, the tied athletes will fire an additional tie-breaking shot(s) until the tie is broken. For tie-breaking shots, the CRO will immediately announce the family names of the tied athletes and their firing points and command them to fire their tie- breaking shots with the normal firing procedure. If there are two athletes tied at the end of the second 5-shot series in the Standing position, they are both eliminated and the tie will be broken by countback as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 1) The highest total score in the second Standing 5-shot series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 2) The highest total score in the first Standing 5-shot series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 3) The highest total value final shot of the prone series; etc. If there are more than two athletes tied after the second 5-shot series, then there will be tie-breaking shots to decide the two athletes eliminated.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) FINALS After the two (2) remaining finalists fire the last shot, and if there are no ties COMPLETION or protest, the CRO will command “STOP…UNLOAD” and then declare “RESULTS ARE FINAL.” The Jury member in charge must assemble the three medallists on the FOP and the Announcer will immediately recognize the bronze, silver and gold medal winners according to 6.17.1.14 q. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 275

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) COACHING Coaches may assist finalists by bringing equipment to the firing line before the Final or removing equipment after the Final During the Final, Coaches are permitted to assist athletes with the removal of prone slings, adjustments of jacket shoulder straps and other minor adjustments of clothing, but no other physical assistance may be given. They may speak to their athletes at those times but all coaching and or assistance described here must only be conducted in the coach’s technical area to the rear of the FOP. Non-verbal coaching is permitted at other times.

chunks.text: 6.17.4 FINALS – 25m RAPID FIRE PISTOL MEN

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The 25m Rapid Fire Pistol Men Final consists of eight (8) 5-shot 4-second series with hit or miss scoring and the elimination of the lowest scoring FINALS FORMAT finalists, beginning after the third series and continuing until the eighth series when the gold and silver medals are decided.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Two (2) groups of five (5) 25m ESTs must be used. Firing points will be designated A-B / C-D. TARGETS & FP Four finalists are assigned to each group. The 1.50m x 1.50m shooting station (firing point) for each group is used. Finals Start numbers from 1-8 will be issued at reporting time. Start numbers will be determined by qualification ranking, the highest ranked position having Finals Start No.1. Athletes 1, 3, 5 & 7 will be allocated to the left side group of targets (A & C) and Athletes 2, 4, 6 & 8 will be allocated to the right-side group of targets (B & D), as shown in the figure below: Two athletes will occupy the Firing Point together when commanded. They must take their positions on the left and right sides of the shooting station when it is their turn to shoot, so that at least one (1) foot touches the line that marks the left or right side of the shooting station. 276 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Ammunition areas will be provided – one for each group of targets. They will be placed behind the firing points. Four finalists are allocated to each area – AMMUNITION AREA as per their firing point allocation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Scoring in the Final is hit or miss; each hit counts one (1) point; each miss counts zero (0) points. Any shot scoring 9.7 or higher on the 25m Rapid Fire SCORING Pistol target counts as a hit. Cumulative total scores (total number of hits) in the Final determine final rankings. Ties for the elimination from 8th to 5th place will be decided by Finals Start number. Deductions for violations occurring before the first MATCH shot will be applied to the score of the first HIT/S in the final. Deductions for other DEDUCTIONS penalties will be applied to the score of the series where the violation occurred.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Not more than 20 min. after the end of the qualification, and before the reporting time for the Final, all Finals athletes must present themselves to the VELOCITY TEST velocity test station with their ammunition (see rule 8.4.4.3).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Athletes must report 30 min. before the Start Time with their equipment, competition clothing and Medal Ceremony uniform. The Jury must complete REPORTING TIME equipment checks as soon as possible after the athlete reports. 30:00 and 20:00 min Athletes or their coaches must be allowed to place their equipment, including before the sealed ammunition, on their firing points not less than 20 min. before the Start Time. Ammunition and magazines must be placed in the Ammunition Area except for one (1) magazine and five (5) cartridges that will be placed at the Firing Point to be used only for the Sighting Series, once finished, the magazine and any remaining ammunition must be moved to the Ammunition Area. Pistols must be placed on the firing points. Other equipment may be placed as required by the athlete. Athlete equipment may include a reserve pistol that can be used to replace a malfunctioning pistol (safety flag must be inserted). If athlete did not present himself for velocity test before final, he will not be

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: allowed to start and will be ranked in 8th and marked DNS in finals results. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 277

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Athletes will be called to the line approximately 11 minutes before the start, one by one and be introduced as they enter the FOP and will continue to face CALL TO LINE the audience until given the command to Approx. 11 minutes “TAKE YOUR POSITIONS”. Athletes 1, 2, 3 and 4 will assume their position before at the Firing Points, and athletes 5, 6, 7 and 8 will assume their position at the Ammunition Areas, as shown in the figure below.

LOAD, after 30 seconds, the CRO will call and LOADING the family names of the of ATHLETE 1, and ATHLETE 3, …. READY” After the command “READY” athletes may place magazines in their pistol and prepare to fire. After 20 seconds – “ATTENTION” – red lights are turned on and athletes must come to the Ready Position. At the end of the series this procedure will be repeated for athletes 2 & 4 When all four athletes have fired, they will retire to the Ammunition Area and may then load up to two magazines. There will be no further load command – magazines will be loaded as needed throughout the Final. And the CRO will command “TAKE YOUR POSITIONS” for Athletes 5, 6, 7 and 8. They will move forward to the Firing Point, after 20 seconds CRO will command “PREPARATION BEGINS NOW”,and the above process will be repeated. After the command READY, the athletes on the right in the 5-target group,

chunks.text: can prepare for the next series, may take his pistol in his hand to prepare, but he may not do aiming exercises, arm lifts or dry firing. 278 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Each Final MATCH series consists of five (5) shots in four (4) seconds. For the first three series finalists will shoot in pairs, first the two located on the left DETAILED side of the Firing Points. Order will be 1&3; 2&4; 5&7 and 6&8. PROCEDURE FOR From the fourth series onwards all finalists remaining in the competition will shoot individually and in succession. The order of firing for all series is from COMMANDS AND left to right (1 to 8). FIRING After an athlete has fired his series, he must immediately move back to the Competition firing Ammunition Area and the next group of athletes must move forward to waiting starts at 0:00 min. area – there will be no further call to the line. Instead, athletes will rotate throughout the Final until they are eliminated, or the Final is completed. When athletes load their magazines, they must move to the waiting area as soon as the athlete on their FP has moved to the ammunition area. The CRO will give the READY command for the next athlete immediately. As athletes move forward to their firing point, they must position themselves

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: as follows. Athlete on the left of each firing point (A & C) - at the firing point. Athlete on the right of each firing point (B & D) – a step back, in the Waiting Area. After 20 seconds the CRO will call “FAMILY NAME OF ATHLETE 1, FAMILY NAME OF ATHLETE 3 – READY”. After 20 seconds the CRO will command “ATTENTION” and turn the red lights on. The two athletes must bring their pistol to the READY position. The green lights will come on after a delay of seven (7) sec. After the four (4) sec. firing period, the red lights will come on for 10-14 sec. (recycling time of the targets). During this 10-14 sec. period, the CRO will report the score for that series (e.g., “FAMILY NAME ATHLETE 1 - FOUR HITS. FAMILY NAME ATHLETE 3 – THREE HITS”). chunks.text: j) After all finalists fire the third series, the two lowest-ranking athletes are eliminated (7th and 8th places) ELIMINATIONS One (1) additional athlete is eliminated after each series that follows. After 4 series – 6th place (no shoot off, decided by Start number) After 5 series – 5th place (no shoot off, decided by Start number) After 6 series – 4th place (shoot off to decide 4th place) After 7 series – 3rd place (bronze medal winner is decided, shoot off if needed) After 8 series – 2nd and 1st places (silver and gold medal winners are decided, shoot off if needed) From the fourth series onwards, athletes will shoot individually and in succession according to their positions at the beginning of the final and in existing order of shooting. Order of firing for all series is from left to right (1 to 8). The Firing positions will not be changed. Athletes must wait for their turn in waiting area and take their positions immediately after their FP is ready.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) If there is a tie for the lowest ranking athlete to be eliminated for positions 8th to 5th, the tie will be broken by Final Start Number. A tie for 4th place and any TIE-BREAKING medal position will be broken by a shoot off series. Athletes will fire a shoot off series separately one by one starting with athlete with lowest final start number.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) After the two (2) remaining finalists fire the eighth series, and if there are no ties or protest, the CRO will command “STOP…UNLOAD” and then declare FINALS “RESULTS ARE FINAL.” COMPLETION The Jury must assemble the three medallists on the FOP and the Announcer will immediately recognize the bronze, silver and gold medal winners according to 6.17.1.14 q. Before any finalist or his coach may remove a pistol from the firing line, the Range Officer must check the pistol to be sure its action is open with a safety flag inserted, magazine removed, and magazines unloaded. Pistols must be boxed before they are taken from the firing line.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: m) If an athlete fires a late shot or does not shoot at all five (5) targets in time, a deduction of one (1) hit for each overtime or unfired shot will be taken from LATE and the score for that series. The shot(s) will be marked with “OT.” IRREGULAR SHOTS If an athlete fires 2 shots on the same target, the second shot on the target will be counted as a miss, and one (1) HIT penalty will be applied to the score of that series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: n) If the Jury determines that an athlete raises his arm too soon, or does not lower it sufficiently, the athlete must be penalized by a deduction of two (2) READY POSITION hits in that series (Green Card). In a Final, no warning will be given. In case (8.7.2, 8.7.3) of repetition, the athlete must be disqualified (red card). To decide a READY position violation, at least two Competition Jury Members must give a sign (e.

chunks.text: o) Malfunctions during the sighting series may not be claimed or refired. Only one malfunction (ALLOWABLE or NON-ALLOWABLE) may be claimed MALFUNCTIONS during the MATCH series. If a malfunction occurs during a MATCH series, a Range Officer must determine if the malfunction is ALLOWABLE or NON- ALLOWABLE. If the malfunction is ALLOWABLE, the athlete must repeat the series immediately, while the other finalists standby, and will receive the score of the repeat series. The athlete has 20 seconds to be ready for the repeat series. If malfunction is NON-ALLOWABLE, a penalty of two (2) hits must be deducted from the score for that series. For any further malfunction, a Range Officer must determine if the malfunction is ALLOWABLE or NON-ALLOWABLE, no repeat series is permitted and the hits that are displayed will be counted, if malfunction is ALLOWABLE. If the malfunction is NON-ALLOWABLE, a penalty of two (2) hits must be deducted from the score for that series.

chunks.text: p) Coaches may assist finalists by bringing equipment to the firing line before the Final or removing equipment after the Final. Coaches may not assist COACHING athletes during the loading. If a coach assists the athlete, loads magazine or touches ammunition or other equipment in the Ammunition Area during Finals, a penalty of 2 first HITS will be applied to athlete score. Non-verbal coaching is permitted while the athlete is at the Firing Point; verbal coaching is only permitted during the loading when athlete is in Ammunition Area but must not disturb other athletes or coaches.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: q) Aiming exercises, arm lifts or dry firing at Firing Points can be done only during Preparation time. SHOOTING Athletes may perform arm lifts and exercises with or without dumbbells or EXERCISE similar weights, while they remain in the ammunition area waiting for their turn to shoot. 282 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF
