chunks.text: 6.17.5 FINALS – 25m PISTOL WOMEN

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The 25m Pistol Women Final consists of ten (10) 5-shot rapid-fire series FINALS FORMAT with hit or miss scoring and the eliminations of the lowest scoring finalists, beginning after the fourth series and continuing until the tenth series when the gold and silver medals are decided.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) TARGETS Two (2) groups of five (5) 25m ESTs must be used. The targets are labelled A-B-R1-C-D-E-F-R2-G-H. In the Final, eight (8) finalists are assigned to positions A-B-C-D-E-F-G-H according to a random draw.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) SCORING The Final starts from zero (0). Scoring is hit or miss; each shot within the hit zone is scored as one hit. Any shot scoring 10.2 or higher on the 25m Rapid- Fire Pistol target counts as a hit. During the Final, results are cumulative with each athlete’s final ranking determined by the total number of hits. If two or more athletes are tied for a place to be decided, they will fire additional series until the tie is broken. DEDUCTIONS Deductions for violations occurring before the first MATCH shot will be applied to the score of the first MATCH series. Deductions for other penalties will be applied to the score of the series where the violation occurred.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Athletes must report at least 30 min. before the Start Time with their REPORTING TIME equipment and competition clothing. The Jury must complete equipment 30:00 and 20:00 min. checks as soon as possible after each athlete reports. Athletes or their before coaches must be allowed to place their equipment, including sufficient ammunition to complete the Final, on their firing points not less than 20 min. before the Start Time. Athlete equipment may include a reserve pistol that can be used to replace a malfunctioning pistol (safety flag must be inserted).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The CRO will call “ATHLETES TO THE LINE” approximately ten (10) min. CALL TO LINE, before Start Time. PREPARATION Athletes will enter one at a time and be introduced as they walk to their PERIOD allocated firing point and must stand facing the audience. The Announcer will AND SIGHTING then introduce the CRO and Jury Member in Charge. After all introductions SHOTS have been made the CRO will announce “TAKE YOUR POSITIONS”. After Approx. 10:00 min. before ten (10) seconds, the CRO will start the two (2) min. preparation period with the command “PREPARATION BEGINS NOW.” After two (2) min., the CRO will command “END OF PREPARATION.” The sighting series consists of five (5) shots fired in the standard Rapid-Fire sequence (Rule 8.7.6.4). Immediately after the preparation period, the CRO will command “LOAD.” Finalists have one (1) min. to load two (2) magazines (Rule 8.7.6.2.d. does not apply for the Final). Only one (1) “LOAD” command is given before the start of the SIGHTING

chunks.text: series. Athletes must bring their pistols to the READY position (Rule 8.7.2). After seven (7) sec., the green lights will come on for the first three (3) sec. rapid-fire series. After the series is completed, the CRO will command “STOP” No score announcements are made after the sighting series. After the commands “STOP” The targets and scoreboard must be cleared and set to MATCH. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 283

chunks.text: f) 30 sec. later, the first MATCH series will start and the CRO will command DETAILED PROCE- “FIRST SERIES…READY.” After this command, athletes are DURE FOR allowed to insert magazines in their pistols and prepare to fire. COMMANDS AND 20 sec. after the command “READY,” the CRO will command “ATTENTION” FIRING and turn the red lights on. Athletes must bring their pistols to the READY Competition firing position (Rule 8.7.2). chunks.text: 6.18.1.2 Mixed Team Composition Two (2) Athletes from the same nation (1 male and 1 female).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.1.3 National identification / Dress code

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athletes from each nation must display their National identification on their shooting clothing as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Rifle: The name of the country denoted by 3 letters as determined by the IOC on their jacket pocket on the side which is turned to the audience. If the NOC is already on the shooting jacket, a National Flag should be placed or attached to the pocket facing the audience.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Pistol: The name of the country denoted by 3 letters as determined by the IOC should be placed on the sleeve of the T-shirt/sports jacket on the side which is turned to the audience.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.1.4 Mixed Team Entries

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Nations may enter a maximum of two teams in one Championship as per ISSF entry rules. Team members may be changed for other athletes registered in the Championship not later than 12:00 hours, two days before the day of the Mixed Team competition. Any team that fails to confirm the registration of team members by this deadline, the team members will be entered by random from those eligible and subsequently cannot be changed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The entry fee for each team is EUR 170.00 (Rule 3.8.4.2 Gen. Regs.).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.1.5 Competition Format 10m Mixed Team events will be conducted in two stages:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) QUALIFICATION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) FINAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.1.6 Mixed Team Scores Scores and rankings are based on the total scores of the two team members.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.1.7 Coaching and Time out

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) During Qualification, non-verbal coaching is allowed,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) During the Final, each team is allowed one (1) Coach who must be seated where he/she can have access to and can communicate with their athletes. The Coach or an Athlete may request a “Time out” by raising a hand immediately after the completion of a round whilst the announcements are EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 285 being made. This may be requested once only during the Final. The Coach may approach and speak to his/her athlete(s) on the firing line, for a maximum time of thirty (30) seconds, commencing when the Coach reaches the athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The time will be controlled by the Jury member in Charge, who must announce “Time” when the thirty seconds has expired, and the Coach must immediately return to his/her seat. If a “Time out” is requested by one team, the Coach of any other team may also approach and speak to his/her athlete(s) at the same time. This does not affect the opportunity of the other teams to request their own Timeout.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.1.8 Firearm Malfunctions

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Malfunctions in Qualification will be governed according to Rule 6.13.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Malfunctions in the Final will be governed according to Rule 6.17.1.6. (Only one (1) allowable malfunction is permitted for each team).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.1.9 EST Complaints and Score Protests

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) EST complaints during the Qualification will be decided according to Rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) See Rule 6.17.1.8 for EST complaints during Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.1.10 Protests

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Protests during the Qualification will be decided according to Rule 6.16.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Protests made during Finals will be decided by the Finals Protest Jury according to Rules 6.17.1.10.d and 6.17.1.13.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.1.11 Medal Ceremonies Medal Ceremonies for Mixed Team events will be conducted according to Rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.2 QUALIFICATION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.2.1 Location Mixed Team Qualifications will be fired on the Qualification Range in one or more relays.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.2.2 Allocation of firing points

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The firing points of the teams will be allocated by a random computer draw according to Rule 6.6.6.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Teams from the same nation must not be positioned next to each other.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Members of each team shoot next to each other with the female athlete on the left.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.2.3 Call to Line

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) For each Qualification relay, the Chief Range Officer will call the athletes to the line twenty five (25) minutes before the scheduled start time.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Athletes will be allowed ten (10) minutes to set up their equipment on their allocated firing points.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Athletes may not unbox their rifle/pistol nor place any equipment on their firing points until the CRO calls them to the line. 286 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) After athletes are called to the line, they are permitted to handle their rifle/ pistol, remove safety flags, dry-fire and carry out holding and aiming exercises before the start of the Preparation and Sighting Time.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) In the Final, athletes may not remove the safety flags or dry fire until the Preparation and Sighting Time starts.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.2.4 Preparation and Sighting Time Athletes must be allowed fifteen (15) minutes Preparation and Sighting Time with unlimited sighting shots before the start of the Qualification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Preparation and Sighting Time must be timed to end approximately thirty (30) seconds before the official starting time of the match.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Pre-competition checks by the Range Officers must be completed during the ten (10) minutes before the Preparation and Sighting Time starts;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Preparation and Sighting Time begins with the command “PREPARATION AND SIGHTING TIME…START”. No shot may be fired before the command “START”;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If an athlete fires a shot before the “START” command for Preparation and Sighting time, the first competition shot must be scored as a miss, (0). If safety is involved the athlete may be disqualified

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) After fourteen minutes and thirty seconds of the Preparation and Sighting Time have elapsed, the CRO must announce “30 SECONDS”;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) At the end of the Preparation and Sighting Time, the Chief Range Officer must command, “END OF PREPARATION AND SIGHTING…STOP”. There must be a brief pause of approximately thirty (30) seconds when the Target Officer will reset the targets for match firing, and;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) If an athlete fires a shot after the command “END OF PREPARATION AND SIGHTING…STOP” and before the “MATCH FIRING…START” command, the shot must not be counted as a MATCH shot and a two (2) point penalty must be applied to the first competition shot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.2.5 Number of Match Shots and Time Limit

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) In Qualification, each team member will fire thirty (30) match shots (60 total shots per team), with a time limit of forty (40) minutes. Each athlete fires independently of their partner.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.2.6 Scoring In the Qualification rounds, decimal ring scoring (Rule 6.3.3.1) will be used for the 10m Rifle Mixed Team event. Full ring scoring will be used for the 10m Pistol Mixed Team event.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.2.7 Team Ranking

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The scores of each team member will be added together and the team results will be ranked.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Ties will be broken by applying Rule 6.15.5 (total of the two team member scores).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The four (4) top-ranked teams will proceed to the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3 FINAL The Final consists of all team members firing 3 x 5 shot series in 250 seconds EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 287 on command, followed by 3 single shots on command in 50 seconds. The Team with the lowest accumulated score at this stage will be eliminated in 4th place. The remaining team members will fire a further 3 single shots on command in 50 seconds, with the lowest accumulated team score being awarded the Bronze medal. After a further 3 single shots by all team members, Gold and Silver medals will be decided. A total of 24 shots will be fired by each team member winning gold and silver medals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3.1 Location 10m Rifle and Pistol Mixed Team Finals must, if possible, be fired on a Finals Range. Results monitors visible to both members of each team must be available on the FOP.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3.2 Procedure

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Athletes, or their Coaches, must be allowed to place their equipment on their designated firing-points at least fifteen (15) minutes before the scheduled Start time. They must then leave the range and wait to be called to the line.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) No bags or transport-boxes may be left on the Field of Play.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3.3 Finals Officials The conduct and supervision of Mixed Team Finals will be in accordance with Rule 6.17.1.10.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3.4 Reporting and Start Times

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Start Time for the Final is when the CRO begins the commands for the first competition shot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) All eight athletes who qualify for the Final must report to the Finals Range Preparation Area, with all necessary equipment, at least thirty (30) minutes before the Start Time of Final. A two-point (2) penalty will be deducted from the score of the first competition series if one or two team members do not report on time. Each team may be accompanied by one Coach.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If an athlete or Team reports later than twenty (20) minutes before the Start Time, the Team will not be allowed to start and will be ranked 4th.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Juries must complete equipment checks during the reporting period and as soon as possible after each athlete reports.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Athletes or their Coaches, must be allowed to place their equipment on their designated firing-points at least fifteen (15) minutes before the scheduled Start time. They must then leave the range to wait to be called to the line.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Teams must be assembled in firing point order, for the call to the line, eight (8) minutes before the Final Start Time.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) If the Medal Ceremony is scheduled after the Final, all athletes must report with a national team uniform appropriate for a Medal Ceremony.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3.5 Allocation of firing points

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) For the Final, teams are assigned to positions A-B/C-D/E-F/G-H according to a random draw.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Team members may change positions for the Final. If a change is desired, the team Coach must inform the RTS Jury which team member will shoot on the left and which team member will shoot on the right, before the end of Protest time when Preliminary Qualification scores are posted. 288 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3.6 Scoring All shots in the Finals, (both Rifle and Pistol) will be scored with decimal scoring. The Final consists of three (3) series of five (5) MATCH shots each fired in a time of 250 sec. per series (5 + 5 + 5 shots). This is followed by nine (9) single MATCH shots each fired on command in a time of 50 sec. Eliminations of the lowest scoring team begins after the 18th shot and continue after every three shots until the gold and silver medals are decided. There are a total of twenty-four (24) shots in the Final. Scoring in Finals is done with tenth-ring (decimal) scoring. Combined cumulative total scores in a Final determine final rankings, with ties broken according to shoot- off scores. Deductions for violations occurring before the first MATCH shot will be applied to the score of the first MATCH shot. Deductions for other penalties will be applied to the score of the shot where the violation occurred. If the scores are tied, each member of the tied teams will shoot additional shots on command until the tie is broken.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3.7 EST Complaints during Finals See rule 6.17.1.8

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3.8 Call to Line At approximately -8:00min. before the start, Teams for Final will enter the FOP one at a time. As each Team enters the FOP the Announcer will introduce them to the spectators. Athletes must stand in front of their designated firing points, facing the audience, and remain in that position until all have been presented, including the Jury Member in Charge, and the Chief Range Officer.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.3.9 Preparation and Sighting Time After 30 seconds for Rifle or 10 seconds for Pistol, the CRO will command: “FIVE MINUTES PREPARATION AND SIGHTING TIME…START”. After four (4) minutes and thirty (30) seconds, the CRO will announce: “30 SECONDS.” After five (5) minutes, the CRO will command “STOP…UNLOAD.”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.4 FINAL PROCEDURE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) One (1) minute after the end of Preparation and Sighting time, the CRO will command:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) “FOR THE FIRST COMPETITON SERIES, LOAD…five (5) seconds… START”.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Each team member will fire a series of five shots in a maximum time of two hundred and fifty (250) seconds.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Either athlete may fire first.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The CRO may call “STOP” after all athletes have fired.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Immediately after the command “STOP,” the team with the highest combined score of each round will be announced.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) The Announcer will give 15-20 seconds of comments on the current ranking of the teams and notable scores. Individual shot scores are not announced. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 289

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) The firing sequence will be repeated with two further five (5) shot series. This is followed by three (3) single shots on command in 50 seconds. After 18 shots the 4th place is decided. The three remaining team members each fire a further three (3) shots on command to decide the Bronze Medal winners. This is repeated by the two remaining Teams to decide the silver and gold medals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.4.1 Bronze Medal Winner.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The announcer will declare the Bronze Medal Winning team.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A Range Officer must verify that the rifle/pistol actions are open with the safety flags inserted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.4.2 Final Completion

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) As soon as the Gold/Silver medals are decided the CRO will command “STOP...UNLOAD” declare “RESULTS ARE FINAL” and the announcer will declare the Gold and Silver Medal Winning teams.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A Range Officer must verify that the rifle/pistol actions are open with the safety flags inserted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Gold and Silver Medallists must be joined on the Field of Play by the Bronze medallists and the Jury will line them up, as in the Individual Finals, for official photographs and announcements. Athletes may be allowed to hold their rifles/pistols for the photographs.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.4.3 Finals Production and Music

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) During the Qualification stage music must be played.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) During the Final music must be played.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Technical Delegate should approve the music programme. Enthusiastic audience support is encouraged and is recommended during the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.18.4.4 Irregular or disputed matters ISSF General Technical Rule 6.17 will apply to matters not mentioned in the above rules. Irregular or disputed matters will be decided by the Jury according to General Technical Rules for each event. 290 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20 THE ISSF DRESS CODE ISSF Rule General Technical Rule 6.7.5 states: “It is the responsibility of athletes, coaches and officials to appear on the range dressed in a manner appropriate for a public sports event. Clothing worn by athletes and officials must comply with the ISSF Dress Code.” This Rule is the foundation of the ISSF Dress Code.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.1 GENERAL All sports are concerned with the images they present to youth, the public and media. Olympic sports, in particular, are judged by whether their athletes, coaches and officials present professional images that demonstrate their best qualities. Shooting’s ability to grow as a sport, to attract new participants and fans and to secure its status as an Olympic sport are affected by how its athletes and officials’ dress. This ISSF Dress Code provides regulations and guidelines for the implementation of Rule 6.7.5.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.2 DRESS REGULATIONS FOR ATHLETES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.2.1 All clothing worn by athletes in Training, Eliminations, Qualifications and Finals must be clothing that is appropriate for wear by athletes in international-class sports competitions. Athletes’ clothing must convey positive images of shooting athletes as Olympic sport athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.2.2 When they appear in competitions, Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun and Moving Target athletes should wear sports-type clothing that incorporates or displays national, NOC or National Federation colours and emblems. Appropriate clothing for wear during competitions includes training suits, tracksuits or warm-up uniforms, etc. as issued by National Federations or NOCs.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.2.3 Members of a team participating in a Team event should wear the same uniform reflecting the nation they represent.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.2.4 During Victory Ceremonies or other ceremonies, athletes are required to be dressed in their official national uniform or national training suits. For teams, all members of the team must wear appropriate national uniforms. If an athlete reports for a Medal Ceremony without a national team uniform, a Jury member may delay the ceremony and require the athlete to change into appropriate clothing before the ceremony can proceed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.2.5 Rifle athletes’ clothing must comply with Rifle Clothing Regulations described in Rule 7.5. If they do not wear special shooting trousers or shoes, the clothing worn during competitions must comply with this ISSF Dress Code.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.2.6 During all Pistol training and competition, women are required to wear dresses, skirts, divided skirts, shorts or trousers, and blouses or tops (must cover the front and back of the body and be over each shoulder). Men are required to wear full-length trousers or shorts and long or short sleeved shirts. Athletes are not permitted to wear any form of performance enhancing clothing. All athlete clothing must comply with the ISSF Dress Code (Rule 6.7.5 and 6.20).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.2.7 Shotgun athletes must comply with Shotgun Clothing Regulations described in Rule 9.12.1.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.2.8 If shorts are worn during competitions, the bottom of the leg must be not more than 15cm above the centre of the knee cap. Skirts and dresses must also comply with this measurement. 300 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.3 PROHIBITED ITEMS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.3.1 Prohibited clothing items for competitions and Medal Ceremonies include blue jeans. Also, jeans or similar trousers in colours not appropriate, camouflage clothing, sleeveless T-shirts, shorts that are too short (see 6.20.2.8), ragged cut-off shorts, trousers with patches or holes as well as shirts or trousers with non-sporting or inappropriate messages (see Rule 6.12.1, no propaganda is permitted). Sporting colours should be national uniform colours. If national colours are not worn, non- appropriate colours that must not be worn are camouflage, plaids, khaki, olive or brown.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.3.2 Athletes may not wear sandals of any type or remove their shoes (with or without socks).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.3.3 Changing clothes must be done in designated areas and not on the field of play. Changing on the firing points or in the ranges is not permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.3.4 All clothing must comply with ISSF Eligibility, Commercial Rights, Sponsorship and Advertising Rules regarding the display of manufacturer and sponsor marks. During the Olympic Games compliance with IOC Rule 50 is required.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.4 DRESS REGULATIONS FOR COACHES AND OFFICIALS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.4.1 The ISSF Dress Code applies to ISSF Jury Members and National Technical Officials including Range Officers and Shotgun Referees. The ISSF Dress Code also applies to coaches when they are working on the field of play during training, competitions or Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.4.2 Unless the organizer provides special official clothing, Jury members should wear dark trousers, or skirts, with light coloured shirts with collars and long or short sleeves. If, due to the climate, a warm sweater or jacket is necessary it should preferably be of a dark colour. In warm climates, lightweight trousers are recommended. Dark normal shoes or sporting shoes are recommended.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.4.3 While on duty, Jury Members must wear the approved ISSF red Jury vests that are available from ISSF Headquarters.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.4.4 While on duty, Shotgun Referees must wear the ISSF official blue Referee vests that are available from ISSF Headquarters.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.4.5 Competition officials and coaches may not wear any prohibited clothing items that are described in paragraph 6.20.3 above. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 301

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.5 DRESS REGULATIONS FOR PHOTOGRAPHERS, COMMENTATORS AND TV CAMERA CREWS.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.5.1 Accredited photographers, Commentators and TV camera crews with access to the FOP must respect the ISSF Dress Code because they are working in the public view.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.5.2 Photographers and TV cameramen should not wear sleeveless shirts, cut-offs, gym or running shorts. If they wear shorts, they must wear socks and shoes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.5.3 Photographers working on the FOP must wear the official POOL or NON- POOL PHOTOGRAPHER bib/vest that is issued by the ISSF. Photographer vests will bear the ISSF logo and may bear one sponsor logo not bigger than the ISSF logo. Photographer vests are numbered so photo coordinators or the ISSF Technical Delegate can identify photographers.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.5.4 TV cameramen working on the field of play must wear the official TV CAMERAMAN bib/vest. These vests must bear the ISSF logo and have easily distinguishable numbers on the front and back of the bib vest so that TV cameramen can be identified.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.5.5  Photographers and TV cameramen are not allowed to wear any other vest or jacket displaying advertising while working on the field of play.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.6 DRESS CODE ENFORCEMENT PROCEDURES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.6.1 ISSF Equipment Control, Rifle, Pistol and Shotgun Juries are responsible for enforcing ISSF Clothing Regulations and the ISSF Dress Code.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.6.2  During ISSF Championships, ISSF Juries will issue written warnings with requests to correct clothing violations for first violations. Athletes who receive written warnings and do not correct clothing violations (change clothing) will be disqualified. Juries will normally give warnings during equipment inspection or training. Juries may allow an athlete to complete Pre-Event Training (Shotgun or 25m Pistol) before changing if sufficient time to change is not available. No athlete will be permitted to participate in a Qualification or Final competition or in a Medal Ceremony while wearing inappropriate or prohibited clothing.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.20.6.3  Before and during the competitions, Juries must use the ISSF Dress/ Advertising Code Violation Warning Form (Form DC) to inform Dress or Advertising Code violators and to request corrective action. 302 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF DRESS/ADVERTISING CODE VIOLATION DC WARNING Incident Report Number: (A record must be kept in Range Register) Date of Violation: Time of Violation: Athlete’s Name: Bib Number: Nation: Description of Dress/Advertising Code Violation: Corrective Action Required: Signature of Jury Member: Printed Name: Time: IMPORTANT: Athletes who receive a Dress/Advertising Code Violation Warning may be disqualified from a competition if the violation is not corrected. chunks.text: 7.1 GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1.1 These Rules are part of the ISSF Technical Rules and apply to all Rifle events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1.2  All athletes, team leaders and officials must be familiar with the ISSF Rules and must ensure that these Rules are enforced. It is the responsibility of each athlete to comply with the Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1.3  When a Rule refers to right-handed athletes, the reverse of that Rule refers to left-handed athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.1.4  Unless a Rule applies specifically to a men’s or a women’s event, it must apply uniformly to both men’s and women’s events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.2 SAFETY SAFETY IS OF PARAMOUNT IMPORTANCE ISSF Safety Rules are found in Rule 6.2.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.3 RANGE AND TARGET STANDARDS Target and target standards are found in Rule 6.3. Requirements for ranges and other facilities are found in Rule 6.4.

chunks.text: 7.4 RIFLES AND AMMUNITION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.1 Standards for All Rifles Single Loader Rifles. Only single shot rifles that must be manually loaded

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.1.1  before each shot may be used, except that in the 300m Standard Rifle event a rifle that is legal for use in International Military Sport Council (CISM) 300m Rifle events may be used if it is checked by Equipment Control before the event. One Rifle Per Event. Only one (1) rifle is allowed to be used in the

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.1.2  Elimination, Qualification and Final Rounds of one (1) event. The action, barrel and stock may not be exchanged, except that a detachable butt-stock may be exchanged. Accessories attached to the action, barrel or stock may be exchanged. A rifle that becomes disabled may be replaced according to Rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.13.3, if the Jury approves.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.1.3 Movement or Oscillation Reduction Systems. Any device, mechanism or system that actively reduces, slows or minimizes rifle oscillations or movements before the shot is released is prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.1.4  Pistol Grips. The pistol grip for the right hand must be adapted or adjusted in such a way that it does not rest on the sling or on the left arm.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.1.5  Barrels and extension tubes must not be perforated in any way. Compensators and muzzle breaks on the rifle are prohibited. Any construction or device inside the barrel or tube, other than rifling and chambering for the cartridge or pellet, is prohibited. Extension tubes must be inspected by Equipment Control when the athlete attends, either for pre-competition or re-checks.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.1.6 Sights The front or rear sights may have light or tinted lenses or a polarizing filter, but the sights may not have any internal system of lenses that magnifies the sight picture. All such devices must display clearly visible identification, such as a red collar, to show that the lenses are non-magnifying. The intent of this rule is to prohibit the use of any “system of lenses” that would act as a telescope to magnify the sight picture seen by the athlete. The EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 321 only exception to this is that an athlete who requires optical correction to see a clear sight picture is permitted to attach a single lens to the exterior of the rear sight but not to the interior. Additionally, the wearing of contact lenses or a natural lens replacement is allowed because these are essential for an athlete to see normally when not shooting and are not external attachments that are deliberately intended to magnify a sight picture;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) No Light enhancing system, optical sight, optical system or telescope may be attached to the rifle;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A single corrective lens may be attached to the rear sight only; or the athlete may wear a corrective or tinted lens;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Any aiming device programmed to activate the firing mechanism is prohibited;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) A blinder may be attached to the rifle or to the rear sight. The blinder must not be more than 30mm deep (A) nor extend further than 100mm (B) from the centre of the rear sight aperture on the side of the non-aiming eye. A blinder must not be used on the side of the aiming eye; and a prism or mirror device may be used when shooting from the right shoulder while aiming with the left eye, providing it does not have a magnifying lens system. It must not be used when shooting from the right shoulder when using the right eye, or vice-versa. Rear Sight Blinder Diagram

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) On Air and Standard Rifles, the foresight tunnel must be circular in profile when viewed through the rear sight and not have an external shape or additions that can be used as a horizontal reference. Internal foresight elements containing a horizontal and/or vertical reference are allowed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.1.7 Electronic triggers are allowed provided that:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) All components are attached to and contained within the action or stock of the rifle so that the battery and wires are not visible externally;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The trigger is operated by the right hand of a right-handed or the left hand of a left-handed athlete;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) All components are included when the rifle is submitted for inspection by Equipment Control; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The rifle with all components installed complies with the rules governing dimensions and weight for that event.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.2 Standards for 300m Standard Rifle and 10m Air Rifle Measurements stated in this rule are also illustrated in the RIFLE MEASUREMENTS DIAGRAM, 7.4.4.1 and in the RIFLE MEASUREMENTS TABLE, 7.4.4.2. 322 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.2.1 Definitions The following definitions are included to eliminate any doubt as to the parts of the rifle referred to in the Rifle Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Stock: The basic frame of the rifle to which the barrel and action, sights, pistol grip and butt-stock are attached. On a traditional wooden-stock rifle, the stock would be of one piece and incorporate the fore-end, cheek-piece, pistol grip and butt-stock.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Butt-stock: The part of the rifle between the pistol grip and the butt-plate. This is the rearmost extension of the stock and may be offset either side of the centre-line of the barrel. The lowest point of the butt-stock may not be more than 140mm below the centre-line of the barrel. This limit does not apply to wooden stocked rifles. The butt-stock may have an adjustable extension on which the butt-plate is mounted. This extension is not included in the 140mm lower limit.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Butt-plate: The moveable end part of the butt-stock that normally rests against the athlete’s shoulder when in the shooting position. The overall width must not exceed 30mm. The butt-plate may be moved up or down, offset to the right or left of the butt-stock centre-line and/or turned on the vertical and/ or horizontal axis, but no part of the outer edges may extend more than 30mm from the Butt-stock centre-line. If a multi-part butt-plate is used, each part may be turned either right or left but all adjustments must be contained within the overall width. The depth of curve must not exceed 20mm, (7.4.4.2.g), measured to the lowest point that is in contact with the shoulder. A template with internal dimensions of 153mm x 30mm may be used to check the overall width of the butt-plate. The butt-plate is acceptable if it fits inside the template and no part is more that 30mm from the apparent centre-line of the butt-stock. The inside edge of the template should act as a reference point for the apparent centre-line.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Cheek piece: The part of the rifle upon which the athlete rests his head or cheek. It may be an integral part of a wooden-stock rifle or an attachment that is adjustable up or down and laterally. If moved laterally, the outside edge must not be more than 40mm from the centre-line of the butt-stock. A soft material can be applied to the cheek piece surface. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 323

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Fore-end: The forward part of the Stock below the barrel that contacts the supporting hand of the athlete. This may have an adjustable or removeable section to extend the depth, but those must provide a straight plane surface. It may be inclined, but the lowest point may not be more than 140mm below the centre line of the bore, nor must the width exceed 60mm. If the width of the adjustable section is wider than the upper part of the fore-end, it may be offset left or right but the outer edge must not be more than 30mm from the centre line of the barrel. Material that gives increased grip may not be added and it must not be anatomically formed. Note: A fore-end extension is not a palm rest and is not contrary to Rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.6.1.3g, even if it is detachable

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The Pistol Grip: The pistol grip must not extend laterally (to the side) more than 60mm from a vertical plane that is perpendicular to the centre-line of the barrel. The lowest point must not exceed 160mm from the centre-line of the barrel. Material that gives increased grip may not be added and it must not be anatomically formed. “Anatomically formed” may be interpreted as “The addition or removal of material to or from an original grip as supplied by a manufacturer, to fit the hand of a specific athlete”. The intention is that the grip should be smooth, as per the diagram below, and not be moulded to the shape of individual fingers or thumb. Grips produced by 3-D printing or with a lattice construction are allowed provided they are not moulded to personally fit an athlete’s hand.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) A thumb hole; thumb rest, palm rest, heel rest and spirit level are prohibited. A thumb rest is any protrusion or extension on the side of the pistol grip on which an athlete could rest the thumb of the trigger-hand. A heel rest is any protrusion or extension on the side of the pistol grip designed to prevent the hand from slipping. A palm rest is defined in Rule 7.4.5.2 and only allowed on 50m rifles. Note: This diagram is intended to illustrate the position of the parts described in a) to g)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.2.2 Weights

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Barrel weights within a radius of 30mm from the centre of the barrel are permitted. Barrel weights may be moved along the barrel. Weights added below the foresight are not regarded as barrel weights but are allowed provided that the overall weight of the rifle remains within the permitted maximum. This also applies to fixtures or mounting-adaptors fixed below the barrel to allow Scatt or similar devices to be attached. The actual devices, when attached in Finals, are not included in the overall weight. (The zone where the fixture must be attached will be specified in a future ISSF publication).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any devices or weights projecting from the buttstock must be attached as a fixed part of the buttstock (screws or other fixation means). They must not protrude sideways more than 25mm from centre line of buttstock or downwards more than 140mm measured from the centre line of the barrel (Rule 7.4.4.2 f). 324 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Weights in addition to barrel weights may be attached to any part of the rifle but must be within the areas shown in the diagram or as in a) above. Weights on or in the lower part of the fore-end may not extend horizontally (laterally) further from the centre-line of the barrel than the distance of the maximum extension of the cheek-piece from the centre line of the barrel, (dimension J1). Weights in the butt-stock area cannot extend further to the rear than a line that is perpendicular to the deepest point of the butt-plate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Weights must be rigidly attached to the rifle by semi-permanent means so that they cannot be accidentally dislodged or move position. The use of any type of visible adhesive tape to attach weights is prohibited. Manufactured metal weights, firmly attached to the rifle within the permitted areas shown on the diagram, are acceptable Athletes are reminded that the image of athletes and their equipment, when being broadcast or photographed, must be in keeping with the presentation of an Olympic sport. Therefore, rifles and attachments should not look as if they are held together with adhesive tape, cable-ties, or other temporary means. Lead automobile wheel-balance weights are allowed, but large clusters are unsightly and should be concealed or avoided if possible. See Rifle Measurements diagram 7.4.4.1 and Rifle Measurements Table

chunks.text: 7.4.4.2 for all dimensions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.3 Standards for 300m Standard Rifle Only All 300m Standard Rifles must conform to the specifications shown in the Rifle Measurements Table and with the following restrictions:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The minimum trigger pull is 1500 grams. The trigger pull must be measured with the barrel in a vertical position. Trigger weight control checks must be conducted immediately after the last series. A maximum of three (3) attempts to lift the weight are allowed. Any athlete whose rifle fails the test must be disqualified;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The same rifle must be used in all positions without change. The adjustment of the butt-plate and hand stop or the changing of front sight inserts or the adjustment of the rear sight or its eyepiece are permitted. The removal of the cheek piece during competition is permitted for barrel cleaning and bolt removal under supervision of the Jury; but its position must not be changed when it is replaced; Quick release fasteners are not permitted and must be removed from the rifle during all MATCH firing times

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The overall length of the barrel including any extension tube, measured from the breech face to the apparent muzzle, must not exceed 762mm. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 325

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.4 Standards for 10m Air Rifle Only Any type of compressed air or gas rifle that conforms to the specifications in the Rifle Measurements Table and the following additional restrictions:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The total length of the air rifle system measured from the back end of the mechanism to the apparent muzzle must not exceed 850mm; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The front sight may not extend beyond the apparent muzzle.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Any Air Rifle must not exceed 7.5 joule and must bear this mark 326 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.4.1 Rifle Measurements diagram (Air and Standard rifles) EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 327
