chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.5 Standards for 50m Rifles All rifles chambered for rimfire 5.6mm (.22” cal.) long rifle cartridges are permitted. These Rules cannot proscribe all possible combinations of attachments which may be fitted to rifles, such as additional sights, etc., but the “spirit and intent”, (as per Rule 6.8.13) of this rule is that 50m rifles should have the general appearance as the diagram below, i.e., only one set of sights, buttstock, palm-rest or extendable fore-end etc., may be fitted to a rifle at a time. This does not prevent these items being swapped during any stage of competition. 328 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The weight of the rifle for men and women may not exceed 8.0kg with all accessories used, including the palm rest and hand stop;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Weights on or in the lower part of the stock or buttstock, may not extend horizontally (laterally) further from the centre-line of the barrel than the distance of the maximum extension of the cheek-piece from the centre-line of the barrel;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Weights cannot extend further to the rear than a line perpendicular to the deepest point in the butt-plate;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Weights attached to the butt-stock must be rigidly attached and may not be fixed using visible adhesive tape or other temporary means.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Weights on the rifle fore-end may extend no lower than 90mm below the centre-line of the barrel and not further forward than 700mm from the back (rear) end of the system; Any such weight must be incapable of being converted into a bipod for use in supporting the rifle, when placed down after shooting or between positions in the 3-Position events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Extension tubes, accessories and fittings intended to attach Scatt or other devices for the fixing or raising of foresights may be attached to the barrel in front of the fore-end but the rifle must remain within the maximum permitted weight. The actual devices, if attached in Finals, are to be disregarded if they cause the maximum permitted weight.to be exceeded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) The lowest point on the butt-stock may not extend down more than 140mm from the centre-line of the bore. This limit does not apply to wooden stocked rifles

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.5.1 Hook Butt Plate A hook butt-plate that complies with the following restrictions may be used; The butt hook projecting rearward from the bottom of the butt-plate must not extend more than 153mm (A) past the rear of a line that is perpendicular to a line drawn through the axis of the bore of the rifle, and that is tangent to the deepest part of the butt-plate depression that normally rests against the shoulder; The butt hook projecting from the bottom of the butt-plate must have a total outside length around any curve or bend of not more than 178mm (B); The top projection of the butt-plate must not extend more than 25mm to the rear of this perpendicular line; and Any devices or weights projecting forward or laterally from the lower part of the butt-plate are prohibited. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 329

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.5.2 Palm Rests A palm rest is any removeable attachment or extension below the fore-end that aids the support of the rifle by the forward hand. Orthopaedic shaping, (finger or thumb grooves or depressions), is allowed. Such attachments must not extend more than 200mm below the centre line of the barrel. Palm rests may not be used on air rifles in any circumstances. They may be used on 50m rifles in the standing position only. NOTE: A fore-end extension that provides a straight plane surface and is not deeper than 140mm is not a palm rest.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.5.3 Pistol Grips No part of the pistol grip may be extended or constructed in any way that would allow it to touch or support the back of the hand or the wrist.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.5.4 Standards for 300m Rifles Standards for 300m rifles are the same as for the 50m Rifle (Men and Women). See 7.4.5 and the RIFLE SPECIFICATION TABLE (7.7.5). 300m rifles may have a mirage band with a maximum width of 60mm.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.4.6 Ammunition Rifle Calibre Other specifications 10m 4.5mm (.177”) Projectiles of any shape made of lead or other soft materi- al are permitted. 50m 5.6mm Rimfire Long Rifle. Only bullets made of lead or similar (.22”) soft material are permitted. 300m Maximum 8mm Ammunition of any description that may be fired without any danger to athletes or range personnel. Tracer, armour piercing, and incendiary ammunition is prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5 CLOTHING REGULATIONS See the General Technical Rules for general standards regarding clothing and the testing of clothing (Rule 6.7).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.1 General Standards for Rifle Clothing

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.1.1 All shooting jackets, shooting trousers and shooting gloves must be made of flexible material that does not materially change its physical characteristics, that is, become stiffer, thicker or harder, under commonly accepted shooting conditions. All lining, padding and reinforcements must meet the same specifications. Any lining or padding must not be quilted, cross-stitched, glued or otherwise affixed to the outer clothing layer other than at normal tailoring points. All lining or padding must be measured as a part of the clothing.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.1.2 Only one (1) shooting jacket and only one (1) pair of shooting trousers may be used by each athlete in all Rifle events in any ISSF Championship. All Rifle shooting jackets, shooting trousers and shoes must have a seal with a unique serial number issued by ISSF Equipment Control and registered in an ISSF database. Athletes with jackets, trousers or shoes that do not have a seal must bring them to Equipment Control to have a seal attached and registered 330 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF in the ISSF database. Two (2) jackets and two (2) trousers may be registered to each athlete. Athletes with more than one jacket and trousers with ISSF seals must inform the ISSF Equipment Control which item will be used in that Championship. Athletes that change jackets, trousers or shoes, or any with no seal (new or changed) must bring them to Equipment Control to obtain a seal and retire the previous seal (6.7.6.2.e). When an athlete is selected for post- competition testing, the test must confirm that the seal number registered to

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: that athlete was the seal number on the clothing used by that athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.1.3 Ordinary athletic type training trousers or normal athletic type training shoes may be worn in any event or position. If shorts are worn during competitions, the bottom of the leg material must be no more than 15cm above the centre of the kneecap. Sandals of any type may not be worn.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.1.4 Athletes are responsible for ensuring that all items of clothing used by them comply with these Rules. The Equipment Control Section must be open to make voluntary inspections of athletes’ clothing from the official Arrivals Day until the last day of Rifle competition and athletes are encouraged to bring their Rifle clothing items for an Equipment Control check before the competitions to be sure they comply with these Rules. In preparing jackets and trousers for competitions, athletes must make allowances for any measurement variations that may occur because of changes in temperature, humidity or other environment conditions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.1.5 Post-competition checks will be made of all Rifle clothing items after Elimination and Qualification Round competitions to ensure compliance (6.7.9). As part of the Post-competition testing following all Rifle Qualifications, all likely Finalists must be included in the Post-competition Testing. Usually the top ten athletes, to allow for possible DSQ’s. This is in addition to any testing carried out in the Finals Preparation area.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.2 Clothing Measurement Standards

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.2.1 Clothing Thickness Standards Table Rifle competition clothing must comply with these thickness measurement standards: Measurement Thickness Jackets Trousers Shoes Gloves Under- Location clothing Normal Single 2.5mm 2.5mm 4.0mm 2.5mm Normal Double 5.0mm 5.0mm 5.0mm Normal Total 16.0mm Reinforcements Single 10.0mm 10.0mm Reinforcements Double 20.0mm 20.0mm Testing will be done by using the Thickness Measurement Device as described in Rule 6.5.1 and using the Procedures described in the current Rifle Equipment Control Guide. No measurement greater than the thickness measurement standards in the chart may be approved, (zero tolerance). NOTE: Jackets and trousers will normally be measured as a Single thickness.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: Double thickness measurements will only be taken if the thickness measuring EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 331 device cannot access specific areas, such as inside the jacket sleeves or trouser legs. No measurement greater than the thickness measurement standards in the chart may be approved (zero tolerance).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.2.2 Stiffness Measurement Standards Rifle competition clothing must comply with these stiffness measurement standards: Testing will be done by using the Stiffness Measurement Device as described in Rule 6.5.2 and using the Control Procedures described in the current Rifle Equipment Control Guide, downloadable from the ISSF website.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the measuring cylinder is depressed at least 3.0mm, the material is acceptable;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If a measurement below 3.0mm is displayed, the material is too stiff. No measurement below the minimum measurement of 3.0mm may be approved; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Every part of the jacket or trousers must be capable of being measured with the 60mm measuring cylinder. If a part is too small for normal testing (no flat area 60mm or larger), measuring must be done over the seams.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Jacket seams must not be constructed so stiff as being unable to bend with their adjacent panels. They must not act as a frame which holds the jacket rigid as if being worn. In cases of doubt, seams must be measured as above and be able to deflect 3mm in 30 seconds.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.2.3 Shoe Sole Flexibility Standard The soles of athletes’ shoes must bend at least 22.5 degrees when a force of 15 Newton-Meters is applied to the heel area while the boot or shoe is clamped in the testing device (See Rule 6.5.3). This is to ensure that the sole can bend when the athlete walks ‘normally,’ heel-toe, and not robotically stiff-legged and flat footed! Warnings will be given and penalties may be incurred if a Range Official or Jury member observes that behaviour whilst on the FOP in Eliminations, and Qualification. In Finals an immediate 2 point/hit penalty will be given. As each athlete is introduced and walks to their firing-point, the Jury Member in Charge (JMIC) and the second Jury member must observe their walking behaviour over at least three consecutive steps. If both consider that it is contrary to the Rule then they should each raise a hand or signal to each other that it was unacceptable. No action is to be taken immediately, and the athlete should not be interrupted. After all athletes have entered and introductions have been made, the JMIC should walk to the relevant athlete, or athletes, and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: show a green card to indicate that a two-point penalty will be deducted from their score. The JMIC will then walk to the CRO and Announcer and explain that the athlete(s) have been penalised for a dress-code infringement to enable them to make an explanation to the audience.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.3 Shooting Shoes Normal street type or light athletic shoes are permitted in all positions. Special shooting shoes not exceeding the following specifications may be worn only in 10m and 50m and 300m 3 Positions events. Special shooting shoes must not be worn in Rifle Prone events: 332 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.3.1 The material of the upper part (above the line of the sole) must be of soft, flexible, pliable material, not thicker than 4mm, including all linings, when measured on any flat surfaces such as point D in the Shooting Shoe Measurements Table (7.5.3.6).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.3.2 The shoe sole must be constructed of the same material and composition throughout its length and breadth and the sole must be flexible in the entire forward part of the foot. Athletes may use removeable inner soles or inserts in their shoes, but any inserts must also be flexible in the forward part of the foot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.3.3 To demonstrate that soles are flexible, athletes must always walk normally when on the Field of Play, (heel-toe and bending the knees). This particularly applies when walking to their firing-points whilst being announced in Finals. If their clothing or shoes are so restrictive and over-supportive that such natural walking is impossible, a warning will be given for the first offence, and a two-point penalty and possible disqualification will be given for subsequent violations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.3.4 The height of the shoe from the floor to the highest point (Dimension C, Shooting Shoe Measurements Table) must not exceed two thirds (2/3) of the length of the sole.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.3.5 Shoes worn by athletes must be a matching pair externally.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.3.6 Shooting Shoe Measurements Table Athlete’s shoes must not exceed the maximum dimensions shown in the drawing and chart: .A .Maximum thickness of sole at the toe: 10mm .B .Overall length of shoe: According to size of wearer’s foot .C .Maximum height of shoe: Not to exceed two-thirds (2/3) length of B .D .Upper part of shoe material maximum thickness 4mm The shoe sole must follow the external curvature of the shoe and may not extend more than 5.0mm beyond the external dimensions of the shoe at any point. Toes or heels may .not be cut square or flat

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4 Shooting Jacket Thickness of material - The body and sleeves of the jacket may consist of

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.1  more than one layer of material, including a thin inner lining, provided that the maximum combined thickness of 2.5mm, (single) or 5mm (double) thickness is not exceeded. (see 7.5.2.1). Closure - Closure of the jacket must be only by non-adjustable means e.g.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.2  buttons or zippers. The jacket must not overlap more than 100mm at the EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 333 closure (see Jacket diagram). The jacket must hang loosely on the wearer. To determine this, the jacket must be capable of being overlapped beyond the normal closure by at least 80mm, measured from the centre of the button to the outside edge of the button hole. The measurement will be taken with the arms at the sides. A measurement must be made with an overlap gauge with a tension of 6.0kg to 8.0kg. The area surrounding the button hole is limited to a maximum of 12mm, and this area may exceed the permitted 2.5mm thickness. A maximum number of five (5) button holes are permitted to be used at any one time, to close the jacket. NOTE: An 80mm overlap requirement is to make the jacket less tight-fitting against the athletes’ body, especially in the chest area. Buttons can be moved towards the edge of the jacket to comply with the 80mm overlap. If, however, there is insufficient material to allow this movement, it is permitted to extend

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: each buttonhole by using strong cord or laces to form a loop into which the button can be fastened. Straps, laces and bindings - All straps, laces, bindings, seams, stitching or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.3  devices which may be construed as artificial support are prohibited. However, it is permitted to have one (1) zipper or not more than two (2) straps to gather loose material in the area of the shoulder pad (see Shooting Jacket Measurements, 7.5.4.9). No other zipper or other closing or tightening device is permitted other than those specified in these Rules and Diagrams. Back panel - The construction of the back panel may include more than one

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.4  (1) piece of material provided this construction does not stiffen or reduce the flexibility of the jacket. All parts of the back panel must comply with the thickness maximum of 2.5mm and the stiffness minimum of 3.0mm. Side panels - The construction of the side panel may not place any seam

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.5  or seams under the elbow of the support arm in the standing position within a seam-free zone that extends 70mm above the tip of the elbow and 20 mm below the tip of the elbow. This must be checked with the athlete wearing the jacket fully closed and while holding the rifle in the standing position. Sleeves -The athlete must be capable of fully extending both arms (straighten

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.6  sleeves) while wearing the buttoned jacket. In the prone and kneeling positions, the sleeve of the shooting jacket must not extend beyond the wrist of the arm on which the sling is attached. The sleeve must not be placed between the hand or glove and the fore-end of the stock when the athlete is in the shooting position. The end of the sleeve may be allowed to touch the rifle if it does not give any apparent support. Velcro, sticky substance, liquid or spray – None of these substances or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.7  similar materials may be applied to the outside or inside of the jacket, pads or shoes and/or floor or equipment. Roughening the material of the jacket is permitted. Violations will be penalized according to the Rules. Reinforcements - Shooting jackets may have reinforcement patches added

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.8  only to their outside surfaces subject to the following limitations:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Maximum thickness, including jacket material and all linings: 10mm single thickness or 20mm when measured as a double thickness;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Reinforcement may be added on both elbows but must not extend to more than half (1/2) of the circumference of the sleeve. On the arm which holds the sling, the reinforcement may extend from the upper arm to a point 100 mm from the end of the sleeve. The reinforcement on the opposite arm may have a maximum length of 300mm; 334 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Only one (1) hook, loop, button or similar device may be fastened to the outside of the sleeve or shoulder seam on the sling arm to prevent the sling from sliding;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Reinforcement on the shoulder where the butt-plate rests must not be longer than 300mm in the longest dimension (see Rule 7.5.4.9);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) All inside pockets are prohibited; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) One (1) external pocket is permitted, located on the right front side (left front side for left hand athletes) of the jacket. The maximum size of the pocket is 250mm high from the lower edge of the jacket and 200mm wide.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.9 Shooting Jacket Measurements Shooting jackets must comply with the specifications shown in the drawings below: The bottom edge of the jacket must not be longer than the bottom of the balled fist when being worn by the athlete with arms to the sides. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 335 Jacket Stiffness - When an athlete is wearing the jacket the entire area above

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.4.10  the lowest point of the shoulder-blades, excluding the arms, may be stiffer than the remainder of the jacket subject to the following proviso: The upper area must pass the stiffness test when measured with the official stiffness-testing device and achieve a deflection of 3mm within a maximum time of thirty, (30), seconds. The jacket below the lowest point of the shoulder blades, plus the sleeves, (single thickness), must pass the same test within fifteen (15) seconds. Stiffness measurements apply to a ‘single’ thickness of jacket panels irrespective of the number of layers of material used in the construction. i.e., unfolded panels with a maximum thickness of 2.5mm, (see 7.5.2.1). These provisions are intended to reduce the stiffness of the jackets so that they do not provide excessive support contrary to the principles of Rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 6.7.4.2 which prohibits the use of special devices, means or clothing, which immobilizes or unduly reduces the movement of the athlete’s leg, body or arms. However, it is accepted that athletes’ need some support to reduce the risk of strain to the upper back and shoulders when holding the rifle ‘on-aim’ in the standing position, which is the reason for the greater stiffness allowance in the upper part of the jacket. Most jackets in current use will not necessarily need tailoring alterations but, when new, will require flexing and manipulation to achieve the required degree of flexibility.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5 Shooting Trousers

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.1 Thickness - The trousers, including the lining, must not exceed 2.5 mm in single thickness and 5mm in double thickness at any point where flat surface may be measured. The number of layers of material is irrelevant provided that the permitted thickness is not exceeded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Height - The top of the trousers must not fit or be worn higher on the body than 50 mm above the crest of the hipbone.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Pockets - All pockets are prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Tightening - The trousers must be loose around the legs. All drawstrings, zippers, or fasteners to tighten the trousers around the legs or hips are prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Waist belt - To support the trousers only a normal waist belt not more than 40 mm wide and 3mm thick or braces (suspenders) may be worn. If a belt is worn in the standing position, the buckle or fastening must not be used to support the left arm or elbow. The belt must not be doubled, tripled etc. under the left arm or elbow.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Waist-band - If the trousers have a waist-band it may not be more than 70mm wide. If the thickness of the waistband exceeds 2.5mm, a waist belt is not permitted. If a waist belt is not worn, the absolute maximum thickness of the waistband is 3.5mm.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Belt loops - There can be a maximum of seven (7) belt loops, not more than 20mm in width, with at least 80mm between belt loops.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Closure - The trousers may be closed by one (1) hook and up to five (5) eyes, or up to five (5) adjustable snap fasteners, or similar closure or Velcro that must not be multi-layered. Only one (1) type of closure is permitted. A Velcro closure combined with any other closure is prohibited. 336 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Ordinary trousers - If special shooting trousers are not worn, ordinary trousers may be worn providing they do not give artificial support to any part of the body. Zippers, buttons, Velcro or similar non-adjustable fasteners or closures, may

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.2  be used in the trousers only in the following places:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) One type of fastener or closure in the front to open and close the trouser fly. The fly must not be lower than the level of the crotch;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any holes that cannot be closed are permitted; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Only one (1) other fastener is permitted in each trouser leg. The opening (fastener) must not start closer than 70 mm from the top edge of the trousers. It may, however, extend to the bottom of the trouser leg (see Shooting Trousers Measurements 7.5.5.5). One (1) fastener is permitted either in the front of the upper leg or the back of the leg, but not in both places in one (1) leg.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.3 Reinforcements - may be added to both knees of the trousers. Knee reinforcements may have a maximum length of 300mm and must not be wider than half the circumference of the trousers leg. The thickness of reinforcement including the trousers material and any linings must not exceed 10mm in single thickness (20mm double thickness).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.4 Shooting Trousers may be worn in the Rifle Prone events, and any stage of Rifle 3 Position events, Men and Women.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.5 Shooting Trousers Measurements Shooting Trousers must comply with the specifications shown in the drawing:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.5.6 Shooting Trousers Stiffness – Trousers may consist of more than one layer of material, including a thin inner lining, provided that the maximum combined permitted single thickness of 2.5mm is not exceeded, or 5mm if it is necessary to measure two total thicknesses (for example a sleeve or a leg) The upper part of the trousers above the level of the crotch may be stiffer than the lower part, subject EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 337 to the following proviso: The trousers above the level of the crotch must pass the stiffness test when measured with the official stiffness-testing device and achieve a deflection of 3mm within a maximum time of thirty, (30), seconds. The material of both legs below the level of the crotch must pass the same test within fifteen (15) seconds. Stiffness measurements apply to a ‘single’ thickness of the trouser panels irrespective of the number of layers of material used in the construction. I.e. unfolded panels with a maximum thickness of 2.5mm, (see 7.5.2.1). The intention is consistent with that outlined for the Jacket, (7.5.4.10); which is

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: to reduce the stiffness of the leg material to comply with Rule 6.7.4.2, but to retain some support for the lower back and lumbar region to reduce the risk of strain or injury when holding the rifle ‘on aim’ in the standing position.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.6 Shooting Gloves

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.6.1 The total thickness must not exceed 16mm when measuring front and back materials together at any point other than on seams and joints. If an athlete is also wearing a lining glove this must be included in the thickness measurement.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.6.2 The glove must not extend more than 50mm beyond the wrist measured from the centre of the wrist knuckle (see drawing). Any strap or other closure device at the wrist is prohibited. However, a portion of the wrist may be elasticated to enable the glove to be put on, but it must leave the glove loose around the wrist.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.7 Underclothing

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.7.1 Clothing worn under the shooting jacket must not be thicker than 2.5mm single thickness or 5mm double thickness. The same applies to all clothing worn under the trousers. Jeans or other ordinary trousers cannot be worn under shooting trousers.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.7.2 Only normal personal undergarments and/or training clothing that does not immobilize or unduly reduce the movement of the athlete’s legs, body or arms may be worn under the shooting jacket and/or trousers. Any other undergarments are prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8 Equipment and Accessories

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.1 Spotting Telescopes The use of telescopes not attached to the rifle to locate shots and judge wind is permitted for 50m and 300m events only. 338 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.2 Slings Maximum sling width is 40mm. The sling must be worn only on the upper part of the left arm and from there be connected to the fore-end of the rifle stock. Slings may be attached to the fore-end of the rifle at a single point only. The sling must pass along one side of the hand or wrist only. If the sling is worn such that it forms a loop between the arm and the forward attachment, both halves must be fastened together or attached so that the width does not exceed 40mm where it passes around the hand or wrist. No part of the rifle may touch the sling or any of its attachments except at the sling swivel and hand stop.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.3 Rifle Rests The use of a rifle rest for resting the rifle between shots is permitted providing that no part of the stand is higher than the athlete’s highest shoulder when holding the rifle in a standing shooting position. A stand for resting the rifle must not be placed in front of the shooting table or bench when shooting in the standing position. Athletes must take care when resting or loading the rifle using the Rest, that it does not intrude on the athlete on either side by keeping the rifle within the width of their firing points. For safety while the rifle is on the rifle rest, the athlete must retain a hold on it with his hand.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.4 Shooting Box or Bag The shooting box or bag must not be placed forward of the athlete’s forward shoulder on the firing line, except that in the standing position a shooting box or bag, table, or stand may be used as a rifle rest between shots. The shooting box or bag, table or stand must not be of such size or construction as to interfere with athletes on adjacent points or to constitute a wind break.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.5 Kneeling Roll Only one (1) cylindrically shaped roll is allowed for shooting in the kneeling position. The dimensions are a maximum of 25cm long and 18cm in diameter. It must be made of soft and flexible material. Binding or other devices to shape the roll are not permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.6 Bipod Bipods may be used to support the rifle before and after shooting or during position changes, but bipods, whether fixed or folding, must be removed from the rifle during all MATCH firing times.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.7 Kneeling Heel Pad A separate piece of flexible, compressible material with maximum dimensions of 20cm x 20cm may be placed on the heel in the kneeling position. The kneeling heel pad may be no thicker than 20mm when compressed with the measuring device used to measure Rifle clothing thickness.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.5.8.8 Visor or Cap A cap or visor may be worn. The cap or visor may extend forward of the athlete’s forehead no more than 80mm. The Cap or visor made with a flexible material may touch the rear sight. A cap or visor that is made of non-flexible and stiff/hard material is not allowed to touch the rear sight. Any type of Cap or visor may not be worn in a way that makes it a side blinder, the jury must be able to see the side of the athlete’s eye when viewed laterally at the same height from the ground. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 339 The original prohibition on caps or visors touching the rear sight was to prevent those being used as a point of reference and to steady the rifle to prevent horizontal rotation. The flexible rubber visors do not offer those advantages and are therefore allowed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.6 SHOOTING EVENT PROCEDURES AND COMPETITION RULES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.6.1 Shooting Positions

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.6.1.1 Kneeling

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete may touch the firing point surface with the toe of the right foot, the right knee and the left foot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The rifle may be held with both hands and the right shoulder

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The cheek may be placed against the rifle stock;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The left elbow must be supported on the left knee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The point of the elbow must not be more than 100mm over or 150mm behind the point of the knee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The rifle may be supported by the sling but the fore-end behind the left hand must not touch the shooting jacket;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) No part of the rifle may touch the sling or its attachments;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) The rifle must not touch or rest against any other point or object;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) If the kneeling roll is placed under the right foot or ankle, the foot must not be turned at an angle of more than 45 degrees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) If the kneeling roll is not used, the foot may be placed at any angle. This may include placing the side of the foot and the lower leg in contact with the surface of the firing point or shooting mat.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) No portion of the upper leg or buttocks may touch the surface of the firing point or shooting mat at any point;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) If the athlete uses the shooting mat he may kneel completely or partially on the mat so that there may be up to three points of contact, (toe, knee, foot). Other articles or padding may not be placed under the right knee. A kneeling roll may be used in conjunction with the mat if required.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: m) Only the trousers and underclothing may be worn between the athlete’s seat and heel, except that a kneeling heel pad may be used. The jacket or other articles must not be placed between these two (2) points; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: n) The right hand may not touch the left hand, left arm or the left side of the shooting jacket or sling.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.6.1.2 Prone

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete may lie on the bare surface of the firing point or on the shooting mat;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) He may also use the mat by resting his elbows on it.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The body must be extended on the firing point with the head toward the target;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The rifle may be supported by both hands and one shoulder only;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The cheek may be placed against the rifle stock. 340 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The rifle may be supported by a sling attached to the fore-end in front of the hand stop.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) No part of the rifle may touch the sling or its attachments;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) The rifle must not touch, or rest against, any other point or object;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Both forearms and sleeves of the shooting jacket forward of the elbow must be visibly raised from the surface of the firing point;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) The athlete’s sling (left) forearm must form an angle not less than 30 degrees from the horizontal, measured from the axis of the forearm;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) The right hand and/or arm may not touch the left arm, shooting jacket or sling; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) The jacket sleeve on the supporting arm may be allowed to touch the underside of the fore-end provided that it is not between the glove and the rifle nor giving additional support.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.6.1.3 Standing

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must stand free, without any artificial or other support, with both feet on the firing point surface or on the shooting mat;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The rifle may be held with both hands and the shoulder or the upper arm near the shoulder. The rifle is allowed to touch the jacket across the upper part of the chest*.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The cheek may be placed against the rifle stock;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The right hand may not touch the left hand or left arm. The left hand may not touch the left shoulder. Neither hand nor fingers may touch the left side of the jacket. “The left side of the jacket” is the area to the left of an imaginary vertical line down the centre of the chest.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The left upper arm and elbow may be supported on the chest or on the hip. If a belt is worn the buckle or fastening must not be used to support the left arm or elbow;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The rifle must not touch or rest against any point or object except in the area permitted by 7.6.1.3.b & d). There must be a clearly visible gap between the rifle and the athlete’s face and rear-sight, including a blinder if attached to the rifle. The width of this gap is deliberately not specified to avoid an athlete being disturbed during match firing by an Official or Jury member taking physical measurements, but the gap must be such that there is no doubt that the rifle, including the rear sight or blinder is not touching any point or object when viewed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) A palm rest may be used but not in 300m Standard Rifle or 10m Air Rifle events;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) A hand stop/sling swivel is not allowed in this position for 300m Standard Rifle and 10m Air Rifle events;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) In this position, the use of the sling is prohibited. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 341

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.7 RIFLE EVENTS See ISSF RECOGNIZED SHOOTING EVENTS Rule 3.3 and Rule 7.7.4, RIFLE EVENT TABLE.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.7.1 50m and 300m 3 Positions events must be fired in order: Kneeling - Prone - Standing.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.7.2 A combined 15-minute Preparation and Sighting Time must be provided before MATCH firing starts (Rule 6.11.1.1).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 7.7.3 In 3-Position events, after athletes complete the kneeling and prone positions, changing from MATCH to Sighting and back to MATCH is the responsibility of the athlete. Athletes may fire unlimited Sighting shots before starting MATCH firing shots in the prone and standing positions. No additional time is allowed for these Sighting shots. If an athlete inadvertently fails to switch from MATCH to Sighting after changing positions, any shots recorded as extra shots in the previous position must be nullified and the target must be reset to Sighting.

chunks.text: 8.1.1  These Rules are part of the ISSF Technical Rules and apply to all Pistol events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.1.2  All athletes, team leaders and officials must be familiar with the ISSF Rules and must ensure that these Rules are enforced. It is the responsibility of each athlete to comply with the Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.1.5  If there is published a differing format for any Olympic event for Los Angeles 2028, the Olympic format will take precedence over these rules.

chunks.text: 8.4.1.1 GRIPS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Neither the grip nor any part of the pistol may be extended or constructed in any way that would allow it to touch beyond the hand. The wrist must remain visibly free when the pistol is held in the normal firing position. This must be visibly determined without the need to mark the athlete’s hand in any way. It is forbidden to use any type of glue or resin to enhance contact between hand and gun. The use of chalk, talcum powder, magnesium or similar substance is allowed. Bracelets, wristwatches, wristbands, or similar items are prohibited on the hand and arm that holds the pistol; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Adjustable grips are permitted providing that when they are adjusted for the athlete’s hand they conform to these Rules. Grip adjustments are subject to random Equipment Control checks to ensure that they conform with these Rules. Compressible materials are not allowed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.text: 8.4.1.2 Sights

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Only open sights are allowed. Sights using fibre optic, light enhancing or reflecting colour surfaces are prohibited. Optical, mirror, telescope, laser beam, electronically projected dot sights etc. are prohibited;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any aiming device programmed to activate the firing mechanism or signal athlete when to fire are prohibited (also safety feature that allows pistol to fire only when pointing at the target);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) No protective covering is permitted on front or rear open sights;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) 10m and 25m Pistols must fit within the specified measuring boxes with sights mounted on the pistols (see PISTOL SPECIFICATION TABLE, Rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Correcting lenses and/or filters must not be attached to the pistol; but

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Corrective lenses or eyeglasses and/or filters or tinted lenses may be worn by the athlete. 352 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) All components are firmly attached to and contained within the frame or grip of the pistol;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The trigger works on the principle of press to fire and there is no delay in sequence (Max delay 0.02 seconds)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) During competition pistol must not be connected with any other device, except charger to charge battery. If athlete connects his pistol to any device during competition or PET he must be DSQ. (either electronically or by cable).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.4.1.4 Movement or Oscillation Reduction Systems. Any device, mechanism or system that actively reduces, slows or minimizes pistol oscillations or movements before the shot is released is prohibited.

chunks.text: 8.4.1.7 Pistols must be examined and, once approved, be registered in an ISSF Equipment Control database. Each athlete will be issued with a card listing up to five (5) approved pistols. Listing must include the serial number of the pistol. Athletes who do not have a valid card for the pistol being used must bring that pistol to the Equipment Control section so that it can be approved and added to the database. The card will be issued/amended at this point.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.4.2 Measuring Trigger Pull Weight The weight of the trigger pull must be measured with the test weight suspended near the middle of the trigger (see illustrations) and the barrel held vertically. The weight must be placed on a horizontal surface and lifted clear of the surface. The tests must be conducted by Equipment Control officials. The minimum weight of the trigger pull must be maintained throughout the competition. A maximum of three (3) attempts to lift the weight are allowed. If it does not pass, it may only be resubmitted after adjustment. When testing air or gas actuated pistols, the propellant charge must be activated. 356 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.4.2.1  Testing the weight of the trigger pull must be done according to the diagrams below. A weight with a metal or rubber knife-edge must be used. A roller on the trigger weight is not permitted. A dead weight must be used with no springs or other devices.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.4.2.2  The appropriate trigger test weight must also be made available to athletes on the range before and during training and competition, and before Finals, to allow them to recheck the weight of the trigger pull on their pistols.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.4.2.3  Random Trigger Weight control checks must be conducted immediately after the last series in all Qualification Rounds of 10m events and 25m stages. Checks in Standard Pistol will be made after 60 shots or, if the competition is fired in two stages (30 + 30 shots), checks will be done after each stage. At least one (1) athlete should be selected from each Range Section (or every eight (8) firing positions for Air Pistol) by the drawing of lots by the Equipment Control Jury. Equipment Control Officers must then conduct the tests before pistols are returned to their cases. A maximum of three (3) attempts to lift the weight are allowed. An athlete whose pistol fails this test or a selected athlete who fails to submit his pistol for testing must be disqualified.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.4.4.1 See ANNEX B Procedures for conducting Rapid Fire Pistol Ammunition Velocity Tests Manual.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.4.4.2  The ammunition of at least one (1) athlete from each relay must be tested. The Equipment Control Jury will supervise the selection of the athletes to be tested and collect the ammunition to be tested before each 30-shot Qualification stage. Athletes should have at least 50 rounds with them for each stage of competition. A Jury Member must take ten (10) cartridges from the ammunition that the athlete is using, place them in a labelled envelope, seal the envelope and hand it to the testing officer. After the stage is completed, the athlete selected must go to the testing station. The testing officer will load a magazine with three (3) cartridges and fire them in that athlete’s pistol and record the muzzle velocity of each cartridge. If the average velocity is under 250.0m/sec, the test must be repeated. If the average velocity of the six (6) shots is less than 250.0m/sec, the athlete must be disqualified.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.4.4.3 Not more than twenty (20) minutes after the end of the qualification stage of the Rapid Fire Pistol event the eight (8) athletes who have qualified for the Final, according to the published results, must report to the velocity testing station with all the ammunition that they will use in finals. If athlete did not present himself for velocity test before the final, he will not be allowed to start and will be ranked 8th and marked DNS in finals results. Samples from ammunition will be taken and a velocity test will be performed. Ammunition will be sealed in the presence of the athlete and will be taken to finals reporting area by the Equipment Control Officer.

chunks.text: 8.5 ATHLETES SHOES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.5.1  Only low-sided shoes that do not cover the ankle bone (below the medial and lateral malleolus) are permitted. The sole must be flexible in the entire forward part of the foot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.5.2  Athletes may use removeable inner soles or inserts in their shoes, but any inserts must also be flexible in the forward part of the foot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.5.3 An ISSF approved testing device will be used to check sole flexibility;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.5.4  To demonstrate that shoe soles are flexible, athletes must walk normally (heel toe) at all times while on the field of play. A warning will be given for the first offence, a two-point penalty or disqualification will be given for subsequent violations; Shoe Sole Flexibility Measurement Device. The device used to measure

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.5.5  shoe sole flexibility must be capable of accurately measuring how many degrees the shoe sole bends while bent with a precise amount of upward pressure; and Shoe Sole Flexibility Standard. The soles of athletes’ shoes must bend at

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.5.6  least 22.5 degrees when a force of 15 Newton-Meters is applied to the heel area while the shoe is clamped in the testing device. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 359

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.6 SHOOTING ACCESSORIES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.6.1 Spotting Telescopes The use of telescopes not attached to the pistol to locate shots or judge the wind is permitted in 25m and 50m events only.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.6.2 Pistol Transport Boxes Athletes may use pistol transport boxes to take pistols and equipment to the shooting ranges. During Finals, pistol transport boxes or equipment bags must not remain on the FOP.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.6.3 Pistol Support Stands Athletes may place pistol support stands or boxes on the bench or table to rest their pistols between shots. The total height of the bench or table with a support stand or box on it may not exceed 1.00m (see Rule 6.4.11.10.c, maximum bench height is 1.00m). During Elimination or Qualification competitions, a pistol transport box (Rule 8.6.2) may be used as a pistol support stand, provided the total height of the bench or table plus the box does not exceed 1.00m. During Finals, a pistol transport box may not be used as a pistol support stand.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7 SHOOTING EVENT PROCEDURES AND COMPETITION RULES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.1 Firing Position The athlete must stand free, without any artificial or other support, with both feet and/or shoes completely within the firing point. The pistol must be held and fired with one (1) hand only. The wrist must be visibly free of support.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.2 Ready Position In the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol event, 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol Rapid-fire Stages and 25m Standard Pistol 20sec. and 10sec. series, shooting must start from the READY position (see drawing). In the READY position, the athlete’s arm must point downward at an angle of not greater than 45 degrees from the vertical. The arm with the pistol must not be pointed at the ground within the forward edge of the firing point. After the series begins, the pistol may not rest on the bench or shooting table. The arm must remain in this position while waiting either for the appearance of the target or, when EST are used, for the green light(s) to come on. 360 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.3 Ready Position Violations A READY position violation occurs when an athlete in the 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol event or in the Rapid-Fire Stage of the 25m Pistol or 25m Centre Fire Pistol event, or in the 20 second or 10 second stages of the 25m Standard Pistol event:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Raises his arm too soon and this movement becomes part of the arm lift (continuous motion);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Does not lower his arm sufficiently; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Raises his arm above 45 degrees before the light changes or the targets start to turn.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.4 Procedures for Ready Position Violations WHEN A READY POSITION VIOLATION OCCURS;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must be warned by a Jury Member and the series must be recorded and repeated;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) When the series is repeated in the 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol event, the athlete must be credited with the lowest value hit on each target. In all other 25m events, the athlete must be credited with the five (5) lowest value hits in the two (2) series (or three (3) series should a malfunction be involved);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the fault is repeated in the same stage of 30 shots in the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol event, or in the Rapid-fire Stage of the 25m Pistol or 25m Centre Fire Pistol event, or in the combined 20 second and 10 second stages of the 25m Standard Pistol event, the same procedure must be applied and the athlete must be penalized by a deduction of two (2) points from his score; and d) If a third violation of this Rule occurs, the athlete must be disqualified. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 361

chunks.text: 8.7.6 Competition Rules

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.6.1 Preparation Time for 25m Events

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Athletes should report to their Range Section, but must wait to be called to their firing points;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) b) 13 minutes before the Start time, and after any preceding relay is finished, the CRO will call the athletes to the line their pistols; safety flags must remain in the pistols. Holding and aiming exercises are allowed

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Pre-competition checks by the Jury and Range Officers must be completed promptly before the Preparation Time starts;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Preparation Time begins with the command “PREPARATION TIME BEGINS NOW.” During the Preparation Time the targets must be visible, facing the athletes. During the Preparation Time athletes may remove safety flags and handle their pistols, dry fire and carry out holding and aiming exercises on the firing line; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Preparation Time allowed before the competition starts is as follows: 25m Standard Pistol 3 minutes 25m Precision Stages 3 minutes 25m Rapid-fire Stages or Events 3 minutes

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.6.2 Specific Rules for 25m Events

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) In all 25m events, timing must start at the moment the green lights come on (or the targets begin to face) and stop when the red lights come on (or the targets begin to turn away); when EST are used, the green lights are on for the required time +0.1 sec.;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The turning of the targets or the switching of lights may be controlled by a Target Operator who is located behind the firing line. His position must not disturb the athlete, but it must be within the sight and hearing of the Range Officer. The targets may also be operated by the Range Officer by means of a remote control system;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) “LOAD.” In all 25m Training or Qualification events, only one (1) magazine or pistol may be loaded with not more than five (5) cartridges on the command “LOAD.” Nothing else is allowed to be inserted into the magazine;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If an athlete in Qualification loads his pistol with more cartridges than he is allowed to load (full series or series completion) or he loads more than one (1) magazine on any command “LOAD” he must be penalized by the deduction of two (2) points from his score in that same series. If the athlete violates this rule in Training, he must be directed to unload his pistol, insert a safety flag and stop training.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) An athlete who fires a shot or shots before the command “LOAD” must be disqualified; and 362 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) “UNLOAD.” In all events, after the series or stage has been completed, the command “UNLOAD” must be given. In any case, immediately upon completing a series (unless there is a pistol malfunction), or when ordered, the athlete must unload the pistol and insert safety flag.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.6.3 Specific Rules for the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol Qualification Event

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The event is 60 competition shots divided into two (2) stages of 30 shots each. Each stage includes six (6) series of five (5) shots each, two (2) series in eight (8) seconds, two (2) series in six (6) seconds and two (2) series in four (4) seconds. In each series, one (1) shot is fired at each of the five (5) targets within the specified time limit for the series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Before the beginning of each stage, the athlete may fire one (1) Sighting series of five (5) shots in eight (8) seconds;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) All shooting (Sighting and MATCH firing series) is by command. Both athletes in the same Range Section must fire at the same time, but organizers may have more than one (1) Range Section to fire simultaneously under centralized commands;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If a pistol of any of the athletes firing together has a malfunction, the malfunction series must be re-fired by those concerned in the same time stage with the following regular series. The final series of this stage will be fired immediately after all other athletes firing together have completed this time stage. Each Range Section may operate independently;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Before the Range Officer gives the command “LOAD,” he must call out the series time (i.e. “eight second series,” “six second series,” etc.), or the series time must be indicated in some manner such as using a numbered sign of sufficient size to be visible to the athlete. When the Range Officer gives the command “LOAD,” athletes must prepare themselves for their series within one (1) minute;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) When one (1) minute has expired, the Range Officer will give the command: “ATTENTION” The red lights must be switched on (if paper targets are used, they must be turned to the edge-on position) and the athletes must bring their pistols to the READY position. When EST are used, the red lights will be switched on. After a delay of 7 sec. +/-

chunks.text: 0.1sec. the green lights will come on for the required time +0.1sec. When paper targets are used, the targets will be turned to the edge-on position. After a delay of 7sec. (+/- 0.1sec.), the targets will be turned to face the athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Before each series, the athlete must lower his arm and adopt the READY position;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) The green lights come on (if paper targets are used, the targets turn to face the athletes) seven (7) seconds+/- 0.1sec. after the command “ATTENTION;” EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 363

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Pistols may be raised the moment the green lights come on (or the targets begin to face);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) The athlete should fire five (5) shots during each series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) A series is considered as having started after the command “ATTENTION”; every shot fired after that must be counted as a MATCH shot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: I) After the firing of each series, there should be a pause of at least one (1) minute before the next command “LOAD;” and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: m) There should be a minimum of 30min., or longer if the programme permits, between the scheduled start times for relays; the published start time for successive relays should be adequate to allow for these relays to start at the published time.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.6.4 Specific Rules for 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol The programme for each event is 60 MATCH shots divided into two (2) stages of 30 shots each: Stage Number of series and shots Time limit for each Sighting or MATCH series Precision Stage six (6) series of five 240 seconds per series (5) shots Rapid-fire Stage six (6) series of five see below (5) shots

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) All athletes will fire the Sighting series as well as all MATCH series at the same time and on the same commands:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Range Officer must give the command “LOAD” BEFORE EACH SERIES; after the command “LOAD,” the athlete must prepare himself within one (1) minute with the correct number of cartridges;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) After the command “UNLOAD” is given at the end of a sighting or MATCH series, there must be a pause of at least one (1) minute before the Range Officer gives the command “LOAD” to start the next series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) A series is considered as having started from the moment the red light is switched on, or the targets turn away from the athlete after the command “ATTENTION”, every shot fired after that must be counted as a MATCH shot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Firing will begin on the appropriate command or signal, the commands for stationary targets are “START” or the signal of a horn and “STOP” or a horn signal, the signals for turning targets are when the targets turn towards or away from the athlete; the signals for EST are the red and green lights.

chunks.text: h) All athletes must complete the Precision Stage before the Rapid-Fire Stage may begin;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Rapid Stage During each series in the Rapid-Fire Stage, the target is shown five (5) times for 3.0sec. -0.0 to +0.2sec. or, when EST are used, the green lights come on for 3.1sec. for each shot; the time between each appearance (the edge-on position) or, when EST are used, when the red lights are on, must be seven (7)sec. ± 0.1sec. one (1) shot only will be fired during each appearance of the target; when EST are used, the green light must go off after 3.1sec., but the target must continue to record a valid shot for an additional 0.2sec. “after time” in accordance with Rule 6.4.13 ”FOR THE SIGHTING SERIES - LOAD“ All athletes load within a time of one (1) minute. After a delay of 7sec.±0.1sec. the green lights will come on. When paper targets are used, the targets will be turned to the edge-on position. After

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) Before each shot the athlete must lower his arm and adopt the READY position in accordance with Rule 8.7.2;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) The pistol must not rest on the bench, or shooting table, during the Rapid stage series

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.6.5 Specific Rules for the 25m Standard Pistol Event The event programme is 60 MATCH shots divided into 3 stages of 20 shots each. Each stage consists of 4 series of 5 shots: EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 365 Stage Number of series and shots Time limit for each series 1 four (4) series of five (5) shots 150sec. 2 four (4) series of five (5) shots 20sec. 3 four (4) series of five (5) shots 10sec.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Before the beginning of MATCH firing, the athlete may fire one (1) Sighting series of five (5) shots within a time limit of 150 seconds;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Before the Range Officer gives the command “LOAD,” he must call out the series time (such as 150sec. series, or 20sec. series etc.), or the series time must be indicated in some manner such as using a numbered sign of sufficient size to be visible to the athlete;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) When the Range Officer gives the command “LOAD,” the athlete must prepare himself immediately for the series within one (1) minute;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

After a delay of 7sec. ±0.1sec. the green lights will come on. When paper targets are used, the targets will be turned to the edge-on position. After a delay of 7sec. ±0.1sec, the targets will be turned to face the athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Before each series, except in the 150sec. series, the athlete must lower his arm and adopt the READY position;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) A series is considered as having started from the moment the red light is switched on, or the targets turn away from the athlete after the command “ATTENTION,” every shot fired after that must be counted as a MATCH shot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) After the command “UNLOAD” is given at the end of a sighting or MATCH series, there must be a pause of at least one (1) minute before the Range Officer gives the command “LOAD” to start the next series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) In exceptional cases the match may be conducted in two parts, in this case each part must consist of: Stage Number of series and shots Time limit for each series 1 two (2) series of five (5) shots 150sec. 2 two (2) series of five (5) shots 20sec. 3 two (2) series of five (5) shots 10sec.
