chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.7.7 In all Post Competition targeted testing, following a Qualification, all Finalists in Rifle and Pistol events must also be tested. (Top 10 athletes to allow for DSQ’s). This is in addition to any testing carried out in the Finals Preparation area.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8 INTERRUPTIONS AND IRREGULARITIES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.1 Interruptions in 25m Events and Stages If shooting is interrupted for safety or technical reasons (without being the fault of the athlete):

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the elapsed interruption time is more than 15min., the Jury must allow one (1) extra sighting series of five (5) shots;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) In the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol and in the 25m Standard Pistol event, if the series is interrupted it must be annulled and repeated. The repeated series must be recorded and credited to the athlete;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) In the 25m Pistol and the 25m Centre Fire Pistol events, the interrupted series must be completed. The completed series must be recorded and credited to the athlete; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) In the Precision Stage the time limit is forty-eight (48) seconds for every shot to be fired to complete the series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2 Irregular Shots in 25m Events and Stages

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2.1 Too Many Competition Shots Fired (25m) If an athlete fires more MATCH shots on a target than the Pistol Events Qualification Table (Rule 8.11) specifies, or more than one (1) shot at one (1) appearance of the target in a Rapid-Fire Pistol Series, the highest value hit(s) must be disregarded from the score of that target;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Two (2) points must also be deducted from the score of that series for each extra shot fired in the series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) This penalty is in addition to the penalty of two (2) points that may be imposed when an athlete loads more than the authorized number of cartridges; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Two (2) points must be deducted on every occasion if two (2) shots are fired during a single exposure of the target in the Rapid-Fire stages of the 25m Pistol and the 25m Centre Fire Pistol events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2.2 Too Many Sighting Shots Fired (25m) If an athlete fires more Sighting shots than are provided for in the Pistol Events Qualification Table (Rule 8.11), or are approved by the Range Officer or Jury, he must be penalized by the deduction of two (2) points from the first series of his MATCH score for each excessive sighting shot fired. This penalty is in addition to the penalty of two (2) points that may be imposed when an athlete loads more than the authorized number of cartridges.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2.3 Early Or Late Shots (25m)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Any shot(s) fired accidentally after the command “LOAD,” but before the start of a MATCH series, must not be counted in the competition and two (2) points must be deducted from the following series. This penalty must not apply in the Sighting series. The athlete who fired accidentally must not continue, but must wait until the other athletes finish that series and then report this to the EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 367 Range Officer as if he had a malfunction. The Range Officer will then permit him to continue and repeat the series in the same time stage with the following regular series. The final series of the stage will be fired immediately after all athletes have completed that time stage. If this procedure is not followed and the athlete continues the original series, the accidentally fired shot will be scored as a miss (zero); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) In a Precision Stage, if a shot(s) is fired after the command or signal “STOP,” that shot must be counted as a miss. If the shot(s) cannot be identified the highest value hit(s) must be deducted from the score of that target and scored as miss(es).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.2.4 Crossfires on Sighting Targets (25m) If an athlete fires a Sighting shot on the sighting target of another athlete, he must not be allowed to repeat the shot, but will not be penalized. If it cannot be established clearly and quickly which hit(s) belong to whom, the athlete who is not at fault has the right to repeat the sighting shot(s).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.3 Incorrect Range Commands (25m)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If, because of an incorrect command and/or action by a Range Officer, the athlete is not ready to fire when the signal to fire is given, he must hold his pistol pointing down range and raise his free hand, and immediately after the series report this to a Range Officer or Jury Member; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If the claim is considered justified, the athlete must be allowed to fire the series; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the claim is considered not justified, the athlete may fire the series, but must be penalized by the deduction of two (2) points from the score of that series; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If the athlete has fired a shot after the incorrect command and/or action, the protest must not be accepted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.4 Disturbances Should an athlete consider that he was disturbed while firing a shot, he must hold his pistol pointing down range and immediately inform the Range Officer or Jury Member by raising his free hand. He must not disturb other athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.4.1 IF THE CLAIM IS CONSIDERED JUSTIFIED:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The series (25m Rapid-fire Pistol, 25m Standard Pistol), must be annulled and the athlete may repeat the series; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The shot (25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol) must be annulled and the athlete may repeat the shot and complete the series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.4.2 IF THE CLAIM IS CONSIDERED UNJUSTIFIED:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the athlete has finished his series, the shot or series must be credited to the athlete;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If the athlete has not finished his series due to the claimed disturbance, the athlete may repeat or complete the series. Scoring and penalties are as follows;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) In the 25m Rapid-fire Pistol Event the series may be repeated and the score must be recorded as the total of the lowest value hit on each target;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) In the 25m Standard Pistol Event the series may be repeated and the 368 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF score must be recorded as the total of the five (5) lowest value hits on the target;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) In the 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol Events the series may be completed and the score must be recorded;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Two (2) points must also be deducted from the score of the repeated or completed series; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) In any repeated series, all five (5) shots must be fired at the target. Any shot(s) not fired or not hitting the target must be scored as a miss(es).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.5 Timing Irregularity Claims

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.5.1  If an athlete considers that the time elapsed between the command specified in the Rules and the green light coming on or the facing of the targets was too fast or too slow, and therefore not according to the time specified in the Rules, he must hold his pistol pointing down range and immediately inform a Range Officer or Jury Member by raising his free hand. He must not disturb other athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If it is found that his claim is justified, he may begin the series again; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If his claim is found not justified, he may fire the series, but a two (2) point penalty must be deducted from the score of that series; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Once the athlete has fired the first shot in the series, such a claim must not be accepted. If an athlete considers that the time of the series was too short, he may

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.8.5.2  inform a Range Officer immediately after finishing the series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Range Officer and/or Jury must verify the timing of the mechanism; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If it is confirmed that there has been an error, the protesting athlete’s series must be annulled and repeated; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the claim is considered not justified, the result of the series must be credited to the athlete and recorded.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9 MALFUNCTIONS IN 25M EVENTS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.1  Malfunctions during a sighting series may not be claimed, however, an athlete may clear the malfunction and continue to shoot the unfired shots within the specified time for the sighting series for that event. Only one (1) malfunction (either ALLOWABLE or NON-ALLOWABLE) may be claimed during each MATCH stage(s) of a 25m Pistol event as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Once in each 30 shot stage of the 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol, 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol events;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Twice in the 60-shot Standard Pistol match. NOTE: In exceptional cases, where the match is shot in two stages (see Rule 8.7.6.5.h), then only once in each 30 shot stage of the Standard Pistol match.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The appropriate Malfunction Form (RFPM or STDP) must be used to score repeated malfunction series. Malfunction Forms are found in the General Technical Rules, Rule 6.19.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Malfunctions (ALLOWABLE or NON-ALLOWABLE) in 25m Finals will be decided according to 6.17.4.o) or 6.17.5.k). EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 369

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.2 Repairing or Replacing a Broken Gun Should a pistol break or cease to function, the athlete is allowed to repair or replace the pistol. In all cases, the Chief Range Officer must confirm that the pistol cannot function safely and the Jury must be informed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) An athlete is allowed a maximum of 15min. to repair or replace a pistol in order to resume the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If the repair is likely to take more than 15min., the athlete, at his request, may be granted more time by the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If extra repair time is granted, he will complete the competition at a time and place determined by the Jury or he may continue to fire with another pistol of the same type of mechanism (semi-automatic or revolver) and of the same calibre; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) In the 25m events the Jury must allow one (1) extra sighting series of five (5) shots.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.3 Malfunctions in 25m Pistol Events

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If a shot has not been fired due to a malfunction, and if the athlete wishes to claim a malfunction, he must hold his pistol pointing down range and must retain his grip. Only the tip of the barrel may rest on the bench, if the magazine is not of the type that is loaded from the barrel end, but the magazine must be clearly not touching the bench or hand and immediately inform a Range Officer by raising his free hand. He must not disturb other athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) An athlete may try to correct a malfunction and continue the series, but after attempting any correction, he may not claim an Allowable Malfunction unless the firing pin has broken, or any other part of the pistol is damaged sufficiently to prevent the pistol from functioning.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4 Types of Malfunctions

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.1 ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTIONS (AM) are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) A bullet is lodged in the barrel;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The trigger mechanism has failed to operate;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) There is an undischarged cartridge in the chamber and the trigger mechanism has been released and operated;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The cartridge case has not been extracted or ejected; this applies even if a case catcher is used;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The cartridge, magazine, cylinder, or other part of the pistol has jammed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The firing pin has broken, or any other part of the pistol is damaged sufficiently to prevent the pistol from functioning;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) The pistol fires automatically without the trigger being released. The athlete must stop firing immediately and must not continue to use such a pistol without the permission of a Range Officer or a Jury Member. When using electronic scoring targets, the first shot will be scored by the system and this will be credited to the athlete. When using paper targets, should the automatically fired shot(s) hit the target, the hit(s) found highest up on the target must be disregarded before the repeat series. After any repeat series, all the shot(s), except those that were disregarded on the one (1) target concerned, must be included to establish the score; or 370 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) The slide jams or the empty case is not ejected, this applies even if a case catcher is used.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.2 NON-ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTIONS (NAM) are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete has touched the breech, mechanism or safety catch or the pistol has been touched by another person before being inspected by the Range Officer;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The safety catch has not been released;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The athlete did not load his pistol;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The athlete loaded fewer cartridges than prescribed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The athlete did not allow the trigger to return far enough after the previous shot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The pistol was loaded with the wrong ammunition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) The magazine was not inserted correctly, or had fallen out during shooting unless this is due to damage to the mechanism; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) The malfunction is due to any cause that could reasonably have been corrected by the athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.3 Determining the Cause of a Malfunction If the external appearance of the pistol does not show an obvious reason for the malfunction and there is no indication, and the athlete does not claim that there may be a bullet stuck in the barrel, the Range Officer must take the pistol without interfering with or touching the mechanism, point the pistol in a safe direction and pull the trigger one time only to determine whether the trigger mechanism had been released.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the pistol is a revolver, the Range Officer must not pull the trigger unless the hammer is in the cocked position;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If the pistol does not discharge, the Range Officer must complete the examination of the pistol to determine the cause of the malfunction and to decide whether or not the malfunction is allowable; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Range Officer decides, after inspection of the pistol, that there is an ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION or a NON-ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION. In the case of a NON-ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION, every shot that is not

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.4  fired will be scored as a miss (zero). No re-fire or completion is permitted. Only the values of shots fired will be credited to the athlete. The athlete may continue to shoot the remainder of the event. ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION PROCEDURES - 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.5  25m Standard Pistol

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If an ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION occurs during a 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol Men or 25m Standard Pistol Men series, record the scores of the shots that were fired on first line of the Malfunction Form (Form RFPM or Form STDP); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete must fire all five (5) shots at the target(s) in any repeat series. After the repeat series, record the scores of all shots fired on the second line of the Malfunction Form; any shots not hitting the target or late shots, fired or unfired, must be scored as zero(s); or EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 371

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If a second malfunction occurs in the repeat series, record the scores of the fired shots in the repeat series on the second line of the Malfunction Form. Then add zeros to the line (first series or repeat series) that has scores for the most fired shots to ensure that one line has five scores. These added zeros must be counted in determining the score for that series; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Determine the scores of the five shots to be counted for the series and record them on the third line of the Malfunction Form (“Final Score”): • RFPM: enter the lowest value scores on each of the five targets and total scores. • STDP: enter the five lowest value scores from all recorded shots, including any zeros that were added to one of the two lines, and total those scores. ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION PROCEDURES - 25m Pistol and 25m Centre

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.9.4.6  Fire Pistol Precision and Rapid-Fire Stages:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The number of shots is recorded and the series may be completed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Shot(s) to complete the series (series completion) must be fired in the next competition series; in the Precision Stage a time of forty-eight (48) seconds will be allowed for each shot to be fired; in the Rapid-Fire Stage, the series completion must start on the first exposure;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Any shot(s) not fired or not hitting the target must be scored as miss(es) (zero(s);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The five-shot series must be scored in the normal manner; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Use Form IR to report series completion.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.10 FAILURE OF EST OR PAPER TARGET SYSTEMS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.10.1 Failure of ALL targets on a Range or Range Section

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The expired shooting time must be recorded by the Chief Range Officer and the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) All completed MATCH shots of each athlete must be counted and recorded. In the event of a range power supply failure, this may involve waiting until power is restored to enable the number of shots registered by the target, not necessarily on the firing point monitor, to be established;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) After the targets are repaired and the full range, or Range Section, is in operation, an additional Sighting series and a one (1) minute pause will be given before starting the completion of the series in accordance with the following rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol Events. The athletes will COMPLETE the series of five shots in the same way as for an ALLOWABLE MALFUNCTION. The athlete should fire the number of shots that had not been recorded by the target when the failure occurred.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) 25m Standard Pistol and 25m Rapid-Fire Pistol Events. If the series was not completed and recorded, it will be annulled and repeated. If the five (5) shots were recorded for any athlete, the series score will be recorded and no repetition will be permitted by that athlete. 372 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.10.2 Failure of a Single Target or Target Group If there is a failure of a single target or group of five targets (25m Rapid-Fire Pistol event) that cannot be repaired immediately, the athlete will be moved to another firing position in the same, or a following relay. After the problem is resolved, a separate sighting series and a one (1) minute pause will be given before the firing of the next series in accordance with the rule above (8.10.1.c).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8.10.3 Failure to Register or Display a Shot If there is a complaint concerning failure to register or display a shot on the monitor(s) of 25m Electronic Scoring Target systems, or the monitor shows a zero (0) that was not expected:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) In the Precision Stages of 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol events and in the 150sec. series of the 25m Standard Pistol event, the athlete must immediately (before the next shot) inform the nearest range official of the failure;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete will then be directed to complete the series (remaining unfired shots only) at a time decided by the Jury; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) In the Rapid-Fire Stages of the 25m Pistol and 25m Centre Fire Pistol events, and in the 25m Standard Pistol and 25m RFP men events, the athlete must continue the five (5) shot series and must inform the nearest range official of the failure immediately after the end of the series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) There will be no repeat series. The score will be determined by the RTS Jury. After the series has been completed, the Procedure for Examination of Electronic Scoring Targets (6.10.8) will be applied. chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.1 GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.1.1 These Rules are part of the ISSF Technical Rules and apply to all Shotgun events during any ISSF Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.1.2 All athletes, coaches, team leaders and officials must be familiar with the ISSF Rules and must ensure that these Rules are enforced. It is the responsibility of each athlete to comply with the Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.1.3  When a Rule refers to right-handed athletes, the reverse of that Rule refers to left-handed athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.1.4  Unless a Rule applies specifically to a men’s or a women’s event, it must apply uniformly to both men’s and women’s events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.1.5  Where figures and tables in these rules contain specific information, the specific information in these figures and tables has the same authority as the numbered rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.1.6  National Federations, in national competitions may deviate or change some of these rules according to their requirements and range constraints. Any changes must be informed at Technical Meeting.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.2 SAFETY

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.2.1 Safety is of Paramount importance The safety of athletes, range personnel and spectators require continued and careful attention to gun handling and caution in moving about the range. It is strongly recommended that all personnel operating forward of the firing line should wear high visibility vests or jackets. Self-discipline is necessary on the part of all.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.2.2 Carrying Shotguns To ensure safety, all shotguns, even when empty, must always be handled with maximum care and must be open (penalty - possible DISQUALIFICATION).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Conventional double-barrelled shotguns must be carried empty with the breech visibly open;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Shotguns not in use must be open and placed in a gun rack, locked gun case, armoury or other secure place.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) All shotguns must be kept unloaded except on the shooting station and only then after the command or signal “START” has been given or when it is the athletes turn to shoot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Cartridges or empty cartridge cases must not be loaded in the shotgun until the athlete is standing on the shooting station, facing the machines with the shotgun pointed towards the target flight area and after the Referee has given permission.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) When shooting is interrupted, the shotgun must be opened and any cartridges or empty cartridge cases must be removed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) No athlete may turn from the shooting station before his shotgun is open and empty.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) After the last shot and before leaving the range or placing the shotgun on a rack, armoury etc., the athlete must ascertain that there are no cartridges or empty cartridge cases in the chamber. The handling of closed shotguns is prohibited when operating personnel are forward of the firing line. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 385

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.2.3 Aiming

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Aiming exercises are permitted only on designated shooting stations with the permission of the Referee, or in designated dry firing areas.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Aiming or shooting at another athlete’s targets or deliberately aiming or shooting at live birds or other animals is prohibited and may lead to disqualification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Aiming in any area other than within the designated dry firing areas and direction is prohibited and may lead to disqualification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.2.4 Shooting and Test Firing

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Shots may be fired only when it is the athlete’s turn and the target has been thrown.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) With the permission of the Referee, test firing of shotguns (a maximum of two (2) shots) is permitted for each athlete on each day of competition immediately prior to the start of their first round of the day.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Test firing of shotguns is also permitted for each athlete prior to the start of the Finals or any shoot-offs after qualification except any shoot off during Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Test shots must not be fired into the ground within the shooting areas. An athlete who shoots into the ground must receive an initial Warning (Yellow Card). For a repetition in the same round, one (1) target must be declared “LOST” whether hit or not.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Test firing of a shotgun after a repair is permitted, but it must be arranged with the Chief Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.2.5 “STOP” Command

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) When the command or the signal “STOP” is given, shooting must stop immediately and all athletes must unload their shotguns and make them safe;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) No shotgun may then be closed until the command to continue (“START” or “READY”) has been given by the Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Shooting may only be resumed at the appropriate command (“START”) or signal of the Referee; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Any athlete who handles a closed shotgun after the “STOP” command has been given, without the permission of the Referee, may be disqualified.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.2.6 Commands

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) All range commands must be given in the English language;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Referees or other appropriate range officials are responsible for giving the commands “START,” “STOP” and other necessary commands; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Referees must then ascertain that the commands are obeyed and that all shotguns are handled safely.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.2.7 Eye And Ear Protection

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) All athletes and other persons in the vicinity of the firing line must wear ear plugs, ear muffs, or similar adequate ear protection;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Hearing protection incorporating any type of sound-enhancing or receiving devices may not be worn by athletes or coaches on the FOP. Hearing impaired 386 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF athletes may wear sound-enhancing devices with the approval of the Jury (see also G.T.R. 6.2.5); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) All athletes, Referees and officials must wear shatterproof shooting glasses or similar eye protection.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If an athlete is found on his shooting station without hearing protection, the athlete will receive a warning by the referee in charge (yellow card), for the first violation and for the second violation during any round in the competition or PET, a deduction of 1 Target will be imposed (green card) by the referee in charge (The deduction will be applied to the athlete’s first hit target in the first qualification round)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) If an athlete is found on his shooting station without the required shooting glasses, the athlete will receive a warning by the referee in charge (yellow card) for the first violation and for the second violation during any round in the competition or PET, a deduction of 1 Target will be imposed (green card) by the referee in charge. (The deduction will be applied to the athlete’s first hit target in the first qualification round)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) If the Chairperson of juries declares that due to bad weather, rain, fog, etc., then the athletes may shoot without the required shooting glasses.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.3 RANGE AND TARGET STANDARDS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Clay target standards are found in G.T.R. 6.3.6

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Range standards for Shotgun ranges are found in G.T.R. 6.4.17/18/19.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) No athlete, coach or team official may interfere in any way with the range equipment (traps, microphones, control units, etc.) once set by the Referee or Jury. For a first violation, a Warning (Yellow Card) will be given to the athlete or the coach or the team official; a second violation will result in a one (1) point Deduction (Green Card) from the last hit target in the last completed round of the athlete or from the first round if shooting has not started. Any subsequent occurrence will result in Disqualification (Red Card). The deliberate switching off of the control unit will result in an immediate disqualification. If a coach or team official violates this rule, the warning or penalty must be given to all athletes involved with that coach or team official.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4 EQUIPMENT AND AMMUNITION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.1 Equipment Restrictions

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Athletes must use only equipment and clothing that comply with the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any shotgun, device, equipment, accessory or other item that may give an athlete an unfair advantage over others and that is not specifically mentioned in these Rules, or that is contrary to the spirit of these Rules, including accessories or devices used to facilitate the counting of targets, is prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The use of cartridges with coloured wads is prohibited (see also (9.4.3.1 (f)).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) For a violation of these Rules, the athlete must receive a Warning (Yellow Card) for the first occurrence. For a repeat violation, the athlete must receive a Deduction (Green Card) of five (5) targets from the last five (5) hit targets in the last completed round. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 387

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.1.1 Equipment Control

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Athletes are responsible for ensuring that all items of equipment and clothing used by them in ISSF Competitions comply with the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Shotgun Jury is responsible for checking the athletes’ equipment to ensure compliance. The Jury must provide an equipment control consultation service that is available to all athletes starting on the first Pre-Event Training Day so that athletes, if they wish, may have their equipment checked prior to the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) To ensure compliance with the ISSF Rules, the Jury will conduct random checks during Competition and any athlete found to be in violation of the rules will be penalized, as per Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Athletes found to be in violation of the rules for shotguns or Skeet marker tapes may be disqualified.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.1.2 Equipment on the Field of Play / Shooting Area Any equipment or accessories on the field of play/shooting area shall be deemed as available for use by the athlete concerned and will be subject to inspection/ check by the Jury. Penalties will be applied.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.1.3 Shooting vests All athletes must wear an appropriate shooting vest (sleeveless) or shooting jacket (long sleeves) when they are on the field of play and ready to shoot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2 Shotguns

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.1 Types of Shotguns

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) During all events supervised by the ISSF, all types of smoothbore shotguns, but excluding semi-automatics and pump action shotguns, may be used, provided their calibre does not exceed 12 gauge. Shotguns smaller than 12 gauge may be used.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Shotguns must not have a camouflage finish.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Due to safety requirements during ISSF competitions, all shotguns must be safe for use and free from any condition that may compromise their structural integrity or safe operation.The following components are considered structural components: barrels, chamber, receiver, locking system, fore-end, and buttstock. Structural components must not be cracked, deformed, or subject to temporary or improvised repair (including but not limited to tape, glue, pins, wire, or similar materials). Any such condition shall result in the shotgun being deemed unsafe and not permitted for use.Modifications to structural components that alter material thickness, pressure tolerance, or mechanical performance — including non-factory or non-professional drilling, porting, or machining — are prohibited. Modifications that are purely ergonomic and do not affect structural integrity or safe operation are permitted. This includes grip shaping, grip filling, and surface adaptations. The grip is not considered a structural component under this rule.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.2 Release Triggers Shotguns with any type of “release” trigger mechanisms are prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.3 Slings Slings or straps on shotguns are prohibited. 388 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.4 Changing Shotguns The changing of properly functioning guns or parts of guns, including interchangeable chokes, is not permitted during the round.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.5 Compensators The addition of compensators and similar devices (designed to reduce muzzle rise) fitted to gun barrels is prohibited, except that ported interchangeable chokes are permitted (see Rule 9.4.2.6 & 7)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.6 Ported Barrels and Ported Interchangeable Chokes (with or without porting) Ported barrels are permitted, provided they do not extend back further than 20cm as measured from the end of the muzzle, or as measured from the muzzle end of any interchangeable fitted choke; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.7 Interchangeable chokes (with or without porting) fitted to the end of the muzzle are permitted. In the case of ported interchangeable chokes, their porting (plus any barrel porting) shall not extend back further than 20cm as measured from the muzzle end of the interchangeable fitted choke.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.8 Optical Sights All devices or scopes fitted to the gun that have magnifying, light emitting, forward lead displacement, spotting properties, video cameras or apparatus that gives visual enhancement of the target, are prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.9 Buttstock Height (Only for Skeet)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.10 The height of the buttstock (either adjustable or “Monte Carlo” type) measured from the highest point of the cheek rest to the lowest point of the butt plate toe must not exceed 170mm (17cm). Any butt plate toe vertical extension which is not an integral part of the buttstock and simply intended to increase its height is not permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.2.11 Barrel Porting The barrel porting shall not extend more than 200mm (20cm) from the end of the muzzle or end of the interchangeable fitted choke (see also: 9.4.2.6 & 7). EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 389

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.3 Ammunition

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.3.1 Cartridge Specifications Cartridges permitted in the ISSF competitions must meet the following specifications:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Shot charge must not exceed 24.0g (+0.5g tolerance). To determine if an athlete is using cartridges that comply with this rule, the cartridge inspection procedure must determine that the average weight of the selected cartridges does not exceed the maximum shot charge plus tolerance (24.5g);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Pellets must be spherical in shape;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Pellets must be made of lead, lead alloy or of any other ISSF approved material;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Pellets must not exceed 2.6mm in diameter;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Pellets may be plated;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Any ejecta (Wad), except for the shot or powder must be translucent or transparent. The shot must not have any colour added. No other element can be added that could be mistaken as a Hit Target.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Black powder, tracer, incendiary, or other special types of cartridges are prohibited; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) No internal changes may be made which will give an extra or special dispersion effect, such as the inverse loading of components, crossing devices, etc.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.3.2 Cartridge Inspection

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Equipment Control or Shotgun Jury must implement a cartridge inspection procedure that is approved by the ISSF Shotgun Committee. Specific details for conducting the cartridge inspection procedure are found in the Shotgun Equipment Control Guide that is available from the ISSF Headquarters.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) During a competition, a Referee (under the instructions of the Jury) or a Jury member, may take out of the normal cartridge control procedure, an athletes’ cartridge/s for inspection at any time when the athlete is in the shooting area.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) When cartridges are sold to participating teams at an ISSF Competition site, the Equipment Control or Shotgun Jury must test selected samples of these cartridges before the Pre-Event Training (PET) for the first event and post the results of these tests so that this information is available to coaches and athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If an athlete uses ammunition that is not in accordance with Rule 9.4.3.1 a) (maximum shot charge), he may be Disqualified (Red Card); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) If an athlete uses ammunition that is not in accordance with Rule 9.4.3.1, he must receive a Warning (Yellow Card) or be penalized according to Rules 8.3.1

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5 COMPETITION OFFICIALS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.1 General All persons who are designated to serve as officials in ISSF competitions must 390 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF possess valid qualifications appropriate to the level of the competition. When on duty, all Jury Members are required to wear the official ISSF Jury (red and black) Vest. Also, when on duty, all Referees are required to wear the official ISSF Shotgun Referee (blue) Vest. Both can be purchased from the official ISSF supplier.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.2 Jury

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.2.1 Duties Before the Competition Starts Before the competition starts, the Jury must:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Check the ranges to ensure that they comply with these Rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Ensure that the targets are correctly set according to these Rules; Note; the Jury may make use of an approved radar speed gun system to check the targets randomly if due to bad weather or other reasons.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Review the competition organization to confirm that it is properly prepared to conduct the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Establish an equipment control consultation service where athletes may have their guns, clothing and accessories checked; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Cooperate with the RTS office in the verification, preparation and distribution of the start lists, both for the Pre-Event Training, the Qualification stage and the Finals, as well as any possible shoot-offs before and during the Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.2.2 Duties During the Competition During the competition, the Jury must:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Supervise the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Advise and assist the Organizing Committee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Ensure the correct application of the Rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Check the athletes’ guns, ammunition and equipment;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Check that the targets are set correctly after a trap machine breakdown;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Make random checks during Qualification Rounds to ensure compliance with the Preparation Time Limits;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Make random checks during Competition to ensure compliance with the rules concerning guns, ammunition, shooting vests and other clothing;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Deal with protests that are properly submitted;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Enforce the ISSF Eligibility, ISSF Commercial Rights and ISSF Sponsorship/ Advertising Rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) Approve the official preliminary and final ranking lists that are produced by the RTS office and confirm/verify the athletes eligibility to participate in the shoot-offs and the finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) Make decisions regarding penalties;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) Implement sanctions where appropriate; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: m) Make decisions in any cases that are not provided for in the Rules, or are against the spirit of these rules. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 391

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.3 Chief Range Officer

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.3.1 General The Chief Range Officer is appointed by the Organizing Committee. He should have a wide experience in shotgun shooting and a thorough knowledge of shotguns, clay targets, clay target throwing machines, acoustic release systems, scoreboards and range equipment. He should hold a valid/current ISSF Shotgun Referee or Judges’ licence. He must have a good command of the English language in order to communicate efficiently with all other officials

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.3.2 The Chief Range Officer is responsible for:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Fulfilling all technical and logistic issues regarding preparation and proper conduct of a competition; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Performing all duties listed below in close cooperation with the Technical Delegate, Jury, Organizing Committee, Chief Referee, the RTS Office and other staff members.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.3.3 The duties of the Chief Range Officer are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) To give instruction and to supervise preparation of the shooting ranges according to technical and safety requirements as described in the ISSF Technical Rules, relevant to the Shotgun events;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) To give instructions and supervise preparation of auxiliary facilities such as shotgun and ammunition storage, technical service, means of communication between the shooting ranges, technical personnel etc.;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) To give direction and supervise the preparation of clay targets for training and competition; and to make sure that all targets are of the same manufacture as mentioned in the general information of the competition

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) To provide special (“Flash”) targets filled with coloured powder for the Finals and any shoot-offs in the Finals;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) To ensure that the traps are adjusted according to the settings of the day;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) To ensure that all necessary range systems are functioning properly;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) To ensure that all range equipment is on each range and properly placed (large scoreboard, tables, range clocks, seats and umbrellas for Assistant Referees, facilities for the athletes, scorekeepers etc.);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) To assist the Organizing Committee to prepare official and unofficial training programmes and give advice in the preparation of the competition schedule.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) To make decisions, with the approval of the Jury, regarding change of competition times and range allocations and interruption of the shooting on the ranges, for safety or other reasons; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) Instruct operating staff regarding the traps, release systems etc. with particular regard to safety.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) After the Jury have approved the target settings, the CRO is responsible for the security of the Trap Pits and the Skeet houses, to ensure there is no interference with the machine settings.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.4 Chief Referee

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.4.1 General The Chief Referee must be appointed by the Organizing Committee in conjunction with the ISSF. He must possess an ISSF Shotgun Referee’s 392 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF licence and must have a wide experience in Shotgun shooting and in the organization of ISSF competitions and a thorough knowledge of the ISSF Rules applying to the competition. The chief referee can be local or international but he must be able to speak and understand the English language

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.4.2 The duties of the Chief Referee, in general, are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) To assist the Organizing Committee and the ISSF, in the selection and appointment of the Referees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) To supervise the Referees and the Assistant Referees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) To give instruction and information to the Referees and the Assistant Referees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Supervise the work of the Referees and evaluate their performance.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) To prepare the schedules and assignments for the Referees, inclusive of Shoot-Offs and Finals;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) To make decisions in cooperation with the Jury, such as when and on which ranges an athlete who had to leave his squad to repair a gun malfunction or was declared “ABSENT” may be permitted to complete his round; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) To keep the Chief Range Officer informed of any difficulties, failures, machine breakdowns, delays etc. on the Ranges;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) To ensure that all Referees are present on time at the Ranges to conduct the competition, in the correct attire.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) To monitor that the competition is conducted according to the timings of the competition schedule and take necessary action in case of delays.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) To cooperate with the Technical Delegate and the Jury, in the proper conduct of the Competition and follow their guidelines and directives.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) To prepare a short, briefing report including the referees’ names, licence number and their performances during the competition and to deliver this report to the jury Chairperson.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) To check that the eyesight certificates are current for all referees.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.5 Referees

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.5.1 Referees must be appointed by the Organizing Committee in co-operation with the Chief Referee and the ISSF, and must:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Possess an ISSF Shotgun Referee’s Licence and a current Eyesight Certificate;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Have wide experience in Shotgun shooting; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Have a thorough knowledge of the Shotgun and ISSF Rules applying to the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The referee must have a good command of the English language to be able to communicate with athletes and officials

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.5.2 The main functions of the Referee are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Before the start of any round to ensure that the ranges are safe;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) To check that the correct squad of athletes is present on the range before the start of a round and ensure that the Assistant Referees are ready in their allocated positions; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 393

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) To ensure that the correct procedure is used to declare an athlete “ABSENT” (See: Rule 9.10.2.6 & 7 for “ABSENT” athlete);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) To make immediate decisions regarding “HIT TARGETS” (in all doubtful cases or a disagreement made by the athlete, the Referee must consult with the Assistant Referees before making a final decision);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) To make immediate decisions regarding “LOST TARGETS” (the Referee must give a clear and distinct signal for all targets declared “LOST”);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) To make immediate decisions regarding “NO TARGETS AND IRREGULAR TARGETS” (if possible, the Referee must call “NO TARGET” or give some signal before the athlete fires); Note: Irregular targets require an immediate decision by the Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) To issue Warnings (Yellow Card) or automatic Deductions (Green Card) for technical violations where appropriate, as per Rules (See: section 9.15);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) To ensure that the result of each shot is correctly recorded (on the scorecards and the scoreboards);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) At the end of each round, to sign the official scorecard and ensure that the final results of the round are correctly posted and any initial warning/s on technical violations recorded. Initial warnings on technical or rule violations must also be recorded on an incident report which must be handed over to the RTS office.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) Any disagreements raised by an athlete regarding his final result recorded on a scorecard, must whenever possible be verified, before the scorecard is handed over to the RTS office.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) To ensure that the athletes are not disturbed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) To monitor illegal coaching (non-verbal coaching is allowed according to

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: m) To rule on any protests received from athletes;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: n) To rule on disabled guns;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: o) To rule on malfunctions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: p) To ensure the correct conduct of the round; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: q) To ensure the application of the safety rules

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: r) Complete an Incident Report and inform the RTS on any matter where any Incident occurred that is not already listed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.5.3 Hand Signals to be used by Referees during Competition 394 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.5.4 Additional Hand Signals to be used by Referees during Finals

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.5.5 Warnings Issued by the Referee

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Referee must give Warnings for rule violations (Yellow Card) and must note such warnings on the official range scorecard (See: section 9.15); also, he must inform the RTS jury and the chief referee about any yellow cards given to ensure it is recorded in a range incident report; but

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Referee may not assess penalties or disqualifications that fall under the responsibility of the Jury.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.6 Assistant Referees

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.6.1 The Referee must be assisted by two (2) or three (3) Assistant Referees:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Organizing Committee will provide qualified Assistant Referees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) They must possess a current National Level Referee’s Licence and a current eyesight Certificate.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.6.2 The main duties of an Assistant Referee are:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) To watch each target thrown;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) To carefully observe whether a target is broken before the shot is fired;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) To give, immediately after a shot, a signal to the Referee if he/she observes that in his/her opinion the target(s) is/are “LOST;”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If required, to mark the result of the Referee’s decision regarding each shot on the official scorecard;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) If asked, to advise the Referee on any other matters relating to the targets;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) To be positioned in such a way that they can observe the whole unobstructed shooting area;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) To indicate to the Referee in a Skeet event if the target is not hit within the boundaries; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) In a Skeet event at the time of shooting on station 8, the two Assistant Referees under the directions of the Referee, must leave their original positions and be placed in the middle of the layout (in line of station 4 and 8), behind the EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 395 Referee, to be able, if necessary, to advise him, whether the target is hit or not within the boundaries.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) To advise the Jury in case of a protest.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) The Assistant Referees have to use either Red Flags or an Electronic Device that indicates a hit (Green Light) or lost (Red Light) target(s).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) Flags can be used for qualification rounds and shoot offs before the finals, the electronic device must be used during all finals and shoot offs during finals

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) When the electronic device is used, it must indicate the doubles by 2 green lamps or 2 red lamps.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.5.6.3 Advising the Referee The Referee must always make the final decision. If any Assistant Referee is in disagreement, it is his duty to advise the Referee by lifting an arm or otherwise attracting his attention. The Referee must then arrive at a final decision.

chunks.text: 9.6.2 Training

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.6.2.1 Pre-Event Training

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Must be provided for each event on the day(s) before the start of the official competition on the same ranges and the same make and colour of targets as those that will be used in the official competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Jury must check that the targets are set correctly for all Pre-Event trainings;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) All training times must be allocated fairly between those athletes present so that no advantage is given; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) For Skeet, two extra Doubles shall be provided (one reverse Double on Station 3 and one reverse Double on station 5).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The PET programme must be revised and approved by the TD before the start.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.6.2.2 Unofficial Training All range availability for unofficial training is the responsibility of the Organizing Committee, and must: EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 397

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Ensure that the unofficial training must not interfere, in any way, with any scheduled competition events;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Be allocated fairly between those nations present so that no advantage is given; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Ensure that all team leaders present are informed of any unofficial training schedules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The organising committee must use the same make and colour of the targets that will be used during the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The unofficial training programme must be revised and approved by the TD or the Chairperson of juries before the start.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The organizing committee with the approval of the ISSF TD may add one extra unofficial training day for the second event in the competition before their PET Day
