chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.10.2.6 Absent Athlete If an athlete is not present on the range when his name is checked with the scorecard, the Referee must have the athlete’s Bib Number and name called out loudly three (3) times within one (1) minute. If the athlete does not appear by the end of that minute the Referee must declare him “ABSENT” and he must not be allowed to join the squad and shooting must start without him.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.10.2.7 Makeup Round of Absent Athlete

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) An athlete who is declared “ABSENT” must present himself to the Chief Referee before the squad has finished for that round and request permission to shoot the missed round. Failure to do so may result in disqualification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete will then be permitted to shoot the missed round at a time and on the range decided by the Chief Referee with a deduction of three (3) points to be applied against the last three (3) targets hit in the make-up round. The athlete should, if possible, shoot a make-up round on the same range as the one he had to leave.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.10.2.8 Exceptional Circumstances If an athlete arrives late for a competition or fails to present himself to the Chief Referee before the squad has finished that round and it can be proved that the lateness was due to circumstances beyond his control, the jury must, whenever possible, give him the opportunity to take part, without disruption of the overall shooting programme. In this case the Chief Referee will determine when and where he will shoot and no penalty will be imposed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.10.2.9 In case of an unexpected medical issue with an athlete, which prevents him from continuing his shooting, regardless of the number of targets he shot or the number of rounds and after the request of his coach or team leader, the Chairperson of jury may take the decision for the athlete to stop shooting to have his health condition checked, then allow him a make-up round on the same day or the next day of the event where he/she is participating. If possible, to shoot the make-up round on the same range and start from the same station where the athlete was forced to stop. The Chairperson of jury before taking his decision may consult the medical services present at the range regarding the athlete’s health condition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11 MALFUNCTIONS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.1 Malfunction Definition Failure of a properly loaded shotgun to fire when the trigger is pulled 414 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF (mechanical failure or misfire), or a defective cartridge that does not deliver its full load when the primer was struck, or when a single pull of the trigger or the involuntary operation of both triggers on a double trigger gun produces a simultaneous discharge, must be recorded as a malfunction.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.1.1 Number of Malfunctions Permitted The athlete is permitted a maximum of two (2) malfunctions per round, whether or not he has changed his shotgun or ammunition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) All regular target(s) on which any additional malfunction of shotgun or ammunition occurs in the same round will be declared “LOST” whether or not the athlete attempted to fire; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If after a malfunction, the Referee agrees with the athlete that the shotgun is in need of repair, then action may be taken in accordance with the Rules for Disabled Shotguns (see Rule 9.11.4.1).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) For malfunctions during Finals in individual events see Rule 9.17.6

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) For malfunctions during Mixed Team events see Rule 6.18.4.7.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.2 Barrel Selection Where an athlete is using a double-barrelled shotgun, it will be assumed that the athlete is firing the bottom barrel first (or right-hand barrel, in the case of a side by side), unless the athlete indicates to the Referee before each of his rounds that he intends otherwise. Procedure in the Event of a Malfunction

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.3  Decisions on malfunctions of either shotgun or cartridge must be made by the Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.3.1  In the event of misfire due to any reason, the athlete must:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Keep the shotgun pointed at the target flight area.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Not open the shotgun.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Not touch the safety catch,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Hand the shotgun safely to the Referee for examination if asked.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Answer any questions from the Referee. Note: The athlete is responsible for checking the shotgun after it is returned by the Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.3.2  The following are not considered malfunctions:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Faulty manipulation of the mechanism by the athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Failure to place a cartridge in the correct chamber of the shotgun; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Any fault attributable to the athlete. Ammunition Malfunctions (Misfires)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.3.3  Decisions on ammunition malfunctions must be made by the Referee. The following are considered ammunition malfunctions when the firing pin indentation is clearly noticeable and:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The powder charge is not ignited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Only the primer fires. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 415

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The powder charge is omitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Some components of the load remain in the barrel.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Cartridges of the wrong size must not be considered as defective ammunition. (Placing a 20-gauge or 16-gauge cartridge into a 12-gauge gun is dangerous and may also subject the individual to penalties for unsafe shotgun handling). Actions after Malfunctions are Declared

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.4.1  Disabled Shotguns Decisions on disabled shotguns must be made by the Referee. A shotgun may be considered disabled if:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) It cannot be fired.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete having already suffered two (2) malfunctions of either shotgun or ammunition in a round obtains permission from the Referee to change it.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c)It fails to eject due to mechanical defect.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d)For any other reason that renders the shotgun unusable

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.4.2  If the Referee decides that the disabled shotgun or that the malfunctioning of the shotgun or ammunition is not the fault of the athlete, and that the shotgun is not repairable quickly enough, the athlete may use another shotgun if it can be obtained within three (3) minutes after the shotgun has been declared DISABLED.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.4.3  The athlete may after obtaining the permission of the Referee, leave the squad and finish the remaining targets of the round, in a Make-Up Round, at a time to be determined by the Chief Referee and without any penalties.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.5 Procedures for Completing a Make-Up Round

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.5.1 Trap The athlete having been allocated a time and Range having the correct scheme (preferably the same scheme as in the original interrupted round and the same range as in the original interrupted round), must stand behind the station to be shot and be shown all three (3) targets from that group, after which the Referee must give the command “START.” The athlete must then move on to the station and shoot in the normal manner. After which he must shoot from the remaining stations in order to complete the round. The referee will consider the allowed preparation time, as the athlete will be shooting alone.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.5.2 Skeet The athlete having been allocated a Range and time (preferably the same range as in the original interrupted round), must stand behind the station to be shot and there he will be permitted to view a regular high and low house target, the Referee must then give the command “START.” The athlete must then move on to the station and shoot in the normal manner at the required number of targets. After which he must shoot from the remaining stations in order to complete the round. The referee will consider the allowed preparation time as the athlete will be shooting alone 416 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.11.5.3 Make-Up Round (Score Certification) The Referee must then ensure that the scores from the make-up round and the original interrupted round are correctly totalled, signed by the athlete and the Referee, before the scorecard is taken to the RTS Office.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.12 COMPETITION CLOTHING AND EQUIPMENT See also G.T.R. 6.7 and G.T.R 6.20 (The ISSF Dress Code)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.12.1 Athletes’ Clothing

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Sports trousers, training (athletic warm-up) trousers and jackets, for men and women and similar sports blouses, skirts/dresses for women are allowed. Blue jeans, jeans or similar trousers in non-sporting colours or any clothing that it see-through or transparent are prohibited;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Open toe or open heeled shoes, sandals or any other similar footwear are not allowed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Shooting barefooted or only in socks is not permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Shorts or skirts with the bottom of the leg not more than 15cm above the centre of the kneecap are allowed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Shirts, T-shirts and similar garments with sleeves less than 10cm in length or without sleeves are not allowed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Clothing made of camouflage material or similar is prohibited.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Any clothing, footwear or accessories which does not give a sports look is prohibited and must be checked by the equipment control jury.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Battery heated clothes: The athletes are allowed to use or wear battery heated clothing with the approval of the equipment control jury.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) During ISSF competitions, all athletes must wear a shooting vest sleeveless or with long sleeves with side pockets to keep the ammunition and to be according to

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: G.T.R. 6.7 and G.T.R 6.20 (The ISSF dress code) EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 417

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.12.2 Bib (Start) Numbers Bib (Start) Numbers must be worn by all athletes:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) On their backs and above the waist;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) At all times while participating in Pre-Event Training and in competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the Bib Number is not worn, the athlete may not start or continue;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) the Bib Number must display the allocated number as large as possible but should not be less than 20mm high.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The Bib number must be securely fixed to the shooting vest preferably from the four corners.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.12.3 National IOC Identity The IOC abbreviation of the nation of the athlete and the athlete’s family name and first initial must be displayed in Latin letters (IOC abbreviation at the top) 418 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF on the back of the shoulder area of the outer shooting garment and above the Bib Number. The national flag should be displayed on the left side of the IOC nation abbreviation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.12.4 Blinders Side blinders (on one or both sides) attached to the hat, cap, shooting glasses or to a headband, not exceeding 60mm in depth are permitted for Shotgun athletes only. The front edge of a side blinder, when viewed from the side, must not extend more than 30mm forward of the centre point of the forehead. Side blinders must be made of plastic material only. A front blinder not exceeding 30mm in width is permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13 RESULTS, TIMING AND SCORING (RTS) PROCEDURES The Jury Member responsible for shotgun results, timing and scoring procedures will be appointed by the ISSF.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.1 RTS Office

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.1.1 It is the duty of the RTS Office BEFORE the competition to:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Prepare score cards for each squad;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Ensure that the correct score card is with the correct squad on the correct range.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.1.2 It is the duty of the RTS Office AFTER each round to:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Receive and check the totals of the targets hit and verify results;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Record scores;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Post preliminary scores on the range bulletin board immediately;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If any result is outstanding because of a protest, such scores must be omitted for the time being and the remaining scores posted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Observe any Incident Reports and any official warnings (Yellow Cards) recorded on the scorecards by the Referees during the competition rounds and prepare the necessary notifications to the Referees for possible deductions in repeated violations, in the remaining rounds of the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.1.3 It is the duty of the RTS Office at the CONCLUSION of each shooting day to:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Total the official scores within the shortest possible time;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Prepare accurate Preliminary Results for distribution to the press, team officials, Jury and Technical Delegate(s);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Prepare and publish accurate Final Results immediately; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 419

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Publish correct Final Results, in cooperation with the results provider, containing the full family name, full first name (without abbreviations), Bib Numbers and IOC abbreviations of each athlete’s nation as soon as possible after the close of any applicable protest period;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The Organizing Committee must retain the range scorecards, which show the results of every target shot at, until the conclusion of the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) At the end of the competition, the RTS jury must prepare a full result book for the competition and to be signed and approved by the TD and the Jury Chairperson.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) The result book must be sent to the ISSF TD within a period of maximum 7 working days after the end of the last day of the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.2 Scoring Procedures Scoring is done officially on each range for each round of 25 targets in Trap and Skeet events:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) In all ISSF Competitions, individual scores must be kept on each range by two (2) separate persons, these are usually Assistant Referees;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) One person must maintain a permanent official scorecard;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The second person must maintain a manual scoreboard, except that where an electronic scoreboard is used, it must be maintained by the Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.2.1 Scoreboards

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.2.2 Ranges with Electronic Scoreboards; The Referee must control the operation of the electronic scoreboard and ensure that the results are correctly registered.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.2.3 Two (2) persons must be appointed as Assistant Referees as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The first person must be positioned at the side of the firing line to function as an Assistant Referee and maintain a permanent official scorecard;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The second person must be positioned at the other side of the firing line to function as an Assistant Referee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) A third person may be appointed to maintain the official scorecard and, in this case, the other two persons will function only as Assistant Referees.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.2.4 Visible Scoreboard Errors If at any stage the visible scoreboard should display an incorrect score, the Referee must immediately stop the shooting and with minimum delay take whatever action is required to correct it. If for any reason, it is not possible to correct the display, the following action will be taken:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The official scoreboard must be examined and verified up to the point where the electronic scoreboard failed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Then, if possible, to substitute quickly a manual scoreboard, enter the scores upon it up to the point of failure and continue the round;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If it is not possible to substitute a manual scoreboard, an additional scorecard must be introduced, the verified scores entered upon it and the round must then continue with the second scorecard under the control of a qualified person appointed by the Chief Referee; and 420 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If there is a difference in the recorded scores between the two (2) scorecards, that which is under the control of the official appointed by the Chief Referee, must prevail.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.3 Ranges with Manual Scoreboards Not permitted to be used during ISSF competitions unless there is a breakdown of the electronic scoreboard, The manual scoreboard can be used as a backup. Three (3) persons must be appointed as Assistant Referees, as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The first person must be positioned on the left or right side of the range to act as an Assistant Referee and also maintain the manual scoreboard;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The second person must be positioned on the opposite side and act as an Assistant Referee.;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The third person must be positioned at the rear of the firing line to maintain a permanent official scorecard and also to check that the scores shown on the manual scoreboard are registered correctly;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Each scorer must mark the card or board independently but based only on the decision given by the Referee;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) At the conclusion of each round the results must be compared and the correct scores entered upon the official scorecard before it is delivered to the RTS Office;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The scores shown on the manual scoreboard must prevail if there are unresolved differences.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.3.1 Score Certification When a round is completed and the individual results have been compared, read aloud and agreed by each athlete, the Referee and each athlete must sign or initial the scorecard, unless the athlete does not agree with the result shown for him and it is his intention to make a protest.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.4 Results and Rankings

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.4.1 Individual Events For each athlete the results of each round must be recorded legibly on official scorecards and the total of the Qualification rounds, and any Shoot-offs must be recorded and the scores ranked in descending order.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.4.2 Countback Rule Any ties to be broken by this method must be decided as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The scores of the last round of 25 targets must be compared. The winner is the athlete with the highest score in that round;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) In a case where the tie is still not broken, the round before last must be compared and if still not broken, the round before that and so on;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the results of all the rounds are still equal, ties must be decided by counting backward, target by target, from the last target of the last round (and if necessary, the next to last round etc.) until a tie-breaking zero (0) is found. If the tied athletes have zeroes (0) on the same target, the countback shall continue until the tie is broken. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 421

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.5 Team Events (Team and Mixed Team)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Scores of each team member must be recorded and the number of all targets hit by the team members of each team in each of the Qualification Rounds must be totalled and the team’s scores ranked in descending order (Ties – see Rule 9.13.4.2).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A team, of which a member has been disqualified, must not be ranked and must be shown in the result list with the remark “DSQ.”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.13.5.1 Team Ties (Applying to both Team and Mixed Team) If two (2) or more teams have the same scores, rankings must be decided by the combined score of the team members in the last round, then by the next to last round, etc. until the tie is broken. If the tie is not broken (i.e. all the combined scores of the team members are the same, in all rounds) then ties must be decided by counting backward, from the combined score of the team members of the last target of the last round (and if necessary, the next to last target of the next to last round etc.). The team with the lower combined score of the last target will be given the lower ranking. Example: TEAM 1 Athlete 1 XXXXXXXXXXXXX00XXXXXXXXXX 23 Athlete 2 XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX0 24 Athlete 3 XXXXXXXXXX0XXXXXXXX0XXX0X 22 Total score 69 Ranking place: 2nd TEAM 2 Athlete 1 XXXXXXXXXXXXX0XXXXXX0XXXX 23 Athlete 2 XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX0XX 24 Athlete 3 XXXXXXX0XXXXXXXXXXXXX0X0X 22 Total score 69 Ranking place: 1st

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14 TIES AND TIE-BREAKS Competitions with Finals

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.1  Ties in events with Finals will be decided according to the following Rules:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.1.1 Ties Before Finals a) After any Individual Qualification stage of 125 targets the eight (8) highest ranking athletes will qualify for the Final. For Mixed Teams, the 4 highest ranking teams will qualify for the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any ties for places 1 to 8 will be decided by a Shoot-off. For Mixed Teams, any ties for places 1 to 4 will be decided by a Shoot-off.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The 8 qualified athletes in the Final will receive new Final Start numbers 1-8 as per qualification ranking and compete in the Final. (Athlete ranked in First place has Finals Start Number 1). For Mixed Teams, the 4 qualified teams in the Final will receive new Final Start numbers 11-12, 21- 22, 31- 32, 41- 42 as per qualification ranking and compete in 422 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF the Final. (Mixed Team ranked in First place has Finals Start Number 1).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Individual tied scores ranking 9th place and below, must be ranked according to the Countback rule. In case of an absolute tie, when quota places are to be decided. in this special circumstance, then a Shoot-off will take place. Otherwise, the tied athletes will share the same ranking, with their names listed in alphabetical order according to their family names.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Mixed Teams tied scores ranking 5th place and below must be ranked according to the Countback rule.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.2 Shoot-Off Procedures

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.2.1 General

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the shoot-off time is not announced in advance, the athletes involved must remain in communication with the competition office whether personally or through their Coach/Team Official in order to be ready to fire when the shoot- off is called;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any athlete or a team member who is not in his assigned position and ready to shoot at the official starting time will be declared “ABSENT,” must not be allowed to participate in the shoot-off and will automatically be given the lower place in the shoot-off results using his qualification score.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The starting positions in the shoot-off will be decided by the interim Qualification ranking (lowest ranking athlete/team to shoot first). In case of a tie with perfect scores or a tie with the same scores that cannot be broken by the count back rule, the shooting order in the shoot-off shall be determined by drawing lots.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) In case of more than one shoot-off, the lower position shoot-off(s) must be shot first; (shoot-off for rank 8 will be before shoot-off for rank 1).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) If the shoot-off result of the athletes/teams qualifying for the Final is the same, those athletes/teams must continue to shoot-off until the tie is broken, in order to establish their ranking;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Any remaining athletes with the same shoot-off result who do not gain a place in the Final (places 9 and below) must have their rankings determined according to the Countback rule; unless a Quota place is to be decided. Any remaining teams with the same shoot-off result who do not gain a place in the Final (places 5 and below) must have their rankings determined according to the Countback rule.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Whenever possible, shoot-offs to break ties before a Final should take place on a range other than the range that will be used for the Final;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Shoot-offs before Finals must be conducted on standard targets, except when flash targets of the same type as those used in the Qualification rounds may be used.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Shoot-offs before Finals, whenever possible, should start within a maximum of thirty (30) minutes after the last qualification round is completed. Preparation Time Limits in Shoot-offs Before Finals

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.text: 9.14.2.3 Trap Shoot-off Procedures before Final

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Before the Shoot-Off starts a left and a right target will be thrown from each of the five (5) stations. All tied athletes must then line up behind Station 1 in the order decided by their interim Qualification ranking (lowest ranking athlete to shoot first). Starting on Station 1 they must shoot at regular targets (left or right) until the tie(s) are broken according to the following sequence: Station 1 left target, Station 2 right target, Station 3 left target, Station 4 right target, Station 5 left target, then Station 1 again this time shooting at a right target and so on;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The first athlete must on command move onto the station, load and call for the target as shown in a) above;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Only one (1) shot is permitted at each target; the gun must be loaded with one (1) cartridge only; the second barrel must not be loaded with any empty, dummy or loaded cartridge. For a first violation the athlete will receive a Warning (Yellow Card). For any second or subsequent violation the target will be declared “LOST;”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) After shooting, the athlete must move to the rear of the athlete(s) who have yet to shoot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Each athlete in the tie must in turn do likewise;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) If after all athlete(s) have shot on Station 1 and a tie remains, all athletes in the tie must move to Station 2 and repeat the procedure;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) This system of shooting station by station must continue as long as a tie remains.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) If an athlete inadvertently shoots out of turn, the result of the shot must be recorded and the athlete given an official Warning (Yellow Card). Any repetition must result in the target shot at being declared “LOST.”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.2.4 Skeet Shoot-Off Procedures Before Final

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Before the shoot-off starts, the first athlete must stand immediately behind Station 4 and be permitted to see one (1) regular double;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) All tied athletes will then shoot in turn on Station 4 in the order decided by their interim Qualification ranking (lowest ranking athlete to shoot first, 9th place is lower than 4th place);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) After the Referee declares “START,” the first athlete must move on to the station, load and shoot at a regular double (high/low). He must then leave the station and go to the rear of the athletes who have yet to shoot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) All athletes in the tie must in turn do likewise;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The athlete(s) who miss the highest number of targets after each double will be eliminated;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) All those who are still tied must remain and the first athlete must then move on to the station, (station 4), load and shoot at a reverse double (low/high). He must then leave the station and go to the rear of the athletes who have yet to shoot; 424 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) All athletes still in the tie must in turn do likewise;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) If any ties remain unbroken, this procedure of shooting at a regular double and a reverse double must continue until all results are determined, this taking place on station 4.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) If an athlete inadvertently shoots out of turn, the result of the shots must be recorded and the athlete given an official Warning (Yellow Card). Any repetition must result in the targets shot at being declared “LOST.”

chunks.text: 9.14.3 Competitions Without Finals

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.3.1 Individual Ties Ties in competitions where there are no Finals will be decided as follows;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.3.2 Ties with Perfect Scores These will not be broken, but will share first place with the names listed in order according to the Latin alphabet (family names). The next rankings must be appropriately numbered.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.3.3 Ties for the First Three (3) Places These must be decided by a shoot-off in accordance with Rule 9.14.2.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Starting positions will be decided by the interim Qualification ranking (lowest ranking athlete to shoot first);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) When several athletes are tied for more than one (1) ranking place, e.g., two tied for first place (places 1 and 2) and two athletes tied for third place (places 3 and 4), they will all shoot-off on the same range to determine the individual ranking; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The tie for the lowest ranking position will be shot first, followed by the next higher-ranking positions until all ties are broken. All tied athletes will be ranked according to the score from the shoot-off series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.3.4 Ties for 4th Place and Below Individual tied scores ranking in 4th place and below, not decided by a shoot- off, must be ranked according to the Countback rule.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15 RULE VIOLATIONS The Jury, the Chief Referee and the Referee will decide on rule violations based on three (3) classes of infringements or violations of the Rules:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) “OPEN” – unconcealed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) “TECHNICAL” – rule infringements of a technical nature; 426 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) “CONCEALED” – deliberate or very serious breaches of the rules or of safety.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.1 The Jury is responsible for examining and deciding the degree of penalties to be imposed for all reported violations, that are not automatically imposed according to these rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.1.1 When rule violation cards are shown, they must be accompanied by the command “Warning” (Yellow Card), “Deduction” (Green Card) or “Disqualification” (Red Card) as appropriate, in a manner that leaves no doubts in the offender’s mind as to the meaning of the action taken. It is not necessary to show a warning card prior to the issuance of any deduction or disqualification card.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.2 Warning (Yellow Card)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.2.1 Open Violations In the case of initial open violations of the rules, such as:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Dress Code violation;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Unnecessary interruption of the shooting;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Receiving illegal coaching during the competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Unauthorized intrusion into the competition area;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Unsportsmanlike conduct;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Deliberate attempt to evade the spirit of the rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Inadvertently shooting out of turn.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Dry firing in unauthorized areas.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Any other incident that requires a warning to be issued.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.2.2 A Warning (Yellow Card) by a Jury Member, Chief Referee or Referee, will first be given so that the athlete, Coach or Team Official may have the opportunity to correct the fault.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.2.3 If an athlete does not correct the indicated fault within the stipulated time, penalties will be imposed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.2.4 In repeated infringements by a Coach, or other Team Official, the Jury will require the offender to leave the vicinity of the shooting range for the remainder of the round and the athlete may be penalized.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.3 Technical Violations In the case of initial technical violations during a competition round such as:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Foot fault;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Exceeding the time limit allowed to call for the target;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) In Skeet, the athlete’s READY position is not according to the rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) In Skeet, on station 4 the athlete opens the gun between the two (2) single shots (this does not apply on station 8);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Following or pointing with the gun at a slow or fast pull target without shooting; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 427

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) A Warning (Yellow Card) will be shown to any offending athlete by a Referee. This must be indicated on the relevant scorecard before it is sent to the RTS office with the use of the below abbreviations while at the same time the Referee must submit also a completed Incident Report form. FF = Foot Fault TL = Time Limit SKRP = Skeet Ready Position OG = Opening the gun between 2 singles FPG = Following or Pointing the Gun at a slow or fast target

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) For each second or subsequent technical violation, of the same kind in any stage of the Competition (except Final) of any of the technical violations listed above, the athlete must be penalized by the deduction of one (1) point (from the first hit target in the double in Skeet), (Green Card) by the Referee (See also: Trap Rule 9.8.4.6; Skeet Rule 9.9.5.6). This must be indicated on the scorecard by the Referee before the card is sent to the RTS Office. Also, a completed Incident Report form must be submitted to the RTS office. Referee Procedure: The Referee must command “STOP,” (before the athlete shoots) inform the athlete of the penalty and display the Green Card, adjust the scoreboard and instruct the next athlete to continue.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) The Jury in charge of RTS is responsible in providing, during all stages of the competition (Qualification and Final) the necessary information to the Referees for any recorded initial cases of Yellow Cards (first time violation), in order that they will be able to impose, if necessary, any deductions (Green Card) for any second or subsequent technical violations as stated above.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.3.1 A Warning (Yellow Card) must also be given if an athlete uses ammunition that is not in accordance with Rule 9.4.3.1.b) to h) (see also Rule 9.4.3.2.e)).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.4 Deduction (Green Card) for Other Offences

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.4.1 Deduction of one (1) point for other offences imposed by at least two (2) Jury Members must be applied to the result of the last round, or the round before the last etc. (last ‘HIT’ target) of a penalized athlete, in the following cases:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Impeding another athlete in an unsportsmanlike manner;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If when asked to give an explanation for an incident, an athlete consciously and knowingly gives false information (in serious cases this might be the cause of disqualification - see Rule 9.15.5.4.h);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Interfering with range equipment after an initial violation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Each second or subsequent occurrence, in case an athlete uses ammunition that is not in accordance with Rule 9.4.3.1.b) to h), unless otherwise stated in the Rules, as in Rule 9.4.1. where the deduction for the use of coloured wads is five (5) points.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) A two (2) point penalty will be deducted from the score of the first hits in the Final if the athlete does not report on time;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.4.2 Leaving the Range without Permission Deduction of all remaining points in the round must be given by decision of the majority of the Jury in cases when an athlete leaves the range without completing the round and without the permission of the Referee. 428 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.5 Disqualification (Red Card)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.5.1 Disqualification (Red Card) may be required in accordance with Rules

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.4.1.1.c) and 9.4.3.2.d) for violations involving shotguns, Skeet marker tapes or ammunition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.5.2 Disqualification according to Rule 9.15.5.4 (below) may only be given by a decision of the majority of the Jury. The disqualification of an athlete is expressed by the Jury by showing a Red Card with the word “Disqualification.”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.5.3 If an athlete is disqualified during any phase of an event (Qualification or Final), the results for that athlete for all phases of that event must be deleted and the athlete must be listed at the end of the results list as a (DSQ) with an explanation in the legend regarding why the athlete was disqualified.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.15.5.4 Disqualification (Red Card) of an athlete, or the banning of a Team Official or Coach from the shooting ranges may be given for:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Serious breaches of safety and violations of the safety rules;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Handling a shotgun in a dangerous manner (repeated accidental discharges may be a cause for consideration);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Handling of a loaded shotgun after a “STOP” command has been given;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Repetition of incidents that have already been the subject of a warning (Yellow Card) or deduction (Green Card);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Deliberate abuse of any team, range or technical official;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Deliberate failure to shoot a previously missed round;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Consciously and knowingly giving false information in a deliberate attempt to conceal the facts in serious cases; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Cases where violations are deliberately concealed. (All of the above require an Incident Report to RTS)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16 PROTESTS AND APPEALS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.1 Disagreement with a Referee Decision during a Round

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.1.1 Action by Athlete

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If an athlete disagrees with a Referee’s decision regarding a particular target he must act immediately before the next athlete fires, raising an arm and saying “PROTEST;”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Referee must then temporarily interrupt the shooting and after hearing the opinions of the Assistant Referees, make his decision. No protest will be accepted after the next athlete fires.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.1.2 Action by Team Official

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If a team official is not satisfied with the final decision of the Referee, except for “HIT,” “LOST,” “NO TARGET” or “IRREGULAR” targets, he must not delay the shooting, but must attract the attention of the Referee who will make a notation on the scorecard that the athlete is continuing under protest; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The protest must be resolved by the Jury.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If any team official protests in an un-sportsmen like manner (example: EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 429 shouting or moving from his seat), the jury member in charge may give him a yellow card for the first incident, for the second incident a red card and then he must leave the range immediately and not be substituted by any other coach or team official.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.2 Verbal Protests Any athlete or team official has the right to protest regarding a condition of the competition, or a decision or action by a competition official immediately and verbally to a Jury Member, the Chief Range Officer, the Chief Referee or a Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.2.1 Such protests may be made on the following matters:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) That the ISSF Rules were not followed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) That the current published competition programme was not followed;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Disagreement with a decision or action of any competition official;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) That an athlete was impeded or disturbed by another athlete, a competition official, spectators, the media or other persons or causes. Note: Only the athlete concerned may question a decision by the Referee on a “HIT,” “LOST,” “NO TARGET” or “IRREGULAR” target by taking action as in Rule 9.16.1.1 a).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.2.2  Competition officials who receive verbal protests must consider them immediately, take immediate action to correct the situation or refer the matter to the Jury for a decision. Shooting may be temporarily stopped if absolutely necessary.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.3 Written Protests

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Any athlete or team official who does not agree with the action or decision taken on a verbal protest may submit a formal protest in writing to the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b). A written protest (Protest Form P) may be submitted without first making a verbal protest.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) When a written protest is received by a jury member, the majority of the jury must meet immediately to discuss the protest and make the decision as soon as possible.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.3.1 Protest Time Limit Any written protest (Protest Form P) must be submitted to a member of the Jury within twenty (20) minutes after the end of the round in which the alleged incident occurred. The protest must be accompanied by a 50,00 EUR fee. If the protest is denied, the fee must be given to the Organizing Committee; if the protest is upheld the fee must be returned.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.3.2 Jury Decision After the jury reach their decision, the written protest form, completed by the Jury Chairperson, is to be notified to the athlete or the team official. If the athlete or the team official disagree with the jury’s decision, then they may appeal.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.16.4 Appeals In the event of a disagreement with a Jury decision the matter may be submitted to the Jury of Appeal, except those decisions by a Finals Protest Jury may not be appealed (see Rule 6.16.6). 430 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.14.4.1 Appeal Time Limit Such appeals must be submitted in writing not later than thirty (30) minutes after the Jury decision has been officially announced. The appeal must be accompanied by a 100,00 EUR fee. If the appeal is denied, the fee must be given to the Organizing Committee; if the appeal is upheld the fee must be returned. Including the initial protest fee of €50 EUR.

chunks.text: 9.17 FINALS IN OLYMPIC SHOTGUN EVENTS Finals may be conducted either on a separate range designated as a Finals Range and not used for Qualification competition or on one of the ranges used for Qualification competition.

chunks.text: 9.17.1 FINALS IN INDIVIDUAL SHOTGUN EVENTS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.1.1 TRAP and SKEET

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.1.2 General The Trap and Skeet individual events consist of two stages: Qualification and Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.1.3 Qualification The Qualification stage will be conducted according to the Competition Procedures specified in the current Shotgun rules (Trap, section 9.8 and Skeet, section 9.9).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.2 FINALS FORMAT PROCEDURES APPLYING TO TRAP & SKEET INDIVIDUAL EVENTS Finals Format:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The full programme (General Regulations, 3.3.5) must be fired in each Olympic event as a Qualification for the Finals. The EIGHT (8) highest-ranking athletes in the Qualification advance to the Finals;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Finals consist of finalists firing at a series of target sequences, with progressive eliminations beginning after all finalists have fired at the required number of targets (10 targets for Trap or 12 targets for Skeet) and continuing until the gold and silver medals are decided

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Finalists start at zero; scores from the Qualification are not carried forward.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.3 General Finals Requirements

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.3.1 Reporting Time:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Athletes in the Final must report to the Finals Range not later than 30 minutes before the Final Start Time;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A two (2) point penalty will be deducted from the score of the first hits in the Final if the athlete does not report on time;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Athletes must report with their equipment, competition clothing and a national team uniform that may be worn in the Medal Ceremony. The Jury must confirm that all finalists are present and that their names and nations are correctly recorded in the results system and on the scoreboards. Juries must complete cartridge and equipment controls as soon as possible after the athletes report; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Any finalist who does not report for the start of the Finals Procedures, 15 minutes before the start time will not start and will be ranked last in the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.3.2 Start Time. The Start Time for the Finals is when the Referee command “READY” is given for the first competition shot. 432 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.3.3 Start Positions and Finals Start Numbers. New Finals Start numbers (1-

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 8) must be issued for the Finals. Starting positions in Finals are assigned according to the Qualification ranking, with the highest-ranking athlete having Start number 1. Any ties for places 1 to 8 will be decided by a Shoot-off. In shoot-offs to decide medals, athletes must shoot in Start number order (lowest number shoots first, 8th is lower than 1st).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.3.4 Test Firing and Showing Targets. Before the start of the final, the finalists must be permitted to test fire then targets must be shown.

chunks.text: 9.17.3.5 Finals Facilities & Special Equipment (see ISSF Guidelines for Organizers for detailed requirements).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Finals Range must have a large spectator stand and a designated reporting area where cartridge controls can be done, where finalists can report.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Finals Ranges must be equipped with the following equipment: A speaker system for use by the Announcer/Commentator and the sound/ music technician.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Seating for Jury members, the Coaches/Team Officials and the Finalists.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) An electronic, colour scoreboard (see ISSF Guidelines for Organizers for detailed requirements).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) An electronic timing system (to control preparation time limits).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Seating and table for the score keeper.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) A big clock positioned in a place where it can be observed by athletes and officials.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) If possible, A Walkie-talkie or similar for communication between the Referees/Jury/Technical Officials.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Eight sealable boxes for cartridge control.

chunks.text: 9.17.3.6 Finals Officials. The following personnel shall conduct and supervise the Final:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Referee: An experienced official with an ISSF Shotgun Referee’s licence, appointed by the Chief Referee, in consultation with the Jury, must conduct the Final. Whenever possible the appointed Referee must originate from a nation which does not have any athlete(s) in the Final;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Assistant Referees & Timing System Referee: Two Referees must be appointed as Assistant Referees to assist and advise the Referee in charge. An additional Referee must be appointed to manage the electronic timing device. A further additional Referee must be appointed to keep a manual scoreboard. All Referees shall be selected by the Chief Referee from the appointed Competition Referees. It is the responsibility of the Chief Referee to ensure that the appointed Referee, Assistant Referees and Timing System Referee are present at the Finals Range on time to conduct the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Jury-Member-in-Charge: One (1) Jury member must be designated, by the Jury Chairperson, as the Jury- Member-in-Charge of the Final. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 433

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Competition Jury: The Competition Jury must supervise the conduct of the Final. One (1) Jury member must be designated as the Jury-Member-in-Charge, of the Final;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Finals Protest Jury, Composed of three (3) The Jury Member-in-Charge and two (2) other members of the Competition Jury, as designated by the Jury Chairperson (can be also the Jury Chairperson), who must decide any protests that may be made during the Final. Their decision is final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Technical Officer: The Official Results Provider appoints the Technical Officer to prepare and operate the technical scoring system and the graphic display of results. In case of technical problems that may influence the Final, he will contact the Jury- Member-in-Charge and the Referee directly so appropriate decisions may be taken quickly;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Announcer/Commentator: An Announcer/Commentator designated by the ISSF or the Organizing Committee must be responsible for introducing finalists, announcing scores and providing information to spectators.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Sound Technician: A technical official responsible for operating the sound and music system during competitions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) RTS JURY: An RTS Jury must be present at the Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) VAR Jury (In case VAR is used) The VAR System Operator, responsible for functioning and controlling the VAR system, will be designated to operate the monitor as needed during matches. This individual will oversee the system’s operation and ensure its proper use in accordance with rule 9.17.8 and VAR Manual.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.3.7. Finals Production and Music

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The conduct of a Final must use music, announcements, commentary, staging and commands in a total sports presentation that portrays the athletes and their competitive performances in the most appealing and exciting ways for spectator and television audiences.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Technical Delegate in consultation with the Jury should approve the music programme. Enthusiastic audience support is encouraged and is recommended during the Finals.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.4  Competition Procedures. Finals competitions are conducted according to these procedures. The Technical Rules for each event also apply to the Finals except where differences are described in this Rule (Rule 9.17).

chunks.text: 9.17.4.3 Tie-Breaking (Shoot-off) Procedures. Ties for places three through eight will be broken according to the Start number order (Qualification ranking). If there is a tie for Gold and Silver medal places, the shoot-off will begin immediately and there will be no showing of targets or test firing. The shoot-off will be conducted according to these procedures:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Trap. The athletes must line up behind station 1 in reverse start number order, with the lowest ranking first. No.8 is lower than No.1. Starting on Station 1, they must each shoot at regular targets until the tie is broken according to the following sequence: Station 1 left target, Station 2 right target, station 3 left target, Station 4 right target, Station 5 left target, then Station 1 again this time shooting at a right target and so on. Only one (1) shot is permitted at each target. After shooting, the athlete must move to the rear of the athlete who has yet to shoot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Skeet. The athletes must line up behind station 4 in reverse start number order, with the lowest ranking first. No.8 is lower than No.1. The athletes must shoot one regular Double; if the tie is not broken with the first Double, they must shoot one reverse Double on that station; if the tie is not broken, they continue on Station 4 to shoot one regular Double, and if the tie is not broken one reverse Double; this sequence continues, again on Station 4, until the tie is broken. 436 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Trap Mixed Teams. The athletes must line up behind station 1 in reverse start number order, with the lowest ranking MT first. No.4 is lower than No.1. Starting on Station 1, they must each shoot at regular target (The man always shoots before the Woman) until the tie is broken according to the following sequence: Station 1 left target, Station 2 right target, station 3 left target, Station 4 right target, Station 5 left target, then Station 1 again this time shooting at a right target and so on. Only one (1) shot is permitted at each target. After shooting, the athlete must move to the rear of the athlete who has yet to shoot. The score of the team is combined.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Skeet Mixed Teams. The athletes must line up behind station 4 in reverse start number order, with the lowest ranking MT first. No.4 is lower than No.1. They must shoot at a regular double (man shoots first) followed by the second member of the team (woman) who will also shoot at a regular double. The athletes of the other mixed team must than do likewise and each member of the team shoot at a normal double. The mixed team with the lowest number of hits out of 4 shots will be eliminated and will be ranked the lower place, If the tie is not broken, the same procedure will continue on the same station in the same order but with reverse doubles, If the tie is still not broken, the same procedure will continue on the same station in the same order but with regular doubles, and so on until the tie is broken. The score of the team is combined.

The Jury will select cartridges for cartridge control and conduct equipment inspections. Cartridge checks must be completed before the presentation. Athletes may leave the FOP without any of their equipment, including their shooting vests, but must return within15:00 min. before the start of the Final, otherwise they may not start and will be ranked last in the final. chunks.text: d) Introduction of The Announcer will introduce, in Start number order (with 4:00 minutes Finalists number one on the right, as they face the audience), the before finalists by giving the name, nation and brief information about each finalist. chunks.text: 9.17.6 Malfunctions during the Final

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the Referee decides that a disabled shotgun, or the malfunctioning of the shotgun or ammunition, is not the fault of the athlete, the athlete must be given not more than three (3) minutes in which to repair the shotgun or obtain another approved shotgun, or replace his ammunition. If this cannot be done within three (3) minutes, the athlete must withdraw.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) After the malfunction is corrected or the athlete withdraws, the Final must continue. A withdrawn athlete’s final ranking will be determined by the total number of targets hit when the malfunction occurred.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) An athlete is allowed a maximum of two (2) malfunctions during a Final, including any shoot-offs, whether or not he has tried to correct the malfunction.

chunks.text: 9.17.7 Protests during the Final

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If an athlete disagrees with a Referee’s decision regarding “HIT,” “LOST,” “NO TARGET” or “IRREGULAR” target(s), he/she must act immediately 438 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF before the next athlete fires, by raising an arm and saying “PROTEST.”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Referee must then temporarily interrupt the shooting and after hearing the opinions of the Assistant Referees, make his decision. No protest will be accepted after the next athlete fires.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Any other protest by the athlete or coach will be decided by the Finals Protest Jury immediately. The decision of the Finals Protest Jury is final and cannot be appealed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If a protest in a Final for any matter other than Referee decisions on “HIT,” “LOST,” “NO TARGET” or “IRREGULAR” targets is lost, a penalty of two (2) points must apply to the last two (2) “HIT” targets.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) No protest fee applies in Finals.

chunks.text: 9.17.8 VAR (VIDEO ASSISTANT REFEREE) Leading up to LA 2028, it is mandatory that VAR must be installed for use in ISSF World Championships and all World Cups where Olympic Quota places are allocated. It is encouraged that it is also made available for Continental Championships and other major competitions, especially where Olympic Quota places are available.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.1 When an athlete disagrees with a Referee’s decision regarding a “LOST TARGET/S” or a “NO TARGET/S”, before the next athlete fires, he/she must act immediately by raising an arm, saying “VAR” and requesting the use of VAR to resolve the protest.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.2 Likewise, a coach (who is assigned a seat in the FOP), can initiate a VAR protest before the next athlete fires, by drawing the attention of the Jury in Charge and showing the “VAR” card, which will be given to all coaches inside the FOP before the start of the final. The Jury in Charge must then attract the attention of the Referee and initiate a VAR protest

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.3 After a VAR protest has been initiated, the Referee must immediately command “STOP” and temporarily interrupt the shooting. The referee must ensure that the athletes empty their Shotguns, face the spectator’s area, and form a rectangle outline, indicating a video screen, to show that the protest must be verified using VAR.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.4 The Referee and the Jury in charge will proceed to the VAR Station, where the display screen is located, to review the recorded video. The VAR must be reviewed by both the Jury member and the Referee in charge. They will jointly examine the slow-motion footage to resolve the protest, with the assistance of the VAR System specialist (either a Technician or a Special Jury member) if available. The final decision, after reviewing the video in slow motion, rests with the Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.5 An athlete or a coach may submit a VAR protest only for himself or on behalf of his own Athletes, not for any other participant in the final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.6 The Referee must then announce openly the decision saying „HIT‟ or „LOST‟ or „NO TARGET„ facing the spectator’s area and make the outline of a rectangle and using and using also the appropriate hand signal for (“HIT” or “LOST” or “REPEAT”).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.7 In case the first “VAR” protest is accepted (meaning that the decision of the Referee has been changed, then the second “VAR” protest can be requested EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 439 without any additional conditions. A MAXIMUM OF TWO VAR REQUESTS ARE ALLOWED FOR EACH ATHLETE.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.8 In case the first “VAR” protest is denied (meaning that the decision of the Referee has not been changed the Athlete, Coach, or Team official cannot ask for any other VAR protest, the VAR card will not be given back to the coach/ team official.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.8.9 The use of VAR can also be requested by the Referee individually, in cases where he/she has doubts whether a target was “HIT,” or “LOST”, or “NO TARGET” for unlimited times.
