chunks.text: 9.17.9 The decision on a VAR protest is final and cannot be appealed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.9.1 The rules apply to each Athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.9.2 Finals referees and conducting officials are to note the following additional and supporting rules and clarification, in addition to those stipulated and quoted above for VAR in Section 9 ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.9.3 The referee in the case of a Skeet VAR request, must ascertain from the athlete and coach which target is being challenged, High or Low House of the double, or both targets if judged by the referee as a double MISS/LOSS.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.9.4 For all VAR referrals challenging a LOST/MISS target, the referee decision must be clear and unequivocal, as either HIT or MISS. Unless there is clear evidence that a MISSED target has in fact been HIT, then the original on-field decision of the referee stands. There must be demonstratable VAR footage showing a HIT target, to overturn the original on-field decision of a MISSED/ LOST target(s). If any doubt still remains after a VAR review, as to whether a target has been hit or not, then the original on-field decision of MISS/LOST must be upheld. There is to be no REPEAT target.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.17.9.5 In the case of VAR Skeet challenges, the referee must announce the VAR adjudication outcome and confirm which target(s) are HIT or MISS/LOST, from the original on-field decision. The Referee is to ensure that the official score keeper and scoreboard reflect the correct VAR decision and score before proceeding with the final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18 SHOTGUN TRAP AND SKEET MIXED TEAM EVENTS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.1 GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Mixed Teams consist of two team members, one male and one female from the same nation. Both Mixed Team members must wear the same competition clothing with national colours and identification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) In one Championship, nations may enter a maximum of two (2) Mixed Teams in one Mixed Team event, as per ISSF General Regulations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Mixed Team members may be changed for other athletes already registered in the Championship not later than 12:00 hours, two days before the day of the Mixed Team competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The Mixed Team event consists of two parts: Qualification and Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.2 QUALIFICATION

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Qualification will be conducted according to the Competition Procedures and Rulings as specified in the current ISSF Shotgun rules for Trap (section

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.8) and for Skeet (section 9.9) unless otherwise specified in these rules. 440 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Team squadding will be done by a random draw. The two members of each Mixed Team must be squadded to fire next to each other in the same squad, with the male firing first and the female second. Teams from the same nation shall not be in the same squad. Athletes will wear the same Bib numbers as those worn in the individual competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Each member of the Mixed Team will shoot 75 targets, in 3 rounds of 25 targets each – (3 rounds X 25 targets = 75 targets X 2 athletes = Total 150 targets for each team).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) After the end of the Qualification, the ranking of the Mixed Teams will be decided by the combined results of the 2 members of each Mixed Team (1 male & 1 female) 75 X 2 = 150 (as per ISSF Shotgun Rules 9.13.5.1).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The four (4) highest-ranking Mixed Teams after qualification will qualify for the Final

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Any ties for places 1 to 4 will be decided by by shoot off.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) After the Qualification stage, new Finals Start numbers (11-12, 21- 22, 31- 32, 41- 42) will be distributed to the top 4 qualified Mixed Teams.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) The ranking of tied Mixed Teams in 5th place or below not decided by a shoot-off will be established on the basis of the ISSF Shotgun Rules 9.13.5.1 &

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.3 PROCEDURE IN CASE OF A TIE In the event of a tie for the Final, or Finals Start numbers, the shoot off rule will be applied. (9.17.4.3.c) and (9.17.4.3.d)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.4 FINAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.4.1 Competition Format of Mixed Team Trap in Final. After the end of the Qualification Rounds, the top 4 teams will qualify for the Final. The final is only (1) stage, consisting of 8 Athletes (4 Teams). Finalists shoot one shot only at each target. Finalists occupy stations 1-2-3-4-5-6+7+8 (Station” 7” 1m behind station “6” and station” 8” 1m behind station “7”) in Final Start Number order. Each athlete is given a Finals Start Number, based on their Mixed Team ranking coming into the Final. Mixed Team ranked in first place from Qualification has Finals Start Number 1, through to Mixed Team ranked in fourth place coming into the Final will have Start Number 4. (see rule 9.18.2.g). The man is always shooting first followed by the woman. After each athlete has shot at a station, he must move to the next station to fire in sequence on that station. A timing system to control the 12-second preparation time limit must be used. The man will always start, followed by the women. Athletes’ presentation; 8 Athletes – 4 Teams – No presentation for coaches –

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: The man will be presented first followed by the woman then the jury member in charge, finally the referee(s) Each Final consists of a series of target sequences followed by progressive EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 441 eliminations that continue until the gold and silver medals are decided, as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) After the 8 finalists (4 Teams) complete a round of 10 (ten) targets per athlete, (4 Right, 4 Left, 2 Centre) (20 targets per team). The 4th team is eliminated, Team Ranked 4th. - The 6 remaining finalists (3 Teams) will be repositioned to fill the 6 stations according to their Finals Start numbers.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) After the 6-remaining finalist (3 Teams) shoot at another 5 (five) targets per athlete (2 Right, 2 Left, 1 Centre), (and complete 30 targets per team), the 3rd team is eliminated (Bronze Medal winning team). - In case there’s a tie up to and including this stage, the highest Finals Start number wins. Finals Start Number 1 is the highest Start Number, Start Number 4 is the lowest Start Number.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) After the 4 remaining finalists (2 Teams) shoot at another 5 (five) targets per athlete (2 Right, 2 Left, 1 Centre), and complete 20 targets per athlete, (40 per team), the gold and silver medals are decided. - In case of a tie between 1st and 2nd place teams, there is an immediate shoot-off. (9.17.4.3.a) Both team members must participate in the shoot off. The team with the lowest Final Start number will shoot first. (Start number 4 is lower than Start number 1). Both team members will shoot (The man shoots first followed by the woman) to obtain a combined score for the team of 2 targets in each station. - Test firing followed by the target showing will be done and finished before the start of the presentation. Total targets: 40 Targets per team Mixed Trap Targets Distribution.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.4.2 Competition Format of Mixed Team Skeet in Final. After the end of the Qualification Rounds, the top 4 teams will qualify for the Final. The final is only (1) stage, consisting of 8 Athletes (4 Teams). Finalists will shoot from stations 3, 4 and 5 in Finals Start number order. A new Finals Start number will be distributed to the finalists according to their qualifications ranking (11-12, 21- 22, 31- 32, 41- 42). Mixed Team ranked in first place from Qualification has Finals Start Number 1, through to Mixed Team ranked in fourth place coming into the Final will have Start Number 4. (see rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.2.g). 442 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF Athletes’ presentation 8 Athletes - 4 Teams – No presentation for coaches - The man will be presented first followed by the woman, then the jury member in charge, finally the referee(s). Finalists shoot one shot only at each target. The man is always shooting first followed by the woman. After each athlete has shot at a station he must move to the next station to fire in sequence on that station. A timing system to control the 30-second preparation time limit must be used. Each Final consists of a series of target sequences followed by progressive eliminations that continue until the gold and silver medals are decided, as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) After the 8 finalists (4 Teams) complete a round of 12 targets each athlete, (24 targets per team), (one regular double and one reverse double on station 3, one regular double and one reverse double on station 4, one regular double and one reverse double on station 5) The 4th team is eliminated, ranked in 4th place. The 6 remaining finalists (3 Teams) will continue according to their Finals Start numbers.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) After the 6-remaining finalist (3 Teams) complete another round of 12 targets each athlete, (24 targets per team), (one regular double and one reverse double on station 3, one regular double and one reverse double on station 4, one regular double and one reverse double on station 5,) and complete 24 targets/Athlete (48 Targets/Team) the 3rd team is eliminated in 3rd place (Bronze Medal winning team). In case there’s a tie up to and including this stage, the highest Finals Start number wins. Finals Start Number 1 is the highest Start Number, Start Number 4 is the lowest Start Number.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) After the 4 remaining finalists (2 Teams) shoot at another 4 targets per athlete, (one regular double and one reverse double on station 4), and complete 28 targets per athlete, (56 targets per team), the gold and silver medals are decided In case of a tie between 1st and 2nd place teams, there is an immediate shoot- off (9.17.4.3.b) Both team members must participate in the shoot off. Both team members will shoot (The man fires first followed by the woman) to obtain a combined score for the team. Test firing followed by the target showing will be done and finished before the start of the presentation. Total targets: 56 Targets per team.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.5 MIXED TEAM TRAP AND SKEET PROCEDURES.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.5.1 Coaching Timeout In the Final, while shooting is in progress, Coaches/Team Officials, without disturbing the athletes, may request from the Jury Member in Charge, one (1) Coaching Timeout for a maximum duration of thirty (30) seconds. The Jury Member in Charge will then, at the turn of that team’s athlete(s) to fire, without disturbing the shooting procedure decide when to stop shooting and allow EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 443 the Coach/Team Official to approach and speak to the his/her athletes, on the shooting station. The other Coach/Team Official may, during this time, also approach and speak to his/her athletes without losing the opportunity for a timeout. The Jury Member in Charge must control the time.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.5.2 Reporting Times and Cartridge Control

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The members of the four (4) qualified Mixed Teams in the Final or their representatives (Coaches or Team Officials) must report to the Finals Range (at the designated area) for cartridge control at least 30 minutes before the scheduled Start Time of the Final. At this time the Jury will distribute the Finals Start numbers to all the athletes of the four (4) qualified Mixed Teams.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Equipment Control Jury will instruct the members of each Mixed Team or their representatives (Coaches or Team Officials) to place all of their cartridges in numbered boxes (corresponding to the Start numbers of their Team). The Equipment Control Jury will select cartridges to be checked and seal the boxes in the presence of the Team members or Coach/Team Official and conduct equipment inspections. Cartridge checks must be completed before the presentations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The members of the Qualified Mixed Teams must present themselves to the Finals Range, 15 minutes, before the start of the Final (Stage 1), for preliminaries and presentation

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) No additional cartridges may be brought to the FOP.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) A two (2) hit penalty will be deducted from the score of the first series of the first athlete, if any of the Mixed Team’s cartridges are not presented 30 minutes before the start of the Final or if either of the Team members does not report 15 minutes before the start of the Final. Any team that does not report at the time of the Presentations will not be allowed to take part in the Final and will be awarded 4th place.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.5.3 Test Fire – Target Observation – Presentation.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) After reporting at the range, the athletes of the Qualified Mixed Teams will be allowed to take their cartridges from the boxes. Then, all four (4) Qualified Mixed Teams will be asked to go to the shooting stations for test firing, followed by target observations.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) After test firing and target observationsthe athletes in the Final will assemble in a designated area to the side of the range, to await being called for presentation. The teams will line up in Start number order. The Qualified Teams in Final will enter the field of play (male athlete first – female athlete second) and the announcer will introduce them to the spectators. The Teams must remain facing the spectators until all have been presented, including the Jury Member in Charge and the appointed Referee.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Jury member in Charge must make sure, that the Teams are assembled in the correct order.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The Final will be conducted in the order specified in rule 9.17

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) At the end of the Final the Gold, Silver and Bronze Medallists are assembled by the Jury Member in Charge, on the field of play for official photographs and announcement, (Rule 6.17.1.14 q).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.5.4 Music and Audience Support During the Final, music must be played. The TD in consultation with the jury 444 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF member in charge should approve the music selected. Enthusiastic audience support is encouraged and is recommended during the matches.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.5.5 Malfunctions During Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the Referee decides that a disabled shotgun, or the malfunctioning of the shotgun or ammunition, is not the fault of the athlete, the athlete must be given not more than three (3) minutes in which to repair the shotgun or obtain another approved shotgun, or replace his ammunition. If this cannot be done within three (3) minutes, the athlete (Mixed Team) must withdraw. After the malfunction is corrected, the Final must continue.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If a withdrawal of a team occurs during the Final the remaining Mixed Teams will continue, unless only one team remaining, then they must be declared as the winner.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) A Mixed Team is allowed a maximum of two (2) malfunctions during a Final, including any shoot-offs, whether or not there was an attempt to correct the malfunction.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Any regular target(s) on which any further malfunction occurs will be declared “LOST” whether or not the athlete attempted to fire.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.5.6 Protest During Final.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If an athlete disagrees with a Referee’s decision regarding “HIT,” “LOST,” “NO TARGET” or “IRREGULAR” target(s), the athlete must act immediately, before the next athlete fires, by raising an arm and saying “PROTEST.”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Referee must then temporarily interrupt the shooting and after hearing the opinions of the Assistant Referees, make his decision. No protest will be accepted after the next athlete fires.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Any other protest by the athlete or coach will be decided by the Finals Protest Jury immediately. The decision of the Finals Protest Jury is final and cannot be appealed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If a protest in a Final for any matter other than Referee decisions on “HIT,” “LOST,” “NO TARGET” or “IRREGULAR” targets is lost, a penalty of two (2) points must apply to the last two (2) “HIT” targets, of the athlete (Mixed Team).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 9.18.5.7 Colour of Targets Qualification: Normal targets Final: Flash targets

chunks.text: 9.18.5.8 Irregular or Disputed Cases

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The General Technical Rules will apply to matters not mentioned in the above paragraphs.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Irregular or disputed matters will be decided by the Jury according to the General Technical Rules or other relevant Rule for each even

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.1 GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.1.1  These Rules are part of the ISSF Technical Rules and apply to all 10m and 50m Moving Target events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.1.2  All athletes, team leaders and officials must be familiar with the ISSF Rules and ensure that these Rules are enforced. It is the responsibility of each athlete to comply with the Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.1.3  When a Rule refers to right-handed athletes, the reverse of that Rule refers to left-handed athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.1.4  Unless a Rule applies specifically to a men’s or women’s event, it must apply uniformly to both men’s and women’s events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.2 SAFETY SAFETY IS OF PARAMOUNT IMPORTANCE ISSF Safety Rules are found in Rule 6.2.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.3 RANGE AND TARGET STANDARDS Target and target standards are found in Rule 6.3. Requirements for ranges and other facilities are found in Rule 6.4.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4 STANDARDS FOR 10m AND 50m RIFLES See MOVING TARGET RIFLE SPECIFICATION TABLE (10.14) Any rifle that meets the following standards may be used:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.1 The weight of the rifle and sight together must not exceed 5.5kg.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.2  An adjustable butt-plate is permitted. The curvature of the butt plate (positive or negative) must not exceed a depth or height of 20mm. The butt plate length must not exceed 150mm. Measurement of the depth or height of the butt- plate will be made at right-angles to the Centre-line of the bore of the rifle (see Table). The lowest point of the butt-plate, in its lowest position must not be lower than 200mm below the Centre-line of the bore of the rifle (see Table).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3 Sights The height of the Centre line of the telescope above the Centre line of the bore must not be more than 75mm. 50m Rifles. Any types of sights are permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.1  10m Rifles. Any type of sights are permitted except that optical sights must

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.2  be non-variable with a maximum of four power (4X) magnification (tolerance = +0.4 x). Examination of magnification power will be done with mechanical or optical devices.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.3  Except when a sight is damaged, through mechanical or optical failure, it may not be exchanged between slow and fast part, before the medal matches, or between the two series of a mixed competition. Sight adjustments during the event are permitted, provided they do not delay the shooting. Barrel Weights. Only barrel weights within a radius of 60mm from the Centre

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.4  of the barrel are permitted. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 461 One Rifle Per Event. The same rifle, including the sight, weights and trigger

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.5  system, must be used for slow and fast, or first and second part in any event.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.3.6 Specific Standards for 50m Rifles

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The trigger pull weight must be not less than 500 grams;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The weight of the trigger pull must be measured with the barrel held vertically;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The length of the system measured from the rear of the closed bolt in the discharged position to the foremost end of the system, including any extension (whether part of the barrel or not), must not exceed 1000mm; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Only calibre 5.6mm (.22”) Long Rifle ammunition is permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.4 Specific Standards for 10m Rifles

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The trigger pull weight is unlimited;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) A set trigger must not be used;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The length of the system measured from the rear of the mechanism to the forward end of the system, including any extension (whether part of the barrel or not), must not exceed 1000mm; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Pellets of any shape, made of lead or other soft material, with a calibre of

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 4.5mm (.177”) are permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.5 Pre- and Post-Competition Equipment Checks

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.5.1  Athletes are responsible for ensuring that all items of equipment used by them comply with these Rules. The Equipment Control Section must be open to inspect athletes’ equipment from the Official Training Day until the last day of Moving Target competition. Athletes are encouraged, if they wish, to bring their equipment for an Equipment Control check before the competitions to be sure they comply with these Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.4.5.2  Random post-competition checks will be made of all equipment items to ensure compliance (6.7.9).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.5 CLOTHING REGULATIONS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.5.1 Marker Tape

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.5.1.1  The ISSF Official Marker Tape must be worn to allow the Range Officer or Jury Member to see the position of the rifle stock.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Marker Tape must be as available from the ISSF;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Marker Tape must be 250mm long, 30mm wide, yellow in colour and bearing the ISSF logo; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) It must be permanently affixed on the right side of the outer garment. 462 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.5.1.2 The correct position of the Marker Tape must be checked as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Any pockets of the outer garment must be empty;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The trigger arm, touching the body, must then be bent into the fully closed upward angled position with no upward lift of the shoulders;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Marker Tape must be permanently affixed, horizontally, below the tip of the elbow (see drawing); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The Marker Tape may be checked by Equipment Control prior to the competition and marked with a seal or stamp (see drawing).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.6 COMPETITION OFFICIALS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.6.1 Duties and Functions of the Chief Range Officer A Chief Range Officer must be appointed for each event on a specific range. The Chief Range Officer is:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) In charge of all Range Officers and range personnel and is responsible for the correct conduct of the shooting event and, where centralized control is exercised, responsible for giving all range commands;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Responsible for ensuring the co-operation of all range personnel with the Jury; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 463

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Responsible for resolving any irregularities which other Range Officers cannot resolve;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Responsible for the rapid correction of any equipment failures and for making available the necessary experts and material to operate the range. A repair service expert must be at the Chief Range Officer’s immediate disposal at all times. For cases that exceed the capabilities of the repair service, additional provisions must be made;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Responsible for the efficient and rapid scoring of all targets in co-operation with the Chief RTS (Results, Timing and Scoring) Officer; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) If necessary, the Chief Range Officer participates in the drawing of lots for the assignment of firing points.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.6.2 Duties and Functions of the Assistant Chief Range Officer If the competition is being shot on several ranges, an Assistant Chief Range Officer should be appointed. He also substitutes for the Chief Range Officer during his absence.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.6.3 Duties and Functions of the Range Officer Range Officers are responsible to the Chief Range Officer for the orderly operation of a particular range. They work closely with the Jury. The Range Officer:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Calls the athletes and announces the preliminary result of the series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Checks the names and bib numbers of athletes to ensure that they correspond with the start list, Range Register and small scoreboards. If possible, this must be completed before the start of the Preparation Time;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Gives the necessary competition commands;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Continually watches the READY and shooting positions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Is responsible for the coordinated work of the Register Keeper (when using paper targets) and other range officials;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Supervises the correct operation of the targets;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Receives protests and passes them on to a Jury Member; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Records all disturbances, disciplinary actions, malfunctions, additional sighting shots, repeats, etc. on the Register Keeper’s score card.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.6.4 Duties and Functions of the Register Keeper – Paper Targets

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Examines the entries on the range assignment list and score cards to ensure that the names of the athletes, bib numbers, range numbers and nations agree;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Writes down the indicated score and compares this with the TV monitor when it is in use; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Make entries on score cards in such a way that the RTS Office can identify if the target moves to right or left.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.6.5 Duties and Functions of the Line Officer

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The Line Officer must be located so he can observe the readiness of the athlete and is able to hear the athlete’s “READY” command;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) He must be able to observe the score keeping system after each shot, 464 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF see the result of scoring, and at the same time observe the signal to start the target;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) He operates the starting button, the stop button, and the switch to change from slow to fast; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If no electronic programme switch is provided for the mixed event, the necessary switching must be executed under a plan approved by the Jury.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.6.6 Duties and Functions of the Pit Officer – Paper Targets A Pit Officer and an assistant must be stationed at each side of all ranges used during the competition. Depending on the system used, target changing can be done with one pit officer and an assistant if adequate safety baffles are available. The pit officer or his assistant is responsible for changing the target during the standard rhythm time. The pit officer is responsible for:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Ensuring that the correct targets are attached to the frame in the specified sequence;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Correct positioning of the targets or repair Centres, correctly applying patches to cover bullet holes, establishing the rhythm of score indicating, etc.;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Examining the target after each shot and ensuring that every shot is correctly signalled for both value and location;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) Ensuring that the target is facing in the correct direction before each shot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Giving bullet holes close to a scoring ring the lower value when indicating the score;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Removing targets from the frame at the conclusion of each stage and place them in a secure container to await transfer to the RTS Office;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) Target couriers must transmit targets and report sheets to the RTS Office at least after every second athlete finishes firing;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) Covering sighting shots on 50 m targets with black patches;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) Each series begins with four 4 sighting shots. In 50 m disciplines, if the athlete does not shoot the sighting shots, black patches must be stuck on the corresponding targets outside the rings; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) Competition shot holes on 50m targets must be covered with transparent patches. Only the outer part of shot holes which are close to a scoring ring should be covered to assist the RTS Office in scoring. The last hit on each target must remain uncovered.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.6.7 Specific Rules For 10m Events Depending on the system used, target changing can be done with one Pit Range Officer and an assistant if adequate safety baffles are available. The Pit Range Officer or his assistant is responsible for changing the target during the standard rhythm time.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.6.8 Technical Officers – Electronic Scoring Targets (EST) Technical Officers may be appointed by the Official Results Provider to operate and maintain EST systems. They may offer advice to Range Officers and Jury Members, but must not make any decisions regarding the application of these rules. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 465

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7 SHOOTING EVENT PROCEDURES AND COMPETITION RULES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.1 Positions

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.1.1  Until the moment that any part of the target becomes visible in the opening, the athlete must remain in the READY position, holding the rifle with both hands in such a way that the lower tip (toe) of the butt-plate is equal to or below the mark on the shooting jacket. The mark must be visible to a Jury Member or Range Officer while the athlete is in the READY position. The Shooting Position is standing without support. The rifle butt-plate must

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.1.2  be held against the shoulder (upper right chest) and supported only with both hands. The left arm (right arm for left-handed athlete) must not rest on the hip or the chest. The athlete must take a position in relation to the bench, table, or wall in such a way that it is clearly visible that they do not give him any support whatsoever. The use of a sling is not permitted. The perfomance is the time when the target is visible in the opening. The

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.1.3  timing of it must start when the leading edge of the target appears and stop when the leading edge of the target reaches the opposite wall. Target can move either “fast” or “slow”

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.2 10m and 50m Events – Programmes

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.2.1 10m and 50m 30 + 30 shots (Men, Women, Men Junior, and Women Junior):

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) 4 sighting shots and 30 shots slow, each in 5.0 seconds (+0.2 seconds); and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) 4 sighting shots and 30 shots fast, each in 2.5 seconds (+0.1 seconds). 10m and 50m 40 shots Mixed (Men, Women, Men Junior, and Women

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The event will be fired in two (2) series. Consisting of four (4) sighting shots (two (2) slow and two (2) fast from each side) and 20 mixed; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Each mixed serie must have 10 slow and 10 fast from each side, arranged in such a way that the athlete must fire an equal number of each speed from each side. They must be mixed in such a manner that it is unlikely the athlete can anticipate whether the next is slow or fast. There must not be more than five (5) continuous (combined right and left) ones at the same speed.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.2.3  All events can be conducted in either one (1) or two (2) days, depending on the number of entries in the competition. If an event is conducted in two (2) days, one (1) complete series must be conducted each day.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.2.4  Categories (Men/Women or Men Junior/Women Junior) can be combined as open category, if there are not enough competitors to reach the minimum requirement for a Championship.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3 Competition Rules

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.1 a) Every athlete must shoot the entire competition on the assigned range.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any change in range assignments may be made only if the Jury decides that there are different range conditions such as light conditions;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the event is conducted in one (1) day, the order of shooting for the second stage must remain the same as the order of shooting for the first stage; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If the event is conducted over two (2) days the athlete in the lowest ranking position at the end of the first day shoots first on the second day, and the 466 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF athlete in the highest-ranking position at the end of the first day shoots last on the second day.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.2  Before the start of the competition, the first athlete must be given the opportunity to dry fire a full series in the event being shot. If the first athlete does not wish to dry fire a full series, it is still necessary to run a full series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.3  At ISSF Championships, the Organizing Committee must open the day’s competition by having a test athlete (someone not in the competition) shoot a full series commencing at the official start time, so that the first athlete may complete the dry firing series under competition conditions.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.4  Only the next athlete in succession may dry fire, at a specially marked point on the firing line (see Rule 6.4.15).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.5  The competition series always starts from the right to left. Only one shot may be fired each time the target moves through the area of fire.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.6 Indication of Shots

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Different methods for indicating the score and location of hits may be used. The method used must allow the athlete to be certain of the score and location of the shot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Television or similar monitoring devices that indicate scores and hit locations are permitted for any competition and are compulsory in ISSF Championships;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The athlete is not required to use the television monitor. If he does not use it, he must accept the alternative method of indicating scores and hit locations; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If an athlete observes a discrepancy between the monitor and the alternative method of indicating scores and hit locations, he may request the signal to be repeated, but he is not entitled to another shot even if the first signal was in error. If a repeat signal is requested, this must be before shooting again.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.3.7 Preparation Time After the athlete is called to the shooting station, he must be given a preparation time of two (2) minutes before the first “READY” is to be given.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4 Firing Procedures

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) When the athlete has finished his preparation on the range, he must call “READY” before each sighting shot and also before the first shot of the series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The Range Officer must start the target immediately. If the target does not appear in four (4) seconds after the order to start is given or after completion of the indication of the score, the Range Officer must stop the shooting and make sure that the range equipment and the athlete are ready, after which he will start the target again;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If the target is started before the athlete has called “READY,” he should refrain from shooting. However, if he shoots, the result must be scored;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If the Range Officer finds that the athlete delays unnecessarily before calling “READY” or taking the READY position, the following action will be taken. In the case of the first occurrence, he will be given a Warning (Yellow Card) for delay of competition. On the second occurrence a two (2) point EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 467 Deduction (Green Card) will be given. Any subsequent violation could result in Disqualification (Red Card) by the Jury;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) After completing the sighting shots, the athlete may pause for up to 60 seconds to adjust his sight. The MATCH series will then be started;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) After each shot, the score and location of each shot hole must be shown for at least 4 seconds. The end of the indication of the score is always the signal to the athlete for the continuation of the series;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: g) It is necessary to set a constant rhythm (time cycle) and system in the time taken to indicate the score, the method to indicate the score and the method to change targets;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: h) In 50m MATCH firing, following the completion, the marking and signalling must be completed and the target available to move in not more than 12 seconds, and the athlete must be ready for the target to be released in not more than 18 seconds;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: i) In 10m MATCH firing, following the completion of a shot, the signalling and target changing must be completed and the target available to move in not more than 18 seconds, and the athlete must be ready for the target to be released in not more than 20 seconds;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: j) The Range Officer and the Jury Members must control carefully the 18 and 20 second timings and immediately penalize an athlete who does not comply with this rule;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: k) When the athlete shoots and the shot is not on the target and he later claims that he was not ready when the target started it will be recorded as a miss and he will not be permitted to re-shoot;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: l) The timing for the 18 second (50m) and 20 second (10m) time limits begins when the target disappears at the end of each time moving. The timing stops when the athlete is in the ready position;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: m) The Jury must verify the correct timing of the targets during the competition; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: n) If the target is started from the wrong side or tail first, it must be cancelled and repeated, even if the athlete has fired.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.1  In case anything should occur that might be dangerous, disturb the athlete, or otherwise interfere with the competition, the Range Officer must stop the shooting with the command “STOP.” Should the athlete fire at the moment of the command, he is entitled to have the shot cancelled if he requests it.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.2  If a series is interrupted for more than 5 minutes or the athlete is moved to another firing point, he may ask for 2 additional sighting shots (4 sighting shots in the mixed event). In such a case the Range Officer must announce “SIGHTING SHOTS” and the score keepers must be informed. These sighting shots must begin from the same side from which the series is to be continued after the interruption. If no sighting shots are requested, the series resumes where it was interrupted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.3  If an athlete should be unable to fire, a miss must be scored, unless the Rules that entitle the athlete to a re-shoot apply.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.4  If the Range Officer neglects to stop the shooting when the respective Rules apply, the athlete may raise his arm and call “STOP” provided he has not caused the situation himself. The Range Officer must stop the shooting 468 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF at once. If the Range Officer finds the action of the athlete justified, he may continue shooting after a check of the situation according to Rules respectively. If the athlete is not justified, the Range Officer must give the command to repeat and the athlete must be penalized by deducting two (2) points from the value of that shot.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.5 Misses

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Every shot prior to the appearance of the competition target must be scored as a miss;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The target will be started without a repeated shot and the miss marked as “Z” on the target, on the score card and on an incident report;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Hits outside the scoring rings must be scored as zero(es) and recorded as “X” on the target;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If the athlete does not shoot, the shot is scored as zero and recorded as “-” on the target;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) Shots not hitting the target are scored as zero(es) and recorded as “Z” on the target; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) Skid shots and ricochets must be scored as zero(es).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.7.4.6 Misses and Penalties in 10m Events:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must not discharge propellant gas from his rifle. For the first such offence, two (2) points will be deducted (Green Card) from the score of the next competition shot. For the second offence, the athlete must be disqualified (Red Card) from further competition;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Any release of the propelling charge, after his first competition target is in place, without a hit on the target will be scored as a miss; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) It is the responsibility of the athlete to ensure his air or gas rifle is fully charged with propellant air or gas prior to commencing the competition. If during the competition he has insufficient propellant air or gas to continue, he will be allowed a maximum of five (5) minutes to renew the supply. He may then continue the series but without any additional sighting shots.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8 MEDAL MATCH RULES A 10m Moving Target Medal Match may be conducted as the second phase

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.1  in the 10m Moving Target Men, Women, Men Junior or Women Junior events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.2  The full 10m Moving Target Men, Women, Men Junior or Women Junior course of fire must be completed as a Qualification for a Medal Match.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.3  The four (4) highest scoring athletes in the Qualification advance to the Medal Match. Their start position in the Medal Match is determined by their rank in the Qualification.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.4  Ties for the second and fourth place in the Qualification will be broken according to shoot-off rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.5  All qualifiers for the Medal Match start at zero (0). No Qualification scores carry forward into the Medal Match.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.6  Medal Match qualifiers must report ready to shoot on the range 10 minutes before the start time. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 469

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.7  In the Medal Match, the first place athlete in the Qualification will compete against the fourth place athlete; the second place athlete in the Qualification will compete against the third place athlete.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.8 An introduction of the athletes must be made.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.9 The Medal Match will be conducted on either two (2) or four (4) ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.10  If there are only two (2) ranges, the first relay will be held with the athletes ranked first and fourth.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.11  If there are four (4) ranges, the athletes ranked first and fourth are on adjacent ranges and second and third are on the other ranges.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.12  The preparation time is one (1) minute followed by two (2) sighting shots, one left and one right (fast). The first sighting shot is on command.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.13 All competition shots are on command in fast (2.5 seconds).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.14  Scoring is in decimals. The athlete with the highest score in each match on each shot receives one point. If there is a tie between a pair, no athlete receives a point.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.15  The athlete who receives six (6) points or more with a difference of two (2) points is the winner of the match.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.16  The losers of the two (2) semi-final matches will compete for bronze medal in the same way as above

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.8.17  The winners of the semi-final matches will compete for gold or silver medals in the same way as above.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.9 INFRINGEMENTS AND DISCIPLINARY RULES

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.9.1  The athlete must not exceed the preparation time of two (2) minutes without justification, or wait longer than 60 seconds after the conclusion of sighting shots to begin competition shots. After 30 additional seconds, the target must be started and the result counted whether the athlete is in the shooting position or not.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.9.2  If an athlete does not report when he is due to start the competition the Range Officer must call his name out loud three (3) times within one (1) minute. If the athlete fails to appear, he must have a new shooting time set by the competition officials and two (2) points must be deducted from his total score. If, however, the Jury is convinced that the reason the athlete was late was beyond his control, no penalty will be enforced. An athlete who violates the Rules concerning the READY or shooting position

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.9.3  must be given a Warning (Yellow Card) after the first violation. On the second occurrence a two (2) point DEDUCTION (Green Card) will be given. Any subsequent violation must result in DISQUALIFICATION (Red Card).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.10 MALFUNCTIONS

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.10.1  If the athlete has a malfunction with his rifle or ammunition in the Qualification round, the rifle must be placed on the bench or table without further touching it. The Range Officer must be called and shown the malfunction. The Range Officer must interrupt the series and start a timer to determine the length of the interruption. Malfunctions in Medal Matches may not be claimed. 470 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.10.2  If the Range Officer determines, after examining the rifle and ammunition, that the malfunction was not caused by the athlete, the shot may be repeated.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.10.3 The athlete must not be considered at fault if:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The rifle is found in a discharged condition, the chamber is found to contain a cartridge of the same type the athlete is using, the cartridge shows a clear impression of the firing pin and the bullet has not left the barrel; or,

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The reason for not shooting was caused by a malfunction of the rifle which is not likely to have been caused by the athlete or could not reasonably have been prevented by him.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.10.4 The athlete must be considered at fault if:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) He or she has not placed the rifle on the bench or table;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) He or she changed something on the rifle before placing it on the table;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The safety catch was not released;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) The breech was not closed all the way;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: e) The rifle was not loaded; or

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: f) The rifle was loaded with the wrong kind of ammunition. If the Range Officer determines that the malfunction was caused by the athlete, a miss must be scored.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.10.5  After the interruption due to a malfunction of the rifle or ammunition, the Range Officer may order the repair of the rifle or a change of ammunition. If the malfunction can be repaired within five (5) minutes, the shooting may be continued. If the repair will take longer than five (5) minutes, the athlete has the right to continue shooting immediately with another rifle or to withdraw to repair his rifle. The Range Officer, with the consent of the Jury, must then decide when the athlete may continue his series, either with the repaired rifle, or with another rifle if a repair is impossible. The series must be continued from the point of interruption.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.10.6  The Range Officer should continue as if the athlete did not withdraw in order to allow the next athlete to complete his dry firing.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.10.7 Faulty Sights

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If the athlete discovers during his or her sighting shots that a faulty sight cannot be corrected by adjustment, the Jury can agree to a change of the sight, if a second sight is available;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) After the change the athlete must receive sighting shots;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The athlete must not receive a repeat or additional sighting shots if the examination by the Range Officer shows that the sight mount was not properly tightened; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) If the sight becomes loose during a competition series because it was not properly tightened, all shots must be scored.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.11 FAILURE OF 10m EST SYSTEMS If there is a failure of ALL targets on a range - also applicable to

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.11.1  conventional ranges:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The actual time must be recorded by the Chief Range Officer and the Jury; EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 471

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) All completed MATCH shots fired by each athlete must be counted and recorded. In the event of a range power supply failure, this may involve waiting until power is restored to enable the number of shots registered by the target, not necessarily on the firing point monitor, to be established; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) After the failure is rectified and the full range is in operation the athletes will be allowed a one (1) minute preparation time to allow them to resume their positions. The time for recommencing is to be announced over the loudspeaker system at least five (5) minutes beforehand. At the end of the preparation time, the athletes will be allowed four (4) sighting shots (2 left ; 2 right). These sighting shots must begin from the same side from which the series is to be continued after the interruption. After the sighting shots a 30 second pause will be allowed. After the sighting shots and pause the series will resume where it was interrupted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.11.2 In the event of the failure of a Single Target If a single target fails to function the athlete will be moved to another target where the same procedure stated in Rule 10.11.1, c will apply. Complaint concerning failure to register or display a shot on the monitor

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.11.3  of an electronic scoring target system.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The athlete must immediately inform the nearest range official of the failure. The range official must make a written note of the time of the complaint. One or more Jury Members must go to the firing position; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The athlete will be directed to fire one more MATCH shot at his target. The athlete must call “READY.” The procedure of a complaint concerning a failure to register or display a shot stated in the Technical Rules (6.10.8) will apply.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.12 TIE-BREAKING

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.12.1 Individual Ties in 50m and 10m Events Ties for athletes with perfect scores will not be broken.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.12.1.1 Ties for places 1 – 3 and below:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) If two (2) or more athletes shoot equal scores, ties for the first three (3) individual places must be decided by a shoot-off to be arranged by the Jury. This shoot-off consists of two (2) sighting shots (one (1) left – one (1) right) and two (2) competition shots (one (1) left – one (1) right) in 2.5 seconds (fast) on command for all competition shots; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) In the event of a further tied score the shoot-off will continue until the tie is broken.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.12.1.2 Rules for Shoot-offs

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The shoot-off must begin as soon as possible after the protest time has expired. If the shoot-off is not held at a prearranged time that was publicly announced, the athletes involved must remain in contact with the Chief Range Officer pending an announcement as to time and place;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Athletes with tied scores will be allocated adjacent firing points by the drawing of lots under the supervision of the Jury. If more athletes have equal scores, the firing sequence will also be determined by the drawing of lots. When several athletes are tied for more than one ranking place, the tie for the lowest ranking position will be broken first, followed by the next ranking higher position until all ties are broken; 472 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If an athlete fails to appear for a shoot-off, he will be ranked last in this shoot-off. If two (2) or more shoot-off athletes fail to appear they will be ranked according to Rule 10.12.1.3 for Individual Ties ranking from 4th place; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) During the shoot-off, malfunctions and other irregularities must be treated according to these Rules, but only one (1) malfunction is allowed during the breaking of the tie and any re-shoot or completion will take place immediately. Ties for 4th place and lower, if not resolved by any Shoot-off, must be

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.12.1.3  decided as follows:

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) 10m Events. Any remaining ties for fourth (4th) place and lower are ranked according to tie-breaking Rule 6.15 (i.e., highest number of inner tens, highest score on the last series, next to the last series, etc.);

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) For 50m Moving Target 30 + 30. Any remaining ties for fourth (4th) place and lower are ranked according to the highest total of the fast part; and if ties remain by comparing the lowest value shot(s) in the total competition for the tied individuals (the athlete with the lowest value shot(s) is declared the loser); if any ties remain, the athletes must have the same ranking; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) For 50m Moving Target Mixed. Any remaining ties for fourth (4th) place and lower are ranked according to the highest total of the second stage; and if ties remain by comparing the lowest value shot(s) in the total competition for the tied individuals (the athlete with the lowest value shot(s) is declared the loser); if any ties remain, the athletes must have the same ranking.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.12.2 Team Ties Team Ties in 10m Events / 50m Events Ties in team events must be decided by totaling the results of all members of a team and applying these Tie-Breaking steps.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The highest total number of inner tens;

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The highest total score on the last series, then the next to the last series etc.; and

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) If any ties remain, total scores will be compared on shot-by-shot basis using inner tens, beginning with the last shot, then the next to the last shot etc.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.1 Disciplines 10m Moving Target Mixed Team

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.2 Type of Event Mixed Team of two (one man and one woman)

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.3 Rules The competition will be organized according to the ISSF Rules and Regulations, if no other way is stated below.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.4 Number of participants in each team A team consist of two (2) athletes from each nation. One man and one woman (juniors or seniors or mixed). A maximum of three (3) teams per Nation is allowed. No mixed nation teams are allowed. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 473

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.5 Number of stages Two stages: - Qualification stage 40 shots of target moving at mixed speed - Medal Match

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.6 Position The two members of the team shoot at the same range. The man stands on the left side and the woman on the right side. Dry firing from the second member is not permitted.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.7 Qualification Stage

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.7.1 Shooting event procedures - Qualification stage

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) The event will be fired in one series of 8 sighting shots (4 sighting shots for each shooter) and 40 competition shots (mixed; 20 for each team member).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) The sighting shots: Both team members alternately; 2 shots each per time, starting with the men (2 men, 2 women, 2 men 2 women).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) The Competition: Both team members alternately; 20 shots for each team member, starting with the men (2 man, 2 women, 2 man, 2 women, …).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: d) No dry- firing allowed for the next team in line preparing for their series.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.7.2 Ranking in qualification The ranking in qualification stage will be the combined results of the two team members. The perfect score in the qualification is 400 points.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.7.3 Tie in qualification stage Rule ISSF 10.8.4 for Medal Match is used. The team decides which athlete shoots the tie breaking shots. The tie will be fired according to the rule

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.8 Medal Match The four highest scoring teams in Qualification advance to the Medal Match.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.8.1 Rules for the Medal Matches The Medal Matches will be conducted as per ISSF Rule 10.8, if no other way stated in the rules here below.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.8.2 Commands for Medal Matches Before the sighting shots the team will have one minute preparation time. Sighting shots: - ‘For the sighting shots load’ - ‘Attention’ - ‘3-2-1 START’ - The next sighting shots are up to the Athletes - STOP, end of sighting shots Competition: - ‘For the first competition shots load’ - ‘Attention’ 474 EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF - ‘3-2-1 START’ - ‘Attention’ - ‘3-2-1 START’ - ‘The point goes to...’ For the next competition shots: - ‘LOAD’ - ‘Attention’ - ‘3-2-1 START’ - ‘Attention’ - ‘3-2-1 START’ - ‘The point goes to...’

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.8.3 Shooting event procedures - Medal Matches and scoring

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: a) Semi-finals The teams compete in the Medal Matches only in fast. The members of the same team shoot at the same range. The Medal Matches will be conducted on two ranges. Four (4) sighting shots (1 going to left for man, 1 going to right for woman, 1 left man and 1 right woman) will be fired. Both Athletes are loading at the same time. A command for every competition shot is given. Scoring is in decimals. The competition starts with 2 shots (1 left men and 1 right women). The team with the highest total score of the 2 shots receives one point. If there is a tie between the teams, no team receives a point. The team who reaches six points or more with the difference of two points is winner of the match.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) Semi-Final Procedure The winner of the semi-finals will compete for the Gold/Silver medal The losers of the semi-finals will compete for the Bronze medal

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: c) Gold/Silver Match and Bronze Match The teams compete in the Medal Matches in fast. The members of the same team shoot at the same range. The Medal Matches will be conducted on two ranges. Four (4) sighting shots (1 going to left for man, 1 right woman, 1 left men and 1 right women) will be fired. Both Athletes are loading at the same time. A command for every competition shot is given. Scoring is in decimals. The competition starts with 2 shots (1 left men and 1 right women). The team with the highest total score of the 2 shots receives one point. If there is a tie between the teams, no team receives a point. EDITION 2025 (Third Print 10/2026) Effective 19 October 2026 © ISSF 475 The team to reach six points or more with the difference of two points is winner of the match.

chunks.text: 10.13.11 National identification, dress-code The Athletes from each nation must display their National identification on their shooting clothing, as follow: The name of the country designated by 3 letters as determined by the IOC on their jacket pocket on the side which is turned to the audience.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 10.13.12 Music & audience support During the Qualification rounds and the Medal Matches, music must be played. The Technical Delegate should approve the music programme. Enthusiastic audience support is encouraged and is recommended during the Medal Matches.

chunks.text: 11.1 GENERAL

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.1.1  These Rules are part of the ISSF Technical Rules and apply to all Target Sprint events. If there is any ambiguity or inconsistency between these Rules and the ISSF Technical Rules these Rules take precedence and shall apply.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.1.2  All athletes, team leaders and officials must be familiar with the ISSF Rules and must ensure that these Rules are enforced. It is the responsibility of each athlete to comply with the Rules.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.1.3  When a Rule refers to a right-handed athlete, the reverse of that rule refers to left-handed athletes.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.1.4  Unless a Rule applies specifically to a man’s or a woman’s event, it must apply uniformly to both men’s and women’s events.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.2 SAFETY

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.2.1 SAFETY IS OF PARAMOUNT IMPORTANCE

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.2.2 Gun Handling Rules

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.2.2.1  To ensure safety, all guns must always be handled with maximum care. Guns must not be removed from the firing line during training or competition except with the permission of a Range Officer (RO).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.2.2.2  Safety flags or muzzle covers constructed of fluorescent orange, red or a similar bright material must always be inserted in all rifles or placed over the muzzle as appropriate, except when their removal is authorized by these Rules. To demonstrate that air rifles are unloaded, safety flags (safety lines) must be long enough to extend through the full length of the barrel of rifles that do not use single magazines. Non-magazine loading rifles must also have their breech open to demonstrate that they are unloaded.

chunks.text: a) Safety flags or muzzle covers must be inserted in all rifles or placed over the muzzle as appropriate in all rifles that are not in gun cases or boxes before athletes are called to the line or when leaving a firing point except when the athlete leaves the firing point during training or during the competition.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: b) If a safety flag or muzzle cover is not used as required by this Rule, a Jury Member must give a WARNING with instructions to insert a safety flag or fit a muzzle cover to the rifle; and

chunks.text: c) If a Jury Member confirms that an athlete refuses to use a safety flag or muzzle cover as required by this rule and after being warned, the athlete must be disqualified (DSQ).

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026

This rule may only be deviated from in the transitional phase between the preparation phase and the start of the race, i.e. when all starters go to the start line and the RO / CRO carries out a final check of the folding targets before the start. chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.2.3.1  The CRO or other appropriate range officials, are responsible for giving the commands “5 Minutes Preparation Time Start “, “5 Minutes Preparation Time Stop”, “Athletes Ready”, “Athletes Set”, “Start” and other necessary commands. The command “Start” may also be by the sounding of a whistle or firing of a starter pistol. Range officers must ensure that all commands are obeyed and that rifles are handled safely.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.2.3.2 Only single shot magazines may be used.

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.2.3.3  A rifle is considered loaded when a pellet touches the chamber or breech, or for single shot magazine rifles when a loaded magazine is inserted in the loading channel of the rifle. When the command or signal to “STOP” is given, shooting must stop

chunks.title: ISSF Rule Book 2026 — Third Print 10/2026
chunks.text: 11.2.3.4  immediately. If the athlete has already loaded their rifle, they must keep their rifle facing safely down range and notify the CRO immediately. Only upon instruction by the CRO may the athlete discharge the loaded pellet, and then, stop shooting immediately. When the command “UNLOAD” is given by the CRO, all competitors must ensure their rifles are unloaded. Preparations for shooting and the shooting itself may only be resumed when the command or signal to ‘START’ is given.
