chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.2 Competition Levels

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.2.1 WSPS categorises Competitions based on their scale, size, and nature to determine the applicable requirements at each Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.2.2 WSPS Recognised Competitions levels are as follows: IPC Games  Paralympic Games WSPS Championships  WSPS World Championships  WSPS Regional Championships WSPS Sanctioned Competitions  WSPS World Cups  Any other WSPS international Competitions determined by WSPS (such as Youth Games, IOSD Games, Asian Para Games, Parapan American Games) WSPS Approved Competitions  International Competitions, also called “Grand Prix”, for the sport of shooting Para sport  National Federation-endorsed Competitions approved by WSPS  Any other Competitions for the sport of shooting Para sport as approved by WSPS

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.2.3 For an overview of the requirements for each level of WSPS Recognised Competition, see the ‘Requirements & Designation of Competitions’ (Appendix 1).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.3 Competition Management

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.3.1 The IPC shall manage the Paralympic Games.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.3.2 WSPS shall have the right to manage and shall have ultimate jurisdiction over all matters related to WSPS Championships and WSPS Sanctioned Competitions (and may delegate or remove such jurisdiction to the Competition Jury or other officials under these Rules and Regulations or as it sees fit) and shall have the power to postpone Events and give directions consistent with rules adopted for conducting any Event. WSPS shall also have the right to oversee all WSPS Approved Competitions.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.3.3 WSPS shall have the right to intercede as necessary in order to resolve any conflicts or issues in a ny WSPS Recognised Competition, including by requiring an LOC to address any aspect of the Competition or issue in relation to the WSPS Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 13

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.3.4 The words ‘World’, ‘Regional’ and ‘World Shooting Para Sport’ may not be used in connection with any shooting Para sport Competition or Event without the prior written consent of WSPS. In addition, the IPC is the owner of all rights of whatever kind or nature in respect of the terms “Paralympics" and "Paralympic", the term “Para” when associated with sport or any IPC activities, the IPC motto, flag and anthem, the Paralympic Symbol (three Agitos design) and any other trademarks, logos and other indicia used or intended to be used in the context of the Paralympic Movement.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.3.5 For further details of competition management requirements for WSPS Recognised Competitions, please refer to Appendix 2.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.3.6 For further details of competition management requirements and related hosting requirements for WSPS Sanctioned and WSPS Approved Competitions, please refer to Appendix 3.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.4 Local Organising Committee (“LOC”)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.4.1 An LOC is the organisation responsible for organising and hosting a Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.4.2 For WSPS Recognised Competitions (excluding Paralympic Games), the LOC must be endorsed by and shall have its structure subject to approval by WSPS.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.4.3 The LOC, in conjunction with WSPS, shall be responsible for the entire management of the Competition, including the arrangement of the Programme of Events, arrangement for the Classification of Athletes, all technical equipment and installation prior to and during Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5 Athlete Eligibility

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.1 Eligibility requirements – Paralympic Games The IPC determines the eligibility requirements for Paralympic Games.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.2 Eligibility requirements – WSPS Championships and W SPS Sanctioned Competitions To meet the eligibility requirements to participate in WSPS Championships and WSPS Sanctioned Competitions an Athlete must:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.2.1 satisfy the requirements of the WSPS Nationality Policy (located on the IPC website www.paralympic.org/ipc-handbook;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.2.2 have a WSPS Licence issued in accordance with the WSPS Athlete Registration and Licensing Regulations by the time of the final entry deadline;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.2.3 be in possession of a valid ID Card and WSPS Licence (to be carried at all times during Competitions);

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 14

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.2.4 be entered by their NPC (or National Federation if such responsibility has been delegated by the NPC) , in either case the NPC being a member in good standing of the IPC;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.2.5 meet the relevant Competition eligibility criteria, as defined in the Competition information package and/or qualification guide;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.2.6 be internationally classified and have been assigned a Sport Class , other than Not Eligible (NE) , in ac cordance with the WSPS Classification Rules and Regulations, or in the case of ‘New’ Athletes, have been determined by WSPS to have an Eligible Impairment in accordance with the WSPS Classification Rules and Regulations; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.2.7 not be disqualified, suspended or otherwise sanctioned.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.5.3 Eligibility requirements – WSPS Approved Competitions In order to compete in W SPS Approved Competitions an Athlete must meet the eligibility requirements determined by the relevant LOC or governing body.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.6 Qualification requirements

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.6.1 In addition to the eligibility requirements listed above, in order to compete in W SPS Recognised Competitions an Athlete must also meet the qualification standards, qualification criteria and any sport entry rules applicable to the relevant Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.7 Gender

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.7.1 Subject to Regulation 2.7.3 below, an Athlete shall be eligible to compete in men’s Competition if he is:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.7.1.1 recognised as male in law; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.7.1.2 eligible to compete under these Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.7.2 Subject to Regulation 2.7.3 below, an Athlete shall be eligible to compete in women’s Competition if she is:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.7.2.1 recognised as female in law; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.7.2.2 eligible to compete under these Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.7.3 WSPS will deal with any cases involving transgender Athletes in accordance with the IOC's transgender guidelines (as amended by the IOC from time to time) and any applicable WSPS regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.7.4 The eligibility of persons recognised as third gender in law will be determined by the WSPS on a case-by-case basis, in accordance with any applicable WSPS regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.8 Anti-Doping

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 15

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.8.1 The IPC Anti-Doping Code (located on the IPC website) applies as set out therein and is binding on all persons involved in the sport of shooting Para sport to the extent set out therein. All persons wishing to participate or have any other involvement in WSPS Recognised Competitions agree to be bound by the IPC Anti- Doping Code as set out therein, as a condition of their involvement.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.8.2 All doping control conducted at all WSPS Recognised Competitions must be conducted in accordance with the anti-doping rules of a signatory to the WADC and International Standards with relevant testing authority and results management authority. WSPS strongly recommends that doping control take place at all WSPS Approved Competitions.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.9 International Classification

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.9.1 International Classification may be conducted in connection with a WSPS Recognised Competition. Classification must always take place in accordance with the WSPS Classification Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.9.2 Prior to the Competition a list and timetable for those Athletes required to be present for Classification will be created by WSPS. Athletes and NPCs will be informed accordingly of their appointment time by WSPS.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.9.3 In accordance with the WSPS Classification Rules and Regulations, all Athletes with Sport Class Status ‘New’, ‘Review’ or ‘Review with a Fixed Review Date’ in the Competition calendar year must attend an Athlete Evaluation Session before competing at any WSPS Recognised Competition, if an Athlete Evaluation Session is available for them at that Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.9.4 Subject to the terms of Regulation s 2.5 and 2.9.3 above, and u nless specified otherwise in the Competition entry requirement s, at any WSPS Recognised Competition:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.9.4.1 Athletes with Sport Class Status ‘New’ may compete but their results will not be recognised, and they will not be eligible to win medals at that Competition. WSPS may retroactively recognise the Athlete ’s results for MQS purposes only, acting in its sole discretion, in the event that a ‘New’ Athlete is subsequently allocated the same Sport Class in which they competed as ‘New’ Athlete; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.9.4.2 Athletes who have Sport Class Status ‘Review’ or ‘Review with a Fixed Review Date’ in the Competition calendar year may compete, win medals and have their results recognised in that Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.10 Technical Meeting

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 16

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.10.1 Unless otherwise specified by WSPS, b efore the start of each WSPS Recognised Competition the LOC, together with the Technical Delegate, must organise a Technical Meeting with representatives of the participating countries and the LOC , supervised by the Technical Delegate.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.10.1.1 The Technical Delegate is responsible for overseeing all technical matters at the Competition in accordance with these Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.10.1.2 Whenever possible, the Technical Delegate will communicate any specific advice or requirements related to technical matters for the Competition at the Technical Meeting.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11 Start Number

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.1 A start number must be assigned to each Athlete and appear on all Competition lists and timetables.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.2 The Athlete start numbers are printed on b ibs, which are produced by W SPS and printed and distributed by the LOC.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.3 SH2 Athletes who are permitted to use a Loader(s) (denoted by ‘(L)’ on the Athlete bib) will also be issued a Loader bib.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.4 VI Assistants will be assigned a VI Assistant bib (denoted by ‘(A)’ on the Athlete bib).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.5 The bib size and design must be as shown in the Athlete Bib Template available on the WSPS website.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.6 The bib must be visible at all times when the Athlete (and/or Loaders/VI Assistant) is on the field of play.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.6.1 Athletes with backrest score A: the bib must be worn on the back of the Athlete.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.6.2 Athletes with backrest score B or C: the bib must be displayed on the back of the S hooting Chair. The bib cannot obscure the view of the f ree sitting height marking tape.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.6.3 Loaders and VI Assistants: must wear the bib on their back. The bib must be properly fixed/pinned so as not to move at the top and bottom to the shirt above the waistline during the entire Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.11.7 In the case that the bib is issued to an Athlete (and/or Loaders/VI Assistants) but not displayed, the Athlete may not commence/continue to shoot in the Event.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.12 Technical Protests and Appeals

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.12.1 Any violation by an Athlete , Team Official, team member or any other individual of these Rules and Regulations (as determined by WSPS) will be resolved in accordance with the procedures set out in these Rules and Regulations and the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 17

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.12.2 All protests and appeals regarding technical matters will be resolved in accordance with the procedures described in the ISSF Rules, following these Rules and Regulations, documentation and forms (available on the WSPS website).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.12.3 All protests and appeals regarding Classification matters will be handled in accordance with the WSPS Classification Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.12.4 The fee for a technical protest or appeal is to be determined in accordance with ISSF Rules, unless otherwise specified by WSPS.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.12.5 If a technical protest or appeal is denied, the protest or appeal fee will be retained by the LOC.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.13 Penalties for Rule Violations

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.13.1 The Competition Jury must decide Rules violations by Athletes at Competitions in accordance with the following procedures:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.13.1.1 In the case of an open violation of the Rules (i.e. where no attempt is made by the Athlete or other member of their team to conceal the violation) , a warning (‘Yellow Card ’) must first be given so the Athlete may have an opportunity to correct the fault. Whenever possible, the warning should be given during training or the p reparation and s ighting time. If the Athlete does not correct the fault as instructed by the Competition Jury, two (2) points must be deducted from their score (‘Green Card’). If the Athlete still does not correct the fault after receiving a d eduction (‘Green Card’), then disqualification (‘Red Card’) (‘DSQ’) must be imposed.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.13.1.2 In the case of a concealed violation of the Rules, (i.e. where an attempt is made by an Athlete or member of their team to conceal the violation) disqualification (‘Red Card’) (‘DSQ’) must be imposed.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.14 Disqualification

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.14.1 In addition to any specific provisions of these Rules and Regulations providing for disqualification, an Athlete, Team Official, team member or any other individual may have their accreditation withdrawn and/or be disqualified from any Event(s) or Competition(s) by WSPS, if, in the reasonable opinion of WSPS, they:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.14.1.1 contravene the spirit of fair -play or obstruct members of any committee, WSPS Officials or the Competition Jury in his/her official duties;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.14.1.2 behave in a manner which may actually or potentially bring into disrepute WSPS, the IPC, any International Federation and/or the LOC; or

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.14.1.3 breach any protocol or procedure put in place by an LOC and/or WSPS for an Event or Competition (for example in relation to the health, safety or security of Athletes, including any protocol put in place in relation to the coronavirus pandemic).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 18

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.15 Disciplinary Action

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.15.1 Further disciplinary action, including in relation to situations that are not covered by these Rules or Regulat ions or ISSF Rules, may be taken against any individual(s) bound by these Rules and Regulations on a case-by-case basis by the WSPS Technical Delegate, in consultation with WSPS. Further action(s) may be taken at WSPS’ discretion.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16 Coaching During Any Event

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.1 Verbal Coaching

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.1.1 Verbal coaching during training and preparation time is permitted, but such coaching must not disturb other Athletes.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.1.2 During training and preparation time coaches are permitted to approach the Firing Line to verbally coach their Athlete (s) (unless prohibited by a member of the Competition Jury).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.1.3 During Competition, coaches are permitted to approach the Firing Line only following a specific request by their Athlete(s) or a VI Assistant and if a member of the Competition Jury permits this request.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.1.4 Subject to 2.16.1.3, while on the Firing Line during Competition, all Athletes may speak only with a member of the Competition Jury or a Range Official (except SH2 Athletes who may speak with their Loader as required).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.1.5 In R7/R8 Finals, verbal coaching is allowed only during changeover times.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.2 Non-Verbal Coaching

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.2.1 In all Events, non -verbal coaching is permitted , including written communication, but such coaching must not disturb other Athletes.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.3 Violation of Coaching Regulation

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.16.3.1 If a Team Official or Athlete violates any provision of this Regulation 2. during any Event, a warning must be issued for a first offence in that Event. For each further violation in that Event, two (2) points must be deducted from the Athlete’s score and the Team Official must leave the vicinity of the Firing Line.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.17 Results

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.17.1 Unless specified otherwise in these Rules and Regulations, scoring procedures for all WSPS Recognised Competitions must be followed as described in the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18 Rankings

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 19

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.1 WSPS shall maintain world and regional rankings to determine the best performing Athletes per Event per season, based on a points system, by considering both the rank and the result achieved by the Athletes.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.2 Rankings shall be calculated on a rolling basis. The rolling ranking will include all WSPS Recognised Competitions from one year ago to the day. (Example: on 15 April 2025, rankings will include all results achieved in WSPS Recognised Competitions from 15 April 2024 - 15 April 2025).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.3 Only Athletes who have a WSPS Licence and have a Sport Class Status ‘Confirmed’, ‘Review’ or ‘Review with a Fixed Review Date’ can have their results recognised for ranking purposes.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.4 Performance Points

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.4.1 After each WSPS Recognised Competition, Athletes will obtain performance points based on their performance.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.4.2 Athletes will be ranked in descending order according to their performance points.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.4.3 Athletes will receive ranking points depending on their performance as outlined below.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.4.4 Performance points will be allocated following the ratification of the Competition results, and are calculated based on the following values:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Value A (rank points) - based on the rank achieved in the qualification and final rounds.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) Value B (Competition weighting) - based on the level and significance of the Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) Value C (q ualification result points) - based on the qualification score achieved by the Athlete , divided by the w orld record (as of 1 January of the Competition year) in that Event.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.4.5 The total p erformance points will be calculated and published to two decimal places (mathematically rounded).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.5 Duration of validity The time for which the allocated performance points remain valid will vary according to the level and significance of the WSPS Recognised Competition:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 20 Competition Code Duration of validity (seasons) Paralympic Games PG 2 WSPS World Championships WCH 2 Regional Games /Championships (only valid for Regional Rankings) RG 1 WSPS Sanctioned Competition (WSPS World Cup) WC 1 WSPS Approved Competition (WSPS Grand Prix) GP 1

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.5.1 Points obtained at the Paralympic Games and World Championships will remain valid in the ranking system for two years from the date of Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.5.2 Performance points obtained at all other WSPS Recognised Competitions will be valid in the ranking system for one year.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.6 Value A (Rank Points)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.6.1 The Value ‘A’ allocated will be determined by the rank an Athlete achieves, both in the qualification and final rounds.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.6.2 A point value is allocated based on the rank in the q ualification rounds (value A1) and final round (value A2): Rank Qualification Round Points (A1) Final Round Points (A2) 1st rank 11 50 2nd rank 10 40 3rd rank 9 30 4th rank 8 20 5th rank 7 18 6th rank 6 16 7th rank 5 14 8th rank 4 12 9th+ rank 1 0

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.6.3 Value A is calculated as a sum of the points for the qualification and final ranking (values A1 + A2). Qualification Rank Points + Final Rank Points = Value A (A1) (A2)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 21

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.6.4 For non-Paralympic Events where no Finals are conducted, in the ranking calculations a value of zero will be assigned for the final rank points (value A2).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.6.5 If an Athlete ranks 1-8 in q ualification but is DNS (“Did Not Start”) in the final, in the ranking calculations a value of zero will be assigned for the final rank points (value A2).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.7 Value B (Competition weighting)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.7.1 The Value B allocated will vary according to the level and significance of the Competition: Competition Code Value B Paralympic Games PG 10 World Championships WCH 8 Regional Games /Championships (only valid for Regional Rankings) RG 6 World Cup WC 6 Grand Prix GP 2

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.8 Value C (qualification result points)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.8.1 The Value C allocated is the q ualification score achieved by the Athlete , divided by the w orld record in that E vent (as of 01 January of the Competition year).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.8.2 For both world and regional rankings, the world record will be used. Qualification Score = Value C World Record

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.9 Calculation

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.18.9.1 Performance points per Competition are calculated by multiplying together Values A, B and C. Value A x Value B x Value C = Performance Points (Rank points) (Competition weighting) (Qualification result points)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19 Records

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19.1 World, regional and junior world records may be established in WSPS Events R1-R11, P1-P6, PT1-PT3, VIS, and VIP.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 22

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19.2 Paralympic Games records may be established only at the Paralympic Games in the relevant Events.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19.3 Only scores obtained at WSPS Championships or WSPS Sanctioned Competitions will be eligible for records recognition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19.4 Athletes must have a WSPS Licence and a Sport Class Status ‘Confirmed’ or ‘Review’ with a ‘Fixed Review Date’ which is after the date the record was achieved in the Competition to be eligible for recognition of a record-breaking performance.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19.5 The Technical Delegate must submit the record report form at the end of the Competition for records to be ratified and recognised.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19.6 Junior records

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19.6.1 To be eligible to obtain junior world records, Athletes must be under the age of 21 on 31 December of the year of the relevant Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19.7 Records definitions

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 2.19.7.1 The obtainable WSPS records are as follows: Record Type Code Description World Record New WR Record to be established in the final of the relevant Event using the Finals result only. Equal EWR Junior World Record New WRJ Equal EWRJ Regional Record New [Region] Equal E[Region] Qualification Record New QR Record to be established in the qualification round of the relevant Event using the qualification result only. Equal EQR Junior Qualification Record New QRJ Equal EQRJ Regional Qualification Record New Q[Region] Equal EQ[Region] Team Record New WR Team records will be established in team Events using the combined qualification scores of the 3 nominated team members. Equal EWR Team Regional Record New [Region] Equal E[Region] Paralympic Record New PR Paralympic records will be established in the Paralympic Games Final of the relevant Event using the Finals result only. Equal EPR Paralympic Qualification Record New PQR Paralympic qualification records will be established in the Paralympic Games qualification round of the relevant event using the qualification result only. Equal EPQR

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 23 Regional Games Record New GR a) Games records will be established in the relevant Regional Games final of the relevant Event using the Finals result only. Equal EGR Regional Games Qualification Record New GQR b) Games qualification records will be established in the relevant Regional Games qualification round of the relevant E vent using the qualification result only. Equal EGQR

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3 Apparel and Equipment Rules

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.1 Compliance with ISSF dress code

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.1.1 All persons on the f ield of p lay and ceremonies area must adhere to the ISSF d ress code.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.1.2 Athletes must also comply with the WSPS-specific dress code provisions as set out in Rule 3.2 below.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2 WSPS-specific dress code provisions (jackets, trousers and footwear)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.1 Shooting Jackets (“WSPS Jacket”)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.1.1 The maximum length of the WSPS Jacket must not be longer than down to the lap in the front and down to the top of the cushion in the back.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.1.2 The length of the WSPS Jacket will be measured in a standing shooting position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.1.3 The Athlete must not sit on any part of their WSPS J acket during Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.1.4 Athletes in Sport Classes SH1B Rifle, SH1 C Rifle and SH2 R ifle must use a WSPS Jacket. Athletes shooting on the floor in the prone position may use an ISSF jacket.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.1.5 Athletes in Sport Class SH1A Rifle may use an ISSF jacket in accordance with the ISSF Rules, in the following circumstances: Maximum length of jacket/vest

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 26 Position Style Regulation Kneeling Shooting as per ISSF position Permitted: Jacket usage as per ISSF Rules Shooting from a Shooting Chair Permitted: Only the top 3 jacket buttons may be fastened, and the buttons may not extend below the bottom of the ribcage or equivalent. Any additional buttons must not be used. Prone Shooting as per ISSF position Permitted: Jacket usage as per ISSF Rules Shooting from a Shooting Chair Permitted: Only the top 3 jacket buttons may be fastened, and the buttons may not extend below the bottom of the ribcage or equivalent. Any additional buttons must not be used. Standing Shooting from a high stool or free-standing Permitted: Jacket usage as per ISSF Rules Shooting from a Shooting Chair ISSF jacket not permitted

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.1.6 A maximum of 1 WSPS Jacket and 1 ISSF jacket per Athlete must be approved by Equipment Control in each Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.1.7 Jackets without buttons

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Even if the jacket has no buttons, the jacket must be shaped in accordance with Rules 3.2.1.1 and 3.2.1.2 above.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.2 Shooting Trousers

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.2.1 Shooting Trousers are prohibited for all Athletes in Sport Classes SH1B, SH1C and all SH2 .

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.2.2 Shooting trousers are permitted for Athletes in Sport Class SH1A Rifle shooting in the standing position from a high stool or free -standing, in the kneeling position, and in the prone position as per the applicable ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 27

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.2.3 In the R7 and R8 Events, athletes with lower limb prosthesis/prostheses are permitted to keep their shooting trousers on in the kneeling position from a Shooting Chair and prone position, only if:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) they are unable to remove their trousers due to a prosthesis; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) the leg zippers and waistband of the trousers are open when in position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.3 Footwear

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.3.1 Footwear must be worn by all persons on the field of play unless prescribed otherwise on their WSPS Licence.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.2.3.2 An Athlete may be permitted to wear orthopaedic footwear or other non - ISSF dress code compliant footwear (e.g. sandals) if there is a valid medical reason. In all cases unless WSPS determines otherwise:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) such exceptions will be assessed and decided by the Classification Panel and recorded on the Athlete ’s Classification and WSPS Licence; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) such footwear will not be tested for flexibility during Equipment Control.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3 Equipment

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.1 Athletes must use only equipment that complies with and is in accordance with these Rules and Regulations and the ISSF Rules. Any equipment that the Competition Jury deem may give an Athlete an unfair advantage or is not expressly permitted in these Rules and Regulations is prohibited.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.2 All equipment must be supplied by the Athlete.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.3 Athlete may not touch the wheels or the sideboards with any part of their body or equipment, unless specified otherwise in these Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.4 Athletes and their equipment must be within the designated area of their firing point and behind the Firing Line.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.4.1 An exception may be made for rifle resting stands, which will be permitted in accordance with the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.5 Athletes are permitted to add material that increases hand grip on the rifle. However:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.5.1 The adaptation must comply with Rule 3.3.1;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.5.2 The material must still allow free movement of the Athlete and rifle;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.5.3 The rifle needs to remain within the specified dimensions; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 28

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.3.5.4 The Athlete’s request t o use a grip adaption must be reviewed and approved by a WSPS Classification Panel during a technical assessment.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.4 Equipment Control

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.4.1 Team Leaders and coaches are equally responsible for ensuring that Athletes ’ equipment and apparel comply with these Rules and Regulations and the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.4.2 ISSF equipment will be checked in accordance with the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.4.3 WSPS-specific equipment

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.4.3.1 ‘WSPS-specific equipment’ is defined as:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Strapping

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) Prosthesis

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) Shooting table(s)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: d) Compensating block

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: e) 10cm block

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: f) Shooting Chair(s)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: g) SH2 rifle support stand

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: h) Loading device (for Pistol only)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: i) Trigger extensions, grips and trigger adaptations

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.4.3.2 WSPS-specific equipment checks will be done in accordance with t hese Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.4.3.3 The Athlete is responsible for submitting W SPS-specific equipment and apparel for official inspection and approval before the start of every Competition. As part of this process:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) The Athlete must present both their valid ID C ard and WSPS Licence; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) The ‘Equipment Control Sheet’ (available on the WSPS website ) must be completed and signed by all relevant parties.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.4.3.4 Each Athlete’s equipment may be checked by the Competition Jury on the Firing Line prior to the start of each Event.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.4.4 Random equipment checks will be done by the Competition Jury from Equipment Control directly after an Event.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.5 Strapping

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.5.1 Athletes are not allowed to hold or touch the straps when competing to gain stability.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.5.2 Straps must not exceed 5cm in width.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.5.3 Below knee: it is permitted to have 1 below knee strap to the Shooting Chair.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal

chunks.text: 3.5.4 Above knee: the legs may be strapped together once above the knees but not to the chair.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.5.5 All Athletes with double above -knee amputation (and not using any prosthesis), a strap across the stumps and strapped to the chair is permitted.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6 Trigger extensions and trigger adaptations

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6.1 In accordance with the ISSF Rules, the style/shape of a trigger is a personal choice as long as it stays within the boundary of the given dimensions (as stated in the ISSF Rules).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6.2 The shape of the trigger is free; however the trigger must remain safe and stay within the permitted dimensions.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6.2.1 Trigger extension: triggers that have modifications compared to standard triggers, but are inside the dimensions of the ISSF Rules and protected by a trigger guard.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6.2.2 Trigger Adapt ations: triggers that have modifications compared to standard triggers, and are outside of the trigger guard and dimensions of the ISSF Rules (see Appendix 4).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6.3 Trigger adaptations are only permitted in the following circumstances:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6.3.1 Athletes must have a medical reason to use a trigger adaptation.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6.3.2 The Athlete’s request to use a trigger adaptation must be reviewed and approved by a WSPS Classification Panel during a technical assessment (in consultation with the Technical Delegate, regarding the safe use of the proposed trigger adaptation).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6.3.3 If approved, the trigger adaptation must be recorded on the Athlete ’s WSPS Licence.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.6.4 All air-operated trigger systems, including blowing and pneumatic systems, are not permitted.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7 Shooting Chairs

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.1 A “Shooting Chair” is any o bject on which an Athlete sits to shoot. This includes wheelchairs, chairs, seats, stools, and high stools.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.1.1 A high stool allows Athletes to compete with their feet on the ground adopting a standing position while supported by a seat. WSPS shall have final discretion as to whether any object shall be deemed a high stool. All Athletes competing on high stools during Rifle/Pistol Events must comply with the following rules:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 30

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) the minimum height of the seat must be equal to or higher than the Athlete’s mid -thigh height. The mid -thigh height is the measurement between the knee joint to the hip joint (measured along the femur bone);

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) the maximum height of the seat is the measurement of the Athlete’s inside leg length minus 7 cm. This measurement must be conducted by a Classification Panel and the height of the high stool must be noted on the WSPS Licence;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) the measurement of the base of the stool must be no greater than 60X60 cm. The base of the stool must be 3 or 4 independent legs. The base must not connect the legs;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: d) the seat must be circular or rectangular . Use of a bike seat is permitted for Athletes with an amputation at the hip(s) joint;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: e) the Athlete’s feet must not touch the base of the high stool; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: f) both feet of the Athlete must be in front of the forward part of the seat.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.2 For Athletes shooting from a S hooting Chair (not including a high stool), the centreline of the barrel must not exceed more than 150cm (measured from the floor).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.3 All Shooting Chairs will be checked with the Athlete in the shooting position during Equipment Control and will be subject to spot checks on the Firing Line before, during or immediately after the Competition. A ny disputes will be resolved by WSPS or the Technical Delegate in their absolute discretion.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.4 Athletes using wheelchairs as Shooting Chairs must be able to remove themselves from the Firing Line without any artificial assistance.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.4.1 For the purposes of this R ule, examples of artificial assistance include any tool used to lock a Shooting Chair on to the firing point (for example a screwdriver).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.4.2 For the avoidance of doubt, the wheelchair’s brakes shall not constitute artificial assistance for the purposes of this Rule.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.4.3 Nothing in this Rule shall prevent another individual (for example a Coach or Loader) from providing physical assistance (e.g. pushing a wheelchair) in removing an Athlete from the Firing Line.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.5 The rules for armrests, sideboards and table per discipline are summarised below.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.6 Handles and side posts may not exceed the height of the backrest.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.7 The height of the wheels of the wheelchair may not exceed the height of the Athlete’s hip when in the sitting position. An Athlete’s hip is not allowed to touch the wheels.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.8 Subject to the other terms of this Rule 3.7, it is not permitted to add any material or modify the structure of the Shooting Chair to gain stability of the pelvis or the spine.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.8.1 Athletes are not permitted to adjust their electronic chairs during Competitions, including Finals unless permitted by a member of the Competition Jury.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.9 Athletes must not lean on the side posts or wheels of their Shooting Chairs to gain stability of the pelvis or the spine.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.9.1 The sides of the torso may touch the side posts; however, it is not permitted for Athletes to use the side posts to gain additional stability of the spine.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.9.2 The spine must not be in contact with the post when the Athlete is in the shooting position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.10 Seat pad and seat cushion:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.10.1 Except as specified in this Rule 3.7.10, the use of seat pads or seat cushions are permitted. The construction of the seat pad or seat cushion, their shape, and their thickness are not limited within the dimensions of the Shooting Chair. However, the seat pads or seat cushion must fit within the seating area of the Shooting Chair and it cannot extend outside of it (for example it is not permitted for the cushion to touch the wheels, sideboards, or backrest).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 32

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.10.2 If a chair is used, the maximum size of the seat pads or seat cushions is 50x50cm.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.10.3 All programmable air cell cushions are prohibited.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.10.4 It is not permitted to add a seat pad or seat cushion between the back rest and the body of the Athlete.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.10.5 All seat pads or seat cushions will be checked during Equipment Control and will be subject to spot checks on the Firing Line before, during or immediately after the Competition. Any disputes will be resolved by WSPS or the Technical Delegate in their absolute discretion.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.11 Seat angle

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.11.1 Subject to Rule 3.7.11.2 and Rule

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.11.3, the sitting angle and backrest angle of the Athlete sitting in a Shooting Chair is free.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.11.2 The seat angle of the Shooting Chair (except wheelchair) in any direction can be a maximum of (±5 degrees).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.11.3 The axis of the wheelchair from side-to side must be horizontal (±5 degrees).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.12 Backrest slack

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.12.1 The backrest may be made of hard or flexible material:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Backrests made from flexible material: the maximum slack (stretch) of the backrest (the distance from the front of the vertical side posts of the backrest to the deepest part of the backrest) shall not exceed 8cm. Slack: < 8cm (flexible backrest), or; < 3cm (hard backrest)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 33

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) Backrests made from hard material: the backrest may be flat or with a curved surfaced; however, the maximum slack (depth of the curve) of the backrest (the distance from the front of the vertical side posts of the backrest to the deepest part of the backrest) shall not exceed 3cm. If the backrest is upholstered with compressible material , the maximum depth of the curve must still not exceed the permitted depth of 3cm when the material is compressed.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.12.2 Backrest slack is to be measured with the Athlete in the Shooting C hair in the shooting position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.13 Visible Free Height

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.13.1 Score A

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) A back-support of any height may be fitted to the Shooting Chair in such a way that Athletes may take a rest against it between shots.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) There must be clearly no contact between Athlete and back-support when firing.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.13.2 Score B

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) A minimum of 60% of the total back length of the Athlete needs to be above the backrest.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) The measurement will be taken from the middle of vertebra C7 - vertebra prominence.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) The measurement will be recorded on the Athlete ’s Classification and WSPS Licence as the minimum ‘Visible Free Height’.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.13.3 Score C

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) The measurement will be taken from the middle of vertebra C7 - vertebra prominence.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) The measurement will be recorded on the Athlete ’s Classification and WSPS Licence as the minimum ‘Visible Free Height’.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.13.4 No part of the backrest may be higher than the minimum Visible Free Height as specified in the Athlete’s WSPS Licence.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.7.13.5 The Competition Jury shall:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 34

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) measure the Visible Free Height of each Athlete and ensure that it is not shorter than the minimum Visible Free Height indicated on the Athlete’s WSPS Licence;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) place a piece of tape on the back of the Athlete’s shooting jacket to indicate the Visible Free Height (the Visible Free Height will be indicated by the bottom edge of the tape). The tape must always remain visible during Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) The Visible Free Height must be indicated on the start/BIB number.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8 Shooting Tables

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.1 Rifle Events

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.1.1 Size - all components of the shooting table (regardless of shape or form) must:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) be of a size no larger than 90cm in diameter;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) remain within the firing point dimensions.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.1.2 Shape

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Shooting tables may have a small upstanding edge fitted to prevent small items from falling (but in no way may be used for additional stability or support of the Athlete).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) The shape of the shooting table is free.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) If the shape of the table is curved (as in ‘U -Form’), the shape of the curve must be wider than the Athlete ’s torso, so that the left and right side of the Athlete 's abdomen cannot touch the table at the same time when in the prone position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.1.3 Form - the construction of the shooting table may:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Either be attached to the S hooting Chair or free standing;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) Consist of a single table, or a multiple small individual tables;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) If two or more small individual tables are used:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: I. They must be joined or placed together in such a way as to provide one stable platform; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: II. The combined surface of the tables must meet all requirements as specified for shooting tables (size, angle, shape).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 35

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.1.4 Angle

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) The shooting table must be horizontal or at the same angle as the floor (measured at the centre of the table).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) A variation of ±5 degrees is allowed.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) Athletes with uneven upper limbs may be permitted to use a compensating block under the shorter limb when shooting in the prone position . This shall be assessed by the Classification Panel and marked on the Athlete’s Classification and WSPS Licence if permitted.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.1.5 Support

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) The shooting table must not be used to gain support or stability for the body in any way, except for in the prone position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) In the prone position, the table can provide support (but Athletes are not allowed to gain stability on the left or right side of the chair with the abdomen).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.1.6 Upholstering

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) The table or board may be upholstered with compressible material of a maximum thickness of 2cm.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) The material on the table must be of uniform thickness for both elbows.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) It is not permitted to make a hollow in the table or board or in the upholstered material.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.1.7 Elbow support table in the kneeling position

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) The maximum surface for support of the elbow in the kneeling position is 10cm in diameter. This support can be from:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: I. a small shooting table (10cm surface diameter); or

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: II. an additional mounted support (hereafter ‘10cm block’) added to the larger shooting table : a removable board with a diameter of 10cm and a thickness of at least 20mm.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.1.8 Shooting stand support

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) An additional separate board or table may be allowed for the rifle rest.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 36

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.2 Pistol Tables

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.2.1 In the event that the range bench is fixed to the ground so the Athlete cannot get close enough to rest and load the pistol, or the bench is designed in such a way that means the Athletes ’ shooting position is compromised and cannot safely operate the loading procedure, the use of an additional small table may be permitted:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) the additional table must be presented at Equipment Control;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) the Competition Jury from Equipment Control will make an assessment on a case-by-case basis and will confirm if the use of an additional small table will be permitted; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) the use of the table will be checked on the Firing Line by the Competition Jury to confirm that the table is used in a safe manner by the Athlete.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.8.2.2 The additional table (if permitted) must be within the following specifications:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Maximum size of 30cm x 30cm.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) Maximum height of 100cm.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) The table must in no way provide additional support to the Athlete in the shooting position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9 SH2 rifle support stands

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.1 All SH2 Athletes must use an approved support stand (see Appendix 5) to support the weight of the rifle.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.2 The Classification Panel will assess muscle power in the shooting arm (arm used to shoulder the rifle) for Athletes in Sport Class SH2 for the purpose of identifying if the Athlete may use a weak or a strong spring on the rifle support.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.3 Depending on the Athlete’s assessment score, they will be allocated a subclass; ‘a’ or ‘b’.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.4 This subclass will be recorded on the Athlete ’s WSPS Licence and determines which spring the Athlete shall use in their support stand: Subclass Spring Characteristics a WEAK SPRING (white plastic part) = flexibility minimum 35mm b STRONG SPRING (black plastic part) = flexibility minimum 25mm

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 37

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.5 The shooting stand may be fixed to the table or on a tripod.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.6 No other support or mechanical devices may be used as a support for the rifle.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.7 No device or substance may be attached to the rifle or the shooting stand in order to hold the rifle in a fixed position in, or against the shooting stand.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.8 The Athlete’s hands must not be placed in front of the spring or interfere with the operation of the spring when firing a shot.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.9 The pin and the spring of the shooting stand must be in vertical position, front to back.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.10 It is allowed to shorten the bottom part of the support stand. The remaining length needs to be at least 20mm , so that it will be possible to check the flexibility of the support stand during Equipment Control.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.11 Yoke (rifle holder)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.11.1 The rifle must not contact both sides of the yoke at the same time.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.11.2 The yoke must be at least 1cm wider than the width of the rifle stock.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.11.3 It is allowed to add material inside the yoke if it is comparable to the surface of a shooting glove and does not interfere with the yoke measurements.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.12 Point of balance

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.12.1 The point of balance of the rifle must be marked at Equipment Control. The rifle must be placed ±5 cm of its point of balance on the rifle support stand and the total 10cm range must be marked. The complete yoke must be within the 10cm range.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.12.2 The point of balance on gas or compressed air rifles will be measured with full containers.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.12.3 The total weight of the upper part of the support stand must be less than or equal to 200 grams. The spring must be an official WSPS- approved model (see Appendix 5).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.13 Test bar for spring flexibility (Appendix 5)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.13.1 Weight and tolerances for testing the flexibility of the springs are:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Bar 1) 250 Grams +2 - 0 (used for zeroing)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) Bar 2) 720 Grams +0 – 2 (used to test the flexibility)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.13.2 All springs must be checked at Equipment Control prior to Competition , according to Appendix 5.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 38

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 3.9.13.3 An Athlete may use two different springs (10m and 50m) during a Competition. Both springs must successfully go through E quipment Control.
