chunks.text: 4.1.4 It is recommended that in Events R3, and all SH2 events at least every third firing point is left vacant to avoid the disturb ance of other Athletes. The final decision on this matter will be made by the Technical Delegate.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.5 Athletes are only allowed to use one rifle per Event distance (10m and 50m) per Competition, unless an allowable malfunction occurs in accordance with ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.6 In the R7 and R8 Events, one coach/team member is permitted to assist the Athlete in the changeover time between positions ; however, Athletes must lead in the changeover process.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.6.1 At qualification stage and Final s, Athletes must lead in the changeover process with rifle adjustments. The Coach/team member may only assist the Athletes with:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: (a) Setting the rifle on the shooting table or on a stable platform for the Athlete to perform the changeover,

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: (b) Hand the Athlete tools or equipment requested by the Athlete to be attached or adjusted,

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: (c) Assist the Athlete with stabilizing the wheelchair on the firing point,

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: (d) Coach/team member may request the Competi tion Jury to assist Athlete s in another manner that does not consist of a direct changeover activity to be completed by the Athletes. The decision to grant these requests is at the sole discretion of the Competition Jury.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.7 No unused equipment or additional chairs may be left on the field of play.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.8 Athletes may not use chairs to rest their equipment on.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.9 Finals

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.9.1 The ISSF Rules regarding timings of Events will be followed in all F inals, unless specified by WSPS. Refer to the WSPS Finals Commands document available on the WSPS website.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.9.2 During the final, Loaders must move to the back of firing point (1m behind the Athlete) between shots. During the single shot series, the Loader must wait until “STOP” is commanded before returning to the Athlete . Loaders must be loading during the finals to be allowed on the field of play.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.9.3 Athletes (and Loaders) must ens ure they do not touch the rifle with a pellet/bullet before the command “LOAD” is given.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 41

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.9.4 The loading process must be completed within 5 seconds from the command “LOAD” being given , except in SH2 Events, where Athletes/Loaders must complete the loading process within 10 seconds from the command “LOAD” being given.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.9.5 The loader must assist the Athlete as follows:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: (a) Ensuring the safety of the rifle during the loading process by standing next to the Athlete, and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: (b) Ensuring the safety of the rifle and assisting the Athlete during the de -shoulder and/or position re-adjustment.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.9.6 The penalty for a first violation in a Competition will be first a yellow card, followed by a green card (two (2) point penalty) for a second violation in that Competition, with a third violation in that Competition resulting in a red card (disqualification).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.1.9.7 If eliminated from the f inal, all Athletes (including SH2) must immediately leave their firing point and move to the side of field of play to their allocated place next to their coach. Coaches/ Loaders may assist Athletes in this process.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2 Shooting positions

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.1 Kneeling

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.1.1 SH1A Athletes with lower limb deficiency can compete in the ISSF kneeling position using a prosthesis or a stool of 35cm maximum height (if marked on the WSPS Licence) to support the rifle-supporting leg.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.1.2 If a Shooting Chair and table is used:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) the Athlete must comply with WSPS Rules 3.7 and 3.8;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) only one elbow must rest on the table or board and the body must be well clear of the board;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) the supporting forearm must form an angle of not less than 30 degrees from the horizontal. Only the point of the e lbow may be supported on the 10cm block;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: d) no support may be gained from the board/table frame/arm rests;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: e) the arm(s) of the S hooting Chair (which are not used to attach the table/board to) must be removed.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 42

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.2 Prone

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.2.1 SH1 and S H2 Athletes are not allowed to fixate their body between the backrest and the table; they may either lean on the backrest or the table for stability but not both.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.2.2 Should an Athlete have uneven upper limb lengths, it is permitted to use a compensating block (under the shorter limb). This shall be assessed by the Classification Panel and marked on the Athlete ’s Classification and WSPS Licence if permitted.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.2.3 50m Rifle Prone: Athletes may choose to compete either in the position as described in the ISSF R ules, or with the use of a S hooting Chair and table and must comply with WSPS Rules 3.7 and 3.8.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.2.4 10m Air Rifle prone: Athletes may not lie down but must use a S hooting Chair and table and must comply with WSPS Rules 3.7 and 3.8.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Both elbows must rest on the table or board.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) The upper arms must not touch the table or board (it is recommended that the part of the table below the upper arm is removed).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) The forearm must not form an angle of less than 30 degrees from the horizontal, measured from the axis of the forearm.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: d) In the case of upper limb deficiency Athletes: it is permitted to hold the rifle with a prosthesis if the prosthesis does not grip the rifle and does not have a fixed elbow.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: e) Both the forearms and the sleeves of the shooting jacket must be visibly raised from the surface of the table as per ISSF rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 43

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) Use of a sling is prohibited.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) Both elbows (if the Athlete ’s Impairment allows) must rest on the table or board.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) If the athlete’s Impairment does not allow for both elbows to be rested on the table, the athlete may rest their non-shooting arm on the table, on top of the rifle, or on their body, provided that the arm is visibly relaxed and not used in such a way as to gain additional support and an unfair advantage.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: d) The upper arms must not touch the table or board (it is recommended that the part of the table below the upper arm is removed).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.3 Standing

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.3.1 Athletes with a trunk function score A may ch oose to compete free- standing (if so , they must stand free of any artificial support, except for medically certified prosthesis/orthosis).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.3.2 The arms and sideboards of the Shooting Chair and the shooting table must be removed.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.2.3.3 When shooting from a high stool, the Athlete must be able to remove his/her feet from the floor, without losing balance and without moving the upper body.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) The rifle must be held with the arms only, without support (as per the ISSF Rules).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) No part of the arms may come in contact with any part of the Shooting Chair.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) No part of the Athlete’s elbows must come into contact with the lap, wheel or gain support other than from the ribcage, hip or abdomen. The penalty for noncompliance with this rule is first a Yellow Card, followed by a Green Card (two (2) point penalty), with a 3rd violation resulting in a Red Card (disqualification).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) In the case of arm -amputee Athletes it is not permitted to hold (touch) the rifle with the prosthesis in standing position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 44

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) In the standing position all Athletes must clearly and visibly de - shoulder (removal of physical contact between butt plate and shoulder) the rifle in between shots. There must be a visible separation of at least 3cm between every shot.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: c) The penalty for not de- shouldering between shots will be first a Yellow Card, followed by a Green Card (two (2) point penalty), with a 3rd violation resulting in a Red Card (disqualification).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3 Loaders (SH2 only)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.1 Loaders apply only to SH2 Athletes competing in SH2 Events and are permitted only as described in the WSPS Classification Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.1.1 A Classification Panel makes t he decision as to whether an Athlete is permitted to have a Loader and the outcome will be marked on the WSPS Licence.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.2 The Loaders must:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.2.1 not speak or give signals during the Event;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.2.2 only load the rifle and/or adjust the sights at the request of the Athlete;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.2.3 only load the rifle, while touching the barrel. Loading while touching the back half of the rifle ( i.e., touching the cheek piece or butt plate) is not permitted.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.3 In SH2 qualification events, every third (3rd) firing point will be left free. This free firing point must be used as space for the Loaders.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.3.1 Depending on the firing point allocated, Loaders must stand to the left or right of their Athlete as specified by the allocated firing point.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.3.2 The Loader’s position (left/right of the Athlete ) is fixed according to the firing point and cannot be changed to the other side of the Athlete.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 45

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.3.3 Loaders must stay in position for the duration of the Competition and must not move to the back of the firing point between shots.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 4.3.4 If the Loader is also the Athlete's coach, they must first ask permission of the R ange Official before speaking to each other, in accordance with Rule 2.16 above.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 46 5 Pistol Rules

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1 Events and times

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.1 All pistol Event times are in accordance with these Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.2 WSPS may, at its own discretion, and at any time, cancel Events for which viability criteria are not met.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.3 WSPS Competitions may comprise the following pistol Events (the “Pistol Events”): Event Discipline Gender Class Shots Time Electronic Targets Time Target carriers & pit-operated Competitions P1 10m Air Pistol Men SH1 60 1:15 1:30 P2 10m Air Pistol Women SH1 60 1:15 1:30 P3 25m Pistol Open SH1 60 - - P4 50m Pistol Open SH1 60 1:30 1:45 *P5 10m Air Pistol Standard Open SH1 40- - - *P6 Mixed Team Pistol Mixed SH1 2 (Athletes) x 30 (shots each) 0:40 N/A *Non-Paralympic Event

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.4 P3 Event is to be shot according to the ISSF 25m Pistol Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.4.1 If the bench of the 25-meter range is too high for sitting Athletes to perform the 45-degree angle in the ready position, the ‘ready position’ can be accepted as the lowest point to the surface of the bench.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.4.2 In no case may the pistol rest on the bench during the ‘ready position’.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.4.3 Athletes may request this modified ‘ready position’. The decision to allow the modified ‘ready position’ is at the discretion of the Technical Delegate.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.5 P5 (10m Air Pistol Standard) E vent is to be shot in accordance with the Rules as set out in Appendix 6.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.6 No equipment or additional chairs may be left on the field of play.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.7 Athletes may not use chairs to rest their equipment on.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 47

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.8 Finals

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.8.1 The ISSF Rules regarding timings will be followed in all Finals as set out in the ‘WSPS Finals Commands’ document available on the WSPS website. Athletes must ensure they do not touch the pistol with a pellet/bullet before the command “LOAD” is given.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.8.2 The loading process must be completed within five (5) seconds from the command “LOAD” being given in Events P1, P2, and P4.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.1.8.3 If eliminated from the Final, all Athletes must immediately leave their firing point and move to the side of field of play to their allocated place next to their coach. Coaches may assist Athletes in this process.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.2 Shooting position

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.2.1 SH1A Athletes may choose to compete free -standing. If so, they must stand free of any artificial support, except for medically certified prosthesis/orthosis.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.2.2 The arms and sideboards of the S hooting Chair and the shooting table must be removed.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.2.3 The non-shooting arm/hand must not be on the Shooting Chair or in a position to give the Athlete an additional support (in accordance with the ISSF Rules).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.2.4 Any additional items between the legs and the non -shooting arm (such as a cushion) are not allowed.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.3 Loading device (safety)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.3.1 Loading safety must follow the ISSF Rules, except for Rule 5.3.2 below.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.3.2 A loading device, to hold the pistol to enable it to be loaded or unloaded safely, must always be used if it is specified on the WSPS Licence following Classification of the Athlete by the Classification Panel.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 5.3.2.1 The loading device will be ch ecked at Equipment Control by the Competition Jury to ensure safe handling.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 48 6 Shotgun Rules

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.1 Events and times

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.1.1 All Shotgun Events and times are in accordance with these Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.1.2 WSPS may, at its own discretion, and at any time, cancel Events for which viability criteria are not met.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.1.3 WSPS Competitions may be comprised of the following s hotgun Events (the “Shotgun Events”): Event Discipline Gender Class Shots Targets Preparation Time Limits *PT1 Trap Seated Open SG-S 125 Day 1 – 75 Targets Day 2 – 50 Targets 15 sec *PT2 Trap Standing (Lower Limb) Open SG-L 125 Day 1 – 75 Targets Day 2 – 50 Targets 15 sec *PT3 Trap Standing (Upper Limb) Open SG-U 125 Day 1 – 75 Targets Day 2 – 50 Targets 15 sec *Non-Paralympic Event

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.1.4 Shotgun Events will be conducted in accordance with ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2 Shooting position

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.1 Sport Class SG-S

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.1.1 Athletes in Sport Class SG -S must compete seated in a wheelchair or on a stool.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.1.2 If seated in a wheelchair Athletes must sit with the spine against the backrest of the wheelchair. Strapping to the backrest is allowed. The buttocks must remain in full contact with the seat of the wheelchair throughout the movement.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.1.3 The feet must rest on the footplate of the wheelchair, or the lower limb must be supported by a leg rest with knees bent to a 90-degree angle or the angle indicated on the WSPS Licence . The feet must not be placed on the ground hereby enlarging the support base of the Athlete as created by the standard wheelchair configuration.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 49

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.1.4 If the Athlete uses a stool , the feet must support the weight bearing in a vertical plane to the stool unless anatomical restrictions do not allow this. Such restriction must be recorded on the WSPS Licence . The buttocks of the Athlete must remain in full contact with the stool throughout the movement.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.1.5 Athletes in Sport Class SG-S must be watched by the Competition Jury or another delegated official to ensure that throughout the shot, the Athletes remain seated, the spine is in contact with the backrest of the wheelchair (if seated in a wheelchair) and the feet adhere to the requirements outlined above.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.1.6 Athletes in Sport C lass SG -S may use strapping on their upper body to ensure safety while firing. The strapping used must not exceed 10 cm in width and must not be elastic. As much body weight may be supported by the strapping as the Athlete determines is necessary.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.2 Sport Class SG-L

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.2.1 Athletes in Sport Class SG-L must compete in the standing position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.2.2 No stool, gadget or any device to support standing is permitted.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.3 Sport Class SG-U

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.3.1 Athletes in Sport Class SG-U must compete in the standing position.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.2.3.2 No stool, gadget or any device to support standing is permitted.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.3 Loading device (safety)

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.3.1 Athletes competing in Sport Class SG-U must use the adaptive loading stand , as set up by the LOC, on each station on the field.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.3.2 During Athlete Evaluation, a Classification Panel may identify circumstances in which an individual Athlete may not be able to, for example, safely load, hold and/or fire a shotgun. In such cases, the Classification Panel will report to the Competition Jury who will conduct a full investigation to determine if the use of an approved prosthesis and/or an adaptive loading stand will alleviate the safety concerns and enable the Athlete to compete. If the Competition Jury determine that the Athlete is unable to safely load, hold and/or fire a shotgun that Athlete will not be e ligible to compete in Shotgun Events.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.3.3 For the avoidance of doubt, if the Classification Panel considers it necessary to disclose medical diagnostic information to the Competition Jury for the purposes of an investigation in accordance with Rule 6.3.2 above, such information shall be treated as confidential in accordance with the data protection provisions of the WSPS Classification Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 50

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.4 Other

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.4.1 Except as provided for in Rule 6.3 above, adaptive devices used by Athletes must be approved by WSPS. All adaptive devices will be inspected, and, if approved will be noted as a permanent approval of the device on the Athlete’s WSPS Licence.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.4.2 No trigger adaptations are permitted for Athletes competing in Shotgun Events.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 6.4.3 Shooting tables and support stands are not permitted for Athletes competing in Shotgun Events.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 51 7 Vision Impairment (VI) Rules

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1 Events and times

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1.1 All VI Events and times are in accordance with these Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1.2 WSPS may, at its own discretion, and at any time, cancel Events for which viability criteria are not met.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1.3 WSPS Recognised Competitions may comprise the following VI Events (the “VI Events”): Event Discipline Gender Class Shots Time Electronic Targets Time Target carriers & pit - operated Competitions *VIS 10m Air Rifle Standing Open SHVI 60 1:15 1:30 *VIP 10m Air Rifle Prone Open SHVI 60 0:50 1:00 *Non-Paralympic Event

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1.3.1 It is recommended that in VI Events at least every third firing point is left vacant to avoid the disturbance of other Athletes. The final decision on this matter will be made by the Technical Delegate.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1.3.2 No unused equipment or additional chairs may be left on the field of play. Athletes may not use chairs to rest their equipment on.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1.4 Finals

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1.4.1 The ISSF Rules regarding timings of Events will be followed in all Finals, unless specified by WSPS. Please refer to the ‘WSPS Finals Commands’ document available on the WSPS website.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1.4.2 In VIS and VIP, the Athlete must complete the loading process within ten (10) seconds from the command “LOAD” being given.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.1.4.3 The VI Assistant must stay in position for the duration of the Finals.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2 Apparel and Equipment

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.1 Shooting Jackets

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.1.1 WSPS Rule 3.2.1 will apply.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.1.2 VI Rifle Athletes may use a n ISSF-approved jacket in accordance with the ISSF Rules, in the following circumstances:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 52 Position Style Regulation Prone Shooting from a Shooting Chair Permitted: only the top three (3) jacket buttons may be fastened, and the buttons may not extend below the bottom of the ribcage or equivalent. Any additional buttons must not be used Standing Shooting free-standing Permitted: Jacket usage as per ISSF Rules

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.2 Shooting Trousers

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.2.1 Shooting Trousers are prohibited for all prone Athletes.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.3 Shooting Shoes

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.3.1 Shooting Shoes must follow ISSF Rules and WSPS Rule 3.2.3

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.4 Equipment

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.4.1 No additional light on the target is required; all lighting must follow ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.4.2 Competition Jury members must test the IR LED system. If a unit fails or is broken it is an allowable Malfunction.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.4.3 The Athlete must bring their own LED for the Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.4.4 During qualification and Finals , all competing Athletes must wear an eye covering which completely covers the eyes and ensures no vision is possible, such as opaque goggles, completely enclosed glasses , safety glasses or a mask deemed suitable by WSPS.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.4.5 The sound unit of the Athlete is not permitted to produce sound outside of the headphones. Audible noise from one (1) meter away is prohibited.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.5 Equipment Control

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.5.1 Team Leaders and coaches are responsible for ensuring that the Athlete has equipment and apparel that comply with these Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.5.2 ISSF equipment will be checked in accordance with the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) VI Shooting specific equipment checks will be done in accordance with these Rules and Regulations.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) The Athlete is responsible for submitting VI Shooting -specific equipment and apparel for official inspection and approval before the start of every Competition. As part of this process:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 53

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: I. the Athlete must present both their current ID Card and WSPS Licence; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: II. the ‘Equipment Control Sheet’ must be completed and signed by all relevant parties.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.5.3 Each Athlete and their VI Shooting-specific equipment may be checked by the Competition Jury on the Firing Line prior to the start of each Event.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.5.4 Random equipment checks will be done by the Competition Jury from Equipment Control following the Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.6 Non-allowable Malfunctions

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.6.1 A claim that there is a Malfunction of the aiming system must be immediately reported to the range staff.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.6.2 Range staff will check the following during Competition:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: a) disconnected wires.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: b) low power bank or battery pack.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.6.3 All other situation s regarding Malfunctions of the aiming system will be dealt with in accordance with the ISSF rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.7 Shooting Chairs & Table for Prone Position

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.7.1 Use of a backrest in the shooting position is prohibited.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.7.2 For the prone position, it is not allowed to have a Shooting Chair with arm rests or sideboards.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.2.7.3 WSPS Rules 3.8.1.1 to 3.8.1.6 will be applied.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.3 Shooting Positions

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.3.1 Prone

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.3.1.1 WSPS Rule 4.2.2.5 will apply.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.3.2 Standing

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.3.2.1 Athletes must be free-standing conforming to ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.3.2.2 The cheek must be used as described in the ISSF Rules.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.3.2.3 The barrel of the rifle must be level with the shoulders of the Athlete.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.3.2.4 It is not necessary that the cheek is touching the cheek piece.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4 VI Assistant

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.1 All VI Athletes must be accompanied by a VI Assistant during their Competition.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.2 The VI Assistant:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 54

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.2.1 must place the LED lights on the target a minimum of ten (10) minutes before the call to the Firing Line;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.2.2 verbal communication between the Athlete and the VI Assistant is prohibited during the Competition. The VI Assistant is permitted to give non-verbal signals during the match for score indication and to show the direction of their target;

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.2.3 may adjust the sights at the request of the Athlete and is not allowed to support the rifle. Only one (1) person may be touching the rifle during aiming; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.2.4 must stand in position for the duration of the Events (VIP & VIS) and it is not permitted to move between shots. The VI Assistant position (behind the Athlete) is fixed according to the rules and cannot be changed. The VI Assistant must stand at a minimum of 50cm behind the Athlete and may only move to give the signals for the score of the Athlete.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.3 A VI Assistant may:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.3.1 assist the Athlete with set up of equipment including the aiming device; and

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.3.2 immediately notify an Athlete if they are not pointing at their own target.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 7.4.3.3 A VI Assistant is only permitted to load if allowed in accordance with the terms of their WSPS Licence.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 55 8 Team Event Rules

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1 Team Events and format

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.1 These will be included in WSPS Recognised Competitions, unless specified otherwise.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.2 Team scores will be calculated by adding the individual Event scores of the Athletes within a team together (i.e. no separate team matches will be shot).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.3 Only an Athlete entered as a ‘Full’ participant may compete in team events. Athletes entered as MQS only may not participate.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.4 Team size:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.4.1 All teams must consist of three Athletes.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.5 Maximum number of teams per NPC:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.5.1 WSPS Sanctioned Competitions and WSPS Championships: only one team per event per NPC.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.5.2 WSPS Approved Competitions: maximum two teams per event per NPC.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.6 Event viability:

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.6.1 Minimum three teams must be on the start list of that E vent (by the final entries deadline); otherwise, the team Event is automatically cancelled.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.1.6.2 If only three teams participate in the Event, medals will be awarded according to the ‘minus -one’ rule (e.g. only gold and silver would be awarded).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.2 Mixed Team – Rifle/Pistol

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.2.1 Maximum of two teams per event per NPC.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.2.2 Mixed team events will follow the current ISSF forma t with the final’s competition format specified in the Commands and Announcements for Finals document on the WSPS website.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.3 Para Trap Two Person Team

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.3.1 Maximum of two teams per NPC.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.3.2 The team will consist of one male and one female athlete per team. The athletes can be entered from any of the Para Trap Events (i.e. PT1, PT2, or PT3).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 8.3.3 Team scores will be calculated by adding the individual Event scores of the Athletes within a team together (i.e. no separate team matches will be shot).

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: World Shooting Para Sport Technical Rules and Regulations, v1. ©2026 International Paralympic Committee – ALL RIGHTS RESERVED 56 9 Medical Rules

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.1 Athlete Safety

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.1.1 The overriding priority is always to safeguard the health and safety of Athletes . The outcome of the Competition should never influence such decisions.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.1.2 It is the responsibility of the team management to evaluate whether a sick or injured Athlete is fit to continue in or return to the Competition. WSPS may delay or prevent any Athlete from entering or participating in any Competition based on the health, safety or security of any Athletes or other participants, at its absolute discretion.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.2 Epilepsy

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.2.1 It is the duty of all Athletes and their NPCs to declare to WSPS if the Athlete has ever suffered any form of epileptic fit/seizure or epilepsy-related episode.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.2.2 All Athletes must complete the ‘Athlete Epilepsy Declaration Form’ (available on the WSPS website) which must be uploaded to the Athlete ’s SDMS profile before they are eligible to have a WSPS Licence for the Competition season.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.2.3 The ‘Athlete Epilepsy Declaration Form’ confirms if the Athlete has epilepsy, and if so, that the epilepsy is stable , and identifies what type of epilepsy the Athlete suffers from.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.2.4 If an Athlete declares that he/she has been medically diagnosed with epilepsy and has had an epileptic episode in the preceding 12-month period, the Athlete’s participation in WSPS Recognised Competitions shall be subject to approval by WSPS.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.2.5 If at any time an Athlete suffers any form of epileptic fit/seizure or epilepsy -related episode, an updated ‘ Athlete Epilepsy Declaration Form’ must immediately be submitted to WSPS.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.3 Pacemakers

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.3.1 The use of pacemakers by Athletes in WSPS Recognised Competition s is subject to approval by WSPS.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.3.2 Any Athlete that uses a pacemaker is required to submit a medical file to WSPS (info@worldshootingparasport.org), detailing the pathology and technical details of the device implemented.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.3.3 The WSPS shall determine whether the device is approved , and this decision is final. The Athlete will only be entitled to use this approved device, and any change must be notified to WSPS immediately.

chunks.title: WSPS Rulebook 2026_vFinal
chunks.text: 9.3.4 Failure to notify WSPS of the use of a pacemaker results in automatic disqualification of the Athlete and any results obtained in Competition where a pacemaker was used.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: REGULAMENTO DE CARABINA F-CLASS Rimfire Atualizado em 05/01/2026 t [IMAGE/DIAGRAM PAGE: embedded text is partial; visual contents require image reading.]

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: Confederação Brasileira de Tiro Esportivo Regulamento de Carabina F-Class Rimfire Atualizado em 05/01/2026

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: I- Finalidade Regulamentar a prova de F-Class Rimfire no âmbito da Confederação Brasileira de Tiro Esportivo.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: II- Descrição da Prova

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: a) Distância 100 (cem) metros.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: b) Alvo

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 1. Alvo oficial CBTE Fabricante: LCL, COD: 09H

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 2. Alvo oficial de F-Class Rimfire compostos por círculos concêntricos azuis com anéis de escore brancos nos valores de 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 e X.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 3. Os alvos terão suas medidas proporcionais nas distâncias que serão utilizados, mantendo a relação de tamanho, de acordo com a regra oficial internacional da NRA.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 4. Para fins de melhor visualização dos impactos, em especial quando não houver trincheiras no estande para sua marcação, o círculo concêntrico será padronizado na cor azul.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 5. Alvo possui a medida total de 700 x 700 mm contendo 06 (seis) alvos circulares de prova à direita com linhas de 1,2 mm com as demais medidas abaixo informadas e 02 dois alvos de ensaio à esquerda sendo 01(um) no formato CROSSHAIR.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 6. Os alvos de prova F-Class Rimfire de 100 metros possui as seguintes medidas: Anéis de pontuação Diâmetr (preto) o (mm) X 13 10 26 9 54 8 82 7 109 6 165 5 220

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: c) Posição

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 1. Deitado (Prone).

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 2. Corpo estendido no chão, vedada a utilização de estruturas elevadas, cabeça na direção do alvo.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 3. O carregador não pode encostar no solo de forma a propiciar apoio artificial.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 4. O Rifle deverá ser disparado a partir do ombro do atirador.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: d) Competição

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 1. Tempo de preparação: 05 minutos, cumprindo as regras de segurança no deslocamento e manuseio das armas.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 2. Tempo de prova: 25 minutos, com número de disparos ilimitados nos (02) alvos de ensaio a esquerda.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 3. Alvos de prova: total de 30 impactos que pontuam nos 06 alvos a direita, sendo 05 impactos em cada alvo:

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: a) Todos os disparos deverão ser feitos alimentando-se ao armar um a um, mesmo que a arma possua carregador para mais de uma munição.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: b) Expressamente vedada a reentrada na disciplina F-Class Rimfire. Obs.: Poderão ser utilizadas armas semiautomáticas, porém será obrigatória a alimentação de um a um no carregador ou diretamente na câmara. 2

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: Confederação Brasileira de Tiro Esportivo Regulamento de Carabina F-Class Rimfire Atualizado em 05/01/2026

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: e) Comandos: • "Atenção senhores atiradores, ocupem seus postos!” • Ocupados os postos… • "Seu tempo de 05 minutos de preparação começará a partir de AGORA!" • Após 5 minutos… • “Tempo de preparação ENCERRADO!” • “Atiradores prontos” • "Seu tempo de 25 minutos para ensaio livre e 30 disparos de prova começará AGORA!" • “CESSAR”! • “Prova encerrada armas abertas em segurança, retirem seus carregadores e utilizem Safety Flag, bandeira de segurança ou indicador de câmara vazia! • Aguardar comando para guardar o equipamento! Obs.: *Armas em segurança significa: abertas e descarregadas, com safety flag ou em seus invólucros. *Não é permitido o municiamento durante o tempo de preparação. *O Árbitro da prova não precisará avisar voluntariamente aos competidores da passagem do tempo. Os atletas poderão perguntar aos Árbitros de prova sobre o tempo restante. A pergunta e a resposta deverão ser feitas em um tom que não perturbe outros competidores. *O Árbitro de Prova poderá dar outros comandos não previstos nesta regra. * Cessar Fogo: Todos os competidores deverão parar de atirar imediatamente ao ouvir o comando

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: “CESSAR”. Todos os rifles devem ser descarregados, os carregadores destacáveis removidos e as ações abertas ao ouvir se este comando. Tal comando pode ser dado por qualquer pessoa no estande que detecte situação de insegurança.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: f) Falhas de munição; Não Serão consideradas como zero, o atleta poderá substituir por outra e deixa-la a mostra para comprovação.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: g) Falhas da arma; Serão consideradas como zero, caso o atleta não consiga sanar a pane em seu posto de tiro em segurança.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: h) Apuração;

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 1. Os alvos poderão ser apurados na linha de tiro ou, a critério do delegado no local da prova.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 2. Os impactos serão computados baseados no diâmetro do projétil disparado naquele alvo, computando- se o anel de maior valor em contato com a borda do furo deixado pelo projétil.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 3. O escore deverá computar a quantidade de pontos e o número de X (centros) em decimais, por exemplo: 280 pontos e 12X = 280,12.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 4. Nos casos de difícil determinação, será dado o maior valor em benefício do atirador.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 5. Impactos fora dos anéis de escores serão computados como zero. O mesmo ocorrendo caso o atirador efetue menos disparos do que o requerido, ou se disparar em alvo errado.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: i) Penalização para tiros dados há mais;

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 1. Em caso de um tiro cruzado, tal fato deverá ser imediatamente comunicado ao árbitro. O tiro cruzado não será contado no alvo que foi atingido acidentalmente. O autor do disparo cruzado, quando identificado, 3

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: Confederação Brasileira de Tiro Esportivo Regulamento de Carabina F-Class Rimfire Atualizado em 05/01/2026 será penalizado em menos 10 (dez) pontos na contagem final. Ao autor do tiro cruzado é vedada, a repetição do disparo.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 2. Se o disparo cruzado impactar um alvo em que um tiro legítimo já tenha sido efetuado pelo atleta e na impossibilidade de identificar o autor do disparo, será considerado o impacto de maior valor não causando prejuízo ao atleta.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 3. Disparos em excesso, nesse caso será penalizado com menos 10 (dez) pontos por disparo a mais realizado, considerando-se os excedentes aos 30 disparos regulamentares.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: III- Divisões

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: a) Divisão Open ● Rifle de fogo circular que utilize calibre igual a 4,5 ou 5,5 milímetros Ex: (17-HMR, 22-LR, 22-MAG). Qualquer sistema de mira ótica e visada é permitido, porém será incluído no peso total do rifle. ● O peso total do rifle inclui todos os equipamentos aderidos ao rifle, como bandoleira, miras, Bipé, etc., e não poderá exceder 9,0 quilogramas (aprox. 19,84 libras). Um equipamento aderido inclui qualquer objeto externo que não o competidor ou sua roupa, que recue total ou parcialmente com o rifle, em que é preso, seguro ou juntado de qualquer forma para cada disparo, ou que seja levantado com o rifle, mesmo que parcialmente, quando este é suspenso de seus apoios. ● Qualquer gatilho manualmente operado que atenda aos requisitos de segurança é permitido. ● A largura do forend (fuste) do rifle não deverá exceder 76 mm aprox. 3 polegadas. ● O rifle deve ser disparado na posição deitado, a partir do ombro do atirador podendo ser utilizados os apoios dianteiro e traseiro definidos no item “b)”.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: b) Apoios na Open

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 1. O rifle poderá ser apoiado na dianteira do final do forend/fuste até a frente do guarda mato por qualquer meio, desde que este não seja um meio mecânico que ativamente retorne a arma ao ponto específico de visada do disparo anterior. Se for utilizado o Bipé, este deve ser preso de qualquer forma ao rifle e este apoio deverá ser incluído no peso total do rifle. Como apoio na parte traseira é permitido o uso de saco de areia, no formato de orelha de coelho ou saco de areia ou mão usando luvas que não sejam rígidas.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 2. Não poderão ser utilizados mais do que dois apoios e estes não poderão ser ligados um ao outro de nenhuma forma.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 3. A utilização de qualquer forma de mesa ou estruturas elevadas que fiquem entre o atleta e o solo é proibida. Placas planas separadas que não excedam o tamanho dos apoios por duas polegadas 5 centímetros são permitidos de serem colocadas abaixo dos apoios dianteiro e traseiro. Não é permitido o uso de qualquer dispositivo de nivelamento nessas placas que devem ser planas nas superfícies superior e inferior.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 4. Nenhuma parte da coronha ou da empunhadura do rifle pode repousar diretamente no chão, placa ou superfície rígida. Qualquer apoio traseiro empregado não pode ser preso ou rigidamente conectado ao rifle de qualquer maneira. Quaisquer apoios traseiros mecanicamente ajustáveis não são permitidos.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 5. Uma alternativa lícita de apoio frontal/central é o uso de uma jaqueta, toalha, coberta enrolada, ou em cima de um saco de areia ou qualquer outro material.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 6. Qualquer número de objetos pode ser colocado abaixo dos apoios para compensar variações de altura no posto de tiro ou para reduzir o desnível entre o atleta e o alvo.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 7. O apoio dianteiro poderá ter até 3 três pés cravados e pressionados sobre o chão, desde que esses pinos de cravação ou espetos não entrem no solo mais do que 2 polegadas ou 5 centímetros e que essa cravação não danifique de forma significativa o posto de tiro. 4

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: Confederação Brasileira de Tiro Esportivo Regulamento de Carabina F-Class Rimfire Atualizado em 05/01/2026

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 8. Os apoios podem ser reajustados após cada disparo de forma a compensar sua movimentação ou ajuste. Uma bandoleira poderá ser utilizada em junção com o(s) apoio(s), mas o seu peso será incluído no peso total da arma.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: c) Divisão F-T/R • Rifle de fogo circular restrito aos calibres 22-LR sem qualquer modificação nas suas dimensões originais, sendo expressamente vedada a utilização de armas com refinador de harmônico, Tuner ou cano BULL com medida superior 16 mm/0.629921’’ na boca do cano. • Para a obtenção da medida da boca do cano que eventualmente possua uma sessão de rosca ou rebaixamento destinado a instalação de acessórios em sua extremidade frontal, a medição será realizada tendo como referência o diâmetro imediatamente anterior ao início do rebaixamento ou fio de rosca. • Qualquer gatilho manualmente operado que atenda aos requisitos de segurança é permitido. • Qualquer sistema de mira ótica e visada é permitido, porém será incluído no peso total do rifle. • O rifle deve ser disparado na posição deitado a partir do ombro do atirador. • O peso total do rifle inclui todos os equipamentos aderidos ao rifle, como Bipé, bandoleira, miras, carregador etc. E não deverá exceder 4,400 quilogramas (aprox. 9,7 libras). Um equipamento aderido inclui qualquer objeto externo que não o competidor ou sua roupa, que recue total ou parcialmente com

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: o rifle em que é preso, seguro ou juntado de qualquer forma para cada disparo, ou que seja, mesmo que parcialmente, levantado com o rifle quando este é suspendido de seus apoios.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: d) Apoios na F-T/R

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 1. O rifle deve ser disparado utilizando-se como apoio dianteiro de um Bipé, rigidamente conectado no fuste dianteiro do rifle e/ou na bandoleira. Qualquer Bipé, atendendo a definição de Bipé, pode ser utilizado, mas seu peso será incluído no peso total do rifle.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 2. Um Bipé e/ou bandoleira são os únicos apoios frontais permitidos. O Bipé e/ou bandoleira não poderá ser ou ter um meio mecânico que ativamente retorne a arma ao ponto específico de visada do disparo anterior, podendo ser usado como apoio na parte traseira um saco de areia no formato de orelha de coelho ou saco de areia ou mão usando luvas que não sejam rígidas.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 3. O Bipé e/ou bandoleira e o apoio traseiro não podem estar interligados de qualquer forma.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 4. A utilização de qualquer forma de mesa ou estruturas elevadas que fiquem entre o atleta e o solo é proibida. Placas ou chapas separadas que não excedam a dimensão individual dos apoios por duas polegadas ou cinco centímetros são permitidas de serem colocadas abaixo desses apoios. No caso de Bipés, a placa ou chapa não pode exceder a largura do Bipé por 2 polegadas ou 5 centímetros ou ser maior do que 12 polegadas ou 30,5 centímetros de comprimento de frente para trás. Nenhuma regulagem de parafuso ou de protrusão existente nas placas ou chapas é permitida. Essa chapa ou placa deve ser completamente lisa na superfície superior e inferior.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 5. Um Bipé é um dispositivo que tem não mais do que duas pernas tocando a posição de tiro. O Bipé deve ser rigidamente conectado ao fuste do rifle. O Bipé pode ser rígido ou ter as pernas articuláveis, bem como podem também ser articulados de forma a compensar eventual desnivelamento do posto de tiro.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 6. Nenhuma parte do rifle poder tocar o solo ou superfície rígida. Nenhum suporte traseiro deve ser conectado, fixado ou seguro no rifle de quaisquer maneiras. Qualquer suporte traseiro ajustável mecanicamente não é permitido.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 7. “Rail Guns” (armas sobre trilhos rígidos) e/ou equipamentos mecânicos que ativamente retornem a arma ao ponto específico de visada do disparo anterior, não são permitidos. 5

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: Confederação Brasileira de Tiro Esportivo Regulamento de Carabina F-Class Rimfire Atualizado em 05/01/2026

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: IV- Outros equipamentos

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 1. Vestimentas ● É permitido o uso de luvas maleáveis, próprias de tiro esportivo; ● Ombreiras, bandoleiras almofadadas e cotoveleiras podem ser utilizadas desde que não sejam constituídos de forma a prestar apoio adicional ao rifle; ● Casacos, calças e outras vestimentas de tiro esportivo (ex: ISSF) poderão ser utilizadas; ● Coberta, pano ou material sintético para separar o contato com o chão pode ser utilizado desde que não possibilitem ou prestem apoio adicional; ● Será permitido o uso de calçados comuns, casuais, de trabalho ou botas do tipo de caça, permanecendo vedado o uso de roupas no estilo jeans e camuflados, bem como sandálias (dedos e/ou calcanhares à mostra) e/ou o não uso de calçados.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 2. Óculos de Proteção e protetor auricular É de responsabilidade e dever de cada atleta e demais pessoas na linha de tiro a utilização de EPI.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 3. Bandeiras de vento É permitido e recomenda-se a instalação a variadas distâncias entre a linha de tiro e os alvos, pela organização da prova ou, mesmo pelo atleta desde que previamente aprovado pelo Árbitro da Prova, e observando a segurança no estande. As bandeiras de vento podem ser as tradicionais de NRA Highpower (forma triangular, com 18 polegadas de largura na base e 12 polegadas na ponta, com 48 polegadas de comprimento, divididas ao meio pelas cores vermelho e amarelo), ou fitas nas cores vermelho, laranja ou amarelo, de preferência com 1 metro de comprimento e pelo menos 2,5cm de largura.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 4. Aparelhos eletrônicos Não poderão ser utilizados nos postos de tiro, dispositivos como rádios, celulares, anemômetros ou qualquer outro equipamento que produza som ou meio de comunicação com atleta.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 5. Luneta de observação É permitido somente pelo atleta em prova utilizar uma luneta de observação para verificar os impactos em seu alvo e/ou condições atmosféricas do estande.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 6. Dispositivos laser Não é permitido o seu uso pelo atleta ou espectador, estando ou não acoplado à arma.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 7. Munição Qualquer tipo de munição pode ser utilizado, desde que não represente perigo para os competidores, pessoal da organização, ou equipamentos e estruturas do estande. Munição traçante ou incendiária são proibidas. Qualquer munição que repetidamente “estoure” as espoletas ou rache ou separe os estojos será considerada como defeituosa ou insegura e deverá ser removida da linha de tiro.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: 8. Compensadores ou quebra-chamas O uso de compensadores ou quebra-chamas é proibido em ambas as divisões. 6

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: Confederação Brasileira de Tiro Esportivo Regulamento de Carabina F-Class Rimfire Atualizado em 05/01/2026

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: V- Classes • Serão disputadas em classes de acordo com regulamento geral.

chunks.title: Regulamento CBTE — Carabina F-Class Rimfire
chunks.text: VI- Casos Omissos, Divergência ou Dúvida neste regulamento Os casos omissos e eventuais divergências caso ocorram, serão resolvidos pela Comissão Técnica. Em qualquer caso, sempre terá prevalência as regras no formato original e que podem ser encontradas em: http://www.nrahq.org/compete/RuleBooks/HPR/hpr-index.pdf 7
